annotation.summary: Domain: agent-projection
assumptions: Single module domain roll-up mirrors mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection.
AGENTS.md managed block merged via marker delimiters.
risks: Snippet drift between clients when only one renderer updated.
patterns: Projection is canonical source for AGENTS.md and client agent files.
invariants: Agent protocol block version tracked in projection metadata.
Doctor fails when required snippets missing from generated files.
extensionPoints: New projection snippets add PROJECTION_REQUIRED_SNIPPETS entries.

annotation.dataFlow: manifest + protocol/template snippets -> projection render helpers -> AGENTS.md/client agent guidance/harness run-brief text; harness annotate phase consumes riskScopeCandidates as advisory candidates, not proof.

annotation.summary: agents domain (5 modules): repovine's Agent Protocol surface — builtin manifests, protocol schemas, role source, compliance validation — plus the harness lib/agents.mjs role-brief loader (resolveRole, roleCatalog) the planner resolves roles against.
assumptions: Agent Protocol v1 used only in harness or explicit compliance runs.
Builtin agent defs live in mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests.
Role briefs are repo-owned prompt material from configured agent directories or bundled defaults.
Agent identity comes from role metadata/name, not display label alone.
The harness side is one member: mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/agents.
risks: An omitted assignment does not skip compliance: it disarms the assignment-derived gates — run-id linkage, phase and scope judgements, the context-session requirement — while manifest fields, declared graph nodes, declared annotations and provenance still run and still hard-fail. Weak tool usage stays a warning because nothing can make it enforceable without an assignment.
Manifest drift from onboarding projections breaks doctor checks.
Stale role files in persisted sandbox affect worker behavior across /new without /reset.
patterns: Subagent handoffs use SubagentHandoff schema in multi-agent workflows.
Project specialists as stand-ins; repovine-owned agents rendered separately.
invariants: Normal client chats do not emit AgentRunResult JSON.
Compliance checks contextSessionId quality on repovine MCP calls.
Fallback and bundled role prose use sub-agent terminology for user/agent-facing instructions.
Role resolution must not introduce provider secrets or runtime config into prompts.
extensionPoints: New builtin agents add manifest entry and onboarding-assets projection.
Add or override role briefs through configured agent directories.
Add role-specific constraints while preserving shared sub-agent result contract.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests; mod:repovine/src/agents/validation; mod:repovine/src/cli/agents; mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection; harness planner and worker execution resolve role descriptions through lib/agents before constructing sub-agent tasks.
annotation.dataFlow: assignment/result JSON → schema validation → checkCompliance → pass/fail report. Harness side: multi.mjs/leaf.mjs loadRolePrompt(role) → configured agent dirs then bundled paths → opts.agentPrompt injected into the worker.

annotation.summary: Repository analysis: the architecture/refactoring detectors, finding selection/balancing/dedup, and on-demand detail expansion behind the analyze_architecture MCP tool.
assumptions: Findings are candidates not proven safe refactors.
Detectors share heuristics module for surface classification.
risks: False positives on generically named modules.
Missing annotations reduce reasoning quality in detail mode.
patterns: Pair analyze_architecture with inspect_node on implicated nodes.
Use detailFindingId for single-finding deep dive.
invariants: Read-only analysis never mutates repo state.
Security categories respect strictness from config.
extensionPoints: New detector categories register in architecture detector suite.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/annotation-secret (shared SsoT for secret-value detection); mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/component-signals (shared SsoT for workflow signal kinds); mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detectors; mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detail; mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/analyze-architecture.
annotation.dataFlow: Graph and annotations feed detector suite consumed by analyze_architecture MCP tool.

annotation.summary: analyze_architecture engine subdomain (14 modules): detector registry/bootstrap, threshold config, heuristics, detail expansion, and runRefactoringReport orchestration. Produces advisory RefactoringFinding candidates for MCP analyze_architecture and architecture audits.
assumptions: Findings are advisory candidates — analyze_architecture never auto-applies refactors.
Strictness and per-category thresholds come from repovine.config.json analyze_architecture section.
risks: Heuristic detectors produce false positives — findings require inspect_node verification.
Missing detector-bootstrap import yields empty detector registry.
invariants: Read-only over graph and annotations — no filesystem writes.
detector-bootstrap must run before getDetectors returns plugins.
Security-sensitive categories honor strictness profiles from config.
extensionPoints: New detector: wrap detect* or add ArchitectureDetector plus register in detector-bootstrap INTERNAL_DETECTORS.
New category: extend RefactoringCategory, config thresholds, and detail/refactoringCategoryDetail branch.
annotation.integrationPoints: mcp/tools/analyze-architecture; mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture index orchestrator; annotations/store for annotationReasoning; detector-bootstrap registry.
annotation.dataFlow: MCP analyze_architecture → runRefactoringReport → detector registry → RefactoringFinding[] → optional detail expansion.

annotation.summary: Surface-gated analyze_architecture detector packs (3 modules): ui-surface adapters for eight frontend/security categories and server-surface adapter for server-handler-orchestration.
assumptions: Detector implementations stay in architecture/detectors — packs are adapters plus appliesTo gates.
UI pack has eight detectors; server pack has one (server-handler-orchestration).
risks: Splitting detector bodies without updating adapters breaks category wiring silently until bootstrap drift guard.
New category without pack adapter never surfaces in analyze_architecture output.
invariants: Pack catalog ids must match detectors registered in INTERNAL_DETECTORS.
appliesTo gates use surface predicates — not inline heuristics in adapters.
Detector-bootstrap assertDetectorPacksRegistered guards registration drift.
extensionPoints: New surface pack: add detectors module plus pack const plus INTERNAL_DETECTOR_PACKS entry plus bootstrap registration lines.
annotation.integrationPoints: architecture/detector-bootstrap; architecture/surfaces/ui and server appliesTo predicates; analyze_architecture MCP tool.
annotation.dataFlow: INTERNAL_DETECTOR_PACKS → detector-bootstrap assertDetectorPacksRegistered → registerDetector at legacy positions.

annotation.summary: Domain: annotations
assumptions: Domain tagged members share annotation queue drain after module pass.
Only mod:repovine MCP tools may write repovine.annots.json.
validateAnnotationHealth reports carrier-link gaps via mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-links; risk-scope candidates are advisory only.

sideEffects.description: AnnotationStore file-lock read/write repovine.annots.json

risks: Hand-editing repovine.annots.json corrupts merge metadata and freshness.
Thin domain roll-ups mislead map_context — keep integrationPoints current.
patterns: importBaseline propagation-stale clears with refreshImportBaseline after upstream review.
Carrier-link gaps validated in validateAnnotationHealth.
Runtime-resource content-hash fingerprinting (service-resource-hash) reduces multi-declared resource ids to an order-independent set-hash, mirroring domain member hashing.
invariants: Unified queue: content-stale before propagation-stale; modules before domain roll-ups.
Quality score 9–10 requires moduleKind recommendedFields + consistency.ok.
extensionPoints: New annotation features extend mod:repovine/src/annotations/store and mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/annotations annotateModule.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/annotations/store; mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance; mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-links; mod:repovine/src/annotations/risk-scope-candidates; mod:repovine/src/annotations/service-resource-hash; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/annotations.
annotation.dataFlow: write_annotation → store → refresh_context → queue recompute.

annotation.summary: Architecture detectors + refactoring findings: the detector registry/bootstrap, per-category detector bodies, scope/heuristics/component-signals helpers, and finding dedup/sort/balance behind analyze_architecture.
assumptions: Findings are candidates requiring inspect_node verification.
strictness tunes security detector sensitivity.
risks: Generic package names can false-positive heuristics.
Stale annotations weaken annotationReasoning in detail view.
patterns: Heuristics classify surfaces before security and structural detectors.
detailFindingId expands one finding with node summaries.

annotationReasoning is opt-in per detector.

annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/annotation-secret (shared SsoT for secret-value detection); mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/component-signals (shared SsoT for workflow signal kinds); mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detectors (legacy detector implementations, now deduplicated to import shared modules); mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detail (detail expansion); mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/heuristics; mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/annotation-context; mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/analyze-architecture.
annotation.dataFlow: ModuleInfo plus annotations plus entrypoints feed detectors producing RefactoringFinding list with optional detail expansion.

annotation.summary: Architecture detector packs: the ui-surface and server-surface packs group frontend/backend-class ArchitectureDetector adapters; detector bodies live in analysis/architecture/detectors and registration stays in detector-bootstrap at legacy positions.
assumptions: 3 modules: architecture-detectors/* individual detector implementations.
Registered via analysis/architecture/detector-bootstrap INTERNAL_DETECTORS.
invariants: A pack is a grouping/identity unit, not a registration loop — detector order is load-bearing for finding-id parity.
Adapters delegate run() to the untouched legacy detect* bodies.
extensionPoints: Add a detector by writing its body in analysis/architecture/detectors, an adapter in the relevant pack, and a bootstrap registry entry at the correct legacy position.

The content lives on mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/attach-guard; this roll-up adds no facts of its own.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wraps mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/attach-guard; the container refuses to run unless the mounted guard file matches this constant byte for byte.

assumptions: Single module lib/blockers.mjs.

Per-chat thread id with MemorySaver checkpointer.

Dual-entry health/doctor checks mirror MCP tool registry.

doctor validates required onboarding snippets.
Removed transport flags have no dedicated branch or compatibility shim in v1.

New onboarding assets added to templates module.

CLI mirrors MCP agent protocol validation for harness and CI workflows.
AgentRunResult block must match protocolVersion=1 schema.

Compliance flags must reflect observable MCP calls, not agent prose.
Manifest templates must stay aligned with agent-protocol.md contract.

Template builders, plugin rendering, setup, clear, and health derive client-specific strings from mod:repovine/src/cli/client-capabilities instead of hardcoding per-client branches.

Roll-up stale when member module annotation changes.
invariants: Client scope drives which managed assets are expected on disk.

annotation.summary: Configuration surface: loading and validation of repovine.config.json (build.scan/linking, MCP + analyzer settings) alongside the harness runtime config, plus default propagation/threshold constants consumed across stages. A cross-cutting layer that groups config producers and their heavy consumers, so it spans both engine and harness modules.
assumptions: repovine.config.json is SSOT — env vars only override select fields.
v1 config has no legacy migration layer and no network transport settings; new tunables should be optional/defaulted unless a future versioned policy is explicitly introduced.
risks: Domain scope misleads without pkg: filter.
build.scan exclude/include drift breaks graph vs workspace intent.
patterns: repovine: defaults < file < env precedence in ResolvedConfig.
Lambda handlers read process.env bound in template.yaml.
annotation.flowDescription: Modules read config from process.env or repovine.config.json; get_config_surface aggregates referenced names; config no longer exposes network listener port/host.
invariants: Invalid config fails fast at loadConfig with Zod path.
Kebab-case JSON keys map to camelCase ResolvedConfig.
STDIO-only v1 config has no network listener key or resolved listener field.
extensionPoints: New tunables add optional Zod fields in mod:repovine/src/config and defaults in CONFIG_DEFAULTS.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/config loadConfig; mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/config; mod:repovine/src/context-quality/types.
annotation.dataFlow: env + config files → graph hints/runtime config → get_config_surface aggregation.

annotation.summary: Config-surface domain (src/mcp/lib/config-surface.ts): collects environment variable names, secret references, and resource bindings behind the get_config_surface tool.
assumptions: Single module mcp/lib/config-surface: aggregates env var names, secrets, and resource bindings from graph InfraResource nodes.
Read-only over RepovineRuntime graph — no filesystem env reads.
risks: Undocumented env additions bypass detectors until get_config_surface refreshed.
Over-broad scope leaks unrelated package config names.
patterns: Read-only aggregation over stage2 graph config nodes.
Pairs with analyze_dependencies for contract changes vs config additions.
invariants: Reports env var names only — never secret values from templates or annotations.
extensionPoints: New config kind filter in collectConfigSurface.
Additional resource binding types from IaC parsers surface here automatically.
annotation.integrationPoints: get_config_surface MCP tool; IaC parsers env extraction; analyze_architecture secret-config-boundary detector.
annotation.dataFlow: get_config_surface MCP call → collectConfigSurface over graph nodes → env/secrets/resources payload with empty-diagnostics on zero scope.

assumptions: Conformance checks run against representative sample inputs for plugin behavior validation.

Validation uses plugin-sdk schemas as canonical acceptance criteria.

refresh_context and cold tool calls share IndexBuildController serialization.

Skipping semantic sync after rebuild serves stale embedding hits.

Boundary index written after successful graph build for hook consumers.

Building state returns status:building with eta_sec — agents must wait or read files.
Annotation store reloads from disk after external merge_annotations.

annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/context RepovineRuntime; mod:repovine/src/mcp/build-controller; mod:repovine/src/mcp/index; mod:repovine/src/semantic/store; mod:repovine/src/mcp/boundary-index.

annotation.summary: Context-quality domain: MCP context session quality types, metrics scoring, and session store persistence.

impact is default mode for module scopes.
risks: Call-graph gaps hide dynamic callers in impact exportName filter.
Barrel files mask boundary violations.

exportName filter applies to impact downstream uses only.

annotation.summary: Client hook dispatcher subsystem: loading the single shipped dispatcher script and recognizing hook entries that repovine already manages, so setup/clear/health stay idempotent across Claude, Cursor, and Codex. mod:repovine/src/cli/dispatcher owns CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME and reads the dispatcher's source bytes via import.meta.url; mod:repovine/src/cli/dispatcher/hook-identity uses that same filename token to test whether a config's existing hook command already points at it, distinguishing a managed exec-form Claude hook or Cursor shell command from a user-defined one.

annotation.summary: Dockerfile IaC parsing domain: the dockerfile plugin wrapper and its parser logic.
assumptions: Dockerfile parser outputs normalized infra deltas compatible with IaC pipeline consumers.

annotation.summary: Egress-gateway domain (1 module): the credential-custody origin proxy that runs inside the gateway sidecar. It terminates plain HTTP on loopback and re-originates upstream over TLS with the real credential injected there, so the worker holds only placeholders, and it pins recipient ids on the messaging path.
assumptions: A directory-derived domain, not a basename one: the gateway ships one JavaScript module and the rest of its behaviour is shell and iptables in the image.
The image installs no npm packages, so the proxy uses built-in modules only.
invariants: The worker never receives the real model or messaging credential — enforced entirely within the single member module, mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/docker/egress-gw/proxy.
annotation.integrationPoints: Holds mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/docker/egress-gw/proxy; the image that runs it is infra:dockerfile:examples/agent-harness-demo/docker/egress-gw/Dockerfile and the runtime service is resource:generic:egress-gw.

annotation.summary: MCP entrypoints library domain (src/mcp/lib/entrypoints.ts): replays slotted EntrypointFragments from stage-2 interpreters by slot key in legacy global order for get_entrypoints.

annotation.summary: Entry-script domain (4 modules): the three channel entries onto the compiled graph — one-shot CLI, long-running HTTP, messaging bot — plus the host-side attach launcher that validates a target worktree before any container starts. The entries are thin: preflight, compile the graph once, hand off.
assumptions: Every channel runs the same compiled graph; the channel decides how a request arrives and how a reply leaves, never what the run does.
Preflight happens before anything binds or spawns, so a misconfigured run fails at startup rather than part way through.
Only real workers run on these paths; without credentials the worker reports blocked and the graph still validates and reports it.
risks: Credentials are exercised only when a worker starts, so every entry passes preflight and fails part way into a run when a provider is misconfigured.
The exit status groups unrelated preflight failures under shared codes, so only the logged line identifies which check failed.
invariants: The compiled graph is built exactly once per process.
The attach launcher makes no Docker call before every check passes, and preflight alone creates nothing.
The exit status carries the outcome, so a pipeline can gate on it without parsing output.
extensionPoints: A new channel adds an entry script and an adapter; the graph and the protocol contract stay untouched.
annotation.integrationPoints: All three channels call invokeGraph from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow; the attach launcher pairs with the attach compose profiles and mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/target-repo.

annotation.summary: Provider-worker domain (12 modules): the adapters that actually run an agent turn, plus the shared wiring they all need. Two provider families — the Claude SDK path and the local OpenAI-compatible path — each with a task adapter and a read-only ask adapter, over common auth, prompt composition, engine MCP wiring, usage accounting and MCP telemetry.
assumptions: A task worker and its ask counterpart share the provider but not the tool surface: the ask path runs a reduced, non-mutating set.
Prompt composition is provider-agnostic; the same policy text and result-shape contract reach every adapter.
The engine is reached as an MCP child, wired identically for every adapter through the shared descriptor builder.
risks: Read-only enforcement rests on enumerated tool lists rather than a property of the tools, so a newly added mutating engine tool is excluded until someone names it, and a permitted name that gains a mutating mode passes under its existing name.
The two provider families duplicate the turn loop shape, so a fix in one adapter does not reach the other.
invariants: Every adapter exposes the same runAgent seam, which is what lets the orchestrator pick one by provider name without knowing the family.
The ask adapters never return a protocol run result; they return answer text.
Usage is accounted per attempt and summed across retries rather than taken from the last one.
extensionPoints: A new provider adds one task adapter and one ask adapter behind the shared runAgent seam, plus a name in the worker selector.
annotation.integrationPoints: Selected by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/model-role and invoked from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/sub-agent; the engine MCP descriptor comes from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/mcp.

annotation.summary: Delivery-mechanics domain (2 modules): the single declaration of which risk-delivery mechanics exist, in what priority, which primitive each reads, and what tag it emits. One registry plus its context types; every consumer resolves priority from here rather than restating it.
assumptions: Detection predicates are composed from the annotation-format and side-effect vocabularies rather than reimplemented in the registry.
Annotation-derived detection is referenced from the modules that own it; topology-derived detection is declared in the registry itself.
A mechanic whose required primitive is absent self-gates to false rather than defaulting, so a caller that cannot supply a primitive loses that tag rather than getting a guess.
risks: Detection is all the registry currently dispatches: the channel and direction metadata is descriptive, and the delivery machinery does not yet route through it.
The consumer mechanic emits a tag under a different name than its own, an inherited skew visible in API responses.
invariants: Array order is the tag priority, pinned by a unit test so a reorder fails loudly instead of silently changing precedence across every delivery channel.
One mechanic is reserved: its detection always returns false and no channel produces it.
extensionPoints: A new mechanic adds a registry entry with its primitive, tag and priority position; consumers pick it up without change.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs for reference tagging and by mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/inspect-node for the attention block.

extensionPoints: New probes add hooks in mod:repovine/src/perf/memory-profiler called from stage1 hot paths.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/perf/memory-profiler; mod:repovine/src/stage1 collectRepositoryFactsAsync.
annotation.dataFlow: Explicit profiler enable → heap snapshots → advisory output.

annotation.summary: Agent harness demo package domain (56 modules): LangGraph workflow with compliance retry and sync-only merges, Telegram channel, multi-agent orchestration against a mode-resolved target — managed sandbox (default) or an attached pre-created Git worktree at /workspace.

Docker mode uses compose egress-gw as network boundary.

Attach (Phase 2) carries a launch-scoped disposable Git repo behind a read-only /workspace/.git pointer (/state/git, baseline commit + attach-baseline tag): git-tree custody and in-repo patch apply work in both modes, /reset restores the baseline, successful runs are snapshotted as attach/run-* for operator fetch/merge; the source common dir is never mounted and worktree parallelism stays sequential by policy.

annotation.summary: Credential-custody origin proxy inside the egress gateway. It shares a network namespace with the worker, terminates plain HTTP on loopback, and re-originates each request to the real upstream over TLS with the real credential injected here, so the worker itself never holds the model or bot token. On the messaging path it pins every recipient id carried by a content-delivering method to the configured allow-list, failing closed; a named set of read-only methods and the file-download path are forwarded without that check. It also runs a fourth, unrelated listener: a raw TCP pipe from a fixed loopback port to a host-side local-model server, carrying no credential and doing no rewrite.
assumptions: The worker is configured with placeholder credentials and a base URL pointing at this proxy; custody depends on that arrangement, not on the worker's own discretion.
Streaming responses are passed through unbuffered so a token stream is not held up by the proxy.
The image ships a runtime but no installed packages, so the implementation uses only built-in modules.
The upstream host, port and transport knobs exist so the proxy can be pointed at a compatible or on-premise endpoint and can be tested against a local mock.

The local-model forward is reachable only once the default-deny OUTPUT chain allow-lists host.docker.internal (EGRESS_ALLOW_HOST_DOCKER_INTERNAL=1 / EGRESS_ALLOW_CIDRS); the listener itself is always up.

sideEffects.description: re-originates requests to the model and messaging upstreams over TLS
pipes raw bytes from a fixed loopback port to a host-side local-model server (no header rewrite, protocol-agnostic)
listens on loopback ports for the model, messaging, health, and local-model-forward endpoints
logs proxy events

risks.text: This proxy is the custody boundary: the credentials live only here and the worker is given placeholders, so changing how the auth header is overwritten, how the token is injected into the path, or where the worker's base URL points moves real secrets into the worker's reach.

risks: Recipient pinning is enforced here rather than in the adapter, so a messaging method that carries a recipient in a shape the pinning does not recognize would be forwarded unpinned; the check fails closed to keep that from silently widening.
Because it listens on loopback within a shared namespace, anything else in that namespace can reach the same ports, so the isolation rests on what else runs there.
The local-model forward carries no custodied secret and does no header rewrite, so its isolation depends entirely on the firewall allow-list rather than anything in this proxy.
patterns: Terminate plain and re-originate secure: the secret is applied at the boundary rather than handed to the component that makes the call.
Placeholder in, real credential out, so a leaked worker environment yields nothing usable.
invariants: The worker never receives the real model or messaging credential.

Content-delivering messaging methods have every recipient id they carry pinned to the configured allow-list, failing closed when the body is unparseable or no recipient is present. A named set of read-only methods and the file-download path are exempt.
Listening sockets are bound to loopback only.
The local-model forward is a fixed loopback address (127.0.0.1:PROXY_LOCAL_PORT), so LOCAL_BASE_URL is one string on every platform.
annotation.integrationPoints: Runs as the egress gateway service defined in the harness compose stack; the worker and the messaging adapter reach it through the base URLs the launch configuration sets.
annotation.dataFlow: worker or adapter -> plain HTTP on loopback -> credential injected and recipients pinned -> TLS request to the real upstream -> response streamed back unbuffered. Separately: worker -> loopback local-model port -> raw pipe -> host.docker.internal.

envDependencies.LOCAL_UPSTREAM_HOST: Host the local-model forward connects to, default host.docker.internal.
envDependencies.LOCAL_UPSTREAM_PORT: Port the local-model forward connects to, default 11434.
envDependencies.PROXY_LOCAL_PORT: Loopback port the local-model raw TCP forward listens on (default 11434).
envDependencies.PROXY_MAX_TELEGRAM_BODY: Upper bound on a buffered messaging body for content-delivering methods; read-only methods forward without it.

keyExports.rolesFromMentions: Extracts catalog role ids mentioned in free text.

assumptions: A role must exist in the catalog: dropping a markdown file into the agents directory does not register it.
Utility roles (repo-explorer, annotation-writer) are backed by bundled prompt copies and can be dropped from the catalog by target mode.
The catalog is initialized once per process; tests must call resetRoleCatalogForTests to re-initialize it.

sideEffects.description: loadRolePrompt reads role markdown from the agents search dirs
reads AGENTS, HARNESS_AGENTS_DIR, HARNESS_APP_FRAME and HARNESS_REQUIRE_TESTS_ROLES
module-level role catalog shared for the process lifetime

risks: A missing or renamed bundled markdown file falls back to a generic inline prompt, so a role silently loses its brief.

risks.text: Callers adding a role must set its contextPhase and modelRole explicitly; an unspecified utility role resolves with implementer defaults and runs write-capable.

patterns: The harness behaves as another IDE client: a projected agents directory takes precedence over the bundled prompts.
Env overrides are comma-separated lists parsed into role id sets.
invariants: An unknown role name resolves to the default role rather than raising.
loadRolePrompt strips YAML frontmatter before the prompt is injected.
The catalog is initialized once per run; later calls read the existing catalog.
annotation.integrationPoints: Resolved specs are consumed by the planner in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/plan, by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/sub-agent, by the channel role validation, and by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/prompt.
annotation.dataFlow: task roles or planner output → resolveRole → catalog lookup + prompt file load → sub-agent spec → provider worker prompt and repovine manifest selection.

envDependencies.AGENTS: Planning mode: single, auto, or keyword
envDependencies.HARNESS_AGENTS_DIR: Overrides the directory searched for role prompt markdown
envDependencies.HARNESS_APP_FRAME: Comma-separated override of the application-frame role set
envDependencies.HARNESS_REQUIRE_TESTS_ROLES: Comma-separated override of which roles must deliver tests

annotation.summary: The read-only question path. Validates the provider, loads that provider's ask adapter, and returns the answer; the adapter runs the same agent stack as a task but with only the read-only engine tools and file reads, and never enters the protocol cycle. Also splits a long answer into message-sized chunks, preferring paragraph, then line, then word boundaries.

keyExports.TELEGRAM_TEXT_MAX: The chunk size, kept below the messaging platform's hard limit.
keyExports.runAsk: Validates the provider, dispatches to its ask adapter, and returns the answer or a failure reason.
keyExports.splitForTelegram: Splits long prose into message-sized chunks at the best available boundary.

assumptions: The ask adapter is imported lazily per provider, so an unused provider's dependencies never load.
Chunking prefers a paragraph break, then a line break, then a word break, and only cuts mid-word when none of those falls late enough in the window.
The read-only guarantee lives in the adapter's tool policy rather than here; this module chooses which adapter runs.

sideEffects.description: the dispatched adapter invokes the provider and the engine's read-only tools

risks: An answer is still a paid provider call, so the credential gate applies to the ask path exactly as it does to a task.
Chunk boundaries are chosen by position rather than by structure, so a long fenced block can be split across messages.
patterns: A read-only path parallel to the full run: same stack, narrower tools, no protocol cycle.
annotation.flowDescription: A question arrives from a channel, the provider is validated, its ask adapter answers using read-only tools, and the reply is chunked if it exceeds the message limit.
invariants: An unsupported provider is rejected before any adapter is imported.
The ask path never runs the protocol compliance cycle.
An empty question returns a failure rather than calling a provider.
annotation.integrationPoints: Resolves and validates the provider through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers, then loads the matching read-only ask adapter; called by the HTTP and messaging channel adapters.
annotation.dataFlow: channel question -> runAsk -> provider ask adapter using read-only engine tools -> answer text -> chunked for the channel's message limit.

annotation.summary: Turns a task, however it arrived, into the protocol assignment the engine validates before anything is dispatched. It fills the required shape, defaults the list fields, coerces contracts to the string form the schema demands, and carries the context session through when intake supplied one.

keyExports.buildAssignment: Builds the assignment object from a task.

assumptions: Contracts are coerced rather than passed through, because a prior sub-agent's reported changes or a planner-emitted object would fail the schema check and block the run before the sub-agent starts.
The context session is included only when intake set one; its absence is a normal state rather than a missing field.
The first pass of a greenfield run is exempted from context scoring by the engine, so nothing here special-cases the opening iteration.
A run identifier is derived from the task id when the task did not carry one, so every assignment is identifiable.
The schema itself lives in the engine; this module only produces a shape that satisfies it.
risks: Omitted list fields become empty arrays, which passes validation, so an assignment with no acceptance criteria dispatches normally and produces work that nothing can be judged against.
The shape is written by hand against a schema owned elsewhere, so a schema change surfaces as a validation failure at dispatch rather than at the point the field was added.
patterns: A thin adapter at the boundary: one intake shape in, one validated protocol shape out, with no decisions of its own.
invariants: The protocol version is always the fixed value.
List fields are always present, empty when the task omitted them.
Contracts always leave as strings.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by the graph nodes that build and dispatch work in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph; contract coercion comes from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/claude-agent; the session identifier placed here is what the worker threads onto its calls and echoes back on the result, which is what the accounting in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/usage attributes against.
annotation.dataFlow: task from a queue, a chat channel or an issue → assignment shape with defaults and coerced contracts → schema validation → dispatch.

annotation.summary: Spec constant module (Phase 2): ATTACH_GIT_POINTER_CONTENT — the VALID pointer ('gitdir: /state/git\n') the launcher writes to control/git-guard and Compose mounts read-only at /workspace/.git; it targets the launch-scoped disposable repo (ATTACH_STATE_GIT_DIR). ATTACH_BASELINE_REF names the baseline tag reset-to-baseline resolves.

keyExports.ATTACH_BASELINE_REF: attach-baseline — tag pinned by the launcher; resetTarget and validation resolve it
keyExports.ATTACH_GIT_POINTER_CONTENT: exact ro-pointer bytes; cross-process contract between launcher and in-container validation
keyExports.ATTACH_STATE_GIT_DIR: /state/git — container path of the disposable repo mount

risks.text: The pointer bytes and ref names are cross-process contracts (host launcher writes, in-container resolver/reset consume); change only with both sides plus the plan record.

annotation.summary: Blocker triage for sub-agent run results: decides which reported blockers are real and which are out-of-scope infra noise. isOutOfScopeInfraBlocker matches the out-of-scope infra wording and clears it only when the sub-agent's own scope is neither '.' nor 'infra'; subAgentGateEffectivelyOk then treats a run as passing when it delivered filesChanged and every surviving blocker is such noise.

keyExports.filterHardBlockers: Drops out-of-scope infra blockers (and falsy entries) from a blockers array.
keyExports.isOutOfScopeInfraBlocker: True when blocker text matches the out-of-scope infra regex (docker-compose / cross-scope validate_annotations) AND the sub-agent scope is neither '.' nor 'infra'.
keyExports.subAgentGateEffectivelyOk: True when the sub-agent is not blocked/failed, delivered filesChanged, and every remaining blocker is out-of-scope infra noise.

assumptions: The OUT_OF_SCOPE_INFRA regex targets docker-compose.yml wording and 'outside the frontend/backend/infra scope' / repo-wide validate_annotations phrasing.
A sub-agent whose scope includes '.' or 'infra' owns infra, so its infra blockers are never filtered.
risks: The regex can miss novel out-of-scope wording (under-filter) or swallow a legitimate blocker (over-filter).

risks.text: Callers must confirm a run's blockers were classified against that run's own scope before treating subAgentGateEffectivelyOk as a pass; the override converts a non-ok result into a passing one.

invariants: Both filters are pure: no IO, no mutation of the input array.
subAgentGateEffectivelyOk returns false unless status is neither blocked nor failed, filesChanged is non-empty, and every remaining blocker is out-of-scope infra.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by the harness sub-agent gate in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/multi when deciding whether an implement run passed.

annotation.summary: The HTTP channel: a small server exposing status, a goal endpoint that runs a full protocol episode, a read-only question endpoint, and a destructive reset. Transport and optional bearer authentication only — step order, workers and protocol gates all live in the graph, exactly as in the chat channel. Built on the standard library alone.

keyExports.startHttp: Starts the server for a resolved target and returns it once listening.

assumptions: The status response is split by authorization: the liveness fields stay open so an unauthenticated healthcheck passes, while the workspace path and the run telemetry — which carry model and cost — are returned only to an authorized caller.
One episode and one question at a time per server; a second gets a conflict rather than queueing, because both would write the same workspace.
Closing the request aborts the run, since the open request is the only handle a caller has on it.
Reset requires an explicit confirmation and an idle server, because in this synchronous model a running episode would be writing the tree the reset deletes.
Reset reaps processes a previous worker left bound before clearing anything, so nothing keeps writing after the wipe.

The target is derived so that an environment-resolved workspace never gets paired with an assumed mode: an explicit workspace alone keeps the sandbox assumption, and with neither the whole target comes from the environment.

sideEffects.description: listens on the configured address and serves JSON
reads run telemetry for the status endpoint
the reset endpoint clears the workspace
the reset endpoint reaps processes a worker left running

risks.text: The request and response body keys are a wire contract callers script against: the outward name is the goal key while the older task key stays accepted on both the path and the body. A change here breaks existing callers silently, since an unrecognized key reads as a missing field rather than an error.

risks: The default binding is every interface and the token is optional, so a deployment that omits the token exposes an endpoint that can run agents and wipe the workspace to anyone who can reach the port; the startup log states this but nothing prevents it.
The reset is irreversible and the confirmation flag is the only guard against an accidental request; the idle check protects the tree from a concurrent writer, not the caller from themselves.
An episode holds its request open for its whole duration, so any proxy or client timeout shorter than a run turns into a client-closed abort of real work.
patterns: Same division as the chat channel: transport here, meaning in the graph, so the two channels cannot drift in behaviour.
Authorization splits one response rather than gating the whole endpoint, which is what lets a healthcheck stay unauthenticated without leaking run details.
invariants: A policy refusal on reset is evaluated before the confirmation and busy checks, so no payload reaches the destructive path.
The workspace path and run telemetry are never returned without authorization.
The target derivation never invents a mode for an environment-resolved workspace.
annotation.integrationPoints: Episodes run through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow; questions through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/ask; the target mode, its policy and the reset itself come from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/target-repo; process reaping from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/sandbox-procs; telemetry from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/telemetry; role resolution from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/agents.
annotation.stateShape: Per server: an episode-busy flag, a question-busy flag, and a map of question threads to their provider and context sessions.
annotation.dataFlow: request → authorization → route → episode through the graph or question through the read-only path, abortable by client disconnect → JSON response; reset reaps, clears and drops question sessions.

envDependencies.HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN: Bearer token; when unset the endpoint is open

annotation.summary: The chat channel: a long-polling loop over the messaging API that gates senders against an allowlist and routes messages to either a full protocol episode or a read-only question. It is transport and access control only — no orchestration decisions are made here. There is no client library; the loop speaks the HTTP API directly.

keyExports.ATTACHMENTS_ROOT: Where downloaded images land, inside the harness directory rather than the workspace.
keyExports.startTelegram: Runs the poll loop against a compiled graph for a resolved target.
keyExports.telegramResetPlan: Turns the target policy into a reset decision, either arming the confirmation or refusing with an explanation.

assumptions: Only an explicit command starts work: plain text shows help rather than being treated as a goal, which is what keeps a bare confirmation word from being run as one.
The fast-path commands never enter the graph, so a destructive confirmation cannot become an episode.
The poll loop never waits on a running episode, so commands stay responsive while one is in flight; a chat may have one episode at a time and a second is refused.
Stopping aborts the in-flight run without preserving provider sessions, since every episode starts fresh and resumption inside an episode is handled by the graph.
Reset and new-thread abort both the episode and any question first, then wipe or re-thread.
Generation counters per chat mean an in-flight run that finishes after a reset cannot restore its session or post its reply.

Attachments are split per flow and live under the harness directory, so an episode and a question never clear each other's images and neither shows up in workspace custody or diffs in either target mode.
Only the file reference is taken from a message; the download is deferred to the command that needs it, so images on unrelated messages never reach the network.
The API base is configurable to a custody proxy that injects the real credential and pins the outbound chat, which is why the credential need not be present in this process at all.
The loop touches a liveness file every iteration, so an external healthcheck detects a wedged loop rather than only a dead process.

sideEffects.description: long-polls the messaging API and sends replies
downloads attachments into the harness directory
reads run telemetry for the status command
runs episodes and questions in the background, tracked per chat

risks: Replies are truncated to the platform's message limit, so a long final answer is clipped and the clipping is not distinguishable from a short answer.
The status command reports best-effort telemetry and is not a protocol verdict; reading it as one overstates what it knows.
A sender outside the allowlist is dropped silently, so a misconfigured allowlist looks identical to an unresponsive bot.
The generation counters are what prevent a stale run from reviving a wiped session, so a new asynchronous path that forgets to check its generation reintroduces exactly that.
patterns: Transport and access control only: what a command means is decided by the graph, not here.
Fast paths bypass the orchestrator entirely, which is what makes a confirmation cheap and safe.
Per-flow attachment directories, so two independent tracks can be in flight without interfering.
annotation.flowDescription: Long-poll loop: getUpdates → parse /task|/ask|/reset|/stop|/status → download attachments to .attachments/{task|ask}/ → invokeGraph with per-chat thread id telegram:chatId:gen → truncate and send replyText; /status reads .harness/current-run.json telemetry.
invariants: Plain text is never treated as a goal.
One episode per chat at a time.
Attachments never land inside workspace custody.
Reset in the attached mode restores the launch baseline through the real message path, which is covered end to end by the live channel test against a stubbed API.
annotation.integrationPoints: Episodes run through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/workflow; questions through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/ask; the target mode and its reset behaviour come from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/target-repo; role mentions resolve through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/agents; status reads mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/telemetry; leftover child processes are reaped through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/sandbox-procs.
annotation.stateShape: Per chat: a thread generation, a pending reset timestamp, the active episode with its abort handle, the question session, and a session generation.
annotation.dataFlow: update → allowlist → command routing → attachment saved on demand → episode or question started in the background → reply truncated and sent.

envDependencies.HARNESS_HEARTBEAT_FILE: Liveness file touched each poll iteration
envDependencies.TELEGRAM_API_BASE: Base URL for both the API and the file endpoint; points at the custody proxy in the hardened path

annotation.summary: The claim model for the repovine-native run. Parses the claim lines the orient sub-agent emits, falls back to a single claim inferred from the user's request when orient produced none, de-duplicates by a stable slug id, applies the verify phase's per-claim outcomes, and assembles the compact orient trail the implement and verify phases read.

keyExports.Claim: The claim record shape: id, text, and the verify outcome once applied.
keyExports.applyVerifyOutcomes: Attaches those outcomes to the matching claims.
keyExports.buildOrientTrail: Assembles the orient artifact: query, summary, graph nodes, suggested scopes, claims, MCP tools and context session id.
keyExports.claimIdFromText: Derives a stable slug id from claim text so the same claim survives re-parsing.
keyExports.inferClaimsFromTask: Builds a single fallback claim from the user's request when orient emitted none.
keyExports.mergeClaims: Merges orient claims over the task fallback, de-duplicating by id.
keyExports.parseClaimsFromContracts: Extracts claim lines from a sub-agent's reported contracts.
keyExports.parseVerifyOutcomes: Parses the verify phase's per-claim outcome lines.
keyExports.scopesFromGraphNodes: Maps graph node ids onto implement scope hints such as backend, frontend or infra.

assumptions: The claim prefix in reported contracts is the canonical way orient communicates claims; free prose is not parsed.
When orient emits no claim lines, a single claim derived from the user's request stands in so the run still has something to verify against.
Claim ids are derived from text, so rewording a claim produces a new id rather than updating the old one.
risks: Scope hints are inferred from node id prefixes, so an unrecognized id contributes no scope and quietly narrows the implement hints.

risks.text: Callers must apply verify outcomes through applyVerifyOutcomes rather than pairing claims positionally; parsing produces outcomes keyed by claim id, and a positional match silently mislabels claims once the sets differ.

patterns: Text-derived stable ids let claims round-trip through prompts and result files without carrying a separate identifier.
invariants: mergeClaims keeps the orient claim when both sources produce the same id.
The orient trail carries claims alongside the graph nodes they were grounded in.
annotation.integrationPoints: Produced and consumed by the orient and verify phases in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/repovine-process; the user request is extracted through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/task-user.
annotation.dataFlow: orient contracts → parseClaimsFromContracts (or inferClaimsFromTask) → mergeClaims → buildOrientTrail → implement phase → verify contracts → applyVerifyOutcomes → per-claim verdicts in the run summary.

annotation.summary: The Claude worker plus the result normalization every provider shares. Launches the agent with the engine exposed as an MCP server scoped to the workspace, appends the phase policy and the role brief to the preset, lets the agent gather context and edit files, then extracts the structured result from its reply and coerces it into the protocol shape. What the agent reports is never taken as fact: the run still passes through the compliance check afterwards.

keyExports.blockedResult: Builds a blocked result carrying the reason when auth or extraction fails.
keyExports.extractResultObject: Finds the structured result in free text: the last fenced block, then the whole reply, then a brace slice.
keyExports.normalizeResult: Coerces the parsed object into the protocol result shape.
keyExports.preserveOptionalArtifacts: Keeps optional artifact fields the agent supplied.
keyExports.runAgent: The full worker session: prompt, agent run, result extraction and normalization.
keyExports.supportsResume: Whether this provider can resume a prior session.
keyExports.toContractStrings: Coerces contract entries to strings when the agent returned objects.
keyExports.userPrompt: Builds the user-facing prompt from the task, the assignment and any attachments.

assumptions: Result extraction is deliberately forgiving, trying three shapes in turn, because a model reply is prose that happens to contain a structure rather than a structured response.
A failure to authenticate or to extract yields a blocked result rather than an exception, so the run reports a reason instead of crashing the graph.
Read-only phases are expected to report nothing changed, and normalization preserves that emptiness rather than filling it in.

sideEffects.description: runs the agent through the provider SDK with the engine MCP server attached
an implementation phase edits files under the workspace root; a diagnostic stderr transcript is appended under .harness when HARNESS_WORKER_STDERR=1
logs worker tool-use events when verbose logging is enabled

risks: A wrong assignment phase pairs the role brief with the wrong permitted behaviour, so the prompt and the tool policy can disagree about what the run may do.

Malformed result output becomes a blocked result rather than an implementation, which is the intended failure but reads in the ledger as a run that produced nothing rather than one that produced unparseable output.
patterns: The role brief is appended to the preset rather than replacing it, so provider defaults survive while the harness adds its own mandate.
Normalization is shared across providers, so the protocol shape does not depend on which model answered.
invariants: A read-only phase reports no changed files, touched nodes or written annotations.
Contract entries are coerced to strings, whatever shape the agent returned.
The result is validated by the compliance check regardless of what the agent claimed.
annotation.integrationPoints: Dispatched through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers; credentials from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/auth, prompt policy from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/prompt, the engine MCP descriptor from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/mcp, the model for the role from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/model-role, and usage accounting through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/usage.
annotation.stateShape: The run returns a protocol result; the capture option collects the session id and usage for resume/logging.
annotation.dataFlow: assignment -> prompt -> agent run with engine tools -> result extracted from the reply -> normalized -> validation and compliance.

annotation.summary: Minimal KEY=value .env loader: parses a file and fills process.env only where a key is unset or empty (a non-empty existing value wins), so docker compose ${VAR:-} placeholders can be filled from the file. Strips matching single/double quotes; returns loaded key names only. Missing file is a silent empty result.
assumptions: Missing file is silent empty array.

sideEffects.description: Reads file; sets unset process.env keys

risks: Tokens on disk in ~/telegram.env — not in repo.
patterns: Minimal parser — no export keyword, variable expansion, or multiline values.
invariants: Only sets env when process.env[key] is undefined or empty string.
Returns list of key names loaded (not values).
annotation.integrationPoints: langgraph-tg-bot.mjs; langgraph-http.mjs.
annotation.dataFlow: langgraph-bot.mjs loads ~/telegram.env before reading TELEGRAM_* vars → loadEnvFile merges into process.env.

annotation.summary: Walk parent directories for a marker file/dir instead of fixed ../ depth; returns containing directory or null at filesystem root.

keyExports.findUp: fs.existsSync upward search from startDir; never throws.

assumptions: Used by lib/repovine.mjs to locate repovine dist from relocated demo nesting.

sideEffects.description: existsSync on each ancestor path

annotation.summary: Assembles the contracts prior runs recorded on the modules this run touched, so the verify phase checks against durable memory rather than only against what the current orient happened to re-declare. Reads the annotation store directly and read-only: the invariants, risks and side effects on the touched nodes become the obligations section of the verify prompt.

keyExports.collectAnnotationObligations: Collects the invariants, risks and side effects recorded on the given node ids, de-duplicated and capped at maxItems (default 24).
keyExports.obligationsSection: Renders the collected obligations as the prompt section the verify phase reads, one OBLIGATION line requested per item.
keyExports.readAnnotationsSnapshot: Captures the annotation store at run start, before any stage has run.

assumptions: The node ids come from the sub-agents' validated touched-nodes lists, so no graph lookup is needed here.
The snapshot is taken at run start because implementers may write annotations while working; without it, obligations would drift toward what this run just wrote.
A missing or unparseable store yields no obligations rather than an error, so verification degrades to claims-only instead of failing.

sideEffects.description: reads repovine.annots.json directly from the workspace root

risks: Obligations are capped at maxItems, so a run touching many annotated modules silently verifies against a subset.
The store is read as a raw file rather than through the engine, so a schema change to the annotation record shape has to be mirrored here.
Reading a stale or partially written store yields fewer obligations rather than an error, which reads as a clean verify.
patterns: Read-only by design: the write path to the annotation store stays with the engine's own tools, and this helper never writes.
A run-start snapshot separates prior contracts from this run's own annotation writes.
invariants: The annotation store is never written here; the write path stays MCP-only.
Obligations reflect the store as it stood before the run's stages, not as it stands at verify time.
Entries are de-duplicated across nodes (by kind+text) and capped at maxItems.
annotation.integrationPoints: The snapshot is captured by the run orchestrator at ingress and the collected obligations feed the verify prompt built in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/repovine-process.
annotation.dataFlow: run start -> readAnnotationsSnapshot -> sub-agents report touched nodes -> collectAnnotationObligations reads the snapshot for those nodes -> obligationsSection renders into the verify prompt.

annotation.summary: Deterministic existence check for declared file references. A compose service naming a Dockerfile that does not exist fails at build time, and no model review reliably checks whether a referenced file is there, so this floor scans a small fixed taxonomy of machine-readable references and reports the targets that are missing as blockers for the fix ledger.

keyExports.missingReferencedArtifacts: Scans the workspace for declared references whose targets do not exist and returns them de-duplicated.

assumptions: Parsing is line-level and tolerant rather than a full document parse, because the files are agent-authored with conventional formatting and the check must never depend on a parser matching every valid form.
A parse miss produces a false negative by design: the floor stays silent rather than raising a blocker it cannot substantiate.
The taxonomy is deliberately small and fixed: compose build and environment-file references, project references between TypeScript configs, and a couple of specific setup mismatches.

sideEffects.description: reads the referencing files and checks whether each referenced target exists

risks: Because a parse miss is silent, a reference written in an unusual but valid form is simply not checked, so a passing floor is not proof that every declared reference resolves.
Reference resolution follows the nearest preceding build context, so an unconventional ordering inside a compose file can resolve a path against the wrong base.
The taxonomy is fixed, so a new kind of declared reference is unchecked until it is added here.
patterns: Prefer a false negative to a false blocker: everything ambiguous is skipped rather than reported.
Deterministic checks sit alongside model review rather than inside it, covering exactly what review is unreliable at.
invariants: An optional environment-file reference, declared in compose's sanctioned long form as not required, is skipped; a required or unmarked one is kept.
A build-file reference is resolved against the nearest preceding context rather than the workspace root.
Findings are de-duplicated before they reach the fix ledger.
annotation.integrationPoints: Findings become blockers in the run's fix ledger alongside the grounded test floor, consumed by the run orchestrator when it assembles the repair work.
annotation.dataFlow: workspace scan → declared references extracted per source file → existence check per target → missing targets de-duplicated → fix-ledger blockers.

annotation.summary: The orchestration node for a multi-agent run. It plans the work, schedules sub-agents into stages with graph refreshes between them, then runs the gates: review, an optional automatic fix, a runtime check, claim verification and annotation sync. What the run is allowed to do — worktrees, git operations — comes from the target policy rather than from probing the environment.

keyExports.annotationSyncSkipReason: Why annotation sync is being skipped, when it is.
keyExports.annotationSyncTargets: The sub-agents whose work needs annotation follow-up.
keyExports.annotationSyncTask: The task text for one scoped annotation sync.
keyExports.assembleFixBlockers: The blocker list handed to a fix sub-agent.
keyExports.deriveAnnotationSyncScope: The annotation scope implied by a sub-agent's role and what it touched.
keyExports.deriveMultiRunStatus: Turns the gate signals into the run's two verdicts, one for process and one for the goal.
keyExports.effectiveReviewSubAgent: The review that counts, preferring one that ran after a fix over the last one overall.
keyExports.findAcceptanceReviewSubAgent: The review used for acceptance rather than for gating.
keyExports.gradePlanFindings: Grades the plan against the advisories, the idle implementers and the optional plan review.
keyExports.groupAnnotationSyncTargets: Collapses targets that share a scope so the work is done once.
keyExports.markReviewedRevision: Records what tree a review covered, persisting a digest rather than a revision object.
keyExports.multiAgent: The node itself: orient, plan, staged execution, the gate sequence, then the composed reply.
keyExports.reviewAcceptedOf: Whether a review accepted the work.
keyExports.reviewFixEligible: Whether the review's blockers are the kind an automatic fix may attempt.
keyExports.reviewGateIsOpen: Whether review permits the run to proceed: a passing post-fix review, an accepted fix, or no blocking review at all.
keyExports.reviewIsFresh: Whether a review still describes the current tree, ignoring paths it was told to exclude.
keyExports.reviewProcessValid: Whether a review followed its own process well enough to be trusted.
keyExports.useWorktreeExecution: Decides whether stages fan out into worktrees, answering before any git probe when git operations are disallowed.

assumptions: Capability is decided from the declared target policy before anything is probed, so a mode without git operations never reaches a git call to discover it cannot.
That decision sits ahead of the environment toggle, so the toggle can turn worktree fan-out off but never back on where the policy forbids it.
Custody travels as digest strings from end to end rather than as revision objects, which is what lets the reviewed base survive persistence.
Refresh barriers between stages are preserved even when stages run sequentially, because a later stage reading a stale graph is the failure this ordering exists to prevent.
Review freshness is a tree comparison with exclusions rather than a timestamp, so a review stays valid when only ignored paths moved.
The run reports two independent verdicts: whether the process was followed and whether the goal was met. A clean process with an unmet goal is a real outcome, not a contradiction.

sideEffects.description: runs a provider session per sub-agent
writes usage, protocol-call and telemetry rollups for the run
creates and merges worktrees when fan-out is permitted

risks: A worktree whose merge conflicts marks its sub-agent unsuccessful with merge blockers, so a conflict surfaces as a failed sub-agent rather than as a distinct conflict state.

The gate sequence has many independent inputs — review, fix, runtime, verification, test and artifact floors — and a run blocked by any of them reports through the same verdict, so the reason has to be read from the signals rather than the outcome.
Several gates are switched by environment variables, so a run's meaning depends on the environment it was launched in and two runs of the same task are not necessarily comparable.
patterns: Policy decides capability, probing only confirms it, which keeps a restricted mode from failing at the first git call.
Stages with barriers between them: parallelism inside a stage, a consistent graph between stages.
Review, fix and re-review are separate sub-agents rather than one loop, so each verdict is attributable.
annotation.flowDescription: planSubAgentsAsync → scheduleStages → runSubAgent → review/fix gates → refreshGraph → runtimeCheck → annotationSync → composeReply.
invariants: Worktree fan-out cannot be re-enabled by environment where the target policy forbids it.
Persisted review custody is always a digest string, never a revision object.
Refresh barriers survive the sequential path.
The whole wiring is guarded end to end by the attach-mode integration test, which runs the real node against blocked workers.
annotation.integrationPoints: Phases come from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/repovine-process; per-sub-agent execution from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/sub-agent; planning from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/plan; custody from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/workspace-revision and mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/worktree; the floors from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/test-floor and mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/artifact-floor; annotation follow-up from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/annotation-obligations; the target policy from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/target-repo; rollup paths from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/harness-paths.
annotation.dataFlow: state and configuration → optional orientation → plan and stage schedule → sub-agent runs with refreshes between stages → review, optional fix, runtime check, claim verification → annotation sync → two verdicts plus usage and telemetry rollups.

envDependencies.HARNESS_REVIEW_FIX: 0 disables the automatic fix sub-agent after review blockers

annotation.summary: The graph node functions for one protocol cycle: intake, assignment build and validation, the worker run, result persistence and validation, the compliance gate, the runtime check, and the composed reply. Intake resolves the target once per invocation and fails an invalid attach workspace before any provider spend. Composing the reply also carries the attach promotion: a successful run is snapshotted onto its run branch, and a failure there is logged and passed over because promotion is a convenience, never custody.

keyExports.clipText: Clips text to a maximum length for the reply.
keyExports.complianceNode: Runs the compliance gate, resolves MCP metrics and records grounding rejections.
keyExports.composeReply: Formats the reply, promotes a successful attach run, and finalizes telemetry.
keyExports.formatReply: The human-facing reply with per-sub-agent status and the runtime-check summary.
keyExports.intake: Resolves provider and target, prepares the run, normalizes the user task, starts telemetry, and routes single versus multi.
keyExports.persistResult: Writes the worker result to the run artifacts.
keyExports.replyVerbose: Whether verbose reply formatting is enabled.
keyExports.runSubAgent: Runs the provider worker with compliance-driven retry folding and sandbox process bracketing.
keyExports.runtimeCheckNode: Runs the runtime check and records its outcome.
keyExports.subAgentBriefSummary: A short summary line derived from a brief.
keyExports.subAgentStatusDot: The status indicator for one sub-agent, allowing for context-quality-only failures.
keyExports.subAgentStepLabel: The step label for a sub-agent, distinguishing annotation sync.
keyExports.validateAssignmentNode: Validates the assignment through the engine before the worker runs.
keyExports.validateResultNode: Schema-validates the result before the compliance gate.

assumptions: The orchestrator never calls the engine's MCP tools directly; every engine interaction goes through the CLI gates.
Telemetry is always finalized when the reply is composed, so a run never ends without its summary.
Target resolution takes the invocation input first and fills the remaining gaps from the environment.

sideEffects.description: persists run artifacts and telemetry events
invokes the provider worker
shells out to the engine CLI for validation and compliance and brackets the worker with process snapshots

risks: Reply wording and the telemetry payload are consumed by several clients, so a change to one has to keep the other aligned.
The attach promotion runs inside reply composition, so a failure there is visible only in the log while the reply still reports success.
patterns: The protocol cycle is expressed as discrete nodes, so each gate is separately observable and separately retryable.
The engine boundary is explicit: nodes call the CLI wrapper rather than reaching into engine internals.
annotation.flowDescription: intake, then assignment build and validation, the worker run, result persistence and validation, compliance, the runtime check, and finally the composed reply.
invariants: An invalid attach workspace aborts at intake with a precise diagnostic and no writes.
The attach promotion happens after run custody has been derived, and it mutates only the disposable repository's refs, never the reply verdicts.
Every path through the cycle finalizes telemetry.
annotation.integrationPoints: Prepares the run through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/harness-run, resolves artifact paths through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/harness-paths, reaches the engine through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/repovine, folds retries with mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/retry, captures revisions through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/workspace-revision, and records telemetry through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/telemetry.
annotation.dataFlow: intake prepares the run and starts telemetry → assignment built and validated → worker runs → result persisted and validated → compliance and MCP metrics → runtime check → reply composed, run promoted and telemetry archived.

envDependencies.GRAPH_VERBOSE: Set to 0 to silence graph node logging

annotation.summary: Decomposes a task into role-and-scope sub-agent specs and schedules them into stages. The orchestration rule lives here rather than inside any LLM worker: explicit mode reads the roles off the task, implicit mode parses them from the text, and auto mode may ask an LLM with a keyword fallback so the demo runs offline. scheduleStages encodes the invariants in code, batching only pairwise-disjoint scopes and placing dependent roles in later stages with a refresh barrier between.

keyExports.applyAppFrame: Adds the missing application-frame roles to a plan.
keyExports.applyGreenfieldParallelStages: Collapses stages for worktree fan-out, but only on a greenfield non-explicit plan and only when git operations are permitted.
keyExports.assignSubAgentInstanceIds: Assigns unique instance ids to repeated roles so artifacts and context sessions do not collide.
keyExports.greenfieldParallelEnabled: Whether greenfield worktree fan-out is enabled; on by default and disabled by its env toggle.
keyExports.overPlannedRoles: Continuation-only advisory naming implement roles that have no orient grounding.
keyExports.parseRolesFromText: Extracts known role ids mentioned in task text, in catalog order.
keyExports.planSubAgents: Deterministic role and scope decomposition for explicit, implicit and single-agent cases.
keyExports.planSubAgentsAsync: Async planner: explicit roles win, auto mode tries the LLM plan and falls back to the keyword heuristic.
keyExports.scheduleStages: Orders specs by dependency depth, then greedily batches disjoint scopes within a depth.
keyExports.scopesDisjoint: True when two scope sets share no path.
keyExports.stripAnnotationStages: Drops planner-authored annotation stages from non-explicit plans.

assumptions: Stage layout is computed here from dependency depth, and in auto mode those dependency edges arrive from the LLM alongside role and scope: the model sets how many stages there are and which role lands in which. The orchestrator owns the batching rule and the refresh barrier unconditionally.
Implicit planning selects only roles registered in the catalog, so an unregistered markdown file is never planned.
Utility roles are scheduled only when a plan names them explicitly or implicitly.

sideEffects.description: auto mode may call the LLM planner
reads the greenfield single and greenfield parallel toggles

risks: Greedy batching can serialize more than strictly necessary when scopes nearly overlap.

risks.text: Callers must pass whether git operations are permitted; the stage-collapsing path checks that capability before any env toggle, and mis-reporting it would let a guarded workspace be collapsed into a fan-out it cannot support.

patterns: Orchestrator invariants live in code while the LLM supplies judgement only.
Capability is checked before configuration: a permission gate cannot be re-opened by an environment variable.
invariants: applyGreenfieldParallelStages requires git operations to be permitted before it consults the parallel toggle, so the attach target policy structurally prevents stage collapsing and no environment override re-enables it.
Stages are ordered by dependency depth, with a refresh barrier separating them.
Only pairwise-disjoint scopes share a batch.
annotation.integrationPoints: Resolves roles through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/agents, reads workspace state from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/workspace-state, may call the LLM planner, and hands stages to mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/multi, which inserts the refresh barriers and runs worktree fan-out through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/worktree.
annotation.dataFlow: task → explicit roles or parsed/LLM roles → resolved specs → optional greenfield stage collapse → scheduleStages → staged execution.

envDependencies.HARNESS_GREENFIELD_PARALLEL: Greenfield worktree fan-out, on by default and disabled when set to 0
envDependencies.HARNESS_GREENFIELD_SINGLE: When set, an empty sandbox with an implicit multi-role plan collapses to a single default sub-agent

annotation.summary: The LLM half of planning. Loads the demo-owned orchestration rule prose, asks a provider for a JSON array of role, scope and dependency entries, and resolves them into sub-agent specs. It supplies judgement about which roles and scopes a task needs; the invariants about disjoint stages, barriers and flat sub-agents stay in the scheduler. It also carries a bounded plan-review pass that critiques a produced plan against the task.

keyExports.parsePlan: Parses the provider's array into role, scope and task specs. One unrecognised role id invalidates the whole plan: parsePlan returns null and the caller runs the deterministic heuristic instead.

assumptions: The planning mode comes from the agent-mode setting resolved in the role module, and any failure falls back to the deterministic keyword heuristic so the demo stays runnable.
An unknown role id invalidates the entire LLM plan rather than being coerced to the default role: parsing returns nothing and the run falls back to the deterministic keyword planner.
The plan critique is advisory: it produces findings rather than vetoing a plan.

sideEffects.description: reads the orchestration rule prose from the rules directory
calls the provider to produce a plan and, when enabled, to critique it
logs planning progress when verbose logging is enabled

risks: A weak plan can produce overlapping scopes or vague sub-agent tasks; the scheduler catches the overlap but not the vagueness.
Parsing tolerates prose around the JSON array, so a response mixing two arrays can yield a plan assembled from the wrong one.
patterns: The model supplies role and scope judgement while orchestrator code enforces the structural rules, so a bad plan degrades quality rather than breaking the run's guarantees.
A run-verb safety net rewrites planned task text so a worker is never instructed to run build, container or lint commands.
invariants: A planned task is file-editing instructions only. The run-verb net replaces a review task that mentions execution; for every other role it appends a write-only disclaimer and leaves the planned text intact, so a run instruction can reach a worker alongside a clause contradicting it.

Only an orient trail carrying graph nodes, or real annotations on disk, marks the workspace as a continuation. Product source alone does not: a workspace with an empty graph and stub annotations is described to the planner as greenfield.
An unparseable or failed plan falls back to the deterministic heuristic rather than aborting.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by the planning path in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/plan, resolves roles through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/agents, reads workspace state from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/workspace-state, reaches the provider through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/llm, and borrows the attachment brief from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/prompt.
annotation.dataFlow: task → orchestration rule plus workspace state → plan prompt → provider → JSON array → parsed and resolved specs → optional critique → scheduler.

envDependencies.GRAPH_VERBOSE: Set to 0 to silence planner logging
envDependencies.HARNESS_RULES_DIR: Optional override for the orchestration rule location

annotation.summary: The repovine-native run process: an orient phase that grounds the task in the graph, the implement sub-agents, and a verify-claims phase that re-checks what was claimed. Builds the prompts for the orient and verify sub-agents, classifies which sub-agents gate the run, and computes the two run verdicts (goal and process) reported back to the channel.

keyExports.ORIENT_INSTANCE_ID: Fixed instance id identifying the orient sub-agent.
keyExports.VERIFY_INSTANCE_ID: Fixed instance id identifying the verify-claims sub-agent.
keyExports.formatOrientVerifyReplyLines: Formats the orient and verify summary lines for the channel reply.
keyExports.isIgnorableOrientFailure: True when an orient failure is tolerable, notably on a greenfield run.
keyExports.isOrientSubAgent: True when a sub-agent carries the orient instance id.
keyExports.isRepovineSupportSubAgent: True for the orient and verify support sub-agents.
keyExports.isRunGateSubAgent: True for the implement and review-fix sub-agents that gate the run verdict, excluding orient, verify and annotation-sync.
keyExports.isVerifyClaimsSubAgent: True when a sub-agent carries the verify instance id.
keyExports.orientTask: Builds the orient prompt, folding in the deterministic CLI pre-orient and greenfield sections.
keyExports.recoverClaimContractsFromAttempts: Recovers claim contracts from earlier attempt result files.
keyExports.repovineGoalOk: The goal verdict: did the run deliver what was asked, given the runtime check and delivering sub-agents.
keyExports.repovineProcessEnabled: Env-gated, default-on switch for the repovine-native process.
keyExports.repovineProcessRunOk: The process verdict: did every gating sub-agent pass, allowing for CSQ-only and ignorable-orient cases.
keyExports.runOrientPhase: Runs the orient sub-agent, recovers claim contracts from prior attempts, and writes the orient artifact.
keyExports.runVerifyClaimsPhase: Runs the verify-claims sub-agent after the implement sub-agents finish and writes the run-level verify artifact.
keyExports.subAgentCsqOnlyDelivered: True when a sub-agent's only errors are context-session-quality ones.
keyExports.verificationAcceptedOf: True when verification is accepted for the run.
keyExports.verificationStatusOf: The verification status of the verify sub-agent against whether verification was required.
