keyExports.verifyClaimsTask: Builds the verify prompt from claims, the orient trail, implement summaries, the tree diff and graph obligations.

assumptions: The repovine-native process is on by default and is disabled through its env switch rather than enabled by one.

The orient and verify sub-agents carry fixed instance ids that keep them out of the gate set, and both verdicts re-check them directly: a failed verify sinks goal and process, and a failed orient sinks the process unless greenfield makes it ignorable.
Goal and process are separate verdicts: a run can satisfy the process while missing the goal, and the reply reports both.

sideEffects.description: spawns the orient and verify sub-agents through the sub-agent runner
invokes the repovine CLI orient query for a deterministic pre-orient pass
writes the run-level orient and verify artifacts and records phase events

risks: A greenfield orient legitimately emits an empty graphNodesTouched set, which must not be read as failure.
isRunGateSubAgent deliberately excludes annotation-sync and pre-fix review sub-agents, so a failure there does not sink the run verdict.

risks.text: Callers must read the goal and process verdicts separately; treating repovineProcessRunOk as the run outcome reports a clean process on a run that never met the goal.

patterns: Fixed instance ids let the support phases be recognized without matching on role names.
Claim recovery reads prior attempt files, so a retry does not lose contracts established earlier in the run.
invariants: Orient and verify sub-agents are excluded from the run gate set.
The verify phase runs only after the implement sub-agents complete.
annotation.integrationPoints: Invoked from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/multi; builds claims through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/claims, calls the CLI wrapper mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/repovine, classifies blockers via mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/blockers, and resolves paths through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/harness-paths.
annotation.dataFlow: multi calls runOrientPhase → implement sub-agents → runVerifyClaimsPhase; both phases write run-level JSON under the active area, later archived with the run.

envDependencies.HARNESS_REPOVINE_PROCESS: Default-on switch for the orient/verify pipeline

annotation.summary: Retry policy for sub-agent runs. Reads a compliance report to decide whether a failed run is worth retrying, classifies the rejection (annotation/graph-sync-only, grounding, missing required fields, contract handoff), folds the reasons into a compact retry prompt, and merges a sync-only retry back into the original work result without inflating its claims. Also separates transient transport blocks and worker timeouts, which retry on their own terms. Reviewed against current source: 16-export surface unchanged from the prior note.

keyExports.COMPACT_RETRY_BASE: Short retry preamble; the resumed session already holds full task context.
keyExports.complianceAccepted: True when the report is valid with neither grounding nor required-field rejection.
keyExports.complianceReport: Normalizes raw compliance JSON into the report shape the predicates read.
keyExports.foldRetryContext: Builds the retry task text; the sync-only preamble scopes annotation work to filesChanged and graphNodesTouched.
keyExports.foldWorkerTimeoutRetry: Builds the time-boxed retry text for a timed-out worker.
keyExports.groundingRejected: True when ungroundedAnnotations or inconsistentAnnotations are non-empty.
keyExports.isRetriable: True for non-blocked, non-failed results that carry actionable retry notes.
keyExports.isSyncOnlyReport: True when every error is annotation/graph-sync wording; contract-handoff and false-claim errors force a full retry.
keyExports.isTransientTransportBlock: True when the block text matches transient transport failure wording.
keyExports.isWorkerTimeoutBlock: True when the block text matches worker timeout wording, which is not a transport failure.
keyExports.mergeSyncOnlyResult: Unions the work result with the sync result, keeping filesChanged, contractsChanged and graphNodesTouched honest.
keyExports.requiredFieldsRejected: True when the report cites missing required result fields.
keyExports.retryNotes: Folds errors, requiredFollowups and grounding facts into retry prompt notes.
keyExports.reviewFixSubAgentAccepted: True when a review-fix sub-agent passed the sync-only retry gate.
keyExports.shouldDeferImplementAnnotationRetry: Defers an implement retry when sync-only annotation work should run first.
keyExports.subAgentSyncRetrySucceeded: True when a sub-agent's sync-only retry attempts succeeded.

assumptions: Consumed by the single-sub-agent workflow retry route and by the multi-sub-agent run loops.
Errors matching the contract-handoff pattern are never treated as sync-only.
A worker timeout is a distinct class from a transport failure: it retries fresh with a time-boxed fold rather than as a transient blip.
risks: The sync-only and contract-handoff regexes can misclassify novel compliance wording, turning a full retry into a sync-only one or the reverse.
Merged summaries grow verbose when the work and sync summaries diverge.

risks.text: Callers must merge a sync-only retry through mergeSyncOnlyResult rather than replacing the work result; the retry does not re-establish filesChanged or contractsChanged on its own.

invariants: Failed worker results are never retried by isRetriable. A blocked result is retried only when it delivered no files and its text marks a provider transport death or the harness wall-clock kill; every other blocked result is terminal.

mergeSyncOnlyResult unions filesChanged and contractsChanged into ordered unique lists. graphNodesTouched is not unioned: a non-empty sync list replaces the work attempt's ids verbatim, duplicates included, and the work list survives only when the sync attempt reports none.

mergeSyncOnlyResult preserves the work attempt's implementation claims and appends what the sync attempt reports; restraint against re-editing code on a sync-only retry is carried by the retry prompt, not by the merge.
annotation.integrationPoints: Driven by the retry loops in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/nodes and mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/sub-agent; merged results are consumed by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/handoff-loader.
annotation.dataFlow: compliance report → classify (sync-only | grounding | required-fields | transport | timeout) → isRetriable → foldRetryContext or foldWorkerTimeoutRetry → worker retry → mergeSyncOnlyResult → handoff.

annotation.summary: Session-map helpers for resuming provider conversations within a single invoke. Collects role-to-sessionId pairs from finished sub-agents so a retry or a follow-up phase can resume the same provider thread, and offers a shallow merge of two such maps.

keyExports.collectSubAgentSessions: Builds a role-to-sessionId map from finished sub-agents; the last writer wins for a role.
keyExports.mergeSessions: Shallow-merges two session maps, with the newer map overwriting matching roles.

assumptions: Sessions are keyed by role rather than by instance id, because provider resume support is role-oriented in this harness.
Intake resets the worker session map for each new task, so resume is intra-task only.
mergeSessions exists for tests and future channels; it is not what drives resume today.

risks.text: Callers must not treat these maps as cross-task state: each task starts from an empty session map at intake, so a resume built on a prior task's ids will not find a live provider thread.

invariants: collectSubAgentSessions skips any sub-agent missing a role or a worker session id.
mergeSessions preserves keys absent from the newer map rather than dropping them.
annotation.integrationPoints: Live sessions are accumulated during an invoke by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/multi and read back by the channel adapters when resuming a role.
annotation.dataFlow: finished sub-agents → collectSubAgentSessions → role-to-sessionId map → provider resume within the same invoke.

annotation.summary: GraphState is the typed channel set the LangGraph orchestrator threads through its nodes, mirroring the State schema in docs/langgraph-orchestrator-design.md. Channels default to last-value-wins via a value() helper, with turn/attempts using a last-non-nullish-wins reducer and usageRecords using an appending reducer.

keyExports.GraphState: Annotation.Root schema grouped as: input (chatId, task); workspace (repoRoot, targetMode: 'sandbox'|'attach'); protocol artifacts (assignment/assignmentFile/assignmentValid, result/resultFile/schemaValid, report, ok); worker/session (llmProvider, agentArgs, workerSessions, turn, attempts); multi-agent (mode: 'single'|'multi', planMode, subAgents, goalOk, processOk, signals, greenfield, repovineOrientTrail, repovineClaims, execution, runtimeCheck, leftRunning, reaped, usage, usageRollup, mcpRollup, usageRecords, telemetry); and control/output (error, replyText).

assumptions: State channel names are internal; client surfaces translate to sub-agent terminology.
workerSessions resets to {} at each ingress for fresh LLM sessions per /goal; intra-task resume accumulates via liveSessions in multi.mjs and run_sub_agent capture within one invoke.
Capabilities are not threaded through state; nodes derive them via targetPolicy(targetMode).

sideEffects.description: LangGraph Annotation.Root schema consumed at workflow compile time

risks: Schema drift if nodes return fields not declared here; LangGraph silently drops unknown keys.
targetMode (sandbox|attach) and mode (single|multi routing) are separate channels with similar names; attach invoke input must never alter mode.
patterns: Last-value-wins channels via value() helper; turn/attempts/usageRecords use custom reducers.
invariants: turn and attempts are last-non-nullish-wins: the reducer keeps the prior value only against an undefined or null partial update. turn persists across invokes on a checkpointed thread; attempts resets to zero at intake so a reused thread does not carry a stale count into the HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES bound.
usageRecords appends arrays across partial node returns rather than overwriting.
usageRollup carries run-level fresh/resume cost split; usage is the top-level total; mcpRollup is the run-level repovine MCP tool-call rollup.
goalOk, processOk, signals, and greenfield are threaded explicitly from multiAgent's return so formatMultiReply and repovine-process read the authoritative values instead of recomputing them.
annotation.integrationPoints: lib/graph/workflow.mjs (StateGraph build), lib/graph/nodes.mjs, lib/graph/multi.mjs, repovine-process.mjs.
annotation.dataFlow: Telegram/CLI input partial -> ingress merges task/repoRoot/mode/workerSessions -> protocol nodes fill assignment/result/report -> multi-agent nodes populate subAgents/goalOk/processOk/signals/repovineOrientTrail/repovineClaims/usageRollup/mcpRollup -> compose_reply sets replyText.

annotation.summary: One protocol sub-agent run, from task composition to a validated result. Builds the scoped task with the inter-sub-agent handoff sections and the phase's context-quality policy, writes and validates the assignment, snapshots sandbox processes around the worker call, then validates the result, runs the compliance check and the contract gate, and drives the retry loop until the run is accepted or out of attempts. Usage and MCP metrics are totalled across attempts.

keyExports.buildSubAgentTask: Composes the sub-agent's task text from the parent task, its spec, the prior handoffs and the phase's context-quality policy.
keyExports.runSubAgent: Runs one sub-agent to a validated result: assignment, worker call, validation, compliance, contract gate, retries, and the per-attempt artifacts.

assumptions: The context phase is taken from the spec when set, and otherwise inferred: the annotation-writer manifest means annotate, the review role means explore, and everything else is implement.

Context-quality calibration is keyed by phase and comes from the target contract; the calibration uses the config field name while the assignment policy names the same knob differently, so the two spellings refer to one threshold.
Every artifact this run writes goes to the active area, keyed by the sub-agent key, including a result file per attempt.

sideEffects.description: writes the assignment, per-attempt results, the final result, and the usage and MCP artifacts under the active run
invokes the provider worker to run the agent
snapshots and reconciles sandbox processes around the worker call, and shells out to the engine CLI for validation and compliance
logs run progress when verbose logging is enabled

risks: Retry classification decides the recovery path: a sync-only rejection retries narrowly, a transport blip retries as-is, and a worker timeout retries fresh with a time-boxed fold, so a misclassified failure retries in the wrong shape.
Process reconciliation happens around the worker call, so a process the sandbox attribution misses survives the run and is attributed to nothing.
The retry budget is bounded per run, and exhausting it yields the last attempt's result rather than an error, so the caller sees a completed run that was never accepted.
patterns: Assignment in, validated result out: every worker call is bracketed by validation on both sides rather than trusting the agent's own report.
Per-attempt artifacts are kept, so a retry chain remains reconstructable after the fact.
invariants: A run is accepted when compliance passes and the contract gate is satisfied, and also when the implement phase delivered files and annotation sync is the only outstanding rejection — that acceptance is recorded separately as sync owed to the post-review sub-agent. A sync-only retry that passed on its own attempt keeps its acceptance even when the re-check of the merged result rejects. The contract gate only ever withdraws acceptance; it never grants it.
Each attempt writes its own result file before the retry decision is made.
Usage and MCP metrics are summed across every attempt rather than taken from the last one.
annotation.integrationPoints: Builds assignments through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/assignment, calls the engine through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/repovine, resolves artifact paths through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/harness-paths, brackets the run with mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/sandbox-procs, dispatches the provider through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers, classifies retries with mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/retry, composes handoffs through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/handoff-loader, and totals metrics through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/usage and mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/mcp-telemetry.
annotation.dataFlow: parent task and spec → buildSubAgentTask → assignment written and validated → process snapshot → worker run → reconcile → result validated, compliance checked, contract gate applied → accepted, or reclassified and retried → final result plus summed usage and MCP artifacts.

envDependencies.GRAPH_VERBOSE: Set to 0 to silence per-run progress logging
envDependencies.HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES: Upper bound on retry attempts for one sub-agent run

annotation.summary: Scope-grounded existence gate for tests. The verify phase is a read-only agent forbidden to run tests, so behaviour coverage cannot be gated there; what is checkable is that every implementer required to deliver tests left at least one test source file under a directory it demonstrably wrote to. Existence only: the reviewer's test assessment remains the advisory quality lens.

keyExports.TEST_FILE_RE: Pattern identifying a test source file by its filename suffix.
keyExports.hasTestFileUnder: Bounded existence scan for a test file beneath one directory.
keyExports.missingTestFloorBlockers: Blockers for eligible sub-agents that left no test file under any directory they wrote to.
keyExports.subAgentTestScanDirs: The top-level directories derived from a sub-agent's reported changed files.
keyExports.testFloorEligible: Whether a sub-agent's role is required to deliver tests.

assumptions: Scan directories come from the sub-agent's reported changed files rather than its declared scope, because the declared scope defaults to the whole workspace and would make the scan vacuous.
Deriving directories from the role instead of from actual writes was tried and produced a false fire, so placement is taken from what the run actually touched.
A change to a root-level file yields no scan directory, so such a run is not gated by this floor.

sideEffects.description: walks the candidate directories looking for a test source file

risks: The floor rests on self-reported changed files, so a sub-agent that under-reports what it wrote evades the gate entirely; this asymmetry is known and accepted rather than closed.
It checks existence, not that the tests are meaningful or that they run, so a placeholder test file satisfies it.
The walk is depth-bounded and skips build and cache directories, so a test placed unusually deep is not seen.
patterns: Gate on what is deterministically checkable and leave judgement to the reviewer, rather than asking a model to assert a fact it cannot verify.
Reported paths are sanitized before use so a confused self-report cannot walk outside the workspace.
invariants: Only roles required to deliver tests are eligible for the floor.
A path that is absolute or points outside the workspace contributes no scan directory.
One test file under any written-to directory satisfies the floor for that sub-agent.
annotation.integrationPoints: Role test requirements come from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/agents; the blockers join the run's fix ledger next to the referenced-artifact floor.
annotation.dataFlow: sub-agent results → eligible roles filtered → scan directories derived from reported changed files → bounded existence scan → blockers for those with none.

annotation.summary: Compiles the node functions into the runnable orchestrator graph and provides a convenience invoke. The orchestration library owns step order, branching, retries and persisted state; it does not choose the model and never reaches into engine internals, because the nodes shell out to the command line instead.

keyExports.buildGraph: Wires the nodes and their routers into a compiled graph, with a checkpointer for threaded state.
keyExports.invokeGraph: Runs one task on a graph, keyed by thread, with an abort signal and a capture hook.

assumptions: Three routers carry all the branching: after intake an error goes straight to the reply and a multi-agent task goes to the fan-out node; after the schema check an invalid assignment goes to the reply, so no worker cost is incurred on work that cannot be dispatched; after compliance a rejected run may loop back once.

The retry policy is shared with the multi-agent loop rather than restated, and it only retries a run that finished and was rejected with actionable notes — a blocked or failed worker will not fix itself on a second attempt.
One retry is the default because the usual rejection is a coverage gate the agent can satisfy once the blocker is folded into its task; setting the limit to zero disables it.
The thread identifier keys the checkpointer, so one conversation keeps its state across invocations.
Every invocation runs intake, which clears the active run state while leaving the archived runs in place until an explicit reset.

sideEffects.description: compiles and runs the orchestration graph
the checkpointer retains state per thread

risks: The retry loop returns to the same node that produced the rejection, so a rejection the agent cannot address costs a second full run before the bound stops it.

Routing is expressed as edge lists alongside the router functions, so adding a branch means changing both; a router that returns a name absent from its edge list compiles cleanly and throws inside the branch on the first invocation that takes it.
The default checkpointer holds state in memory, so a restart loses every thread's history.
patterns: The orchestration library is swappable: the node functions carry the logic, and replacing the library means re-wiring the same functions while the protocol boundary stays where it is.
Cost gates come before spend: the schema check routes an invalid assignment away from the worker rather than letting it fail inside one.
annotation.flowDescription: intake → multi_agent OR the single-agent chain → compose_reply; routeAfterCompliance loops back to run_sub_agent, otherwise runtime_check, bounded by HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES.
invariants: An intake error never reaches a worker.
A multi-agent task goes through the fan-out node and then straight to the reply.
Retries are bounded, and the bound is configurable down to none.
annotation.integrationPoints: The state shape comes from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/state, the single-task nodes from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/nodes, the fan-out node from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/multi, and the shared retry predicate from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/retry; the graph is driven by the command-line, service and chat entrypoints under scripts.
annotation.dataFlow: input → intake → either the fan-out node or the single-task chain of assignment, schema check, worker, persistence, result check and compliance → optional bounded retry → runtime check → composed reply.

envDependencies.HARNESS_MAX_RETRIES: How many times a compliance-rejected run may be retried, defaulting to one; zero disables retries

annotation.summary: Workspace revision custody on a single git-tree backend for both target modes. Captures a revision as a tree digest written through a throwaway index, compares revision pairs, and derives the changed-file list and the reviewable patch with repovine's own committed artifacts and the harness internals excluded. commitAttachRun snapshots a successful attach run into the real index under a run branch, which is the operator's promotion hook.

keyExports.REPOVINE_ARTIFACT_RE: Pattern matching annotation backup filenames to filter out.
keyExports.REPOVINE_COMMITTED_ARTIFACTS: repovine's own committed filenames, excluded from the changed-file view.
keyExports.captureWorkspaceRevision: Captures a git-tree revision; returns null on failure so the caller fails closed, and rejects any other backend.
keyExports.commitAttachRun: Commits a successful run into the real index and moves the run branch; reports no commit on a clean tree and null on git failure.
keyExports.diffChangedFiles: Changed-file list between two revisions, filtered of committed artifacts, harness internals and annotation backups.
keyExports.diffReviewablePatch: Binary-safe patch bytes between two revisions with the same exclusions.
keyExports.revisionsEqual: Compares two revisions by backend and digest rather than by object identity.

assumptions: The git-tree digest is the exact tree oid the earlier capture returned, so persisted values such as the reviewed diff base stay byte-identical across the refactor.
In attach mode the capture reads through the read-only pointer into the disposable repo rather than the operator's checkout.
commitAttachRun is a convenience for promotion, never the custody mechanism: custody is the captured revision.

sideEffects.description: runs git plumbing to write trees, diff revisions and commit the run branch
commitAttachRun writes to the real index and moves the run branch; capture writes only a throwaway index outside the workspace

risks.text: A backend mismatch or a falsy revision yields a null diff, and callers must treat that as unknown and fail closed rather than substituting the sub-agent's self-reported file list.

commitAttachRun is the only path here that writes a real git index: it stages the workspace, commits, and force-moves the run branch. Under the launcher topology those refs land in the launch-scoped disposable repo the workspace pointer targets, not in the operator's checkout, which acquires the branch by fetching from launch state.

patterns: Capture through a throwaway index keeps observation free of side effects on HEAD, the index and the working tree.
Exclusions are applied by explicit pathspec rather than by trusting the workspace ignore file.
invariants: Capture never moves HEAD, the real index or the working tree; it uses a throwaway index file outside the workspace.
Harness-internal directories are excluded by pathspec from capture, diff and the promotion commit, never by relying on the workspace ignore file alone.
commitAttachRun runs after the run status is derived, so custody and review freshness are established before the promotion commit mutates refs.
annotation.integrationPoints: Revisions are captured and compared by the run flow in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/multi and the workflow node that composes the reply; the git primitives and repository guards come from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/worktree.
annotation.dataFlow: baseline capture before the run → sub-agents modify the workspace → capture after → diffChangedFiles and diffReviewablePatch feed the review and the reply → commitAttachRun promotes a successful attach run onto its branch.

annotation.summary: Tells the planner whether the sandbox is greenfield or an existing product. Probes the workspace root for product source markers, treats a missing or entry-empty annotations file as still-greenfield, and renders the state as a prompt sentence for the planner and the orient phase. Reviewed against current source: 6-export surface unchanged from the prior note.

keyExports.describeWorkspaceState: Renders the greenfield/existing verdict as a prompt sentence for the planner.
keyExports.hasOnlyStubAnnotations: True when the annotations file is missing, unreadable, or carries no entries at all.
keyExports.isGreenfieldSandbox: True when no PRODUCT_SOURCE_MARKERS path exists under the workspace root.

assumptions: The repovine graph remains the semantic source of truth about the product; these markers are only a fallback guard for an empty sandbox.
Any single annotation entry ends greenfield regardless of its depth; the check counts entries and never grades them.

sideEffects.description: checks marker paths and reads the annotations file under the workspace root
reads the force-multi override that suppresses greenfield detection

risks: Marker heuristics can misclassify an unusual repo layout, and adding a marker name can make a freshly scaffolded sandbox read as an existing product.

risks.text: Callers propagate this boolean into engine compliance and the run gate. A marker path appearing under the workspace root tightens context-session enforcement for every sub-agent and makes a failed orient count against the run verdict.

invariants: Workspace-state detection lives with the planner and orchestration code rather than in the handoff document.

Greenfield detection reaches the compliance exemption and the run verdict, not planning alone: the pre-orient sandbox check rides along as every sub-agent's greenfield-run flag, and the orient-derived context decides whether a failed orient sinks the run.
annotation.integrationPoints: isGreenfieldSandbox is consumed by the planner in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/plan, describeWorkspaceState feeds the planner prompt, and isGreenfieldContext gates the greenfield orient section in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/repovine-process.
annotation.dataFlow: workspace root → marker existence checks and stub-annotation check → greenfield boolean → planner prompt wording and the greenfield orient path.

envDependencies.HARNESS_FORCE_MULTI: Set to '1' to suppress the marker-based sandbox check, keeping an implicit multi-role plan from collapsing to a single sub-agent. Orient-driven greenfield detection ignores it.

annotation.summary: Git worktree isolation for parallel sandbox sub-agents, plus the shared ensureGitRepo primitive. Creates a throwaway worktree and branch per role, commits the worker's changes there, merges the branch back into the sandbox root, and cleans up. isRepo accepts a root .git of either shape (a directory in the sandbox, a gitfile pointer in attach) while still refusing to treat an enclosing repository as this workspace. Reviewed against current source: 7-export surface unchanged from the prior note.

keyExports.addWorktree: Creates a temporary worktree and a sub-agent branch for one role.
keyExports.available: True when git is on PATH and the repo root is a git repository.
keyExports.commitWorktree: Commits everything in a worker's worktree, permitting an empty commit.
keyExports.ensureGitRepo: Initializes a sandbox git repo with a baseline commit when one is missing.
keyExports.mergeWorktree: Merges a sub-agent branch back into the sandbox root and reports conflicts.
keyExports.preserveWorktreeArtifacts: Copies harness artifacts out of a worktree before it is removed.
keyExports.removeWorktree: Best-effort removal of the worktree and its branch.

assumptions: Worktree isolation is used only for the parallel stages the planner authorizes, and only when the stage's scopes are disjoint; the gate itself lives in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/plan, not here.
When git is unavailable the caller falls back to a sequential shared sandbox rather than failing the run.

This module reads no environment itself; every policy decision reaches it as an argument. Greenfield worktree fan-out is on by default and HARNESS_GREENFIELD_PARALLEL=0 disables it, read in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/plan after the git-capability and plan-mode checks.

sideEffects.description: runs git commands synchronously via spawnSync
creates worktree directories, branches, commits and merges, and copies preserved artifacts

risks: A merge conflict becomes a run blocker, and the branch name can surface in operator-facing blocker text.
Cleanup is best-effort: a failed removal leaves a stale worktree directory and branch behind.

risks.text: Callers must confirm the stage's sub-agent scopes are disjoint before requesting worktree isolation; overlapping scopes surface as merge conflicts at join rather than as an early error.

patterns: Best-effort synchronous git with no retry layer: each helper reports failure rather than recovering.
ensureGitRepo distinguishes a fresh sandbox init from an attached workspace so an attached repo never gains harness files.
invariants: ensureGitRepo writes its harness .gitignore only on a fresh init, so an attached workspace is left as it was found.
On an attach workspace ensureGitRepo is a no-op beyond config: the baseline HEAD already exists, and no baseline commit is made.
annotation.integrationPoints: Driven by the parallel stage runner in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/multi; the decision to run a stage in worktrees is made by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/plan.
annotation.dataFlow: planner authorizes a parallel stage → ensureGitRepo → addWorktree per sub-agent → worker runs with cwd set to the worktree → commitWorktree → mergeWorktree at join → preserveWorktreeArtifacts → removeWorktree.

annotation.summary: Loads the handoff policy and templates from repo-owned markdown and applies them: checks a finished sub-agent's result against the contract expectations its role carries, normalizes an accepted result into a handoff record, and renders the prior-work section and per-role constraint that the next sub-agent's task carries.

keyExports.HANDOFF_CONFIG_FILE: Basename of the handoff policy document.
keyExports.buildInterSubAgentSectionFromTemplate: Renders the prior-sub-agent section from sibling results using the template.
keyExports.buildInterSubAgentTaskSection: The task-facing wrapper over that renderer.
keyExports.contractHandoffViolations: Checks a result against the contract expectations its role requires.
keyExports.finalizeHandoff: Normalizes an accepted result into the handoff record passed forward.
keyExports.handoffSearchDirs: The directories searched for that document, bundled default plus any override.
keyExports.interSubAgentConstraintFromTemplate: Renders the per-role handoff constraint from the template.
keyExports.interSubAgentHandoffConstraint: The task-facing wrapper over that renderer.
keyExports.isAnnotationOnlySummary: Recognizes a summary that reports only annotation work.
keyExports.loadHandoffConfig: Reads and caches the parsed policy and templates.
keyExports.loadHandoffPolicy: The policy portion of the parsed configuration.
keyExports.parseHandoffMarkdown: Parses the document into frontmatter flags, named template sections and the minimal example.

assumptions: The handoff document is repo-owned markdown: a bundled default with an optional override directory, so wording is editable without a code change.
Finalization runs after the compliance check has accepted a result, not before.
The parsed configuration is cached per file, so editing the document mid-process is not picked up.

sideEffects.description: reads the bundled and overridden handoff markdown
caches the parsed configuration per file

risks: Template wording and the structured contract check are edited separately, so prose can drift from what is actually validated and a sub-agent can read as compliant while failing the check.
The override directory replaces the bundled document wholesale, so a partial override silently loses the sections it does not restate.
patterns: Markdown as runtime configuration: frontmatter flags plus named template sections, with a generated bundled default and a local override path.
invariants: Review roles are exempt from the required contract expectations.
Greenfield detection is never sourced from the handoff document; that state comes from the workspace inspection.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/sub-agent when composing a task and finalizing a result; the handoff document itself is projected into the workspace by the engine's agent-asset projection.
annotation.dataFlow: handoff document → parsed policy and templates → per-role constraint and prior-work section in the next task → result checked against the contract expectations → finalized handoff record passed forward.

envDependencies.HARNESS_HANDOFF_DIR: Optional override directory for the handoff document

annotation.summary: Path layout and lifecycle for the .harness artifact tree. Resolves every run, sub-agent and telemetry path under an ephemeral active/ area and a durable runs/ archive, and owns the transitions between them: clearing active at ingress, archiving a finished run, recovering orphaned runs after a crash, and migrating the legacy flat layout.

keyExports.HARNESS_DIR_NAME: Name of the harness root directory under the repo root.
keyExports.RUN_LEVEL: Basenames of the run-level artifacts (summary, orient, verify, rollups, meta, events).
keyExports.appendRunIndex: Appends one JSON line to the run index with an archive timestamp.
keyExports.archiveActiveRun: Moves an active run tree into the archive, writes its meta, copies events, and clears live telemetry.
keyExports.archiveOrphanActiveRuns: Archives active run directories left behind by a crash or stop.
keyExports.clearHarnessActive: Removes every child of the active area; called at ingress.
keyExports.findLatestArchivedRunId: Most recent archived run id that has sub-agent results.
keyExports.harnessIndexPath: Path of the append-only run index.
keyExports.harnessRoot: The harness root directory for a repo root.
keyExports.listSubAgentResultFiles: Lists a run's sub-agent result files.
keyExports.migrateLegacyFlatHarness: One-time migration from the flat layout to the run-tree layout.
keyExports.runDir: Run directory, selecting active or archived via the active flag.
keyExports.runLevelPath: Path of a run-level artifact within a run directory.
keyExports.splitSubAgentKey: Parses a composite sub-agent key into its run id and sub-agent id.
keyExports.subAgentAssignmentPath: Assignment file path resolved from a sub-agent key.
keyExports.subAgentAttemptResultPath: Per-attempt result path under a sub-agent's attempts directory.
keyExports.subAgentMcpPath: MCP telemetry path for a sub-agent.
keyExports.subAgentResultPath: Result file path resolved from a sub-agent key.
keyExports.subAgentUsagePath: Usage ledger path for a sub-agent.
keyExports.writeJsonFile: Writes JSON, creating the parent directory first.

assumptions: The active area is ephemeral and cleared each ingress; the archived runs area is durable until an explicit reset.
A sub-agent key encodes runId and subAgentId; splitSubAgentKey falls back to a default sub-agent id when the key has no separator.
migrateLegacyFlatHarness is idempotent and runs before orphan archiving.

sideEffects.description: creates, renames, merges and deletes files under the harness active and runs directories
stats and reads run directories, result files and the run index

risks: Renaming a RUN_LEVEL basename breaks telemetry, the handoff loader, and the HTTP status readers that read those files by name.
A bind-mounted workspace needs its ownership initialized before harness services start, or the first write to the harness tree fails.

risks.text: Callers must pass the active flag that matches where the run currently lives; a path built for the wrong area silently points at a directory that does not exist after archiving.

patterns: Active and archived paths share one helper set, selected by an active flag rather than duplicated path builders.
Legacy basename parsers exist only to feed the one-time migration.
invariants: RUN_LEVEL basenames are the single source of truth for run-level artifact filenames.
writeJsonFile always creates the parent directory before writing.
archiveActiveRun clears the active current-run file and truncates the active events log after copying them.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/harness-run for clear and prepare, by the telemetry writer for current-run and event paths, by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/nodes and mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/sub-agent for assignment, result, usage and MCP files, and by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/multi for run rollups.
annotation.dataFlow: ingress → clearHarnessActive → graph writes through the subAgent* path helpers → archiveActiveRun moves the active run into the archive and appends the run index.

annotation.summary: The run boundary at ingress. Reads a compact summary of the last archived run, formats it as a bounded markdown block injected into the new task for continuity, then clears only the active area so archived runs survive. Also re-exports the migration and archival helpers so callers need one import rather than two.

keyExports.DEFAULT_PRIOR_SUMMARY_MAX_BYTES: Byte cap on the prior-run block injected into a task.
keyExports.clearHarnessArtifacts: Deprecated alias that clears only the active area.
keyExports.findLatestTaskPrefix: The newest archived run id, after any legacy migration.
keyExports.formatPriorRunSummaryForTask: Renders that summary as the prior-run markdown block, clipped to the byte cap.
keyExports.prepareHarnessRun: The ingress barrier: migrate the legacy layout, archive orphaned runs, read the prior summary, clear the active area, and return the summary and its text.
keyExports.readPriorRunSummary: Aggregates the latest archived run's sub-agent result files into a compact status, files, contracts and blockers object.

assumptions: Only the active area is wiped each run; archived runs persist until an explicit reset.
The prior-run text is coordination memory, while the annotations and the workspace code remain the durable truth.
Worker sessions are reset separately at ingress; intra-task resume is handled by the run orchestrator.

sideEffects.description: reads archived run results and the run-level summary
clears the active area and archives orphaned runs during the ingress barrier

risks: A corrupt sub-agent result file is skipped silently, so a partially unreadable archive yields a quietly thinner prior-run summary.
The prior-run block is prompt context, not an audit record: treating it as protocol truth would let a summary stand in for the run artifacts.
patterns: Cross-task memory reads the archive while per-task artifacts are written to the active area until the run is archived.
Selected path helpers are re-exported so the ingress path imports one module.
annotation.flowDescription: Ingress calls the barrier, which migrates and archives, reads the prior summary, clears the active area, and hands back the text to prepend to the task.
invariants: The injected block is capped at the byte limit, measured as UTF-8 rather than character count.
readPriorRunSummary reads archived runs only, never the live active area.
The deprecated clear alias removes the active area and never touches the archive.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called at graph ingress; migration, archival, path resolution and the archived-result listing all come from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/harness-paths, which this module also re-exports.
annotation.dataFlow: ingress → prepareHarnessRun (migrate, archive orphans, read the prior summary from the archive) → clear the active area → prior-run text prepended to the task → the run writes fresh artifacts under the active area.

annotation.summary: The planning completion seam: one cheap request that returns text and nothing else. The worker adapters run full coding agents that edit files and produce a run result; the planning node needs the opposite, so this path disables tools entirely and asks a single question. Two providers are wired, and every failure is reported rather than thrown so the caller can fall back to the deterministic planner.

keyExports.askLLM: Sends one planning prompt to the selected provider and returns the text or a reason it failed.

assumptions: Tools are switched off rather than merely unused on the provider path: no tools and no protocol servers, so a planning call cannot edit anything.
Any failure is a reported refusal rather than an exception, because the caller's answer to a failed plan is the heuristic planner, not an error.
Both providers normalize to the same result shape despite completely different transports.
An unrecognized provider falls through to the default rather than failing, so a misspelled name still produces a plan.
The local path asks for zero temperature and no streaming, since the reply is parsed as structured output rather than shown to anyone.

A caller-supplied timeout is threaded to the provider as an argument and resolved once per call, with the environment variable serving only as the default. It is deliberately not passed through the shared environment slot: a provider that suspends before reading it would miss the value, and two concurrent calls would observe each other's.

sideEffects.description: loads and calls the provider library for the default path
posts a completion request to the configured local endpoint

risks: A blocked credential, an absent provider library, a timeout and an empty reply all return the same failure shape, so a caller that only checks the flag cannot tell a configuration problem from a slow model.
The default provider loads its library before the timeout is armed, so a slow or hanging module resolution is not covered by the caller's budget.
An unrecognized provider silently becomes the default rather than being rejected, so a typo produces a plan from the wrong backend.
patterns: The planning seam is deliberately separate from the worker adapters: cheap, single-turn and incapable of editing, which is what makes it safe to call speculatively.
Every provider path collapses to one result shape, so the caller's fallback logic does not branch per provider.
Per-call budgets are arguments rather than ambient state, which is what makes two concurrent planning calls independent.
invariants: The default provider runs with an empty tool list and no protocol servers.
Every path returns a result object; none throws.
The planner timeout is never written to the process environment; it travels as an argument.
Each call resolves its own budget, so concurrent calls cannot interfere.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by the planning node in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph; credentials come from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/auth; model selection per role from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/model-role; endpoint, key and reply cleanup for the local path from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/local-config; numeric parsing from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/num.
annotation.stateShape: Either a success carrying the text, or a failure carrying a reason.
annotation.dataFlow: planning prompt → provider dispatch → credential check → a single no-tools completion → text, or a reason → caller parses the plan or falls back to the heuristic one.

envDependencies.PLANNER_TIMEOUT_MS: Planner request timeout, defaulting to ninety seconds

annotation.summary: Shared harness logging helper for daemon/runtime logs. Adds app-side ISO timestamps by default and consistent scoped line/bullet formatting for graph, channel, provider, runtime_check, and reaper logs.

keyExports.logBullet: Writes one or more indented bullet-style worker trace lines with optional ISO timestamp and [scope].
keyExports.logLine: Writes one or more scoped log lines to a stream, prefixing each line with an optional ISO timestamp and [scope].

assumptions: Used for daemon/container logs, not for human-facing langgraph-cli result output.
Timestamps are evaluated at write time; multiline messages receive a fresh prefix per line.

sideEffects.description: Writes formatted log lines to the provided stream, defaulting to stderr
Reads HARNESS_LOG_TIMESTAMPS once at module load

risks: HARNESS_LOG_TIMESTAMPS is read at import time, so tests or long-lived processes cannot toggle it after modules load.
High-volume provider streams can still produce many log lines when verbose flags are enabled.
invariants: HARNESS_LOG_TIMESTAMPS=0 restores the old no-timestamp style.
logLine prefixes with [scope]; logBullet prefixes with [scope] and a bullet marker.
No external logging dependency is introduced.
annotation.integrationPoints: Imported by graph nodes, multi/leaf/planner, runtime-check, sandbox-procs, Telegram/HTTP channels and entrypoints, Claude/Codex/Cursor workers, cursor-config, and cancel-guard.
annotation.dataFlow: Caller formats scope/message -> logLine/logBullet -> stream.write lines with timestamp/scope/bullet prefixes.

envDependencies.HARNESS_LOG_TIMESTAMPS: Set to 0 to disable app-side ISO timestamps

annotation.summary: Per-role model and reasoning defaults for harness LLM calls. Maps a sub-agent spec role onto one of four buckets (planner, implementer, verify, ask), then resolves each bucket to a provider-specific setting: Claude gets model+effort (planner opus:high, implementer sonnet:medium, verify and ask sonnet:low), the local OpenAI-compatible provider gets a model id only because a bare chat endpoint has no effort knob.

keyExports.HarnessModelRole: JSDoc typedef for the role union 'planner' | 'implementer' | 'verify' | 'ask'.
keyExports.LOCAL_DEFAULT_MODEL: Fallback local model id (qwen2.5-coder:32b) when no local env is set.
keyExports.formatRoleLabel: Human-readable provider+role label for logs and status output.
keyExports.parseRoleSetting: Parses a role override string into {model, effort}: 'opus:high', bare effort 'high', or bare model 'opus'.
keyExports.resolveClaudeRole: Claude model/effort for a role: env override merged over the role default.
keyExports.resolveLocalRole: Local provider model id: per-role LOCAL_*_MODEL, else LOCAL_MODEL, else LOCAL_DEFAULT_MODEL.
keyExports.subAgentModelRole: Maps a sub-agent spec role to one of planner/implementer/verify/ask; defaults to implementer.

assumptions: Role override env vars are read dynamically as process.env[ENV_BY_ROLE[role]], so static env detection does not see PLANNER_REASONING, IMPLEMENTER_REASONING, VERIFY_REASONING or ASK_REASONING; they are real and the graph's envVars list is incomplete here.
CLAUDE_AGENT_MODEL survives only as a legacy fallback for the implementer role, and only when IMPLEMENTER_REASONING is unset.
Effort tokens are limited to minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max.

sideEffects.description: reads role and provider model env vars at call time via process.env

risks: Role default drift: verify and ask default to a cheaper tier, and a weaker model there produced basic-tier annotations where the annotate phase requires detailed.

risks.text: Callers must confirm which role bucket a spec resolves to before relying on a model tier; an unrecognized role silently falls back to implementer defaults.

patterns: Role-keyed env indirection (ENV_BY_ROLE) means new roles need only a table entry.
Per-role reasoning env supersedes the legacy per-provider model env.
invariants: Every role resolves to a model: per-role env, then role default, then LOCAL_DEFAULT_MODEL on the local provider.
The local provider returns model only; temperature and timeouts live in lib/workers/local-config.mjs.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by provider config builders and status labels; mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/sub-agent calls subAgentModelRole when a resolved role omits modelRole. Local tuning beyond model id lives in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/local-config.
annotation.dataFlow: spec.role → subAgentModelRole → bucket → resolveClaudeRole/resolveLocalRole (env override merged over default) → provider config.

envDependencies.ASK_REASONING: Read-only /ask and annotation model/effort override (default sonnet:low)
envDependencies.CLAUDE_AGENT_MODEL: Legacy implementer-only Claude model override, used when IMPLEMENTER_REASONING is unset
envDependencies.LOCAL_ASK_MODEL: Per-role local model override for ask
envDependencies.LOCAL_IMPLEMENTER_MODEL: Per-role local model override for implementer
envDependencies.LOCAL_MODEL: Base model id for the local OpenAI-compatible provider
envDependencies.LOCAL_PLANNER_MODEL: Per-role local model override for planner
envDependencies.LOCAL_VERIFY_MODEL: Per-role local model override for verify

annotation.summary: Fail-safe numeric env parsing shared across the harness. finitePositive(raw, fallback) coerces to a finite positive number, else returns the fallback — guarding against NaN (Number('abc')) which would make setTimeout(fn, NaN) fire immediately and abort a run at t=0 with a misleading 'timed out'.

keyExports.finitePositive: Returns Number(raw) when finite and > 0, otherwise the fallback.

assumptions: Callers use it for timeout/limit envs where a non-numeric or non-positive value must degrade to a safe default.
risks: A zero or negative configured value silently falls back to the default rather than erroring.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by the worker/config helpers (claude-config, codex/local-config, llm, workers/ask-*) for timeout and byte-limit env parsing.

annotation.summary: The harness's only contact surface with the repovine engine: a thin wrapper that spawns the built repovine CLI file-in, JSON-out. buildCliCommand is the pure command constructor that pins both the child's cwd and its workspace root to the same repo root for every subcommand, which is what keeps a sandbox or attached workspace consistent across CLI, MCP, compliance, refresh and status calls.

keyExports.REPOVINE_CLI: Resolved path to the built repovine entrypoint, overridable by env.
keyExports.agents: Spawns a repovine agents subcommand with the pinned root and parses its JSON.
keyExports.annotationHealth: End-state annotation needsWork/clean snapshot taken from the repovine status --json command; returns null when the CLI is unavailable or errors.
keyExports.buildCliCommand: Pure {command, args, cwd, env} constructor; the seam tests assert root-pinning against without spawning the engine.
keyExports.compliance: Re-checks a run's claims against observable repository state; greenfieldRun passes --greenfield-run so the context exemption holds for every sub-agent.
keyExports.getManifests: Fetches the manifest for a role.
keyExports.harnessBrief: Role brief text for provider prompts, derived from runBrief.
keyExports.orientQuery: Deterministic search_context + trace_flow pre-orient query used before the orient sub-agent runs.
keyExports.projectRoles: Fetches the repository's own role source (agents.roles in repovine.config.json) via the read-only 'roles' CLI subcommand; --at pins the read to a committed tree-ish. Returns parsed JSON or { errors }.
keyExports.refreshGraph: Orchestrator-level refresh barrier (runs repovine build), optionally cleaning orphaned annotations.
keyExports.runBrief: Fetches a role's run brief (repovine agents run-brief), memoized per process by role/name key.
keyExports.sessionQuality: Fetches the context-session quality report for a worker's contextSessionId.
keyExports.validateAssignment: Validates an assignment file against the agent protocol.
keyExports.validateResult: Validates a result file (schema-only) and maps the CLI's 'valid' field onto the graph node's schemaValid flag.

assumptions: The engine path can be overridden by env; otherwise it is discovered by walking up to the built entrypoint.
The workspace root is passed explicitly so the graph builds against the sandbox rather than the host checkout.
The run-brief cache is process-local and keyed independently of the repo, so it must not outlive a single process.

sideEffects.description: spawns the repovine CLI synchronously for every subcommand
memoizes run briefs in a process-local map

risks: A missing built engine entrypoint breaks every gate at runtime rather than at startup, so the failure surfaces mid-run.
A very large JSON stdout can exceed the configured buffer and be truncated, which reads as a parse failure rather than a size problem.

risks.text: Callers must pass the repo root they intend the engine to operate on; an omitted root silently pins the child to the host process cwd instead of the sandbox.

patterns: A single contact surface mirrors the black-box CLI spawn pattern the engine's own tests use.
The pure command constructor is separated from the spawn so root-pinning is testable without an engine build.
invariants: The boundary is file-in, JSON-out: repovine never runs the agent itself.
validateResult maps the engine's validity field onto the schemaValid flag the graph node expects.
annotation.integrationPoints: Locates the engine through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/find-up; consumed by the graph nodes, the workers, and the orient path in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/repovine-process.
annotation.dataFlow: harness call -> buildCliCommand pins cwd and workspace root -> spawn the repovine CLI -> JSON parse -> validation, compliance, brief or session-quality consumer.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_CLI: Overrides discovery of the built repovine entrypoint

annotation.summary: Resolves the active role catalog for a resolved target, once per entrypoint after the target is prepared. In sandbox mode it initializes the bundled catalog. In attach mode it reads the repository's role source from the launch baseline revision rather than the working tree, because the worktree is agent-writable and a working-tree read would let one episode's agent edit the system prompt of the next.

keyExports.initCatalogForTarget: Initializes and returns the role catalog for a target, reading the project role source from the launch baseline when attached.

assumptions: Roles are a property of the launch: changing them means committing and preparing a new launch, not editing files in the running workspace.
A target that has not opted into project roles falls back to the bundled specialist roles, and that fallback is logged rather than silent.
The catalog is initialized once per entrypoint; later callers read the catalog that this call established.

sideEffects.description: invokes the engine CLI to read the project role source at the baseline revision
initializes the process-level role catalog
logs the resolved catalog and any per-role advisories

risks: A repository that opted into project roles but ships an invalid source aborts startup by design, so a malformed brief stops the harness rather than letting it run on the bundled fallback.

The distinction between not configured and invalid is what decides between falling back and aborting, so a config change that makes the section unreadable rather than absent turns a silent fallback into a hard startup failure.
Per-role advisories are logged and not enforced, so a role owning paths excluded from the scan still starts normally.
patterns: Fail loud on an invalid opt-in, fall back quietly on no opt-in: the two cases are deliberately not treated alike.
invariants: In attach mode the role source is read from the launch baseline revision, never from the agent-writable working tree.
An invalid role source in attach mode raises rather than degrading to the bundled roles.
annotation.integrationPoints: Calls the engine wrapper mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/repovine to read the role source, installs the catalog through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/agents, takes the baseline reference from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/attach-guard, and logs through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/log.
annotation.dataFlow: resolved target -> sandbox: bundled catalog; attach: role source read at the baseline revision -> configured source installs the project catalog, an absent section falls back, an invalid one raises.

annotation.summary: The orchestrator-run runtime check: discovers package directories under the workspace, installs dependencies where node_modules is missing, then runs the configured build and test commands with a scrubbed environment. Classifies failures, derives the scopes a repair sub-agent should touch, and builds its task from a bounded log tail. Annotation sync is gated on this check passing, and attach mode forces the whole check off.

keyExports.buildRuntimeCheckFixTask: Builds the write-only repair task text from the failure and its blockers, with canned guidance for the two recognized failure shapes.
keyExports.canAttemptRuntimeCheckFix: Whether another repair attempt is permitted for that command under the budget.
keyExports.deriveRuntimeCheckFixScopes: Scopes for the repair sub-agent, widened to root+backend+frontend for a missing test script.
keyExports.deriveScopeFromRuntimeLog: Infers which scopes (backend/frontend/infra/.) a failure touches from the log text.
keyExports.discoverPackageDirs: Walks the workspace for package.json directories, bounded by depth and a skip list.
keyExports.failedRuntimeCheckCommand: The failed command string, used as the repair-attempt budget key.
keyExports.formatRuntimeCheckSummary: Formats the check summary for the channel reply.
keyExports.isExpressParamsTypeFailure: True when the failure is the known Express req.params string|string[] TS2345 error.
keyExports.isMissingTestScriptFailure: True when the failure is only an absent npm test script.
keyExports.recordRuntimeCheckFixAttempt: Increments the per-command fix counter in place.
keyExports.runRuntimeCheck: Installs dependencies and runs the check commands; returns a skipped result when the gate is off or no package.json exists.
keyExports.runtimeAcceptedOf: True when the check outcome is acceptable for the run (a pass, or an honest optional skip).
keyExports.runtimeCheckBlockers: Blocker lines derived from a failed check.
keyExports.runtimeCheckCommands: The ordered command list from configuration (HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_CMDS/_CMD, else the npm build+test default).
keyExports.runtimeCheckEnabled: The single on/off gate; false in attach mode regardless of the explicit env setting.
keyExports.runtimeCheckFixAttemptsForCommand: Attempts already spent on a failing command (Map or plain-object accumulator).
keyExports.runtimeCheckFixEnabled: Whether the repair loop is allowed (HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_FIX != '0').
keyExports.runtimeCheckFixMaxAttempts: Upper bound on repair attempts per failing command (HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_FIX_MAX, default 2).
keyExports.runtimeCheckOverriddenByAttach: True when an explicit enable was overridden off by attach, so ingress can report it rather than swallow it.
keyExports.runtimeCheckPassed: True when the check completed without a failing command (also true for a skipped or missing result).
keyExports.runtimeCheckShortLabel: Short status label for the reply.
keyExports.runtimeFailureLogTail: Bounded, de-duplicated failure tail selected around error lines, segment-aware for monorepo builds.
keyExports.runtimeRequired: Enabled and at least one package.json exists under the workspace.
keyExports.runtimeStatusOf: Tri-state status of a result against whether runtime was required: passed/failed/skipped.

assumptions: Dependency installs run with --ignore-scripts and only in package directories that lack node_modules.
Repair attempts are counted per failing command rather than per run, so one flaky command cannot exhaust the whole budget.
The repair prompt is built from a bounded log tail rather than the full output.

runtimeCheckEnv() scrubs process.env to an allowlist plus HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_*/NPM_CONFIG_* prefixes, dropping anything matching the secret-name pattern and any proxy var carrying embedded credentials.

sideEffects.description: discovers package directories under the workspace root by probing for package.json and walking directories, bounded by depth and a skip list; also probes for node_modules per package
runs npm install --ignore-scripts and operator-configured check commands via spawnSync in the sandbox, with a per-command timeout
logs install/check progress lines via lib/log.mjs when GRAPH_VERBOSE is not '0'

risks: Check commands are operator-configured and run in the sandbox, so a long-running or side-effecting command affects the workspace.
The repair prompt relies on a bounded log tail, so a very verbose failure can push the root cause out of the excerpt.

risks.text: Callers must distinguish a skipped check from a passing one; in attach mode the gate is forced off, and reading skipped as success reports a verified run that never built or tested anything.

invariants: Attach mode forces the check off: a fresh worktree has no node_modules, so the install would hit the locked egress and fail correct work at the goal gate.
An explicit HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK=1 under attach is reported once at ingress rather than silently ignored.
runRuntimeCheck runs once at repo root when repoRoot itself has package.json, otherwise once per nested package directory.
annotation.integrationPoints: Invoked for the single-agent path by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/nodes and for the post-review repair loop by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/multi; the check status is recorded through the harness telemetry for the client surfaces.
annotation.dataFlow: workspace root -> discoverPackageDirs -> dependency installs (skipping dirs with node_modules) -> configured check commands run per root-or-package dir -> result classified and log-tailed -> gating in the graph plus a repair task when the fix loop is enabled.

envDependencies.GRAPH_VERBOSE: Verbose runtime-check logging (default on, off when '0')
envDependencies.HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK: Disables the runtime check when set to 0
envDependencies.HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_CMDS: Ordered command list separated by semicolons or newlines
envDependencies.HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_FIX: Disables the repair sub-agent loop when set to 0
envDependencies.HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_FIX_MAX: Upper bound on repair attempts per failing command
envDependencies.HARNESS_RUNTIME_CHECK_LOG_TAIL: Number of log lines kept in a failure tail
envDependencies.HARNESS_TARGET_MODE: Attach mode forces the runtime check off

annotation.summary: Observes and reaps the processes, listening ports and Docker containers a worker run leaves behind in the sandbox. Attribution is by sandbox path through /proc on Linux (a working directory under the repo root, or an argv that references it) and degrades to a no-op elsewhere. Snapshot before a run, reconcile after it, and sweep everything on reset.

keyExports.harnessReapEnabled: Whether reaping is active; currently always true, so reaping is unconditional.
keyExports.reapAll: Sweeps every sandbox-attributable process and compose resource, used on reset.
keyExports.reconcile: Diffs a pre-run snapshot against the current state, logs what was left behind, and optionally reaps it.
keyExports.snapshot: Captures the attributable processes, listening ports and containers for the sandbox root.

assumptions: Attribution is by sandbox path on two channels: processes and listening ports through /proc, which is Linux-only and degrades to a no-op elsewhere; Docker containers by the compose working-directory label, which is live on every platform.

Containers are torn down semantically with a compose down first, then a forced removal of container ids new since the baseline. Reset brings the sandbox's compose project down with its volumes regardless of platform.
The harness never reaps its own process, nor any process holding a controlling terminal, which is what keeps an operator's shell safe.

sideEffects.description: reads /proc entries and compose files to attribute processes, ports and containers to the sandbox
runs docker and socket-listing commands and sends signals when reaping

risks: Attribution is heuristic, so a mis-attributed process can be killed or a genuine leftover missed.
reconcile never throws: a failed teardown is reported rather than surfaced as a run failure.

risks.text: Callers must take the snapshot before starting the worker; reconciling against a snapshot captured afterwards attributes nothing and silently leaves the sandbox dirty.

patterns: Attribution by sandbox path rather than by process bookkeeping, so a process that escapes the harness's own records is still recognized.
invariants: The harness never reaps its own process id.
A process with a controlling terminal is never reaped.
Container teardown removes only ids that appeared after the baseline snapshot.
annotation.integrationPoints: Logs through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/log; snapshot and reconcile bracket each sub-agent run in the graph, and reapAll runs on reset.
annotation.stateShape: A snapshot holds the attributable processes keyed by pid, the listening ports keyed by port, and the set of container ids; reconcile returns what is still running and what was reaped.
annotation.dataFlow: sub-agent run: snapshot before → worker executes → reconcile after, optionally reaping; reset: reapAll followed by the sandbox clear.

envDependencies.GRAPH_VERBOSE: Set to 0 to silence reaper log lines, which are verbose by default

annotation.summary: The target contract: resolves whether the harness runs against a disposable sandbox or an attached workspace, maps that mode onto a capability policy, prepares the target, and resets it. Sandbox mode seeds repovine stubs and initializes git; attach mode only validates what it can prove from inside the container and never writes stubs or initializes git.

keyExports.ATTACH_RESET_DISABLED: The failure code used when the baseline is missing and by the policy-driven refusal.
keyExports.CSQ_CALIBRATION: Context-session quality calibration values for the target.
keyExports.clearWorkspaceContents: Removes the children of the workspace while keeping the directory itself, which is what a bind mount requires.
keyExports.ensureTarget: Sandbox: creates and seeds the workspace. Attach: validation only.
keyExports.resetTarget: Sandbox: wipes the workspace. Attach: restores the launcher-pinned baseline and fails loud when that baseline tag is absent.
keyExports.resolveTargetFromEnv: Turns the environment into {mode, repoRoot}; fails loud on an unknown mode, a missing attach root, a root that is not the pinned mount point, or a conflicting workspace-root override.
keyExports.targetPolicy: Pure mode-to-capability map returning whether reset and git operations are allowed.
keyExports.validateAttachedWorkspace: In-container checks: the repovine files, the git pointer bytes plus a write probe that must fail, a writable state git dir with a resolvable HEAD, and the runtime mounts.

assumptions: resolveTargetFromEnv reads mode/repo-root/root-override through an injected env object (default process.env) rather than direct process.env.X property access, so only REPOVINE_IN_DOCKER is graph-detected as a literal env reference; HARNESS_TARGET_MODE, HARNESS_REPO_ROOT and REPOVINE_ROOT are equally real inputs read the same indirect way.
Host-side worktree registration and the disposable-repo baseline are established by the attach launcher script, not here.

sideEffects.description: sandbox mode only: seeds repovine stubs and the harness home, initializes git, and wipes workspace contents on reset; an attach reset discards uncommitted working-tree state through git plumbing
runs git plumbing against the workspace

risks.text: validateAttachedWorkspace proves only what is observable inside the container; callers must not read a passing result as evidence about the host's git state.

risks: An attach reset without the launcher-pinned baseline tag fails loud rather than falling back to a wipe, so a mis-provisioned attach target refuses to reset instead of destroying the operator's tree.
patterns: Capability is derived from mode alone: targetPolicy takes no environment input, so no variable can widen what a mode is allowed to do.
The harness starts from an empty application and lets workers create the project on demand.
invariants: Attach never writes repovine stubs and never initializes git: ensureTarget in attach mode is validation only.
Under docker attach the repo root is pinned to the mount point, the git pointer is byte-compared against the expected content, and the write probe must fail, proving a read-only mount.
targetPolicy is pure: no environment input reaches the capability decision.
An attach reset moves only the working tree and HEAD; the run branches and the disposable object database survive.
Sandbox seed and reset behaviour is byte-identical to the pre-refactor implementation, held by characterization tests.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates git primitives and the repository guard to mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/worktree and mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/attach-guard; the resolved target is consumed at graph ingress and pins the workspace root for the engine wrapper.
annotation.dataFlow: environment → resolveTargetFromEnv → {mode, repoRoot} → targetPolicy for capabilities → ensureTarget prepares or validates → workers run with the workspace as their working directory → resetTarget on reset.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_IN_DOCKER: Marks the in-container path that enforces the mount pin and the read-only probe (only literal process.env access the graph detects here; HARNESS_TARGET_MODE/HARNESS_REPO_ROOT/REPOVINE_ROOT are read indirectly, see assumptions)

annotation.summary: Recovers the user's original request from a harness task object. The ingress path prepends a '## Prior harness run' preamble to the task text for continuity; extractUserTask returns the explicit userTask field when present, otherwise the task body with that preamble stripped, so orient, claims extraction, and CLI queries see the request rather than the run history.

keyExports.extractUserTask: Returns the task's userTask field, else the task body with the prior-run preamble removed.
keyExports.stripPriorRunBlock: Removes the '## Prior harness run' marker block and the blank-line-separated preamble that follows it.

assumptions: The prior-run marker block is injected at ingress and must be stripped before orient, claims, and CLI query use the text.
An explicit userTask field takes precedence over the raw task string.
The preamble ends at the first blank-line boundary after the marker.
risks: A change to the prior-run marker wording at ingress leaves the preamble unstripped, so run history leaks into orient and claim extraction as if it were the user's request.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by the harness orient/claims path in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/claims and the graph ingress node; the preamble it strips is produced by mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/harness-run.
annotation.dataFlow: task object → extractUserTask → stripPriorRunBlock → clean request text for orient, claims, and CLI query.

annotation.summary: Operator-facing run telemetry for the demo: a rolling current-run document plus an append-only event log under the active area, archived per run. Events are appended as JSONL and folded into the running snapshot by a reducer; the finished run gets a summary and is archived. Run metadata records the workspace path as the process sees it, so host source paths never enter telemetry.

keyExports.CURRENT_RUN_FILE: Basename of the rolling current-run document.
keyExports.EVENTS_FILE: Basename of the append-only event log.
keyExports.TELEMETRY_SCHEMA_VERSION: Schema version stamped on the current-run document.
keyExports.buildRepovineProcessSummary: Summarizes the orient trail, the claims and the implement sub-agent outcomes into the finished run's plan field.
keyExports.compactRunTelemetry: Client-safe compact projection with per-sub-agent entries and the slowest sub-agent.
keyExports.finishRunTelemetry: Finalizes the status, writes the run summary, archives the active run and clears the live telemetry.
keyExports.formatCurrentRunStatus: Multi-line progress view for the status endpoints.
keyExports.formatTelemetrySummary: Human summary line: duration, tokens and cost, MCP counts, retries.
keyExports.formatUsageMetrics: Formats token and cost figures for display.
keyExports.readCurrentRun: Reads the live current-run document, falling back to the latest archived summary when no run is live.
keyExports.recordRunEvent: Appends an event to the log and merges it into the current-run snapshot.
keyExports.runSucceeded: Whether a finished run's state counts as successful.
keyExports.startRunTelemetry: Creates the current-run document with the run's task, provider, mode and target identity.

assumptions: The schema uses sub-agent terminology throughout, in both the snapshot fields and the event names; the legacy leaf-keyed fields are gone.
Live state lives under the active area and is moved to the archive by the finish path.
This is operator and dev-session feedback only; the agent protocol run result is a separate contract and is unaffected by anything here.

sideEffects.description: writes the current-run document, appends the event log, and writes the run summary
reads the live current-run document or the latest archived summary
durations and elapsed figures come from wall-clock timestamps

risks: Consumers written against the older leaf-keyed schema will not find those fields; the snapshot exposes sub-agent terminology throughout.

The current-run document is a bounded snapshot: it grows with the number of sub-agents and the fixed phase vocabulary, not with the event count. Per-event history lives only in the separate append-only log, which the snapshot never folds back in.
patterns: An append-only event log folded by a reducer into a rolling snapshot, so the log stays the record and the snapshot stays derived.
Phase and sub-agent lifecycles are tracked as arrays on the run rather than as ad-hoc fields.
invariants: Run-level usage and MCP totals are recomputed from the per-sub-agent entries when no run-level totals were recorded.
Formatting helpers tolerate missing provider cost fields rather than failing.
Telemetry never alters the agent protocol validation semantics.
annotation.integrationPoints: Resolves every path and performs the archive through mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/harness-paths, and folds in the token and MCP rollups from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/usage and mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/mcp-telemetry. The graph nodes, the run orchestrator and the channel adapters call in to start, record and finish runs.
annotation.dataFlow: startRunTelemetry writes the current-run document → recordRunEvent appends events and updates the snapshot → finishRunTelemetry writes the summary and archives the run → formatters serve the status surfaces.

annotation.summary: Worker selection for the graph path. One graph, with the provider as the variable: resolveProvider picks claude or local from the environment, isSupportedProvider lets ingress fail fast on an unknown id, and getWorker dynamically imports the matching adapter so an unused SDK never loads. Every adapter implements the same runAgent seam.

keyExports.DEFAULT_PROVIDER: The provider used when none is configured (claude).
keyExports.PROVIDERS: The supported provider ids: claude and local.
keyExports.getWorker: Dynamically imports the adapter module for a provider.
keyExports.isSupportedProvider: True only when auth knows the provider and it is in the supported list; used by ingress to fail fast.
keyExports.resolveProvider: Normalizes the provider from an argument or the environment, falling back to the default.

assumptions: Auth is resolved once in the shared credential resolver; adapters never duplicate it.
Adapters are imported lazily so an unused provider SDK is never loaded into the process.
Every adapter exposes the same async runAgent(task, assignment, repoRoot, opts) seam, which is what keeps the graph provider-agnostic.

sideEffects.description: dynamically imports the provider adapter module
reads the provider selection from the environment

risks: getWorker falls through to the claude adapter for any unrecognized id, so a provider that slipped past isSupportedProvider silently runs on Claude rather than failing.
patterns: One graph with a variable provider: the orchestrator is unchanged across providers.
Fail fast at ingress rather than at the first SDK call.
invariants: isSupportedProvider requires both that auth knows the provider and that it is in the supported list.
The default branch of getWorker routes to the claude adapter.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by the worker dispatch node in mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/graph/nodes; credentials come from mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/workers/auth, which is the single place a provider's credential contract is declared.
annotation.dataFlow: graph worker dispatch → resolveProvider → getWorker dynamic import → adapter.runAgent through the shared seam.

envDependencies.LLM_PROVIDER: Selects the claude or local worker adapter; defaults to claude

annotation.summary: The read-only question path. It runs a provider session limited to reading: the three file-reading built-ins plus the non-mutating engine tools, with writes and command execution refused by the permission callback rather than merely discouraged by the prompt. It answers questions about the repository and returns text, never a run result.

keyExports.ASK_ALLOWED_TOOLS: The read-only allow-list: file read, glob and grep plus the non-mutating engine tools.
keyExports.ASK_DISALLOWED_TOOLS: The hard block-list: the write and execute built-ins plus the mutating engine tools.
keyExports.askReadOnlyGate: The permission callback: allows a tool only when it is on the allow-list and denies everything else with an explanation.
keyExports.runAsk: Runs the session and returns the answer text with the context session id, or a refusal carrying the reason.
