One is a facade that delegates to a node carrying a consumer obligation without naming it, so an agent inspecting the facade never learns the obligation exists. The other is an annotation naming a node the graph cannot deliver, so the pointer reads as authoritative but leads nowhere. Both are advisory findings reported with counts and a bounded sample.

keyExports.CARRIER_LINK_DEP_GUARD_DEPTH: How far the forward closure walks when checking deliverability.
keyExports.CARRIER_LINK_GAP_SAMPLE_LIMIT: How many concrete pairs are returned.
keyExports.CarrierLinkGapKind: The two kinds: an unnamed delegation, and a named target that cannot be delivered.
keyExports.CarrierLinkGapSample: One concrete pair: the kind, the importer and the target.
keyExports.CarrierLinkGaps: The reported shape: both counts, the suppressed count and the sample.
keyExports.EMPTY_CARRIER_LINK_GAPS: The zero result, used when the graph cannot support the analysis.
keyExports.NODE_ID_TOKEN_RE: The token pattern for node ids appearing in prose.
keyExports.computeCarrierLinkGaps: Scans importers against consumer-risk targets and returns both gap counts, the suppressed count, and a sorted sample.
keyExports.nodeInValidateScope: Decides whether a node falls inside the scope hints a validation run was given.
keyExports.parseIntegrationPointTargets: Pulls node ids out of annotation prose, optionally keeping only those the graph knows.

assumptions: An unnamed delegation is reported only for a runtime two-hop shape: an intermediate that is neither the importer nor the target, reached by value imports on both hops. A type-only import is erased at build time and cannot delegate behavior.

Chains longer than two hops are deliberately not reported, because every hop already carries the structural flag at its own boundary; a direct one-hop import is likewise excluded since the graph edge already carries it.
An importer inside the target's own equivalence set is skipped, which is what keeps an import cycle from reporting a node as delegating to itself.
Suppression is decided by the caller, which validates it against the target's current risk state; this module only honours the set it is handed and reports how many it excluded.

What counts as a runtime import edge is taken from the shared predicate in mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/heuristics rather than restated here, so this advisory and the architecture analysis cannot disagree about the same edge.
risks: The analysis needs the graph's import edge maps and returns an empty result without them, so a graph built without them reports no gaps at all rather than reporting that it could not look.
Node ids are recovered from prose by pattern match, so an id written inside an unrelated sentence counts as a pointer while a target described only in words does not.
The sample is capped, so a scope with many gaps shows the same small set until those are fixed and the counts are the only signal of the true size.
patterns: Two failure modes, one pass: an obligation that is reachable but unnamed, and a name that is written but unreachable.
Advisory rather than blocking: the result is counts and examples for a human or agent to review, not a gate.
The runtime-edge test is shared with the analysis layer rather than duplicated, so a change to what counts as a runtime edge lands in one place.
invariants: A direct one-hop import is never reported as a missing link.
A node is never reported as delegating to itself.
Suppressed targets are excluded from the search and counted separately rather than silently dropped.
The sample is deterministically ordered before it is truncated.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by the annotation health scan in mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance and by the validation tool under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools; the same prose parser backs pointer resolution in mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs; risk-scope predicates come from mod:repovine/src/annotations/format, graph traversal from mod:repovine/src/graph, and the runtime-import predicate from mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/heuristics.
annotation.dataFlow: graph plus stored annotations → consumer-risk targets, minus the suppressed set → per importer, the delegation test and the named-pointer deliverability check → counts and a bounded sorted sample.

annotation.summary: Workspace-local review state for carrier-link advisories. Records which consumer-risk targets a reviewer decided are not gaps, stamped with a hash of the target's consumer-risk texts at the moment of the decision, so a target whose risks later change re-surfaces instead of staying silently suppressed. The state lives under the engine cache directory and is not committed, so triage does not travel with a clone.

keyExports.CARRIER_REVIEW_FILENAME: Basename of the review state file inside the engine cache directory.
keyExports.CarrierReviewEntry: One decision: the risk hash at decision time, the decision timestamp, and an optional reason.
keyExports.CarrierReviewFile: The file shape: a version and the reviewed targets keyed by node id.
keyExports.carrierReviewFilePath: Absolute path of the review file for a repo root.
keyExports.carrierTargetRiskHash: The invalidation key: a truncated sha256 over the target's sorted consumer-scoped risk texts.
keyExports.mergeCarrierReviewEntries: Merges new decisions into the existing state and persists it.
keyExports.readCarrierReviewFile: Reads the state, returning an empty result for a missing, corrupt or wrong-version file.
keyExports.readValidSuppressedTargets: The set of targets still suppressed, keeping only those whose current risk hash matches the recorded one.

assumptions: Only consumer-scoped risk texts feed the hash, sorted first, so re-ordering the risks does not invalidate a decision while changing their wording does.
The state is deliberately workspace-local rather than committed: a suppression is one reviewer's judgement about one checkout, not a repository fact.
The same hash function is used both when a decision is stamped and when it is checked, which is what keeps the two from drifting apart.

sideEffects.description: reads the review state file from the engine cache directory
writes the review state atomically

risks: Reading fails open toward visibility: a missing, corrupt or wrong-version file suppresses nothing, so every reviewed pair re-surfaces rather than a damaged file silently hiding advisories.

Because the hash covers only consumer-scoped risks, editing a target's local risks leaves an existing suppression in force, which is intended but means the decision is narrower than 'this annotation was reviewed'.
The state sits in the ignored cache directory, so clearing that directory discards every review decision with no other copy.
patterns: A content hash as the invalidation key, so a suppression expires by the target changing rather than by a timestamp or a manual sweep.
invariants: A suppression survives only while the recorded hash equals the target's current consumer-risk hash.
The stamping path and the checking path compute the hash through this one function.
annotation.integrationPoints: Resolves its location through mod:repovine/src/paths, writes through mod:repovine/src/fs/atomic, and normalizes risks through mod:repovine/src/annotations/format. The decisions it stores are produced by the advisory decline tool and consulted when carrier-link gaps are validated.
annotation.dataFlow: reviewer declines a target → the target's consumer risks are hashed → the decision is merged into the review file → later validation reads it back and keeps only the entries whose hash still matches.

annotation.summary: Cross-process annotation-file lock with O_EXCL acquisition, PID ownership/liveness checks, serialized atomic stale takeover, orphan-claim recovery, typed 5s timeout, and sync/async critical-section wrappers.

keyExports.AnnotationFileLockTimeoutError: Typed failure raised when ownership cannot be acquired before the wait deadline.
keyExports.withAnnotationFileLockAsync: Runs an async callback only after verified lock ownership and releases only the caller's lock.
keyExports.withAnnotationFileLockSync: Runs a sync callback only after verified lock ownership and releases only the caller's lock.

assumptions: Lock file content is the ownership token and must equal process.pid before entry, takeover success, or release.
Stale threshold assumes a crashed writer can leave a lock without unlinking it.

sideEffects.description: Creates and deletes .lock files beside annotations JSON
Atomics.wait / setTimeout backoff while waiting for lock

risks: NFS or network filesystems may weaken O_EXCL and atomic rename semantics.
patterns: Cross-process lock with verified PID ownership and atomic stale-lock takeover.
invariants: Lock file lives beside repovine.annots.json.
The critical section never runs without verified ownership.
Deadline expiry throws without deleting a live foreign lock.
Release removes the lock only while its content still equals process.pid.
annotation.integrationPoints: AnnotationStore read/write paths acquire cross-process lock on repovine.annots.json.
annotation.stateShape: Exclusive file lock handle held for duration of read-modify-write on repovine.annots.json; no persistent in-memory state beyond lock fd.
annotation.dataFlow: exclusive create → verify own PID → read/write callback → ownership-checked release; stale owner → PID temp file → atomic rename → ownership re-check.

annotation.summary: Zod schemas and canonical serialization for repovine.annots.json: AnnotationContentSchema (with the sideEffects min(1) guard that rejects empty arrays and propagationSlice) and StoredAnnotationSchema, risk-scope helpers (normalizeRisks/hasConsumerScopedRisk/hasBoundaryScopedRisk + the consumerRiskMarkingHints authoring nudge), the ANNOTATABLE vs ANNOTATION_EXEMPT NodeType partition (law-enforced), hydrate-with-quarantine, and deterministic canonicalAnnotation ordering for merge diffs (toDiskAnnotation strips default pass=1/schemaVersion=1).

keyExports.ANNOTATABLE_NODE_TYPES: module, export-symbol, domain, runtime-resource, template — satisfies NodeType.
keyExports.AnnotationContentSchema: Zod schema incl. propagationSlice and SideEffectSchema min(1) guard.
keyExports.hasBoundaryScopedRisk: True when any risk has scope boundary.
keyExports.hasConsumerScopedRisk: True when any risk has scope consumer.
keyExports.hydrateAnnotationMap: Splits valid data vs quarantine vs AnnotationHydrationError list.
keyExports.normalizeRisks: Coerces RiskEntry[] to NormalizedRisk[] with default scope local.
keyExports.serializeAnnotationFileFromRaw: Pretty JSON with sorted node ids and stripped defaults.

assumptions: ANNOTATABLE_NODE_TYPES and ANNOTATION_EXEMPT_NODE_TYPES partition NODE_TYPES (enforced in test/laws/annotatable-surface.test.ts).
inferAnnotationNodeType maps mod:/infra:→module, export:→export-symbol, resource:→runtime-resource.
sideEffects rejects empty arrays — omit field or use [{kind:pure}].
risks: Manual JSON edits outside schema land in quarantine until merge/validate repair.
patterns: Invalid hydrate results quarantine raw value for merge_annotations review.
DISK_ANNOTATION_KEY_ORDER omits nodeId/nodeType (map key is node id).
invariants: propagationSlice {anchor, path, reviewedAt} validated when present.
canonicalAnnotation sorts content fields and importBaseline keys for merge diffs.
toDiskAnnotation omits default pass=1 and schemaVersion=1 on disk.
annotation.integrationPoints: annotations/store load/save; write_annotation validation; merge_annotations; validate_annotations; imports mod:repovine/src/annotations/side-effect-vocab SideEffectSchema.
annotation.dataFlow: repovine.annots.json → parseAnnotationFile → hydrateAnnotationMap (StoredAnnotationSchema + canonical sort) → in-memory map; serializeAnnotationFileFromRaw writes sorted disk form via toDiskAnnotation.

annotation.summary: The on-disk lifecycle of the annotation file: create it, merge it after a version-control conflict, normalize it to canonical form, and report its health. A merge prefers exact sides from the index over reconstructed ones, backs up whatever it replaces, and refuses guesses worse than stopping.

keyExports.ensureEmptyAnnotationsFile: Create empty file for repo without one.
keyExports.getAnnotationMergeStatus: Pre-flight: does file exist, parse OK, carry markers, index unmerged, next actions.
keyExports.mergeAnnotationFiles: Three-way field-level merge with audit trail.
keyExports.mergeAnnotationsOnDisk: Merge conflicted file under lock from index stages (preferred) or markers, reporting base source and backup path.
keyExports.normalizeAnnotationsFile: Rewrite in canonical form without merging.
keyExports.validateAnnotationHealth: Full health report: staleness, orphans, merge review, carrier gaps, advisory scope candidates.

assumptions: Merge base from index when genuinely unmerged; from reconstructed sections of conflicted file otherwise.
Ambient version-control env vars stripped from every child process.
Base compared against but never taken as output side; pass/schema version taken as maximum.
Missing base parsed leniently and raises warning.

sideEffects.description: reads annotation file and backups
writes merged/normalized files under lock, snapshots replaced bytes
runs version-control commands with env vars removed

risks.text: Caller resolving conflict must not rely on hand-edits to conflicted file: index-stage merge recomputes from pre-merge blobs.
Caller must hand removed node list to live store before refresh, or store's never-drop restores exactly those nodes.

patterns: Prefer exact source, fall back to approximate, always say which.
invariants: Each resolved field records which side was chosen and why.
Array fields union and deduplicate.
Marker-free file with unmerged index entry never silently normalized.
annotation.integrationPoints: MCP merge/validation/status tools; annotations/store; annotations/file-lock, annotations/backup, annotations/format.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root → annotation path → repository identity check → index stages, or marker sides including a reconstructed base → lenient base parse → field-level three-way merge → backup of replaced bytes → canonical serialization under lock → report, with removed nodes handed to the live store before the next refresh.

annotation.summary: Git merge conflict review markers in annotations: applyMergeReviewHints embeds merge-review: field patterns and ours/theirs assumption prefixes after scalar conflicts; clearMergeReviewHints strips them once resolved via write_annotation.

keyExports.clearMergeReviewHints: Removes review markers when field updated.
keyExports.listMergeReviewFields: Lists fields still carrying review hints.
keyExports.mergeReviewPatternForField: Stable pattern string per annotation field.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream types/format; merge-review helpers unchanged.
risks: Agents must rewrite final field content — hints are not authoritative merged text.
patterns: Git conflict markers in JSON trigger merge_annotations workflow.
invariants: Never hand-edit conflict markers in repovine.annots.json.
annotation.integrationPoints: merge_annotations MCP tool and git merge conflict resolution workflow in AGENTS.md.
annotation.dataFlow: conflict markers in JSON → parse ours/theirs assumptions → agent picks merged summary via write_annotation → validate_annotations.

annotation.summary: Classifies a node into one of ten kinds so annotation scoring and field guidance can be specific to what the node is rather than uniform. The classification is an ordered decision tree over the node type, the export shapes, the path and the semantic hints, falling through to a neutral kind when nothing is decisive.

keyExports.ModuleKind: The ten kinds, from type-only declarations through interface, handler, adapter and service shapes to the aggregate node types.
keyExports.inferModuleKind: Returns the kind for a graph node, a module record, or both.
keyExports.recommendedFieldsForKind: The fields an annotation of that kind is expected to carry.

assumptions: The order of the checks is the classification: the first that matches wins, so moving a check changes what a module is called.
Node-type kinds are settled first because they are facts rather than guesses.
Infrastructure is recognized by identifier prefix rather than by module record, because those live outside the module index and the record is usually absent.
Type-only modules are decided early, since they need only a shape description and nothing about behaviour.
The backend check runs before the interface checks, so a weak frontend signal such as an imported client library does not turn a server module into an interface one.

Interface classification is gated on the owning language plugin declaring that it produces interface surfaces, so a module from a backend-only language is never called one even when its path happens to match.

The built-in plugins are registered by importing the bootstrap for its side effect, so this works outside a build; the import is cheap because it registers plain descriptors and leaves the heavy parser lazy.

sideEffects.description: imports the source-plugin bootstrap so plugin capabilities can be resolved

risks: A module whose plugin cannot be determined is treated as capable of interface surfaces, which preserves the historical default but means a new backend-only language mislabels its modules until its plugin is resolvable here.
Path tokens are a fixed vocabulary, so a repository using different folder names classifies everything as neutral and receives generic field guidance rather than a warning that classification failed.
The kind decides which fields are expected, so a misclassification produces a confident but wrong checklist — an annotation can score well against the wrong standard.
patterns: Facts before guesses: node type, then identifier prefix, then export shape, then heuristics over path and hints.
The detection helpers are shared with the architecture analysis rather than duplicated, so both agree on what a frontend surface or a request handler looks like.
annotation.flowDescription: inferModuleKind applies a ordered decision tree: fixed kinds for domain/service/infra nodes → types-only → backend-context gate → ui heuristics → api-handler → adapter → service-mgr → generic fallback.
invariants: Every input yields a kind; the neutral one is the fallback rather than a failure.

The per-kind field list is one input to the expected-field set. The scoring pass adds demands from module facts — env vars pull in side effects and env dependencies, size pulls in risks, a wide export surface pulls in integration points — and it decides data flow by its own size-and-kind rule that ignores the list. The score itself is kind-independent: each populated field carries a fixed weight whatever the kind, and a summary is always required.
A plugin without interface surfaces never yields the interface kind.
annotation.integrationPoints: The kind and its field list are consumed by the annotation quality scoring in mod:repovine/src/annotations/store; the shared detection helpers come from mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/heuristics; plugin capabilities are resolved through mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/registry after mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/bootstrap registers the built-ins.
annotation.dataFlow: graph node or module record → fixed kinds by node type and identifier prefix → export-shape check → backend, interface, handler, adapter and service heuristics in order → kind → the expected field list for that kind.

annotation.summary: Pure annotation-v2 propagation engine for entrypoint-bounded derived stale, dependency cones, contract hubs, previews, and audit slices; per-call module/content-hash maps keep hot-path lookups linear.

keyExports.buildPropagationSlice: Shortest importer chain from anchor module to nearest entrypoint for write_annotation audit.
keyExports.collectEntrypointRoots: Collect moduleId roots from interpreter EntrypointFragment list.
keyExports.computeDepCone: BFS downward from entrypoints following imports outEdges.
keyExports.computeEntrypointBoundedDerived: Entrypoint-bounded derived-stale set; hubModules widen importers in depCone.
keyExports.computePropagationPreview: Read-only blast preview { hard, derived, domains, entrypoints } for a changed module.
keyExports.reachesEntrypoint: Consumer-direction BFS via importer inEdges until an entrypoint module is hit.

assumptions: Entrypoint-bounded derived stale uses importBaseline snapshots on write_annotation.
Contract hubs and dep cones gate propagation preview scope.
PropagationConfig from mod:repovine/src/config controls domain roll-up hash policy.
risks: Missing entrypoints under-propagates narrow derived.
Hub list omission misses contract review on widely imported modules.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/annotations/store queue classification; mod:repovine/src/config propagation section; analyze_architecture entrypoint roots.
annotation.dataFlow: EntrypointFragment list → collectEntrypointRoots → computeDepCone → computeEntrypointBoundedDerived compares importBaseline vs graph; buildPropagationSlice records shortest importer chain for audit.

annotation.summary: Computes deterministic advisory candidates for plain/local annotation risks that look like consumer or boundary scope authoring opportunities.

keyExports.computeRiskScopeCandidates: Scans stored annotations plus graph/snapshot context, returns aggregate counts, reasons, samples, and optional paged items for candidate review.

assumptions: Only risks with effective local scope are considered; explicit consumer and boundary risks are skipped.
Path and integrationPoint matches are supporting cues only and cannot create a boundary candidate without a strong text cue.
risks: Regex cue rules are conservative but can still produce false positives; reviewers must inspect source before rewriting annotations.
Candidates are advisory-only and must not feed inspect_node investigate delivery or the boundary pre-edit index.
invariants: A single risk entry emits at most one candidate; boundary precedence wins overlap and total equals consumer plus boundary.
Candidate sorting stays deterministic: boundary first, then reason count descending, nodeId, and riskIndex.
annotation.integrationPoints: Uses normalizeRisks from mod:repovine/src/annotations/format and validate scope/integration token helpers from mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-links.
annotation.dataFlow: annotations.getAll plus graph/snapshot context -> local risk entries -> cue reason extraction -> sorted candidates -> validation aggregate or paged status view.

annotation.summary: Resolves content-hash fingerprints for runtime-resource (resource:) nodes: buildRuntimeResourceContentHashLookup groups every snapshot declaration per id and reduces each group to an order-independent set-hash; getResourceContentHashForServiceId aggregates the same way without a lookup; resolveServiceResourceContentHash falls back to graph RuntimeResourceNodeData.contentHash.

keyExports.buildRuntimeResourceContentHashLookup: Groups snapshot.infraModules declarations per makeRuntimeResourceId; reduces each group with the set-hash (single distinct hash returned verbatim).
keyExports.getParentInfraContentHash: InfraModuleInfo.contentHash for parent infra module id.
keyExports.getParentInfraModuleId: Parent infra module id via contains inEdge on resource: node.
keyExports.getResourceContentHashForServiceId: Collects all snapshot declarations matching makeRuntimeResourceId and reduces with the same set-hash; a provided lookup value wins.
keyExports.resolveServiceResourceContentHash: Primary fingerprint: snapshot set-hash, else graph node data.contentHash.

assumptions: Set-hash = sha256 over the deduped, sorted declaration hashes, sliced to 16 hex; a single distinct hash is returned verbatim, so single-declaration and identical-duplicate resources keep byte-stable fingerprints.
risks: Parser contentHash algorithm change marks all service annotations stale until rewrite.
Adding or removing a differing declaration of an id changes the set membership, re-staling that id's annotation once.
patterns: Ties runtime-resource annotation freshness to parsed IaC resource payload hashes; multi-declaration reduces to a sorted sha256 set-hash mirroring domain member hashing.
invariants: makeRuntimeResourceId must stay stable across refreshes for hash lookup.
Lookup and no-lookup paths reduce the identical universe (snapshot.infraModules), so a multi-declared id resolves to one order-independent value on every surface: write, inspect, queue, coverage.
Returns undefined when neither snapshot nor graph node carries contentHash.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/annotations/store service and domain roll-up content hash (hashDomainMembers consumes the set-hash); uses mod:repovine/src/graph/make-runtime-resource-id.
annotation.dataFlow: resource: serviceId → resolveServiceResourceContentHash → compared on refresh for service/runtime-resource annotation freshness; multi-declared ids converge to the set-hash regardless of infra file-scan order.

annotation.summary: Canonical vocabulary, Zod schema, and query helpers for the structured sideEffects array on annotations. Declares the closed SIDE_EFFECT_KINDS list with per-kind documentation, validates writes through SideEffectSchema, offers predicates for detectors (isPure, hasKind, hasSubtype, hasKindSubtype, hasPersistentEffect), and maps graph SemanticHints into kinds so a declared-pure module can be checked against detected effects.

keyExports.SIDE_EFFECT_KINDS: The closed list of eleven kinds (io-read, io-write, state-local, state-global, process, concurrency, time, subscribe, external, resource, pure); authoritative for detectors and the agent-facing docs.
keyExports.SideEffect: One entry: required kind plus optional subtype and description.
keyExports.SideEffectSchema: Zod schema for the array; rejects an empty sideEffects list.
keyExports.detectSideEffectKindsFromHints: Derives kinds from SemanticHints runtimeActions and effectImports; undefined when no reliable signal exists.
keyExports.hasKind: True when any entry matches the given kind.
keyExports.hasKindSubtype: True when any entry matches both kind and subtype.
keyExports.hasPersistentEffect: True when an entry is state-global, or io-write with a subtype other than stdout/stderr.
keyExports.hasSubtype: True when any entry carries the given subtype, compared case-insensitively.
keyExports.isPure: True when every entry declares kind pure.
keyExports.serializeSideEffect: Canonical kind:subtype:description string used for search token indexing.
keyExports.truncateSideEffect: Clips an entry's description to a maximum length.

assumptions: Eleven SideEffectKind values including the pure sentinel; subtype is diagnostic and not part of the closed enum.
detectSideEffectKindsFromHints returns undefined rather than an empty list when hints carry no reliable runtimeActions or effectImports.
Subtype comparisons are case-insensitive.
risks: hasPersistentEffect is narrower than 'not pure': external, resource, process and concurrency entries do not satisfy it, so a detector that means 'has any effect' must not reach for it.
Adding a kind requires updating the detectors, the agent-facing docs, and existing annotations that were written against the old list.
Over-mapping hints to kinds would false-flag legitimately pure client modules as privileged.

risks.text: Callers must declare the pure sentinel rather than an empty array: the annotation content schema refuses an empty sideEffects list, and an omitted field is treated as unknown rather than pure.

patterns: kind is the primary detector signal while subtype stays diagnostic, so detectors never branch on free text.
The pure sentinel separates an intentional zero-effect declaration from a field the author forgot.
invariants: sideEffects is never written as []: the field is omitted or declares [{kind: 'pure'}].
CONSOLE_WRITE_SUBTYPES limits the io-write exemption to stdout and stderr.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by write_annotation validation, mod:repovine/src/annotations/format, and the architecture detectors that classify privileged client-side effects; imports SemanticHints from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/types.
annotation.dataFlow: SemanticHints → detectSideEffectKindsFromHints → compared against the declared sideEffects in the annotation consistency axis.

annotation.summary: Core annotation persistence and queue engine: unified stale classification, quality/consistency scoring, importBaseline propagation, and domain rollups over repovine.annots.json. The store instance is reused across refreshes and survives state swaps.

keyExports.AnnotationStore: In-memory store: getQueue, set/delete, flush, reloadFromDisk({signal}) under cross-process lock, forgetDeletedOnDisk for external deletions.
keyExports.computeAnnotationQuality: 0–10 completeness by moduleKind recommendedFields + consistency check.
keyExports.isDerivedStaleModule: Propagation-stale when importBaseline differs from current graph.
keyExports.resolveDomainContentHash: Rolls up member hashes per domain stale policy.

assumptions: Same store reused across builds; fresh build re-reads disk.
Quarantined parse entries must not flush until merge resolves.
Hard consistency issues block refreshImportBaseline only when alone; annotation fields alongside it skip check.

sideEffects.description: reads/writes repovine.annots.json under cross-process file lock

risks.text: forgetDeletedOnDisk must be called before next flush or external deletions re-appear; external rollback of annots.json needs re-apply after server exit.

patterns: importBaseline captured on write; refreshImportBaseline clears propagation-stale.
invariants: Queue orders content-stale before propagation-stale, bottom-up by depth.
annotation.integrationPoints: fs/atomic (durable save), annotations/file-lock (cross-process lock), annotations/backup (snapshots), annotations/service-resource-hash (runtime-resource hashing).
annotation.stateShape: Map<nodeId, StoredAnnotation> with nodeType, contentHash, updatedAt, annotation object, optional mergeReview fields.
annotation.dataFlow: loadAsync → getQueue compares contentHashes / importBaselines → write merges annotation + refreshes baseline → debounced save chain → JSON via fs/atomic; refresh → reloadFromDisk(signal) merges disk into memory under lock: disk is the base, pending writes overlay it field-wise, keys we hold that disk lacks or has regressed below stay ours, our deletes apply.

annotation.summary: Core annotation schema: RiskEntry (plain or scoped), AnnotationContent (15+ optional fields including summary, keyExports, sideEffects, risks), and StoredAnnotation (nodeId, contentHash, importBaseline, pass/updatedAt). Re-exported by mod:repovine/src/types for compatibility.

keyExports.AnnotationContent: 15+ fields: summary, keyExports, assumptions, sideEffects, risks, patterns, flowDescription, invariants, extensionPoints, integrationPoints, stateShape, dataFlow, envDependencies, propagationSlice.
keyExports.CURRENT_ANNOTATION_SCHEMA_VERSION: Bump when adding optional fields to trigger stale backfill (currently 1).
keyExports.StoredAnnotation: Persisted memo: nodeId, nodeType, contentHash, pass, updatedAt, annotation, importBaseline (direct-import snapshot), schemaVersion.

assumptions: RiskEntry without explicit scope defaults to local scope.
importBaseline absent = no propagation-stale tracking (non-module node types).
StoredAnnotation importBaseline is always a snapshot taken at write time, never stale or edited.

risks.text: CURRENT_ANNOTATION_SCHEMA_VERSION bump requires coord with repovine.annots.json migration; stale-trigger logic in mod:repovine/src/annotations/store.

patterns: RiskEntry scope:consumer marks importer obligations; scope:boundary marks frozen surfaces.
AnnotationContent summary is REQUIRED; all other fields optional.
invariants: StoredAnnotation.nodeType ∈ {module, export-symbol, domain, runtime-resource, template}.
AnnotationContent.sideEffects: never write []—omit or use [{ kind: pure }].
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exported by mod:repovine/src/types (compat barrel); consumed by mod:repovine/src/annotations/store, mod:repovine/src/annotations/format, and annotation validation.
annotation.dataFlow: AnnotationContent is JSON-serialized to repovine.annots.json by StoredAnnotation wrapper; RiskEntry scope controls queue/boundary machinery.

annotation.summary: Engine-internal re-export facade for the @repovine/plugin-sdk fact types (ModuleInfo, PackageInfo, InfraResource, SemanticHints, Ui* hint shapes, IaC vocabulary, and known kind-metadata). Engine and MCP layers import through here so the SDK package stays the single source of truth for the fact layer. Third-party plugins import @repovine/plugin-sdk directly, not this facade.
assumptions: Pure type re-export: erases at compile time, adds no runtime edge.
Engine call sites reach these types through this facade or the src/types barrel; the graph model and node-view modules import the SDK package directly.
The set tracks the SDK's layer-1 fact exports, excluding ReExportInfo (TypeScript source plugin only) and the graph ontology (RepositoryGraph, NodeType, EdgeKind, Interpreter).

risks.text: Frozen against the @repovine/plugin-sdk contract: a type added, renamed, or removed here must track the SDK, and it must stay limited to layer-1 fact types rather than graph ontology.

patterns: Pure type re-export barrel with no exports of its own.
annotation.flowDescription: SDK package declares the fact types → this facade re-exports them → engine and MCP layers import them here or through the internal src/types barrel.
invariants: Only fact-layer types are re-exported; RepositoryGraph, NodeType, EdgeKind, and Interpreter stay engine-internal.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exports mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src; consumed internally through the src/types compatibility barrel.

annotation.summary: Read-only check that the agent assets on disk still match what setup would write. Managed files are compared byte for byte against the canonical render; files the project owns are only scanned for references to tool names that no longer exist. Nothing is repaired here — the report names the command that would.

keyExports.AgentAssetDoctorCliFinding: One display row: area, severity, message and optional action.
keyExports.AgentAssetDoctorInput: The repository, the currently valid tool names, and an optional client scope or pre-resolved scope.
keyExports.AgentAssetFinding: One finding: the file, its severity, a stable code and a message.
keyExports.DoctorAgentAssetsReport: The whole outcome: the pass flag, both versions, the resolved and detected clients, what was scanned and what is governed, the findings and their counts.
keyExports.agentAssetDoctorCliFindings: Turns the report into display rows, each with the action that would resolve it.
keyExports.doctorAgentAssets: Runs both checks for the resolved client scope and returns the report.
keyExports.parseDoctorClientScopeArg: Validates the client argument, naming the accepted values on error.
keyExports.runAgentAssetDoctor: The entry the command line uses, so scope resolution is consistent across output formats.

assumptions: The two checks are deliberately different in strength: a managed file that differs from its canonical render is an error, while a project-owned file is never compared to a template and can only raise a warning about a stale tool name.
The pass flag counts errors only, so warnings report without failing.
Client scope is auto-detected unless overridden, and a pre-resolved scope can be passed in to avoid resolving twice.
Findings carry stable codes so the action mapper can name a specific command rather than a generic one.
Having both managed rules and a generated always-on file is reported as a warning rather than an error, because it is the expected result of setting up every client at once.

sideEffects.description: reads managed and project-owned agent files

risks: Comparison is exact content, so a projection version bump marks every managed file stale at once and the report says nothing about the difference being mechanical rather than meaningful.
Auto-detection decides which managed set is expected, so a repository whose client cannot be detected is checked against the wrong set and reports drift that is really a scope mismatch.
The action mapper still branches on finding codes this module no longer produces — the handoff and brief-section cases — so those branches are unreachable and read as supported behaviour.
patterns: Governed files are held to an exact standard, project files to a loose one, which is what lets a repository customize its own agents without the check fighting it.
Every finding carries the command that resolves it, so the report is actionable without a lookup.
invariants: The check never writes; regeneration is always a separate command.
A file the project owns is never compared against a template.
The pass flag reflects errors alone.
annotation.integrationPoints: The expected content comes from mod:repovine/src/cli/managed-setup-assets; scope resolution and detection from mod:repovine/src/cli/client-scope; the managed-region markers from mod:repovine/src/cli/templates; the two versions stamped on the report from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol and mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection; the valid tool names are supplied by the caller from the server's own tool list.
annotation.dataFlow: repository and client scope → canonical managed asset list → byte comparison against disk → project-owned files scanned for unknown tool names → findings with codes → report and display rows with actions.

annotation.summary: Pure string renderers for Agent Protocol projections: result templates, role guidance, implementer briefs, context-quality guidance, and doctor markers. The projected context-quality text now states that score thresholds are advisory until the labelled-corpus return bar is met, while evidence-backed annotation checks remain enforceable.

keyExports.AGENT_PROTOCOL_GUIDE_PATH: Path of the protocol guide the projections point at.
keyExports.AGENT_PROTOCOL_MARKER: Stable comment marker the doctor greps to read the protocol and projection versions.
keyExports.PROJECTION_REQUIRED_SNIPPETS: The marker strings the doctor requires to be present in a projected asset.
keyExports.PROJECTION_VERSION: Version stamped on the projected assets.
keyExports.RESULT_BLOCK_HEADING: Heading under which the structured result block is projected.
keyExports.renderClientProtocolGuidanceSection: Per-role client asset section, with provenance and quality-axis guidance.
keyExports.renderContextQualityGuidance: The block explaining context-session scoring and how to inspect it.
keyExports.renderImplementerBrief: The autonomous worker mandate: graph as truth, annotation-constraint checkpoints, the annotate-phase workflow and the result honesty rules.
keyExports.renderMainAgentProtocolSection: The main-agent explicit-protocol section, including context-session guidance.
keyExports.renderRequiredArtifactHints: The required-artifact hints derived from a manifest.
keyExports.renderResultBlockSection: The result-block section combining the template and its hints.
keyExports.renderStructuredResultBlock: The run-result JSON template for harness submissions.

assumptions: The harness loads the implementer brief through its own command, and that brief is deliberately stricter than client-facing instructions.
Result blocks belong only to explicit protocol mode.
The projection version stays fixed pre-release, so content changes require re-rendering assets rather than a version bump.
Protocol and context-quality doc paths are pointers into the repovine source repository.
risks: Projected assets go stale independently of this module until re-rendered.
Context-quality guidance must not imply a hard score gate while D5 validation remains below the return bar.
If the implementer brief omits annotation constraints, workers may treat risks as background prose rather than obligations.
patterns: The annotate phase is documented as an explicit sequence: refresh, take the queue, inspect each node, write, clean orphans, validate.

Implementation and review phases convert annotation fields into constraints before edits: invariants must hold, risks must be mitigated or explicitly accepted, declared flow and integration order must be preserved or deliberately changed, and protected side effects need a preceding gate.
Provenance rule: inspecting an export grounds a module, while naming a package or domain scope alone does not.
invariants: Projected context-quality guidance describes the score as advisory until validation succeeds.
Observable claims in a run result are validated against post-refresh graph state.
An annotate-phase run must not edit code.
Relevant annotation invariants left unresolved are blockers, not routine residual risk.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by the onboarding-asset and render commands in the CLI and by the harness run-brief path; the manifests and protocol constants come from mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests and mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol.
annotation.dataFlow: manifest plus protocol constants -> render helpers -> projected client instructions, rules, and briefs -> doctor drift checks and worker prompts.

annotation.summary: Projects the agent assets into their per-client locations and, when asked, writes them. It renders agent files for each supported client, the managed block for the always-on instructions file, the project subagent scaffold, and the raw manifests as a preview. The always-on file is merged rather than replaced, so instructions the project owns survive a re-render.

keyExports.RENDER_CLIENTS: The five render targets, one of which is preview-only.
keyExports.RenderAgentAssetsOptions: What to render: the repository, an optional client, and whether to write.
keyExports.RenderAgentAssetsResult: What was produced: the versions, the per-asset sizes and write status, and the full content when previewing.
keyExports.RenderClientArg: A render target or the request for all of them.
keyExports.RenderedAgentAsset: One rendered file: its client, target path, content, and whether it may be written.
keyExports.computeAgentsMdDiskContent: Works out what the always-on file should contain after a render, given whatever is on disk now.
keyExports.renderAgentAssets: Renders the assets for one client or all of them, returning what was produced and writing it when the write flag is set.

assumptions: Merging the always-on file follows three branches: replace between the markers when they are present, replace the file outright when it looks like one this tool generated, otherwise leave it.
The manifest target is descriptive only and is never written, which is why every asset carries a writable flag rather than the caller inferring it from the path.

Preview returns the full rendered content, and for every asset except the always-on instructions file that content is byte-for-byte what a write would put on disk. The always-on file is the exception: its preview carries the canonical managed block alone, because reconciliation against what is already on disk runs only on the write path, and the reported size is the block's rather than the file's.
Both the protocol version and the projection version travel with the result, so a consumer can tell what produced the files.

This is a leaf: it imports the asset definitions and templates, and two callers import it — the setup path that writes the rendered files, and the doctor's canonical asset manifest, which declares the content those same paths should carry.

sideEffects.description: creates directories and writes the rendered files when the write flag is set

risks: When the markers are absent, a heuristic decides whether the existing always-on file was generated by this tool, and if it decides yes the file is replaced whole rather than appended to; a hand-written file that resembles a generated one loses its content.
Assets are written one at a time with no staging, so an interruption partway leaves some client configurations updated and others not, with nothing recording which.
Rendering targets fixed paths, so renaming an asset leaves the previous file behind in every repository already set up.
patterns: Render and write are the same pass with a flag, which is what keeps the preview honest.
Managed content is delimited by markers so a shared file can have both an owned region and a project-owned one.
invariants: Preview-only assets are never written, whatever the write flag says.
Content outside the markers is preserved when the markers are present.
Rendered files carry no live secrets.
annotation.integrationPoints: Asset bodies and render helpers come from mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets; the managed block and its markers from mod:repovine/src/cli/templates; the projection version from mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection; the protocol version and its builder from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol; the manifests from mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests. Invoked by the render command and by the setup path, and the same file list is what the doctor check inspects.
annotation.dataFlow: client selection → assets rendered per client → the always-on file reconciled against disk → optional directory creation and write → per-asset report with sizes and write status.

annotation.summary: CLI surface for Agent Protocol JSON operations: protocol/manifests, schema validation, graph-backed compliance, orientation, run briefs, roles, and context-session reports. The session-quality command still prints acceptHandoff and rejectReasons, but an existing report exits zero in both modes while the score is unvalidated; evidence-backed validation and compliance failures retain non-zero verdicts.

keyExports.AgentsCliEnv: The repository root and the artifacts directory the subcommands work against.
keyExports.runAgentsCli: Dispatches the subcommands and returns the process exit code.

assumptions: JSON remains on stdout and progress on stderr so callers can parse the contract.
Schema-only commands never build a graph; compliance and orient may build one.
Callers that need the advisory context verdict must read acceptHandoff/rejectReasons from JSON rather than treating the session-quality process exit code as a gate.
Cross-object review linkage is checked without a graph; graph existence is left to compliance.

sideEffects.description: reads the protocol object files given as arguments
writes JSON results, with progress on the error stream
builds a graph on a thread pool for the commands that need one
shells out to git to read a committed tree when the role inspection is pinned to a revision
redirects the pipeline log sink to the error stream on entry and again before a build

risks: The compliance and orient commands can pay full cold-build cost.
An unrecognised manifest name falls back to weaker default requirements.
Until the context score clears its validation bar, automation that previously treated session-quality --mode harness as a hard exit-code gate must consume the JSON advisory fields instead.
patterns: One dispatch, two cost tiers: structural checks stay cheap and graph-backed checks are opt-in by which command you run.
Output stream for the contract, error stream for everything else, which is what makes the whole surface pipe-safe.
invariants: The output stream carries only JSON.
Schema-only commands never build a graph.
Evidence-backed validation failures exit non-zero.
session-quality exits zero when a report exists, even when acceptHandoff is false; a missing/unreadable session still exits non-zero.
annotation.integrationPoints: Validation and the compliance gate come from mod:repovine/src/agents/validation with the descriptor and manifests from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol and mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests; the role source from mod:repovine/src/agents/roles-source; orientation from mod:repovine/src/cli/orient; the pre-run brief from mod:repovine/src/cli/run-brief; session reports from mod:repovine/src/context-quality/session-store; the graph for the gated commands from mod:repovine/src/mcp/context. The JSON shapes are consumed by the harness wrapper.
annotation.dataFlow: arguments and optional JSON files -> subcommand dispatch -> schema check, graph-backed compliance/orient, or context session lookup -> JSON on stdout; exit code gates validated operations while context-quality remains advisory.

annotation.summary: Runs a full build ahead of time and prints its progress, for the build command and for setup, which builds by default. It returns the live runtime so a caller that needs the freshly built state does not have to build again.

keyExports.runBuild: Builds the context for a repository, optionally sweeps orphaned annotations, prints a summary, and returns the runtime.

assumptions: Progress goes to the error stream and the summary to the output stream, so a caller can capture the result without the progress noise.
Progress is printed in place and continuously, because a host that sees a silent subprocess on a large repository kills it on its startup timeout — the output is what keeps the build alive.
Orphan cleanup is opt-in and flushes on both sides of the delete: pending writes land before anything is removed, and the removal itself is durable before the call returns.
It exists to move the cost of the first build to an explicit moment rather than into the first tool call.
Verified 2026-07-23: runBuild signature and imports (mcp/context, config, cli/ui) unchanged; content-hash refresh only.

sideEffects.description: persists the snapshot cache and may rewrite annotations during cleanup
prints the build summary, with pipeline progress on the error stream

risks: An interrupted build leaves the previous cache in place. The snapshot is written once, after extraction finishes, through a temp file renamed over the target, so a half-written snapshot is never published and never read back. What an interrupt leaves behind is this run's worker-sizing calibration, which only advises the next build's parallelism.
Orphan cleanup deletes annotations whose nodes are absent from the freshly built graph, so a build that under-discovers — a missing plugin, a narrowed scan — removes notes for code that still exists.
On a large repository this runs for minutes with no timeout of its own; progress goes to the error stream, so a programmatic caller that discards stderr sees nothing until the summary lands.
patterns: Progress on one stream, result on the other, so the command is scriptable without losing the feedback that keeps it alive.
Cleanup is a deliberate sweep rather than a default, because agents normally clear their own scope.
annotation.flowDescription: User-facing eager build invoked by `repovine build` and `repovine setup --build`; prints module/graph/annotation counts on completion.
invariants: No tracked source is modified; writes are confined to the local cache and the annotation file.
The live runtime is returned rather than discarded.
annotation.integrationPoints: Builds through mod:repovine/src/mcp/context, reads settings through mod:repovine/src/config, and formats output through mod:repovine/src/cli/ui; the returned runtime is used by the setup path's domain advisor.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root → configuration → full build → optional orphan sweep with flushes either side → summary printed → live runtime returned.

annotation.summary: Undoes setup. It walks every place setup touched — the per-client server entries, the hook registrations, the managed block in the always-on file, the generated agent and skill files, and the ignore-file block — and removes only what it put there, leaving everything around it intact. Each target reports its own outcome, and a dry run produces the same plan without writing.

keyExports.ClearOptions: Whether this is a dry run.
keyExports.ClearResult: One target's outcome, with any backup that was made and a reason when skipped.
keyExports.ClearStatus: The six outcomes: planned removal, planned update, removal, update, skip, or error.
keyExports.RunClearOptions: Dry-run flag plus the confirmation hook the tests substitute.
keyExports.clearWorkspace: Processes every target and returns one outcome per path.
keyExports.runClear: The command entry: prints the plan, asks for confirmation unless running unattended, then applies it.

assumptions: Recognition by content applies to the always-on pointer file and to the shared configs, where a mismatch means the file is edited in place instead. Generated client assets — agents, skills, rules, the current dispatcher hook and copy-me subagent scaffolds — are removed by path: the file is not read, so an edited generated asset is deleted like any other.
Shared files are edited rather than deleted: only the recognized server entry, the recognized hook commands or the marked region come out.
Hook removal matches on the current dispatcher command strings setup registers, so unrelated hooks in the same file are untouched.
The supported hook cleanup surface starts with repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs. Pre-release per-action hook filenames are intentionally not scanned or removed.

Backups cover the shared files edited in place: the file is copied before its repovine region is rewritten, or before an emptied file is removed, and the path appears with the outcome. Whole-file and whole-directory removals take no backup. A backup path is also reported when a prior .bak already exists; that copy holds whatever was in place when the .bak was first made.
A dry run reports planned outcomes through the same code path that performs them, so the plan and the action cannot disagree.
Confirmation declines by default when there is no interactive terminal, which keeps an unattended invocation from waiting or from proceeding blindly.

sideEffects.description: removes and rewrites generated files, creating backups first

risks: A file the user edited is skipped rather than removed when removal is guarded by generated-content recognition, which is the safe choice but means a completed run does not imply every customized file disappeared.
Targets are processed one at a time with no overall transaction, so an interruption leaves some clients unwired and others still configured.
Recognition of content-guarded generated files is exact apart from supported uniform line-ending normalization, so other content differences leave the file in place.
patterns: Remove only what was generated, and only when it is still recognizable — the check is content equality rather than a record of what was written.
Delete whole files, edit shared ones: which of the two applies is decided per target rather than per client.
Every outcome is reported, including skips and their reasons, so the result explains what it did not do.
invariants: Source trees are never touched; only files setup created or regions it inserted.
Content outside a managed region is preserved when that region is removed.
A dry run writes nothing.
The annotation memory is preserved by default.
annotation.integrationPoints: The inverse of the setup path in mod:repovine/src/cli/init; expected file contents come from mod:repovine/src/cli/templates and the generated asset list from mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets; the ignore-file block from mod:repovine/src/cli/repovine-gitignore; merge and marker handling from mod:repovine/src/cli/merge-config; workspace paths from mod:repovine/src/paths; output through mod:repovine/src/cli/ui.
annotation.dataFlow: workspace root → per-target recognition against the expected content → removal, region edit or skip with a reason → outcomes printed, then applied after confirmation unless this is a dry run.

annotation.summary: Single source-of-truth record (CLIENT_CAPABILITIES) of how each supported client (claude, cursor, codex) launches hook commands and declares MCP servers. Template builders, plugin rendering, setup, clear, and health derive their client-specific strings from this descriptor instead of hardcoding per-client logic.

keyExports.CLIENT_CAPABILITIES: Record<ClientId, ClientCapabilities> — the concrete contract values for claude, cursor, and codex.
keyExports.CODEX_WINDOWS_PLUGIN_ROOT_REF: '%PLUGIN_ROOT%' — Windows (cmd-style) reference to the Codex plugin install root, used in command_windows values. Comment flags verification on a real Windows Codex client as pending.
keyExports.ClientHookContract: Per-client hook shape: commandForm ('shell-string'|'exec-or-shell'), windowsOverrideField, supportsShellField, projectRootExpr/projectScriptsDir, pluginRootExpr/pluginScriptsDir.
keyExports.ClientId: 'cursor' | 'claude' | 'codex' — same union as PluginClient (plugin-render) and DoctorClient (client-scope).
keyExports.ClientMcpContract: Per-client MCP config shape: format ('json'|'toml'), stdioTypeField ('required'|'optional'|'absent'), projectRootValue.
keyExports.HOOK_ACTIONS: ['boundary-notice', 'stale-graph-notice', 'session-mcp-hint'] — hook actions the client dispatcher serves.
keyExports.hookDispatcherPath: Builds the dispatcher file path as the client addresses it for a given HookScope ('project'|'plugin'); throws if the client defines no plugin install root and scope is 'plugin'.
keyExports.shellHookCommand: Builds the full shell invocation string: `node "<dispatcherPath>" <action> <client>`.

risks: CODEX_WINDOWS_PLUGIN_ROOT_REF's interpolation syntax is explicitly unverified on a real Windows Codex client per the source comment.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/cli/dispatcher — imports CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME to compose hookDispatcherPath.

annotation.summary: Decides which AI client surfaces the repovine doctor inspects. Detects Cursor, Claude and Codex by looking for the repovine server entry in each client's MCP config, resolves an explicit --client choice or the auto default, and reports which surfaces are in scope plus whether AGENTS.md checks apply. Reviewed against current source: 8-export surface unchanged from the prior note.

keyExports.DOCTOR_CLIENT_MCP_LABEL: Display labels for each client's MCP config location.
keyExports.DoctorClient: The supported client ids: cursor, claude, codex.
keyExports.ResolvedDoctorClients: The resolution outcome: the clients to check, the scope that produced them, and what was detected.
keyExports.describeDoctorClientScope: Human-readable scope line for doctor output.
keyExports.detectConfiguredDoctorClients: Scans the Cursor, Claude and Codex MCP configs for a repovine server entry.
keyExports.resolveDoctorClients: Resolves auto to the detected clients (or all three when none are detected), and an explicit scope to itself.
keyExports.scopeUsesAgentsMd: True when the active scope includes a client that reads AGENTS.md.

assumptions: The repo root is the workspace holding the client config directories.
JSON clients use the mcpServers object shape; Codex uses a TOML section marker.
A client whose config exists but omits the repovine entry counts as not configured.

sideEffects.description: reads the Cursor, Claude and Codex MCP config files under the repo root

risks: A non-standard MCP config shape is skipped as 'not configured', so doctor silently narrows its scope rather than warning about a config it could not parse.

risks.text: Callers must distinguish the detected list from the resolved client list; under auto with nothing detected the resolution widens to all three, so a non-empty client list is not evidence any client is actually configured.

patterns: Auto scope widens rather than fails: no detection means check everything.
invariants: Auto scope expands to all three clients when none are detected.
A scope including Codex or Claude implies the AGENTS.md doctor checks run.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by the doctor paths in the repovine CLI agent-doctor and health commands; the config shapes it detects are written by mod:repovine/src/cli/merge-config.
annotation.dataFlow: repo root → scan the client MCP configs for a repovine server entry → detected clients → resolveDoctorClients against the requested scope → client list plus the AGENTS.md flag for doctor.

annotation.summary: Loader for the shipped client hook dispatcher: reads the standalone ESM file repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs that setup copies verbatim into client hook directories and plugin bundles, using a URL-relative read so it resolves next to this module in both src/ (tests) and dist/ (runtime build copies the .mjs alongside).

keyExports.CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME: 'repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs' — file name of the dispatcher in every client hooks directory and plugin bundle.
keyExports.readClientDispatcherSource: Reads and returns the dispatcher's source bytes (LF) from the file shipped beside this module via fs.readFileSync + import.meta.url.

assumptions: repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs is physically present next to this module's compiled output (dist/cli/dispatcher/) — the build step must copy it there or the read throws.

sideEffects.description: fs.readFileSync of repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs resolved via import.meta.url

annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/cli/client-capabilities imports CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME to build hookDispatcherPath/shellHookCommand for setup, clear, and health across clients.

annotation.summary: Identity predicates that let setup (dedupe on re-run) and clear (removal) recognize repovine-managed hook entries in client configs by their dispatcher-invocation shape, so user-defined hooks — including exec-form hooks that happen to run plain `node` — are never matched.

keyExports.isManagedClaudeHook: True for Claude exec-form dispatcher hooks: command === 'node', args is an array, and args[0] is a string containing CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME. command === 'node' alone never matches.
keyExports.isManagedCursorHookCommand: True when a Cursor shell-string command contains CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME.

annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/cli/dispatcher — imports CLIENT_DISPATCHER_FILENAME as the match token for both predicates.

annotation.summary: Walks the user through the domain suggestions a build produced, one at a time, and applies the decisions. Each suggestion can be accepted, kept, hidden or the walk abandoned; what a decision changes depends on which it is.

keyExports.DomainsAdvisorCliResult: Those counts plus whether anything was written and where the backup went.
keyExports.runDomainsAdvisorAfterBuild: Runs the walk and reports what was accepted, kept, hidden and left pending.

assumptions: The four decisions land in two different places: accepting or keeping writes the committed domain configuration, while hiding records the suggestion locally so it stops resurfacing without the repository ever learning about it.
Keeping is offered only for the infrastructure-noise suggestions, since it means committing a marker that deliberately keeps a resource visible; it makes no sense for the other kinds.
A non-interactive run applies nothing and leaves every suggestion pending, for an agent to review as a structured diff through the tool instead.
The committed file is backed up once before either kind of write, and both sets of decisions are layered onto the same copy so a single run produces a single rewrite.
Abandoning the walk leaves the remaining suggestions pending rather than treating silence as a decision.
Verified 2026-07-23: runDomainsAdvisorAfterBuild signature and imports (stage2/domains-advisor, mcp/onboarding-state, cli/prompt, cli/ui) unchanged; content-hash refresh only.

sideEffects.description: backs up and rewrites the committed domain configuration when suggestions are accepted or kept
prints each suggestion and the outcome

risks: Accepting changes domain tagging for the whole repository, so a decision made per suggestion has repository-wide effect and the backup is the only way back.

Hidden suggestions live only in the untracked local state, so clearing the cache brings every one of them back while accepted and kept decisions persist — the two kinds of decision have very different durability.
Nothing re-validates the resulting configuration here; a suggestion accepted against a stale build writes an exclusion for a shape that may no longer exist.
patterns: Two destinations, one prompt: what the repository should agree on is committed, what one person chose to ignore stays local.
Nothing applies without an explicit answer, in either the interactive or the tool-driven path.
annotation.flowDescription: Post-build hook → runDomainsAdvisorAfterBuild reads graph + domains config → prints/returns DomainsAdvisorCliResult.
invariants: Suggestions never apply without confirmation.
The committed configuration is backed up before it is overwritten.
Declined identifiers never reach the committed file.
Unanswered suggestions remain pending.
annotation.integrationPoints: The suggestions and the functions that apply them come from mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-advisor; the declined set is read and written through mod:repovine/src/mcp/onboarding-state; the configuration path from mod:repovine/src/paths; prompting from mod:repovine/src/cli/prompt. Invoked after a build by the setup path.
annotation.stateShape: DomainsAdvisorCliResult tracks suggestion counts and whether config was applied or declined.
annotation.dataFlow: suggestions on the built state → per-suggestion decision → accepted and kept layered onto one backed-up copy of the committed configuration → hidden ids merged into the local advisory state → counts returned.

annotation.summary: EOL detection/normalization helpers for comparing and writing managed files: templates are LF constants but user checkouts may be CRLF (core.autocrlf), so compares normalize to LF and writes restore the file's dominant EOL.

keyExports.applyEol: Normalizes content to LF first, then converts to the target eol if it is CRLF — never double-converts.
keyExports.detectEol: Returns the dominant EOL of content by counting CRLF vs total LF; ties/none default to '\n'.
keyExports.isUniformEol: True when every newline in content shares one form (all CRLF or all lone LF) or there are none; mixed-EOL files fail and callers must fall back to byte-exact handling.

assumptions: Callers that need lossless round-tripping on mixed-EOL files must check isUniformEol first and take a byte-exact path when it is false.

annotation.summary: CLI health surface: repovine doctor diagnoses MCP global configs, snapshot cache, annotation merge/health, managed agent-asset projections, boundary index freshness; repovine status reports graph stats and annotation coverage. Read-only — remediation via setup or config.

keyExports.runDoctorCli: repovine doctor: MCP setup, cache, annotations, asset drift, boundary index diagnosis.
keyExports.runStatusCli: repovine status: graph stats and annotation coverage summary.

assumptions: Boundary hook scripts record schema version as index.version comment.
Boundary index lives alongside graph build artifacts.
Doctor never mutates: whole surface is reads + stdout.

sideEffects.description: MCP configs, AGENTS.md, cache files, boundary-index.json, hook scripts

risks: Auto-detected client scope may miss multi-client setups.
Stale graph if doctor runs without recent build/refresh.

risks.text: Boundary index schema version mismatch silences advisories until setup re-run; importers must verify alignment.

patterns: --json via printJson for scripting.
Diagnosis is fail-loud only (no auto-repair).
invariants: Doctor never mutates repo files.
Accepted boundary-index schema version owned by mcp/boundary-index; mismatch with installed hooks emits warning not repair.
annotation.integrationPoints: mcp/context, mcp/boundary-index, agent-doctor, annotations/maintenance, cli/client-scope, cli/ui.
annotation.dataFlow: argv → flag parse → inspections or RepovineRuntime → validateAnnotationHealth + boundaryPushChannelFindings → stdout + exit code.

envDependencies.WINDIR: Read in detectLongPaths() on Windows to locate the system directory (System32/reg.exe) for the long-paths registry check; absent or ignored on non-Windows platforms. parseLongPathsRegOutput only parses the reg.exe output string and does not read env.

annotation.summary: Slim CLI formatter for annotation coverage stats: CompactCoverage type records total/annotated/fresh/stale/unannotated module counts; formatModuleCoverageLine renders one summary line for health/status output.

keyExports.formatModuleCoverageLine: Returns '<fresh>/<totalModules> modules fresh, <unannotated> unannotated, <stale> stale' from a CompactCoverage.

assumptions: Used by CLI health/status paths that print module coverage.
Pure string formatter; callers handle stdout themselves.
risks: Output format is not a stable API; scripts should use JSON flags instead of parsing this line.
patterns: Thin formatter — not a stable API; prefer MCP JSON for automation.
invariants: No I/O — returns a formatted string only.
annotation.integrationPoints: CLI health and annotation coverage reporting commands.
annotation.dataFlow: CompactCoverage counts -> formatModuleCoverageLine -> string for the caller to print.

annotation.summary: Workspace onboarding CLI: inspects workspace support, bootstraps repovine.config.json and annotations file, and renders Cursor/Claude/Codex MCP configs, hooks, skills, and rules from canonical templates.

keyExports.initAll: Bootstrap all supported clients in one pass.
keyExports.inspectWorkspaceSupport: Preflight tsconfig/workspace detection for cold build ETA.
keyExports.runWorkspaceBootstrap: CLI entry for repovine setup/init command.

assumptions: initAll writes Cursor + Claude + Codex projections unless client-specific init called.
replaceMcp overwrites existing MCP server blocks when true.
ensureWorkspaceBootstrap creates repovine.config.json and repovine.annots.json when missing.
Each client hook directory contains one managed repovine-client-dispatcher.mjs; all three hook actions are selected through generated client config rather than separate hook files.
Re-running setup merges current dispatcher registrations idempotently and does not retain duplicate managed hook entries.

sideEffects.description: Writes client config, hooks, skills, rules, and default repovine.config.json

risks: replaceMcp:true clobbers user MCP customizations.
Cold build recommendation ignored when autoBuild false on large monorepos.
patterns: Idempotent merge for AGENTS.md managed block and hook markers.
annotation.flowDescription: Preflight → confirm (interactive) → bootstrap workspace → per-target MCP JSON + projected agent assets.
invariants: ensureEmptyAnnotationsFile creates repovine.annots.json only when missing, so re-running setup never overwrites accumulated annotation memory.
Setup without a client argument runs the workspace bootstrap alone, writing config and the annotations file and no client projections.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/cli/templates; mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets; mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance ensureEmptyAnnotationsFile; mod:repovine/src/config loadConfig.
annotation.dataFlow: cwd + InitOptions → templates from mod:repovine/src/cli/templates and mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets → write .cursor/.claude/.codex files + hooks.

annotation.summary: Builds the list of files setup would write for a given set of clients, each with the exact content it should hold. The doctor check compares what is on disk against this list, so it has to reproduce not only what setup writes but the order in which setup overwrites shared paths.

keyExports.ManagedSetupAsset: One entry: the relative path, the expected content and what kind of asset it is.
keyExports.ManagedSetupAssetKind: The four kinds: agent, skill, rule and the always-on instructions file.
keyExports.SETUP_ALL_MERGE_ORDER: The client order a full setup writes in, which decides who wins a shared path.
keyExports.listCanonicalManagedAssets: The managed files and their expected content for the selected clients.
keyExports.mergeManagedAssetsBySetupOrder: Collapses paths claimed by more than one client the way a full setup would leave them.
keyExports.readManagedFile: Reads a managed file for comparison, returning nothing when it is absent.

assumptions: Two of the three clients project their skills into the same directory, so a full setup necessarily overwrites; the merge here reproduces that rather than reporting a conflict.
Later clients in the order win, because that is the order setup writes and therefore what ends up on disk.
Agent files are obtained by rendering with writing switched off, which is what keeps the expected content identical to what a real setup would produce instead of a second description of it.
That render is done with an empty repository root, which holds because agent target paths do not depend on the root; the always-on file does depend on it and is handled separately with the real one.
Only writable assets enter the manifest, so preview-only output is not compared against disk.
The always-on file is included only when the selected clients actually use it.

sideEffects.description: reads managed files for comparison

risks: The write order is restated here as a literal list rather than derived from the setup path, so changing the order in setup without changing it here makes the doctor expect the wrong content on exactly the paths two clients share — and it reports drift on a correctly set up workspace.
Expected content is produced by rendering, so any render input that varies by environment produces a mismatch the doctor attributes to the file rather than to the render.
A path claimed by no client is simply absent from the manifest, so a file setup once wrote under an older name is never compared and never reported.
patterns: Expected content comes from the same renderer setup uses, so the comparison cannot drift from what is written.
Overwrite semantics are modelled explicitly rather than assumed away, because shared paths are the normal case rather than an error.
invariants: The manifest reflects what a full setup leaves on disk, including which client won each shared path.
Preview-only assets never appear in it.
A missing file reads as absent rather than as empty content.
annotation.integrationPoints: Asset bodies and render helpers come from mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets; agent previews and the always-on file reconciliation from mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-render; the client scope and whether it uses the always-on file from mod:repovine/src/cli/client-scope; the manifest is consumed by the doctor check.
annotation.dataFlow: selected clients → per-client agent, rule and skill entries → shared paths collapsed in setup order → the always-on file appended when in scope → manifest compared against disk.

annotation.summary: Safe merge of the repovine MCP server entry into a client's existing config. Inspects the target file to classify what is already there (missing, invalid, empty, only-repovine, has-other-servers), resolves that into a write plan (create, merge, replace-all, skip), and applies it with a backup. Handles both JSON clients via an mcpServers key and Codex TOML via an [mcp_servers.repovine] block plus hooks.

keyExports.REPOVINE_MCP_SERVER_NAME: Canonical 'repovine' server key written into client configs.
keyExports.formatMcpPreflight: Plain-text preflight lines describing the file, its current state, and the resolved plan.
keyExports.inspectCodexMcpConfig: Classifies a Codex TOML config as missing | has-repovine | has-other-mcp | no-repovine.
keyExports.inspectMcpJsonConfig: Classifies a JSON MCP config as missing | invalid | empty | only-repovine | has-other-servers.
keyExports.resolveCodexWritePlan: Turns a Codex inspect result plus the replaceMcp flag into a plan with a stated reason.
keyExports.resolveMcpJsonWritePlan: Turns a JSON inspect result plus the replaceMcp flag into a plan with a stated reason.
keyExports.writeCodexMcpConfig: Appends or replaces the [mcp_servers.repovine] block and hooks in Codex TOML.
keyExports.writeMcpJsonConfig: Runs inspect then plan then apply for a JSON client, honouring the confirm callback.

assumptions: The confirmExistingWrite callback comes from interactive init; non-interactive callers must handle a skipped write.
Foreign MCP servers in the target file must survive, so merge is mandatory once inspect reports has-other-servers.

sideEffects.description: reads the client MCP config file during inspect
writes the client MCP config and a backup file when a plan is applied

risks: replace-all is refused while foreign servers exist, leaving the user to reconcile manually.

risks.text: Callers must treat a skipped status as a write that did not happen; the confirm callback returning false is a normal outcome, not an error.
The written server entry is the contract other clients read to launch repovine: the REPOVINE_MCP_SERVER_NAME key and block shape are what an installed client resolves at startup.

patterns: Inspect, then plan with a reason, then apply: the plan is inspectable before any file is touched.
Every destructive path records a backup path in the result.
invariants: A backup path is recorded in the write result whenever an overwrite is planned.
replace-all is chosen only when inspect reports only-repovine or the user confirms.
annotation.integrationPoints: Driven by cli init preflight and writes; mod:repovine/src/cli/templates supplies the server blocks and mod:repovine/src/cli/clear removes the managed blocks. Preflight text is styled by styleMcpPreflight in mod:repovine/src/cli/ui.
annotation.dataFlow: client path + replaceMcp flag → inspect → resolve plan → optional interactive confirm → backup + write → ConfigWriteResult.

annotation.summary: The single source for everything the tool writes into a host client. Guidance constants compose into asset bodies, asset bodies render through per-client helpers, and setup projects the result into Cursor rules, Claude skills and agents, and Codex TOML. Files in those client directories are projections: a change belongs here, then a re-render.

keyExports.AGENTS: The four utility subagents: annotation writer, repo explorer, architecture auditor, code reviewer.
keyExports.ANNOTATIONS_MCP_ONLY_GUARDRAIL: That the annotation file is only ever changed through the tools.
keyExports.ANNOTATIONS_SKILL: The annotation skill: queue drain order, scope-candidate advisory handling, and the quality and provenance rules.
keyExports.ANNOTATION_CARRIER_LINK_AUTHORING: How a facade names the delegated single source when the dependency is more than one hop away.
keyExports.ANNOTATION_RISK_SHAPE_GUIDANCE: How scoped risks are written: name the obligation or the frozen status, withhold the mechanism.
keyExports.COMMANDS: Lifecycle skills for refresh, status and annotation maintenance.
keyExports.CURSOR_RULES: Cursor managed rules, including the pre-edit annotation checkpoints.
keyExports.DEFAULT_PROJECT_SUBAGENT_NAME: The implementer a host delegates to by default after setup.
keyExports.OnboardingAsset: The shape every asset shares: name, description, body, plus optional per-client body and model overrides.
keyExports.PROJECT_SAMPLE_SUBAGENT_MD: Body of the ready-to-use project implementer.
keyExports.PROJECT_SUBAGENT_SCAFFOLD_PATHS: The six scaffold files init writes and clear removes, two per client.
keyExports.PROJECT_SUBAGENT_TEMPLATE_MD: Body of the placeholder template a repo copies to define a specialist.
keyExports.SEARCH_CONTEXT_INTERPRETATION_POLICY: How to read a weak or relaxed search result before drilling in.
