keyExports.SHARED_SKILLS: Work-intent skills covering the implementation, review and annotation flows.
keyExports.SIDE_EFFECTS_VOCABULARY: The closed effect enum reproduced for annotation authors.
keyExports.SINGLE_QUEUE_GUIDANCE: That the backlog is one queue across node types, content-stale ahead of propagation-stale.
keyExports.SUBAGENT_ORCHESTRATION_CORE: Main-agent delegation policy shared by the Cursor rule and the always-on file: when to delegate, how named sets resolve, and the standing ban on parallel annotation writers.
keyExports.renderClaudeFrontmatter: Agent frontmatter in the Claude dialect.
keyExports.renderCursorAgentFrontmatter: Agent frontmatter in the Cursor dialect.
keyExports.renderCursorBody: Asset body adjusted for a Cursor agent file.
keyExports.renderProjectSampleSubagentToml: The default project implementer as Codex TOML.
keyExports.renderProjectSubagentTemplateToml: The placeholder template as Codex TOML, placeholders intact.
keyExports.renderSkillMarkdown: Wraps an asset body in skill frontmatter.

assumptions: Guidance lives in small named constants rather than inline prose so one edit reaches every client surface at once.
Agent identity comes from the frontmatter or TOML name, not the filename, which is what lets a repo rename a scaffold file freely.
Identity strings come from mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests rather than being repeated here.
The lifecycle skills and the work-intent skills are separate collections on purpose: one covers upkeep, the other covers intent.
Projected doc paths point humans to the repovine source repository; consumer workspaces are not assumed to contain a local `node_modules/repovine` installation.
risks: Editing shared guidance text reaches every client surface and the doctor snippet checks at once, so a small wording change lands far from where it was made.
A generated projection edited in place is overwritten on the next render, and the change is lost without warning.
The scaffold path list is literal, so renaming a scaffold file leaves the old name behind in every repo already onboarded; clear only knows the names it currently ships.
Guidance text is read by agents in arbitrary repositories, so anything stack-specific in it becomes wrong advice elsewhere.
patterns: Constants compose into bodies, bodies render per client: the same content reaches three hosts without three copies.
The annotation checkpoint turns note fields into a pre-edit checklist, which is how a note becomes a constraint rather than background.
Scoped-risk guidance names the obligation and withholds the fix, and that shape propagates through every generated surface.
annotation.flowDescription: repovine init/setup reads SHARED_SKILLS/COMMANDS/AGENTS/CURSOR_RULES, applies renderSkillMarkdown/renderCodexAgentToml, writes .cursor/.claude/.codex/.agents projections.
invariants: The annotation file is never hand-edited; the guardrail constant states this on every surface that mentions it.
Annotation writers run one at a time, including across disjoint scopes, because every write goes through one debounced store.
The backlog is one queue, content-stale ahead of propagation-stale.
Generated skills present annotation claims as constraints to act on, not as summaries to read.
annotation.integrationPoints: Rendered by mod:repovine/src/cli/init and mod:repovine/src/cli/plugin-render; snippet presence is enforced by mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection and checked by mod:repovine/src/cli/managed-setup-assets; identity strings come from mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests.
annotation.dataFlow: guidance constants → asset bodies → per-client render helpers → setup or render → rule, skill and agent files in the host client's directories.

annotation.summary: Deterministic orientation: run a search for a natural-language task, pick a scope from what it found, then trace the runtime flow around it — all without a model. Used to give a harness a factual starting context before any agent runs.

keyExports.OrientReport: The report: the query, whether anything was found, the graph nodes, the traced scope, and both tool summaries.
keyExports.buildOrientReport: Runs the search and the trace for a query and returns the combined report.
keyExports.normalizeOrientQuery: Reduces a harness prompt to the part worth searching for.

assumptions: Matching is left on the adaptive setting rather than forced strict: it requires every token first and falls back to a bounded any-token match when no single node carries them all. A natural-language task rarely lands every token on one node, and strict matching returns nothing whenever token extraction is even slightly reduced — so orientation degrades to a looser match instead of orienting to nothing.
Search results are read from the nested match object rather than the outer envelope; reading the envelope yields an empty node list every time regardless of what was found.
The query is normalized first: a prior-run preamble is stripped, an over-long coordination blob is reduced to its last paragraph, and the result is length-capped.
The trace scope comes from the caller when given, otherwise from the first module or package the search returned.
A fresh runtime is built per invocation rather than reusing a long-lived server, since this runs as a command rather than inside one.
Finding nothing is reported as such; there is no fallback query, because a repository-specific guess would be wrong everywhere else.

sideEffects.description: invokes the search and trace handlers against a freshly built runtime
builds the graph for the repository on each invocation

risks: Every invocation builds the graph from scratch, so orientation costs a full build on a cold cache — acceptable once per run, expensive if called repeatedly.
The scope for the trace is inferred from the top search hit, so a search that lands on an unrepresentative module traces the wrong area while still reporting success.
Reporting nothing found is honest but indistinguishable from a repository where the search index is thin, since both produce an empty node list.
patterns: Two tools in sequence with no model between them, so the same query always yields the same orientation.
Degrade the match rather than the answer: a looser search beats an empty one.
invariants: No model is involved.
An empty query returns a report saying so rather than searching.
There is no hard-coded fallback query.
annotation.integrationPoints: Exposed through the orient subcommand in mod:repovine/src/cli/agents and called by the harness before a run; the tools are mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/search-context and mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/trace-flow, driven against a runtime from mod:repovine/src/mcp/context; result identifiers are extracted with mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve.
annotation.dataFlow: raw query → normalized → search with adaptive matching → node identifiers from the nested matches → scope chosen → trace over services, resources, flows and entrypoints → one report.

annotation.summary: Generates the distributable plugin repository from the same asset definitions setup uses. For each of the three clients it writes a bundle and a marketplace manifest, pins the server invocation to the engine's current version, and adds the shared licence and readme. The output directory is a separate repository, so the render clears its own previous output and leaves that repository's own files alone.

keyExports.REPOVINE_PLUGIN_REPOSITORY: Where the rendered bundles are published.
keyExports.RenderPluginRepoOptions: Engine root, output root, an optional version override and an optional client subset.
keyExports.RenderPluginRepoResult: Both versions, the roots, the clients rendered, the paths written and the entries cleared.
keyExports.defaultEngineRoot: The engine package root, derived from this module's own location.
keyExports.defaultOutRoot: The default output root, a sibling of the engine checkout.
keyExports.readEngineVersion: The version from the engine's package manifest, failing loudly when absent.
keyExports.renderPluginRepo: Renders the bundles for the selected clients and reports the version, the paths written and what was cleared.
keyExports.wipePluginOutRoot: Clears prior output: everything unowned on a full render, only the selected clients' entries on a scoped one.

assumptions: A full render clears the output root so an asset dropped from the projection disappears with it; a scoped render touches only the selected clients' own entries, which is what keeps the other bundles installable while one is being reworked.
Hand-placed assets and the output repository's own version-control files are never cleared, because the output root is a real repository rather than a scratch directory.
The server invocation is pinned to an exact engine version in every bundle, so an installed plugin does not silently follow the latest release.
The install instructions share one body with a per-client preamble, so the three cannot drift apart.
The bundles are a projection: a change belongs in the asset definitions, followed by a re-render.

sideEffects.description: clears prior output and writes the bundle trees and manifests

risks: A full render deletes everything under the output root except the small preserved set, so pointing it at a directory that holds anything else destroys that content; the default is a dedicated sibling repository for exactly this reason.
The version is read from the engine's package manifest at render time, so rendering from a checkout whose version has not been bumped publishes bundles pinned to the previous release.

Version pinning in the command-line client's configuration works by text substitution on the expected argument form, so a change to how that argument is written leaves the bundle unpinned without failing.
patterns: One asset source, three client dialects: the bundles differ in packaging rather than in content.
Clearing is scoped to what the render is about to rewrite, which is what makes a single-client render safe against a shared publish repository.
annotation.flowDescription: Release packaging pipeline: resolve engineRoot/outRoot and readEngineVersion -> wipePluginOutRoot (full wipe for every client, CLIENT_OWNED_ENTRIES only for a subset; preserve assets/.git/.gitignore) -> for each selected PluginClient render bundle files from onboarding-assets/templates/agent-projection -> emit marketplace index + LICENSE/README -> return RenderPluginRepoResult with paths and projectionVersion stamp.
invariants: Marketplace manifests reference their sources by relative path, which is what the host installers accept.
A bundle carries no project-scoped settings file; its components sit at the plugin root's default locations and its hooks run from the plugin root.
The manifest does not point at the default hook file, because the host loads that file itself and naming it again trips duplicate validation.
The generated documentation keeps installation marketplace-first and does not ask for a separate asset setup afterwards.
Every bundle documents the optional embedding install, because the server starts through the package runner and the embedding package resolves from the workspace rather than from beside the engine.
A scoped render leaves the other clients' bundles and manifests installable.
annotation.integrationPoints: Asset bodies and render helpers come from mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets, file contents from mod:repovine/src/cli/templates, the projection version from mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection, and the server name used for pinning from mod:repovine/src/cli/merge-config; the result feeds the publish workflow.
annotation.dataFlow: engine root and version → output root cleared to the render's scope → per-client bundle files with the version pinned → marketplace manifests, licence and readme → report of paths written and entries cleared.

annotation.summary: Synchronous one-line stdin prompt for interactive repovine init/doctor: opens /dev/tty (or CONIN$ on Windows), reads until newline, throws with caller-provided message when no TTY.

keyExports.promptLineSync: Writes prompt to stdout, returns trimmed answer or throws nonTtyMessage.

assumptions: Used only for yes/no or short confirmations in CLI commands.
EAGAIN on non-blocking fd retries with 25ms sleep.

sideEffects.description: readSync from TTY fd until newline
Writes prompt string before read

risks: Hung stdin if user never sends newline.
patterns: Sync TTY read for short confirmations only.
invariants: Throws when stdin is not a TTY — callers must catch in CI.
annotation.integrationPoints: cli/init and merge-config confirmations.
annotation.dataFlow: prompt string → /dev/tty readSync → trimmed answer or throw in non-TTY CI.

annotation.summary: The canonical .gitignore block repovine manages in a workspace: a header comment recording that the annotations file is committed while the engine cache directory is ignored, plus the ignore entry itself. The recognized header and entry sets are what lets the clear command remove exactly the block it wrote.

keyExports.REPOVINE_GITIGNORE_ENTRIES: Entry lines the clear command recognizes as repovine-managed.
keyExports.REPOVINE_GITIGNORE_ENTRY: The ignore entry for the engine cache directory, derived from the artifacts directory name.
keyExports.REPOVINE_GITIGNORE_HEADER: The comment line written by setup.
keyExports.REPOVINE_GITIGNORE_HEADERS: Header lines the clear command recognizes as repovine-managed.
keyExports.formatRepovineGitignoreBlock: Returns the newline-wrapped header and entry ready to append.

assumptions: The entry is derived from the artifacts directory name rather than hardcoded, so renaming the cache directory moves the ignore rule with it.
The recognized sets are kept plural so a previously written header can still be matched after the current wording changes.
risks: A hand-edited header stops matching the recognized set, so the clear command leaves the block behind rather than removing something it no longer recognizes.
patterns: The managed block is identified by exact header and entry membership rather than by parsing, which keeps removal conservative.
invariants: The engine cache directory stays ignored while the annotations file stays committed.
annotation.integrationPoints: The block is appended by the CLI init path and removed by the CLI clear path; the cache directory name comes from mod:repovine/src/paths.
annotation.dataFlow: formatRepovineGitignoreBlock → appended to the workspace .gitignore on init → clear removes the lines matching the recognized header and entry sets.

annotation.summary: Produces the pre-run prompt material a harness gives an agent before it starts. It looks up a built-in capability manifest by explicit name or by role, renders the implementer brief from it, and returns that text alongside the protocol and projection versions it was rendered under. Reachable through the command line only; it is not exposed as a server tool.

keyExports.RunBriefOptions: What the caller may specify: a role, a name, or nothing.
keyExports.RunBriefResult: The rendered brief plus the role, name, protocol version and projection version behind it.
keyExports.buildRunBrief: Resolves the manifest and returns the rendered brief with its versions, or an error object naming what could not be resolved.
keyExports.resolveRunBriefManifest: Looks up the manifest: an explicit name wins, then the role, and with neither the implementer role is assumed.

assumptions: An explicit name takes precedence over a role, so a caller naming an agent gets that agent rather than whatever its role would resolve to.
Omitting both selectors is a supported call, not an error: the implementer role is the default a harness wants.
Both versions travel with the brief so a consumer can tell which protocol and which rendering produced the text it received.
Only built-in manifests are reachable here; there is no lookup path for an externally supplied one.

risks.text: The result is a union rather than a thrown error, so a caller must check for the error member before reading the brief; an unresolved name or role otherwise flows onward as a missing field rather than a failure.

patterns: Resolution and rendering are separate exports, so a caller that only needs to know whether a manifest exists does not render a brief to find out.
annotation.flowDescription: role or name → resolveRunBriefManifest (explicit name, else role, else 'implementer') → renderImplementerBrief(manifest) → RunBriefResult carrying the brief text plus protocolVersion and projectionVersion, or an error object naming the unresolved role/name. No file is written here; this module only resolves and renders text.
invariants: A missing manifest yields an error object rather than an exception.
The returned role and name come from the resolved manifest, not from what the caller asked for.
annotation.integrationPoints: Manifest lookup comes from mod:repovine/src/agents/manifests, the role type and protocol version from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol, and both the projection version and the brief renderer from mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection.
annotation.dataFlow: role or name → manifest lookup with the implementer default → brief rendered from the manifest → result carrying the text and both versions, or an error object.

annotation.summary: The literal file contents setup writes: config and domains scaffolds, per-client launch blocks for the stdio server, the marker-delimited managed block for the always-on file, and the hook wiring each client runs. Everything here is a string, a data row, or a function returning one; writing it to disk belongs to the callers.

keyExports.AGENTS_MD: The managed quick-reference block merged into the always-on file.
keyExports.AGENTS_MD_BEGIN_MARKER: Opening delimiter of the managed block.
keyExports.AGENTS_MD_END_MARKER: Closing delimiter of the managed block.
keyExports.CLAUDE_HOOKS_SETTINGS: Claude hook settings built for the 'project' scope, covering the pre-edit boundary check, the post-edit stale-graph check, and the session-start MCP hint.
keyExports.CLAUDE_MD: The thin pointer file that defers to the always-on file.
keyExports.CODEX_CONFIG_TOML: The full Codex config fragment: server block plus hooks block.
keyExports.CODEX_HOOKS_BEGIN_MARKER: Opening delimiter of the managed hook region in the Codex config.
keyExports.CODEX_HOOKS_BLOCK: The Codex hook registrations, one TOML stanza per row in the internal CODEX_HOOK_ROWS table.
keyExports.CURSOR_HOOKS_SETTINGS: Cursor hook settings built from the internal CURSOR_HOOK_ROWS table.
keyExports.McpLauncher: How the server is launched: a command and its arguments.
keyExports.NPX_LAUNCHER: The default launcher for a published install.
keyExports.REPOVINE_CONFIG_JSON: Default build, server and analyzer configuration for a new workspace.
keyExports.REPOVINE_DOMAINS_JSON: Starter domain configuration: an empty map plus infrastructure excludes.
keyExports.buildClaudeHooksSettings: Builds the Claude hooks settings for a given scope ('project' or 'plugin'); each row spawns node directly against the dispatcher script rather than a shell string.
keyExports.buildClaudeMcpJson: The Claude server entry serialized to its config file.
keyExports.buildClaudeMcpServer: Server entry in the Claude dialect.
keyExports.buildCodexConfigToml: The full Codex config fragment, server block plus hook markers.
keyExports.buildCodexHooksBlock: Renders CODEX_HOOK_ROWS into TOML hook stanzas, including a Windows command_windows alternate per row.
keyExports.buildCodexMcpServerBlock: The Codex server entry as a TOML block.
keyExports.buildCursorHooksSettings: Renders CURSOR_HOOK_ROWS into the Cursor hooks.json shape.
keyExports.buildCursorMcpJson: The Cursor server entry serialized to its config file.
keyExports.buildCursorMcpServer: Server entry in the Cursor dialect.

assumptions: All three clients render hook commands from the same three action names (boundary-notice, stale-graph-notice, session-mcp-hint) declared per event in a client-local ROWS table (CODEX_HOOK_ROWS, CURSOR_HOOK_ROWS, CLAUDE_HOOK_ROWS); only the command shape differs, since Claude spawns node directly with args while Codex and Cursor build a shell command string.
The default configuration must load through the real config loader, which is what the setup tests assert.
Both marker pairs exist so setup can rewrite its own region of a file the user also edits.
The launcher is a parameter rather than a constant so a local checkout and a published install can share these builders.
Claude's dispatcher path is anchored to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for the 'project' scope or CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT for the 'plugin' scope, per buildClaudeHooksSettings' scope argument.
risks: These strings are copies of contracts owned elsewhere, so a change to the config schema or the server surface leaves them stale with nothing failing until onboarding produces a broken workspace.

The hook scripts resolve the workspace root from the host variable, fall back to the working directory, then walk parents for .repovine, so an unset variable leaves them working. The advisory goes quiet instead when the on-disk boundary index is missing, unparseable, or carries no entry for the edited path.

risks.text: The boundary hook only reports when the on-disk index matches the version it accepts, so an importer changing either side must confirm advisories still fire in a real workspace.

patterns: One source for every client, so onboarding stays consistent and the doctor checks have something to compare against.
Setup is stdio only: the launcher is a command and arguments, with no network transport anywhere in the generated config.
Hook wiring is table-driven: a small ROWS array of event/action pairs per client is mapped through a shared dispatcher command builder, rather than three independent hardcoded scripts.
annotation.flowDescription: Setup/init copies or merges template strings into .cursor, .claude, .codex, repovine.config.json, and repovine.domains.json; the boundary-notice, stale-graph-notice and session-mcp-hint actions are wired per client into CODEX_HOOKS_BLOCK, CURSOR_HOOKS_SETTINGS and CLAUDE_HOOKS_SETTINGS.
invariants: Managed regions are always delimited by their markers so a merge never overwrites user content around them.
The default configuration contains no network listener block.
The default launcher is the published-install form.
extensionPoints: A new client adds its own server builder plus its own ROWS array of event/action pairs.
A new hook action needs a name recognized by the shared HookAction type and by the dispatcher script; adding one to a client's ROWS table is not enough on its own.
annotation.integrationPoints: Written to disk by mod:repovine/src/cli/init, mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-render and mod:repovine/src/cli/plugin-render; the managed protocol section comes from mod:repovine/src/cli/agent-projection; merge and marker semantics live in mod:repovine/src/cli/merge-config; hook command rendering (shellHookCommand, hookDispatcherPath, HookAction) comes from mod:repovine/src/cli/dispatcher; the generated boundary hooks read the index produced by mod:repovine/src/mcp/boundary-index.
annotation.dataFlow: template constants → init, agent render or plugin render → client config, hook and managed-block files; at runtime the generated hooks read the boundary index from the local cache directory.

envDependencies.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT: Claude hook dispatcher root when scope is 'plugin'
envDependencies.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: Claude hook dispatcher root when scope is 'project'

annotation.summary: Splits user-facing output from build progress. logCli writes to stdout; logCliError and the pipeline loggers write to stderr, with a settable sink so MCP stdio mode can silence pipeline logs. Also formats package/semantic-embed progress bars and file-result lines for the CLI.

keyExports.formatPackageProgressLine: Renders a per-package build progress bar with elapsed time and RSS
keyExports.formatSemanticEmbedProgressLine: Renders the semantic-embedding pass progress bar (done/total, elapsed)
keyExports.logPipelineProgress: In-place \r with pad/clip/truncate; TTY or setProgressInPlace; else newline logPipeline
keyExports.setPipelineLogSink: Routes pipeline logs to silent sink for MCP stdio mode
keyExports.setProgressInPlace: Force \r progress on piped stderr (Cursor MCP subprocess)
keyExports.styleMcpPreflight: ANSI styling for merge-config preflight lines

assumptions: Node CLI or MCP child with real WriteStreams.
Tests use stripAnsi on styled output.
MCP host pipes stderr (isTTY=false) but still renders \r updates in the log panel.

sideEffects.description: logCli writes user-facing CLI lines to process.stdout
logCliError writes red-styled error lines, and logPipeline/logPipelineProgress/logPipelineWarn write build progress, to process.stderr, including in-place \r rewrites

risks: Silent pipeline sink hides build progress during long graph builds.
Very long progress lines still need clipProgressLine when column count is unknown (default 120).

risks.text: Callers that emit machine-read output on stdout must confirm the pipeline sink is not routing progress there; stdout is the MCP stdio transport.

patterns: Dual sinks: stdout for user-facing CLI, stderr for pipeline/build progress.
MCP refreshPipelineLogSink calls setProgressInPlace when pipeline logs are visible.
invariants: MCP stdio mode must route pipeline logs away from stdout.
setProgressInPlace(true) enables in-place progress when stderr is piped.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage1/index and context.ts call logPipelineProgress; MCP sets setPipelineLogSink('silent').
annotation.dataFlow: logCli/logPipeline → FORCE_COLOR/NO_COLOR + TTY check → ANSI SGR strings → stdout/stderr; pipeline sink routes build progress away from MCP stdio.

envDependencies.COLUMNS: Terminal width for progress line clipping

annotation.summary: The configuration spine. It reads the workspace configuration file, validates it against a schema, and resolves it into a shape where every field is present, filling defaults for whatever was omitted. One resolved object serves the build, the server, the architecture analysis, the annotation propagation policy and the plugin set.

keyExports.DEFAULT_CONTRACT_HUB_THRESHOLDS: When a module counts as a shared contract hub.
keyExports.DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE: How many cards are embedded at a time.
keyExports.DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL: The embedding model, fixed rather than configurable.
keyExports.DEFAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS: The ceiling on a serialized response.
keyExports.DomainStalePolicy: Whether domain staleness follows every tag or only the path tag.
keyExports.MIN_RESPONSE_CHARS: The floor a configured ceiling may not go below.
keyExports.PluginsConfig: Whether the built-ins apply, plus additions and exclusions.
keyExports.PropagationConfig: How annotation staleness propagates: the domain policy, whether package domains queue hard, how far consumer reach walks, and the hub overrides.
keyExports.RepoContextFileConfig: The shape a workspace may actually write.
keyExports.ResolvedConfig: The fully resolved shape, with no optional fields left.
keyExports.loadConfig: Reads and resolves the configuration from a directory.

assumptions: Unknown keys are stripped but reported: a typo produces a warning naming the path rather than being silently ignored, which is the difference between a setting that did not apply and one nobody noticed.
Every field is optional with a default, so a missing or empty configuration is a supported state rather than an error.

The response ceiling is empirically derived rather than round: it is set below the point where a dense response exceeds a host's context budget, with margin, because dense structured text tokenizes far denser than prose.
An environment override is applied only when it parses and clears the floor; otherwise the configured value stands and a warning explains why.
The embedding model is deliberately not configurable, since the index and the model have to agree.
There is no network transport in the configuration shape; the server speaks over standard streams only.
There is no migration path, which is why new fields must be optional and defaulted rather than breaking.

sideEffects.description: reads the configuration file from the given directory

risks: A schema-invalid configuration is discarded whole rather than repaired: the load warns, then resolves as if the file were absent. One bad value drops every valid sibling setting in the same file, and the build proceeds on defaults with nothing but a warning line to say so.
Turning the plugin defaults off leaves an empty registry, so a configuration that does so without supplying replacements yields an empty graph.
Environment overrides win over the file, so a workspace can behave differently from its committed configuration.
patterns: One resolved object for every consumer, so no component reads the file itself or reimplements a default.
Validate, warn, then resolve: unknown input is surfaced before it is discarded.
annotation.flowDescription: Single configuration spine for CLI, MCP, graph build, architecture analysis strictness, and context-session quality gates.
invariants: A resolved configuration has no absent fields.
A configured response ceiling never falls below the floor.
The configuration shape contains no network listener.
annotation.integrationPoints: Architecture thresholds are resolved through mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/config; the context-quality defaults come from mod:repovine/src/context-quality/session-store; scan patterns from mod:repovine/src/scan-filters; workspace path safety from mod:repovine/src/paths; warnings are reported through mod:repovine/src/cli/ui. The resolved object is consumed by the build stages and the server runtime.
annotation.dataFlow: configuration file → schema validation with unknown keys reported → defaults filled → environment overrides applied where valid → one resolved configuration used by the build, the server, the analysis and the annotation policy.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_ANNOTATIONS_FILE: Overrides the annotations file path after a safety check
envDependencies.REPOVINE_MCP_MAX_CHARS: Overrides the response ceiling when it parses and clears the floor
envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Enables verbose server and pipeline logging

annotation.summary: Turns one scored MCP tool response into the event the context-quality session store records. Echoes back only a whitelisted set of request fields, measures the response size, and derives the per-event metrics the scoring uses: whether a search fell back to OR, how export-symbol-dominated a response was, which stable anchor it established, whether a dependency query asked for impact, and whether the result leaned on test packages.

keyExports.BuildContextEventInput: The inputs: sequence number, tool name, arguments, parsed result, response text, and the two configured thresholds.
keyExports.buildContextEvent: Builds the event: whitelisted request echo, response size, and the derived metrics.

assumptions: The request echo is a whitelist of structural argument names, so annotation bodies and merge payloads stay out of the session record. Free-form arguments on the list — the search query and the body grep pattern — are copied verbatim and persisted with every recorded call.
The flood ratio and the recovery window come from configuration rather than being fixed here, so calibration is a config change.
A stable anchor is recorded only for the navigation tools and only when the response's confidence and scope kind make it anchor-eligible.
risks: Flood detection is a ratio heuristic over a search's returned page, so a legitimately broad search can be flagged as export-symbol dominated.
OR-search recovery is measured within a configured window, so mis-tuning that window shifts the noise penalty in both directions.
Metrics are derived from the parsed result envelope, so a tool whose envelope shape changes stops contributing its metrics without any error.
patterns: A capability-dominant search is recognized by the ratio of export symbols in the response rather than by the query text.
Empty results are scored by why they were empty: the diagnostic reason and an unresolved scope drive the low-confidence penalty.
invariants: Metrics come from the parsed result envelope, not from raw transport bytes alone.
The request echo is a whitelist, so a new argument is absent from events until it is explicitly added.
annotation.integrationPoints: Events are appended by the session store in mod:repovine/src/context-quality/session-store and read back when a session quality report is produced; the event and metric shapes come from mod:repovine/src/context-quality/types.
annotation.dataFlow: MCP tool result and response text → buildContextEvent → event appended to the session → session quality report.

annotation.summary: Stores context-quality sessions, rolls MCP responses into aggregates, persists compact session state, and produces the advisory ContextQualityReport. After D5 falsification the shipped default overall is the observable inspect_node baseline (1 after any inspect, otherwise 0); the former multi-signal weights remain configurable only for experiments, while aggregates and rejectReasons remain fully reported.

keyExports.ContextSessionStore: The store: records tool calls, produces reports, consumes or purges sessions, and optionally persists them.
keyExports.DEFAULT_CONTEXT_QUALITY_CONFIG: Fallback weights, thresholds and enforcement mode when the workspace config omits them.
keyExports.GetContextQualityReportOptions: Report options, including whether reading the report consumes the session.
keyExports.RecordToolCallInput: One recorded call: session id, tool, arguments, parsed result and response text.
keyExports.ResolvedContextSessionPolicy: The effective policy: phase, mode, thresholds, minimum anchors, byte budget, and whether the session is required and retained.
keyExports.bootstrapContextSessionsOnMcpStart: Purges stale session files at server start when the workspace asks for it.
keyExports.calculateReport: Builds the report: score, noise penalty, structure bonus, anchors, reject reasons and follow-ups.
keyExports.resolveContextSessionPolicy: Merges the per-assignment policy over the workspace defaults for the active phase.

assumptions: A session is identified by the id the caller passes on each MCP call, so a run that omits or rotates it fragments its own record.
Stable anchors are recorded as graph ids and remain provenance evidence independently of the advisory overall score.
Non-default context-quality weights are experimental until a labelled corpus meets the documented AUC, false-reject, and false-accept return bar.
Persistence is unconditional for calls carrying a session id; configuration controls event detail, retention, and purge behavior.

sideEffects.description: loads persisted sessions from the engine cache directory
persists a compact session form and removes files on purge or consume
holds the per-process session map

risks: A scope that does not resolve to graph nodes cannot establish stable anchors, so a session over off-graph work fails the anchor requirement for a structural reason rather than because the work was poor; the reject reason names the missing anchors, not the real cause.
Rotating session ids without purging accumulates session files in the cache directory.
A mis-tuned byte budget or anchor minimum turns the gate into a source of false rejections in enforcing mode.
patterns: An in-process map with optional compact persistence: the harness expects one stable session id per run rather than durable cross-run history.
A recovery discount applies when a weak search is followed by a narrowing call within the configured window, so the score measures the trajectory rather than a single bad query.
invariants: With the shipped default weights, overall is 1 exactly when inspectCallCount is non-zero and 0 otherwise.
Reject reasons and aggregate diagnostics remain available even though compliance does not hard-gate the unvalidated score.
A report carrying reject reasons never sets acceptHandoff=true.
The assignment policy is merged over workspace defaults, never the other way round.
Anchors are recorded as graph ids, so provenance checks compare like with like.
annotation.integrationPoints: Events are built by mod:repovine/src/context-quality/metrics and typed by mod:repovine/src/context-quality/types; the MCP layer records every scored call here, the annotation write path checks provenance against the recorded anchors, and the compliance check reads the resulting report.
annotation.stateShape: ContextSessionStore holds Map<sessionId, ContextSession> with rolling aggregates and optional requestEchoes.
annotation.dataFlow: contextSessionId on MCP calls -> response-derived events -> persisted aggregates and anchors -> binary default overall plus full rejectReasons/followups -> advisory MCP/CLI/compliance report.

annotation.summary: Type-only contracts for MCP context-quality scoring and Agent Protocol handoff gates: session lifecycle (ContextSession, ContextEvent), per-tool metrics (ContextEventMetrics), weighted noise/structure scoring (ContextQualityWeights), phase-specific thresholds, enforcement modes (harness vs client), and the ContextQualityReport consumed by get_context_session_quality and compliance validators.

keyExports.ContextPhase: explore | implement | annotate — drives per-phase threshold lookup.
keyExports.ContextQualityConfig: Repo defaults: weights, thresholds per phase, recoveryWindow, exportSymbolFloodRatio, purgeSessionsOnMcpStart.
keyExports.ContextQualityReport: Handoff verdict: overall score, acceptHandoff, rejectReasons, aggregates.stableAnchors.
keyExports.ContextRejectReason: Stable reject codes including NO_RECORDED_EVENTS, NO_STABLE_ANCHORS, CAPABILITY_FLOOD.
keyExports.ContextSessionPolicy: Per-assignment overrides: required, mode, phase, thresholds, minAnchors, byteBudget, retain.

assumptions: Consumers are session-store, metrics, MCP middleware, and harness compliance — no runtime logic here.
Reject reason string literals are part of the stable harness API.
ContextSessionPolicy.assignmentScope filters which graph nodes count as stable anchors.
risks: Schema drift vs repovine.config contextQuality JSON breaks policy resolution at MCP startup.
New ContextRejectReason values require harness validator updates.
patterns: Phase-specific thresholds in ContextQualityConfig.thresholds mirror repovine.config contextQuality section.
invariants: Session ids are opaque strings; metrics store scope kinds/ids, not source code.
ContextRequestEcho stores whitelisted request fields only.
annotation.integrationPoints: session-store, metrics, repovine.config contextQuality, Agent Protocol contextSessionId.
annotation.dataFlow: Config + assignment policy types → session-store scoring → ContextQualityReport → harness compliance and client warnings.

annotation.summary: A development script that builds the graph and serializes a readable projection of it to the cache directory, in one or both of two formats. It exists so the graph can be inspected as a file rather than through the tools, which is what makes a structural regression visible in a diff.
assumptions: The serialized form is a trimmed projection rather than the graph itself: per module its identity, file, domains, imports and a flattened view of its exports, with the optional route, environment and conditional-render detail when present.
Export detail is gathered by walking the export children of each module node, so the dump reflects what the graph holds rather than re-reading source.
Command-line flags select the format; with neither, both are written.
Output goes to the cache directory, which is untracked, so a dump never enters the working tree by accident.
It runs at module top level and exports nothing; it is invoked directly.

sideEffects.description: scans the repository through the first stage
writes the serialized graph to the cache directory
prints progress

risks: The dump contains the full structure of the analyzed repository — paths, module names, exported symbols — so a copy moved out of the untracked cache discloses the shape of a private codebase.
On a large repository the serialized output reaches multiple megabytes, which is fine as a file and unwieldy as anything else.
It rebuilds from scratch every run rather than reading an existing snapshot, so it costs a full cold build each time.
patterns: A file-shaped view of the graph, which is what lets a structural change be reviewed as a diff rather than inspected node by node.
annotation.flowDescription: Top-level CLI script: argv flags → collectRepositoryFactsAsync → composeRepositoryGraph → buildDump → write graph.yaml/json under .repovine/.cache.
invariants: It is not part of the server runtime or any published entry point.
It exports nothing.
Output is confined to the cache directory.
extensionPoints: A new node field worth reviewing is added to the projection so it appears in the dump.
annotation.integrationPoints: Builds through mod:repovine/src/stage1 and mod:repovine/src/stage2, walks the result with mod:repovine/src/graph, and resolves locations through mod:repovine/src/paths; the record shapes come from mod:repovine/src/types.
annotation.dataFlow: flags → first-stage snapshot → second-stage graph → trimmed per-module projection → one or both serialized files in the cache directory.

annotation.summary: Crash-atomic, power-loss-durable filesystem writers: async/sync writeFileAtomic use per-write PID+UUID temp files (write → fsync → rename → dir fsync), while writeJsonObjectStreamed emits one large JSON field in batches without a full in-memory stringify. The streamed path loops on bytesWritten so a short write never publishes truncated JSON, and directory fsync is fail-closed. writeFileAtomic/writeFileAtomicSync additionally retry the final rename on win32-only transient errors (EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY), up to 10 attempts with linear backoff (15ms * attempt).

keyExports.StreamedJsonField: Describes one large JSON object field streamed as array or record members.
keyExports.writeFileAtomic: Async atomic write: mkdir, temp write, fsync, rename, cleanup on failure.
keyExports.writeFileAtomicSync: Sync variant used on hot paths like annotation serialize.
keyExports.writeJsonObjectStreamed: Streams one large array/record field in byte batches; returns the byte count written.

assumptions: Same-directory temp file (.tmp.<pid>.<random>) + fsync + rename gives crash safety on the local filesystem.
The directory-open fd used for directory fsync exists on POSIX; Windows cannot open a directory this way.
Rename retry (renameWithRetry/renameWithRetrySync) only engages on process.platform === 'win32'; the same errno on POSIX is a real permission failure and is not retried.
EXDEV is deliberately excluded from the retry code set: the temp file lives in the target's directory, so cross-device rename cannot occur.

sideEffects.description: mkdir, temp write, fsync, rename, parent-directory fsync; rm temp on failure
opens the parent directory read-only to fsync it

risks: The streamed writer must loop until the whole chunk lands (write(2) may persist fewer bytes on ENOSPC / network FS) — counting intended bytes instead publishes a truncated, unparseable cache.

Directory fsync is fail-closed: the open() errno tolerance is platform-gated (EISDIR/EPERM tolerated ONLY on win32); the same errno on POSIX, every other errno, an unknown code, and a no-code exception rethrow, so a real fd-exhaustion / disk error surfaces rather than silently dropping durability.
writeJsonObjectStreamed's final rename calls fsPromises.rename directly, not renameWithRetry — it does not get the win32 transient-rename retry that writeFileAtomic/writeFileAtomicSync have.
patterns: Crash-safe persistence primitive for .repovine cache and repovine.annots.json.
invariants: Temp files use .tmp.<pid>.<random> suffix beside target path.
Parent directory fsynced after rename on supporting platforms.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used by mod:repovine/src/stage1/cache, mod:repovine/src/semantic/store, and mod:repovine/src/annotations/store for disk persistence.
annotation.dataFlow: snapshot/cache/semantic-index/annotation writers → writeFileAtomic|writeFileAtomicSync|writeJsonObjectStreamed → temp path → fsync → rename to final path → parent-dir fsync.

annotation.summary: Path containment primitives shared by every surface that must keep a read inside the repository root. Two rules are kept separate on purpose: a lexical rule that judges the name a path spells, and a symlink-resolving rule that judges the bytes the path would actually yield. Only node builtins are imported, so the module has no load-time side effects and can be pulled in from any layer.

keyExports.isLexicallyInsideRepo: Name-only containment; suits labels and cheap pre-filters, and never touches the filesystem.
keyExports.isPathInsideRepo: Read guard: the path clears the lexical test and its realpath resolves inside the resolved root.

assumptions: A relative filePath is meant relative to repoRoot, not to the process working directory.
A target that cannot be resolved yields no bytes, so it keeps the lexical verdict and the caller's own read reports the errno.
Comparison is case-sensitive, matching the rest of the engine's security-sensitive path handling.

sideEffects.description: isPathInsideRepo resolves both the target and the root through realpathSync

risks.text: isLexicallyInsideRepo is a label, not a guard: it accepts a symlink that resolves out of the repository. A caller about to read bytes wants isPathInsideRepo.

risks: The guard resolves the path and the caller reads it separately, so a target replaced between the two calls is read as the caller found it.
Hard links are invisible to realpath, so a hard link to an out-of-repo file reads as contained.
patterns: The lexical test runs first, so an obviously outside path is refused without any filesystem work.
Both rules share one relative-escape predicate, so a name that leaves the base is judged identically everywhere.
invariants: A path whose realpath resolves outside the resolved root is never reported as contained.
The root itself is contained.
annotation.integrationPoints: Guards the MCP source-body reads in mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/node-body and the brief-path validation in mod:repovine/src/agents/roles-source.
annotation.dataFlow: repoRoot + filePath -> resolve against the root -> relative-escape test -> realpath both ends -> contained or not.

annotation.summary: One-line-per-entry JSON serializer for .repovine/ cache files whose bulk is a single keyed map, mirroring the annotations file layout (serializeAnnotationFileFromRaw) so a changed entry is a one-line diff rather than a moved block.

keyExports.serializeKeyedRecordFile: (header, mapKey, entries) => string. Emits scalar header fields in insertion order, then one sorted-by-key line per map entry as `    "key": <compact-json>`. A value that stringifies to undefined is written as null. Output always ends with a trailing newline.

invariants: Entry keys (ids) are always sorted before serialization, so identical input produces byte-identical output regardless of insertion order.

annotation.summary: In-memory RepositoryGraph utilities and MCP projection: graph mutators, containment/link queries, capped/deduplicated NodeView links, breadcrumbs, bounded impact traversal with one-hop reexports, import closure, and stats.

keyExports.MAX_NODE_VIEW_LINKS: Maximum unique links embedded in a single NodeView response.
keyExports.addEdge: Adds a directed edge with optional GraphEdgeMetadata to adjacency indexes.
keyExports.buildNodeView: Projects a node with children and at most MAX_NODE_VIEW_LINKS unique relation/target links, reporting total when capped.
keyExports.forwardImportClosure: BFS over import edges from a start module up to maxDepth.
keyExports.getImpact: Bounded impact BFS that includes a re-export target but does not expand through a node reached only by reexports.
keyExports.getLinks: Returns the complete non-contains outbound edge list; response capping happens only in buildNodeView.
keyExports.graphStats: Counts nodes/edges and their types/kinds for refresh deltas.
keyExports.pathFromRoot: Builds ancestor NodeView breadcrumbs to a focus node.

assumptions: Per MCP refresh cycle RepositoryGraph is the authoritative snapshot for tool responses.
buildNodeView levelMap: root=0, package/runtime-resource/domain=1, module/template=2, export-symbol=3.
getImpact downstream follows inEdges (importers), upstream follows outEdges.
risks: getImpact maxDepth and the one-hop reexport rule intentionally omit distant transitive consumers.
Capped NodeView links require analyze_dependencies or trace_flow when complete traversal is needed.
Mutable addNode/addEdge are intended only for graph construction.
patterns: graph/index barrel re-exports applyValidated, validateGraphDelta, emptyGraphDelta from graph/delta and owningModuleId from graph/node-ids.
invariants: getChildren follows contains edges only.
getLinks remains complete and exposes tagSource on tagged edges.
buildNodeView preserves first-seen link order while deduplicating relation+target and caps only the response projection.
A node reached through reexports is included in impact but not recursively expanded unless another non-reexport path reaches it.
Edge validation, endpoint checks, and build-time dedup remain in graph/delta applyValidated.
annotation.integrationPoints: RepovineRuntime.graph; MCP inspect_node/map_context; analyze_dependencies; re-exports mod:repovine/src/graph/delta and mod:repovine/src/graph/node-ids.
annotation.dataFlow: Stage2 mutates RepositoryGraph → buildNodeView/pathFromRoot create bounded MCP projections → getImpact feeds dependency analysis with one-hop barrel inclusion; graph/delta remains the validated mutation boundary.

annotation.summary: Validation and merge layer for graph patches produced by the stage-2 interpreters. Validates a patch against the node and edge schemas, keeping the entries that pass and reporting the rest, then merges it into the live graph in a deterministic order with node and edge de-duplication. An untrusted merge additionally drops edges whose endpoints exist neither in the graph nor in the patch.

keyExports.ApplyGraphDeltaOptions: Merge options: the trusted flag and an optional logger.
keyExports.GraphDeltaLogLevel: The levels the logger is called with.
keyExports.GraphDeltaSchema: Schema for a patch of nodes and edges.
keyExports.GraphDeltaValidationResult: The validation outcome: overall success, the surviving patch, and the error messages.
keyExports.applyValidated: Merges a validated patch into the graph in sorted order, de-duplicating nodes and edges.
keyExports.emptyGraphDelta: The shared empty patch, used for no-op and error paths.
keyExports.validateGraphDelta: Validates a patch and returns the surviving entries alongside the errors.

assumptions: Validation is partial rather than all-or-nothing: entries that pass are kept even when siblings fail, so one bad edge does not discard an interpreter's whole contribution.
Application order is sorted rather than input order, which is what makes repeated builds byte-identical.
The default logger writes warnings and errors unconditionally; the verbose flag gates only a debug level this module never emits.

sideEffects.description: the merge mutates the repository graph in place
the default logger warns on every dropped entry, regardless of verbose settings

risks.text: Validation runs only when the caller opts in with trusted:false. The option defaults to trusting, so a call that omits it merges whatever shape it was handed straight into the live graph, and nothing in the signature says so. The stage-2 composer omits it.

risks: The endpoint check drops an edge whose from or to is absent from the merged graph on every path; the trusted default drops it silently, an untrusted merge logs a warning. Interpreters run one delta each in sequence, so an edge pointing at a node a later interpreter has yet to contribute is discarded with no record.
patterns: Deterministic sorted application keeps graph builds reproducible regardless of interpreter order.
invariants: Edges are de-duplicated by their endpoints, kind and stable metadata, so re-contributing the same edge is a no-op.
An untrusted merge admits an edge only when both endpoints are present in the graph or in the same patch.
annotation.integrationPoints: Re-exported through the graph barrel; the interpreter composer in mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/composer applies the built-in interpreters' patches through it, and the node and edge shapes come from mod:repovine/src/graph/model.
annotation.dataFlow: interpreter contribution -> validateGraphDelta -> applyValidated -> mutated repository graph.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Enables the default logger's debug level, which this module never emits

annotation.summary: Deterministic runtime-resource identity from InfraResource; Kubernetes ids encode namespace and original manifest kind while labels remain the plain logical resource name.
assumptions: Propagation review 2026-06-20: upstream types hash changed; InfraResource id normalization unchanged.
risks: Normalization must stay stable for annotation content hashes.
patterns: Normalization rules must stay stable across rebuilds for annotation hashes.
invariants: Collisions logged at debug only — callers should treat ids as opaque.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage2 runtime-resource node ids; annotations service-resource-hash.
annotation.dataFlow: provider resource keys → canonical resource:id string stable across rebuilds.

annotation.summary: Core repository-graph data model: NODE_TYPES/EDGE_KINDS taxonomy, NodeDataByType-keyed GraphNode discriminated union, RepositoryGraph container, and the stage1 RepositoryFactsSnapshot. Split from src/types.ts, which re-exports this as a compatibility barrel.

keyExports.EDGE_KINDS: 14 graph edge kinds const array (contains, imports, reexports, tagged, implements, publishes, consumes, binds_to, uses_env, infra, routes_to, renders, extends, includes); EdgeKind derives from it.
keyExports.GraphNode: Discriminated union keyed by NodeType; data is typed per type via NodeDataByType.
keyExports.NODE_DATA_KEYS: Runtime mirror of NodeDataByType keys, validated at compile-time to stay in sync.
keyExports.NODE_TYPES: 7 graph node kinds const array (root, package, module, export-symbol, runtime-resource, domain, template); NodeType type derives from it.
keyExports.NodeDataByType: Discriminated record mapping NodeType to its data shape: RootNodeData, PackageNodeData, ModuleNodeData, ExportSymbolNodeData, RuntimeResourceNodeData, DomainNodeData, TemplateNodeData.
keyExports.RepositoryFactsSnapshot: Stage1 facts output: repoRoot, timestamp, packages, modules, infraModules, templates, linkingConfig, bundleOutputHandlerMap.
keyExports.RepositoryGraph: In-memory graph container: nodes, edges, out/inEdges, byType, memoized hubInDegreeThreshold.

assumptions: Downstream consumers import PackageInfo/ModuleInfo/InfraModuleInfo/SsrMarkers from @repovine/plugin-sdk; this module shapes how those facts become graph nodes.
engineBuildId is set only in development so a rebuilt engine is not silently reused against cached facts; it is undefined in an installed package.
A GraphNode's data field is optional per type; consumers must not assume every node carries populated fields.

risks.text: Wide contract (~52 downstream importers): changing NodeData interfaces, EDGE_KINDS/NODE_TYPES, or the GraphNode shape ripples through stage1, stage2, MCP, annotations, and plugins. Off-limits to casual edits.

risks: NODE_DATA_KEYS must mirror NodeDataByType exactly; compile-time guard _assertNodeDataKeysExact fails the build on drift.
patterns: Core types split into focused modules; src/types.ts is a compatibility barrel.
invariants: NodeType derives from NODE_TYPES and EdgeKind from EDGE_KINDS — single source of truth.
NODE_DATA_KEYS is exactly the key set of NodeDataByType; enforced at compile time.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage1, stage2, graph/index, graph/node-view, annotations, MCP tools; consumes @repovine/plugin-sdk types.
annotation.dataFlow: source plugins produce facts → stage1 snapshot assembly → stage2 maps snapshot entries to GraphNode/GraphEdge → stored in RepositoryGraph.

annotation.summary: Pure helper mapping export-symbol node ids to owning module ids. export:${modulePath}/${exportName} → mod: path before final slash; used by annotation provenance and Agent Protocol grounding.

keyExports.owningModuleId: export: → mod: string transform; undefined for non-cap ids or ids without separable export segment.

assumptions: export: prefix is seven characters; slice after prefix not cap-era four-char slice.
risks: Malformed export ids without slash return undefined.
patterns: Used by Agent Protocol compliance and write_annotation provenance.
annotation.flowDescription: export: node id → owningModuleId pure string transform for annotation provenance checks.
annotation.integrationPoints: agents/validation provenance gate; mcp/lib/annotations write_annotation provenance warning; graph/index re-exports for backward compatibility.
annotation.dataFlow: export: anchor in context session stableAnchors → owningModuleId → mod: id compared to annotationsWritten node for grounding.

annotation.summary: The projection types for a node as the MCP layer returns it: the core view with its children, links and symbol detail, the detail shape adding body, search and investigate enrichments, the child entry with access metadata, and the tag union naming why a reference must be inspected. Split out of the shared types so the projection lives beside the graph that builds it.

keyExports.InvestigateTag: The must-inspect reasons a reference can carry: risk, boundary, effect, unannotated, wiring, co-change and hub.
keyExports.NodeView: The core projection: identity, level, children, links with pagination, symbol detail, and the annotation with its metadata.
keyExports.NodeViewChild: A child entry extended with access and internal-declaration metadata.
keyExports.NodeViewDetail: The view plus the MCP enrichments: body slices, body search results and their truncation reporting, and the investigate pointers.

assumptions: The projection is built beside the graph and consumed by the MCP layer, so the dependency runs one way and the MCP layer never defines the shape it receives.
Link and body payloads carry their own truncation reporting, so a caller can tell a complete list from a capped one.

risks.text: The tag union is the published vocabulary the MCP responses expose: a tag is only meaningful when the projection actually emits it, and adding one without a producing mechanic yields a value no response ever carries.

risks: The union has grown as delivery mechanics were added, so a reader working from an older description will not find the topology-derived tags.
patterns: Truncation is reported rather than hidden, so a capped projection is distinguishable from a complete one.
annotation.integrationPoints: Takes its node and edge vocabulary from mod:repovine/src/graph/model and its annotation shape from mod:repovine/src/annotations/types; built by the projection helper in the graph barrel and consumed by the MCP tool handlers. The tag union is kept in step with the mechanics declared in mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry.

annotation.summary: Scoped resolution of an infra logical id to one runtime-resource node. Candidates matching the label are narrowed by the reference's own scope — declaring template for cloud providers, namespace for Kubernetes — and ambiguity scope does not settle is returned unresolved rather than picked. Also owns the nested-stack alias table (FooTableName → FooTable).
assumptions: Called from both the graph builder (interpreters/infra-runtime-links/graph) and the query-time projection (mcp/lib/topology), so both sides read the same resolution.
A resource declared by two documents collapses onto one node; RuntimeResourceNodeData.declaredIn carries every declaring path.

risks.text: A caller passing an empty scope gets no in-scope candidate, so a repo-wide unique label still resolves but two same-named resources return unresolved. Callers must thread the declaring document.

patterns: Prefer same-scope, fall back to repo-wide uniqueness, otherwise report a gap.
invariants: The exact label decides on its own: an alias match is only consulted when the exact label matched nothing.
A Kubernetes reference never resolves outside its own namespace; an absent namespace on both sides is the same scope.
Two or more candidates that scope does not separate yield status 'unresolved', never an arbitrary pick — resolution order must not depend on scan order.
extensionPoints: New provider scoping rules extend candidateInScope; new nested-stack identifier conventions extend resourceLogicalIdAliases.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/interpreters/infra-runtime-links/graph records unresolved results on the referencing node; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/topology reuses the same resolution for the trace_flow projection.
annotation.dataFlow: logicalId + InfraRefScope → label match over runtime-resource nodes → scope filter → resolved serviceId or unresolved{reason, candidates}.

annotation.summary: Registration descriptor for the built-in Compose plugin. Wraps the compose parser and declares the domain its services and secrets land in. All parsing lives in the parser module; this file only tells the engine the plugin exists and what territory it owns.

keyExports.default: The same descriptor as the module's default export.
keyExports.dockerComposeIacPlugin: The descriptor: plugin id, its parser, and the compose domain.

assumptions: Only files this plugin's parser recognizes by name are claimed; an arbitrary YAML file with a services key is not.
Service inheritance is not resolved and external compose files are not merged, so the parse covers what one file declares.
risks: An inheritance chain or an included external file leaves the graph describing only the local declarations, which understates what the stack actually runs.
A secret reached only through an environment file yields a synthesized stub rather than a resource with real content behind it.
patterns: A thin registration barrel delegating to the parser module.
invariants: Service inheritance is never resolved.
The services map is the root of the parse.
annotation.integrationPoints: Built through the plugin factory in mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, wraps mod:repovine/src/iac-plugins/docker-compose/parser, and is registered by the stage1 IaC bootstrap.
annotation.dataFlow: compose files → the parser → service and secret resources → stage2 links each service's build file to its dockerfile resource.

annotation.summary: Docker Compose parser. Recognizes a compose file by name and by the presence of a services map, emits one resource per service carrying its image, build context and resolved build file, and records the secret references a service reaches through mounted secrets, the file-suffixed environment convention and its environment files. Declared top-level secrets become resources, and secrets implied by an environment file are synthesized.

keyExports.dockerComposeParser: The parser: services first, then declared and synthesized secret resources, each with attributes and references.

assumptions: A service's secret references are gathered from three conventions: mounted secrets, environment variables whose value points at the mounted secret path, and referenced environment files.
Services are emitted before secrets so the resource order follows the order a reader scans the file in.
The build file path is resolved against the service's build context rather than the workspace root, using posix-joined relative paths regardless of host platform.
risks: Service inheritance through the extends keyword is not resolved, so an inherited image, build or secret is invisible.
A secret mounted under a renamed target is reached by the file-suffixed environment convention under that new name, so the reference links to a synthesized stub rather than the declared secret.
An external secret with no file path yields only a stub, so it appears as a resource with nothing behind it.
Service dependency conditions are read but not modeled as edges, so startup ordering is not represented in the graph.
patterns: Three independent secret conventions are collected into one reference set, so a service is linked however its author expressed the dependency.
invariants: The extends keyword is never resolved.
Services are emitted before secret resources.
annotation.integrationPoints: Implements the parser contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src and uses the attribute, hashing and path-domain helpers in mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/utils; the build file it records is what stage2 links to the resource produced by the dockerfile parser.
annotation.dataFlow: compose document -> per-service resources with image, build and secret references -> declared and synthesized secret resources -> infra delta -> stage2 runtime links the build file to its dockerfile resource.

annotation.summary: Registration descriptor for the built-in Dockerfile plugin. Wraps the Dockerfile parser and declares the domain its resources land in.

keyExports.default: The same descriptor as the module's default export.
keyExports.dockerfileIacPlugin: The descriptor: plugin id, its parser, and the dockerfile domain.

assumptions: The plugin exists mainly to give build references a target: it anchors each Dockerfile in the graph so compose can point at it.
Only files matching the conventional naming are claimed.
risks: Only the first base image is captured, so a multi-stage build's runtime image is not what the resource reports.
Build directives beyond the base image are not parsed, so a Dockerfile's environment and copied paths are invisible to the graph.
patterns: A thin registration barrel delegating to the parser module.
invariants: The parse is read-only and static.
Each Dockerfile yields one resource identified by its repo-relative path, and that path is the identity a compose build reference resolves against.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wraps the parser in mod:repovine/src/iac-plugins/dockerfile/parser and is registered by the stage1 IaC bootstrap.
annotation.dataFlow: Dockerfiles → the parser → one resource each carrying the base image → stage2 container linking and the cross-reference from a compose service's build declaration.

annotation.summary: Minimal Dockerfile parser. Matches the conventional filenames, reads the text for the first base-image directive, tags the resource with its path-derived domain, and emits one resource per file. Its purpose is to give the compose parser's build reference something to link to rather than to model the build itself.

keyExports.dockerfileParser: The parser: one resource per Dockerfile, carrying the first base image and the path domain.

assumptions: Only the first base-image directive is captured, which identifies the file rather than describing its build stages.
Build directives such as environment, argument, run and copy lines are deliberately not modeled; this parser exists to anchor the file in the graph.
Matching is by filename pattern, so a Dockerfile under a non-conventional name is not picked up.
The resource id is the file's relative path with backslashes normalized to forward slashes, so the id matches regardless of host platform.
risks: A multi-stage build surfaces only its first base image, so the final runtime image can differ from what the resource reports.
A base-image directive written in an unusual form may not match the line pattern, leaving the resource without a base image rather than failing.
patterns: A line parser rather than a syntax tree: it recognizes one directive and stops.
invariants: The parse is read-only over the supplied text; no filesystem or network access happens here.
One file yields exactly one resource.
The resource id is always posix-separated, never carrying a backslash even on a Windows-produced relative path.
annotation.integrationPoints: Implements the parser contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, uses the hashing and path-domain helpers in mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/utils, and is the target the build reference from mod:repovine/src/iac-plugins/docker-compose/parser links to (that parser also posix-normalizes its build path so the two ids match).
annotation.dataFlow: Dockerfile text -> first base image and path domain -> single resource with a posix-normalized id -> infra delta -> stage2 cross-links it to the compose service that builds it.

annotation.summary: Registration descriptor for the built-in Helm plugin. Ships two parsers, the values parser and the chart-manifest parser, and declares the domain both land in. The parser order is deliberate: values files must be claimed here before the Kubernetes parser, registered later, would treat them as plain manifests.

keyExports.default: The same descriptor as the module's default export.
keyExports.helmIacPlugin: The descriptor: plugin id, its two parsers in values-first order, and the helm domain.

assumptions: Chart templates are never rendered, so a value that a chart would compute at install time stays as written.
The values parser is listed before the chart parser, which matters only for a document both could claim.
risks: Because templates are not rendered, a resource name or image that a chart assembles at install time is absent from the graph.

Both parsers gate on document shape, so registration order settles almost nothing here: the Kubernetes parser claims a document only when it carries top-level apiVersion and kind, which a values file does not. Order decides only for a values file shaped like a manifest.
patterns: A thin registration barrel: both parsers live in their own modules and this file only declares them and their domain.
invariants: Template rendering never happens at parse time.
The values parser is listed before the chart parser.
annotation.integrationPoints: Built through the plugin factory in mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, wraps mod:repovine/src/iac-plugins/helm/parsers/values and mod:repovine/src/iac-plugins/helm/parsers/chart, and is registered by the stage1 IaC bootstrap.
annotation.dataFlow: chart manifest and values files → the two parsers → infra resources → snapshot → the helm domain in the graph.

annotation.summary: Helm chart-manifest parser. Recognizes a chart manifest by its filename and by the version-and-name contract, explicitly rejecting a document shaped like a CloudFormation template, and emits a single release resource carrying the chart's version, application version and description. Chart metadata only: the templates directory is not parsed here.

keyExports.helmChartParser: The parser: one release resource per chart manifest, named from the manifest or from its directory.

assumptions: A chart is identified by a second-generation API version together with a name; anything else is skipped rather than guessed at.
The resource id falls back to the chart directory name when the manifest omits a name, a path parse() carries defensively even though supports() already gates on the name being present.
Only the manifest is read; the values file is handled by its own parser and the templates are not parsed at all.
risks: A chart declaring an older API version is skipped entirely, so it contributes no resource and the chart directory looks empty in the graph.
Because only the manifest is read, a chart's actual workloads and images come from the values parser, so a chart with no values file yields little more than its name.
patterns: An explicit negative check against the CloudFormation shape, so one YAML document cannot be claimed by two parsers.
invariants: supports() requires the name string, so in the normal engine call path parse() only ever runs on a manifest that has a name.
annotation.integrationPoints: Implements the parser contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src and hashes its payload through mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/utils. Emits kind 'helm', which the plugin maps to the infra-helm domain -- the manifest and the values file remain separate infra modules, keyed by their own file paths, and meet only under that domain tag.
annotation.dataFlow: chart manifest -> release resource with version and description attributes -> infra delta -> its own infra module, tagged into the infra-helm domain alongside every other helm module in the repo.

annotation.summary: Helm values parser. Recognizes a values file by its chart layout or a sibling chart manifest, walks the document for nested image references and explicit secret references, and emits container-image resources plus de-duplicated secret resources, linking co-located secrets to the images that sit in the same values subtree.

keyExports.HelmImageRef: A discovered image: the dotted key path, the repository and an optional tag.
keyExports.HelmSecretRef: A discovered secret reference: the dotted key path and the secret name.
keyExports.collectHelmImages: Recursive walk for nested image objects carrying a repository and tag.
keyExports.collectHelmSecrets: Recursive walk for explicit secret reference keys, without guessing from substrings such as password.
keyExports.helmValuesParser: The parser: emits container-image resources and de-duplicated secret resources with linking references.

assumptions: The parser receives a path suitable for locating a sibling chart manifest, which is the authoritative fallback when the directory layout is ambiguous.
Secret discovery is deliberately explicit-key based, so a values entry merely named like a credential is not reported as a secret.

sideEffects.description: checks for a sibling chart manifest when the path heuristics do not identify the chart

risks: Templated image strings are reported as written: chart templates are not rendered, so a value assembled at render time is only best-effort.
Parsing cost grows linearly with the values document, so a very large file slows the scan.
patterns: Chart detection accepts the conventional directory layouts and falls back to a sibling chart manifest as the authoritative marker.
Images are linked to the explicit secret references sharing their values subtree, which is what turns two independent findings into one relationship.
invariants: A chart-manifest-shaped document is rejected rather than parsed as values.
Support requires both a chart-location signal and at least one image or secret signal.
Secret resources are marked external with the helm-values source.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered first among the helm plugin's parsers; implements the parser contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src and hashes payloads through mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/utils.
annotation.dataFlow: values document plus chart marker → image and secret walkers → container-image and external secret resources with linking references → the runtime and config-surface views.

annotation.summary: Registration descriptor for the built-in Kubernetes plugin. Wraps the workload parser and declares the domain its resources land in. The parser list is the extension point: additional sub-parsers, for networking or for custom resources, are added there rather than by changing the workload parser.

keyExports.default: The same descriptor as the module's default export.
keyExports.kubernetesIacPlugin: The descriptor: plugin id, its parser list, and the Kubernetes domain.

assumptions: This plugin registers after the Helm plugin, which is what lets Helm values files be claimed before they would be read as plain manifests.
Manifests are parsed as written; overlay and patch mechanisms are not applied.
Cluster-scoped defaults are invisible, since only the repository's files are read.
risks: A manifest assembled by an overlay or patch tool parses as its base, so the graph shows what is committed rather than what would be applied.
Custom resources beyond the mapped kinds fall into the generic bucket until a dedicated sub-parser is added.
patterns: A thin registration barrel whose parser array is the documented extension point for further manifest families.
invariants: Overlays are never applied during parse.
Workload parsing is delegated to the parser module rather than done here.
annotation.integrationPoints: Built through the plugin factory in mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, wraps mod:repovine/src/iac-plugins/kubernetes/parsers/workloads, and is registered by the stage1 IaC bootstrap after the Helm plugin.
annotation.dataFlow: manifest files → the workload parser → infra resources in the Kubernetes domain → later enriched by the runtime linking stage.

annotation.summary: Kubernetes manifest parser. Accepts a document carrying an API version and a kind, explicitly refusing the CloudFormation and serverless-transform shapes so one YAML file cannot be claimed by two parsers, maps the standard workload and service kinds onto the engine's resource kinds, enriches the resource with pod-level attributes and environment references, and emits one resource per document.

keyExports.kubernetesParser: The parser: one resource per manifest, with its kind mapped and its attributes enriched.

assumptions: Several workload kinds collapse onto one deployment kind, since for graph purposes they are the same sort of thing: something that runs containers.
A secret manifest maps onto the generic secret kind so it lines up with secrets discovered by the other parsers.
An unrecognized kind falls back to the custom-resource kind rather than being dropped.
risks: Templated image strings pass through as written, so a manifest rendered by a chart reports the template rather than the resolved image.
Overlay and patch mechanisms are not applied, so the parsed manifest is the base rather than what would actually be deployed.
The refusal of CloudFormation-shaped documents is by shape, so a manifest that happens to carry those fields is skipped even if it is genuinely Kubernetes.
patterns: Kind mapping through a table, so supporting another workload kind is a table entry.
Negative shape checks up front, which is how the several YAML parsers stay mutually exclusive.
invariants: Support requires both an API version and a kind on the document.
An unknown kind becomes a custom resource rather than being discarded.
annotation.integrationPoints: Implements the parser contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, enriches through mod:repovine/src/stage1/k8s-workload and hashes through mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/utils; registered by the kubernetes plugin index.
annotation.dataFlow: manifest document -> kind mapping and attribute enrichment -> one resource -> infra delta -> stage2 container and ingress linking.

annotation.summary: Registration descriptor for the built-in AWS SAM and CloudFormation plugin. Wraps the parser, places both infra kinds in one shared domain because they are the same territory, marks lambda resources as owning code the linking stage should resolve back to a module, and declares the trigger-type metadata that drives entrypoint labelling and stream-edge wiring downstream.

keyExports.default: The same descriptor as the module's default export.
keyExports.samIacPlugin: The descriptor: plugin id, its parser, the shared domain for both kinds, the code-handler marker for lambdas, and the trigger-type metadata.

assumptions: SAM and plain CloudFormation share one domain, so a repository mixing both does not split into two unrelated infra territories.
