Trigger metadata is declared here rather than hardcoded downstream, so the entrypoint kinds and which triggers count as stream-like travel with the plugin.
The descriptor is published twice — a named binding and a default that aliases the same object — so the bootstrap can consume either without changing what is registered.
risks: Template intrinsic functions are not evaluated, so a resource whose logical id is computed at deploy time can fail to link its environment references.
A template carrying resources but no serverless transform still parses, and is reported as plain CloudFormation rather than SAM.
patterns: A thin registration barrel: all parsing lives in the parser module, and this file only declares what the engine needs to know about the plugin.
invariants: Both infra kinds resolve to the same domain.
Lambda is the only resource kind this plugin marks as owning a code handler; the marker is written into a registry shared with the other IaC plugins.
annotation.integrationPoints: Built through the plugin factory in mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, wraps mod:repovine/src/iac-plugins/sam/parser, and is registered by the stage1 IaC bootstrap.
annotation.dataFlow: template files → the parser → infra delta → stage1 assembles the infra module → stage2 resolves lambda handlers and labels entrypoints from the trigger metadata declared here.

annotation.summary: Parser for AWS SAM and plain CloudFormation templates. Turns each template resource into an infra resource with a classified kind, merges the global function environment into every template resource, resolves environment references, reads the access a lambda's Policies grant on each DynamoDB table, and synthesizes secret resources from parameters and dynamic references.

keyExports.samParser: The parser: walks the template resources, classifies kinds, merges globals, extracts environment and secret references, parses inline and standalone triggers, synthesizes secret resources, and reports the document as SAM or plain CloudFormation based on its transform.

assumptions: Only the top-level resources of a single template are interpreted: nested stacks, macros and transform expansions are not evaluated.
A template is reported as SAM when its transform names the serverless transform, and as plain CloudFormation otherwise.
Secret resources synthesized from parameters and dynamic references are de-duplicated by logical id, so the same secret referenced twice yields one resource.
risks: An unrecognized resource type is classified as other. Standalone trigger wiring never reaches it -- that path is gated on the lambda kind -- but its own inline events are parsed whatever its kind, so an unrecognized type carrying an events block does carry triggers.

A template that declares a global function environment gives every resource in it those variable names and their resolved references, so a queue or table is emitted carrying environment and secret references it does not declare.
A substitution-style environment reference can resolve without a target logical id, leaving the reference recorded but unlinked.

A route key that is not REST-shaped falls back to a websocket trigger that keeps the raw route key as its path and the API logical id as its queue reference, with no method. An inline websocket event carries neither method nor path.
Because nested stacks are not expanded, a template that delegates its resources to a child stack parses as nearly empty rather than as an error.
patterns: A resource-type map drives classification, so supporting a new AWS type is a table entry rather than new branching.
Triggers arrive from two directions, inline events on a function and standalone resources that point back at one, and both are merged onto the target.
invariants: Nested stacks and macros are never expanded; the view is a single template.
Table references discovered through IAM policies are appended as environment references on the owning lambda.
Synthesized secret resources are sorted deterministically, so identical input yields identical output.

Grant parsing reads three shapes: an inline Statement list, a referenced AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy document, and a SAM policy-template id. Deny statements are skipped — a subtraction the parser cannot evaluate must not widen a reported grant.
A target whose grant shape yields no verb keeps its env ref with access absent; the binding is reported with the access left unread rather than defaulted.
extensionPoints: SAM_POLICY_TEMPLATE_ACCESS maps new policy-template ids to modes; READ_ACTION_PREFIXES/WRITE_ACTION_PREFIXES classify new action verbs.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered by the SAM plugin index, implements the parser contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, and hashes resource payloads through mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/utils.
annotation.dataFlow: template document -> samParser -> infra delta of per-resource records with kinds, attributes, environment variables, references (with access where a grant was read) and triggers, plus synthesized secrets -> stage1 assembles the infra module -> stage2 links handlers and the runtime environment and secret edges -> trace_flow reports the access mode.

annotation.summary: Registration descriptor for the built-in Terraform plugin. Wraps the HCL parser, declares the terraform domain, and re-declares the lambda code-handler marker that the SAM plugin also registers, so a repository using only Terraform still gets its handlers linked back to code.

keyExports.default: The same descriptor as the module's default export.
keyExports.terraformIacPlugin: The descriptor: plugin id, its parser, the terraform domain, and the lambda code-handler marker.

assumptions: Resource-kind metadata is declared by every plugin that can produce the kind, so the marker is intentionally duplicated with the SAM plugin rather than shared.
Provider types the parser does not recognize still reach the graph as generic resources rather than being dropped.
Remote module sources are never fetched, so the parse describes the declarations present in the repository.
risks: A module block pointing at a remote registry stays opaque, so the resources it would create are absent from the graph.

The block scan balances braces over character offsets and handles heredocs, quoted strings with escapes, and `#` comments; nesting depth is unbounded. Braces inside `//` or `/* */` comments are read as code, so one of them ends a block early and drops its attributes, or unbalances the file and drops every resource after it. Env-map scanning skips no comments at all, so a `#` line inside an env map ends the map early and loses the remaining variables and references. All of these surface as missing resources or missing env refs; parsing never reports an error.
patterns: A thin registration barrel: the HCL work lives in the parser module and this file declares only what the engine needs.
invariants: Remote module sources are neither downloaded nor expanded at parse time.
An unrecognized provider type still appears in the graph, as a generic resource.
annotation.integrationPoints: Built through the plugin factory in mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, wraps mod:repovine/src/iac-plugins/terraform/parser, and is registered by the stage1 IaC bootstrap.
annotation.dataFlow: HCL files → the parser → resources with environment variables and references → snapshot → stage2 links lambda handlers back to code.

annotation.summary: Terraform parser built on a brace-balanced line scanner rather than a full HCL parse. Extracts resource, data and module blocks, maps their types onto the engine's resource kinds, pulls out string attributes and environment maps, and records environment references so the runtime linking can connect a resource to the code that reads it.

keyExports.terraformParser: The parser: scans blocks, resolves kinds, extracts attributes, environment variables and references, and emits one resource per block.

assumptions: Parsing is line-based with brace balancing, skipping escaped quotes and heredocs; it is deliberately not an HCL syntax tree.
Interpolation-bearing prefixes such as variables, locals and iteration symbols are excluded from environment reference targets, so only real resources become link candidates.
Module blocks are recorded as a generic kind carrying their module type rather than being expanded.
risks: The scanner can truncate a block on unbalanced braces inside an expression it does not understand, and the result is a silently thinner resource set rather than a parse error.
Module blocks are not expanded, so resources declared inside a module are invisible to the graph.
The reference kind is inferred from whether the expression carries an interpolation, which does not always match Terraform's own reference semantics.
patterns: A tolerant scanner over a fixed shape: the parser aims to recognize the common declarations rather than to be a complete implementation.
invariants: Variable, local and iteration prefixes never become environment reference targets.
A module block is modeled as a generic resource carrying its module type.
annotation.integrationPoints: Implements the parser contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, hashes payloads through mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/utils, and is registered by the terraform plugin index.
annotation.dataFlow: HCL text -> brace-balanced block scan -> per-block resource with kind, attributes, environment variables and references -> infra delta -> stage2 runtime linking where a handler attribute is present.

annotation.summary: Registration descriptor for the built-in Vercel plugin. Wraps the project-config parser, declares the vercel domain, marks its function resources as owning code the linking stage should resolve, and re-declares the schedule trigger metadata so scheduled entrypoints are labelled even in a repository where no other plugin registered it.

keyExports.default: The same descriptor as the module's default export.
keyExports.vercelIacPlugin: The descriptor: plugin id, its parser, the vercel domain, the function code-handler marker, and the schedule trigger metadata.

assumptions: Trigger metadata is declared by each plugin that can emit the trigger, so re-declaring schedule here is an idempotent overwrite rather than a conflict.
Only the committed project config is read; anything configured in the hosting dashboard is outside what a repository scan can see.
risks: Environment values managed in the dashboard rather than referenced in the committed config leave no trace, so the project's real secret surface is wider than the graph shows.
Routes defined only in application code are invisible here, since this plugin reads configuration rather than source.
patterns: A thin registration barrel: the config parsing lives in the parser module.
invariants: Serverless bundling is out of scope; the plugin describes declarations rather than build output.
A project identifier in the config is not correlated with the package graph.
annotation.integrationPoints: Built through the plugin factory in mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, wraps mod:repovine/src/iac-plugins/vercel/parser, and is registered by the stage1 IaC bootstrap.
annotation.dataFlow: project config → the parser → project, function, schedule, route and secret resources → stage2 HTTP and schedule entrypoint labels.

annotation.summary: Vercel project-config parser. Emits the project itself as a resource with its settings and environment variable names, recovers legacy prefixed secret references as external secret resources with links back to the project, and models serverless functions, scheduled jobs with their trigger, and the rewrite, redirect, header and route rules as typed resources.

keyExports.vercelParser: The parser: project resource, synthesized secrets, one resource per function pattern, scheduled jobs with schedule triggers, and route-rule resources.

assumptions: Only the canonical config filename is recognized; older Vercel config filenames are not parsed.
Secret recovery keys off the legacy prefixed reference syntax, which is the only form visible in the committed config.
A function's pattern string is used as its handler identity, and resolving that to a repository source file is left to the later linking stage.
risks: An encrypted environment value that does not use the legacy prefix produces no secret resource and no reference, so the project appears to have fewer secret dependencies than it does.
Because the function pattern is a glob rather than a path, a project whose layout does not match the linking heuristics ends up with functions that never connect to code.
patterns: Environment references are scanned in both the root and build environment blocks, so a secret used only at build time is still recorded.
invariants: Only the canonical config filename is accepted.
Every rule array is turned into route resources through one shared path, so the four rule kinds cannot drift apart.
annotation.integrationPoints: Implements the parser contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src and uses the attribute and hashing helpers in mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/utils; the function and scheduled-job kinds are what the entrypoint interpreters read as HTTP and schedule surfaces.

Handler references are resolved by asking each language plugin's resolver in turn; the first answer naming a module the index actually contains wins, and a resolver that throws is skipped rather than failing the pass.

The composed graph is swept afterwards for dangling edges and unprojected modules, which throws under REPOVINE_DEV and warns otherwise.
Handler resolution is heuristic and ordered, so two modules whose names collide can produce a confident but wrong link.
The deferred edges assume every resource node already exists, so a resource introduced by a later interpreter gets no edge.
patterns: Resolution is delegated to whichever language plugin can answer, so a handler reference format belongs to its language rather than to this layer.
Two passes over the same snapshot: create the nodes, then draw the edges that need them all present.
invariants: The domain configuration is threaded in rather than loaded here.

annotation.summary: Projects the boundary-scoped risks in the annotation store into a path-keyed file the pre-edit hook can read on its own. It is the push half of boundary delivery: the hook needs no running server and does one constant-time lookup per edited file, while the inspection tool delivers the same facts on the pull side.

keyExports.BoundaryIndexEntry: One boundary-carrying node a file owns: the node, a label, and the risk texts verbatim.
keyExports.BoundaryIndexFile: The file: version, build time, and entries keyed by repository-relative path.
keyExports.buildBoundaryIndex: Builds the index from the current state, deterministically.
keyExports.readBoundaryIndex: Reads it back, or nothing when it is absent.
keyExports.writeBoundaryIndex: Writes it into the local cache directory after a build.

assumptions: Both delivery channels read the same structured source — the risks marked with the boundary scope — so what the hook warns about and what an inspection surfaces cannot diverge, and neither depends on ranking or fuzzy matching.

Modules and their exports are keyed by their absolute path made relative to the snapshot root, not by the stored relative path, because the stored one is relative to its package and would drop the package prefix in a workspace with several — the hook computes its key from the repository root, so the two must agree.
Infrastructure and template paths are already repository-relative and are used as they are.
An export inherits the file of the module that owns it, so editing a file surfaces the boundaries on both.
Domains and runtime resources are absent, since neither has a single owning file; they still reach an agent through the inspection path.
Risk texts are carried verbatim and in stored order rather than summarized, because the wording is the delivery.
Output is sorted by key and within each key, so the same graph and annotations produce a byte-identical file.

reads it back on request

risks: The version is checked by the hook as a literal it cannot import, so a bump made here alone pauses every boundary advisory until the installed hooks are regenerated. The pause announces itself: the hook returns an actionable notice on every edit it sees, and the doctor reports the drift from both the installed hook and the index on disk. A test locks the literal to this constant so the bump cannot land in one place only.

Both annotation-writing tools keep the index current without a rebuild, so it goes stale only against a change made behind them — a file edited by hand or by another process — and the hook then warns from the previous state.
Several nodes can share a file key, so a consumer reading only the first entry misses the rest of that file's boundaries.
patterns: Push and pull from one source: a file for the editor hook, an attention block for the agent, both derived from the same marked risks.
A build-time artifact rather than a query, so the consumer needs neither a server nor the graph.
invariants: Only boundary-scoped risks are indexed.
Keys match what the editing hook computes from the repository root.
The same input always produces the same bytes.
Risk text is reproduced unchanged.

annotation.summary: The state machine around the startup build. It runs one build at a time, tracks which stage it is in and how far along, answers status queries while it runs, and supports cancelling and restarting it without stopping the process.

keyExports.BuildHooks: The progress callbacks the pipeline invokes as it advances.
keyExports.IndexBuildController: The controller: start, cancel, rebuild, the long-poll wait, and the status snapshot.
keyExports.IndexBuildStage: The stages a build passes through and the three it can end in.
keyExports.IndexBuildStatus: The reported state: stage, progress counts, percentage, elapsed and estimated time, a retry delay and a message.

assumptions: A build is single-flight: repeated starts return the same promise, so concurrent callers all await one build.

A cancellation is recognized by a flag set when it was requested, not by the type of the error that surfaced — the stages raise whatever their abort produces, so the error alone cannot distinguish a cancel from a failure.

What a cancel leaves behind depends on whether a usable graph already existed: a previous one is kept and the controller returns to ready, while a cancelled first build ends in a terminal cancelled state with the promise cleared so a fresh start can follow.

A restart is reachable only from that cancelled state and reuses the build function captured at the first start, which is what keeps the whole cancel-and-retry cycle inside the tools rather than requiring a process restart.
A build in progress is a successful answer rather than an error, and it always carries a suggested retry delay.
The long-poll never rejects and settles on whichever comes first: the build finishing, the caller cancelling, or the wait expiring.
Verified 2026-07-23: IndexBuildController state machine (stages, single-flight, cancel/restart) and dependency on mod:repovine/src/mcp/context unchanged; content-hash refresh only.

sideEffects.description: holds the build status and the ready runtime handle
drives the single in-flight build and its cancellation

risks: The time estimate is a linear extrapolation from the modules finished so far, so it is absent until the first package lands and skews long early on, while startup time is still counted against the measured rate.
A cancelled first build leaves no graph at all, and every tool then answers from that state until something starts another build.
The controller holds the ready runtime handle, so a configuration reload publishes by replacing it here.
patterns: Progress is pushed in through hooks rather than polled out, so the pipeline stays unaware of who is watching.
Cancel and rebuild are ordinary operations rather than lifecycle events, which is what makes an abandoned cold build recoverable in place.
invariants: A status reporting a build in progress always includes a retry delay.
Only one build runs at a time and all callers share it.
A cancel never discards a graph that was already serving.
The long-poll resolves rather than throwing, whatever the outcome.
annotation.integrationPoints: Runs the build supplied by mod:repovine/src/mcp/context and holds the resulting runtime; driven by the server entry under mod:repovine/src/mcp, which exposes the status and long-poll through its tool, cancels on shutdown, and swaps the held handle on a configuration reload.
annotation.dataFlow: start with a build function → stage transitions and progress callbacks update the status → settle into ready, failed or cancelled → status queries and long-polls read that snapshot; a cancelled cold build can be restarted with the same function.

annotation.summary: The server runtime. It owns the current graph, snapshot, annotations and indexes, rebuilds them on request, and replaces the whole state at once when a build succeeds. Concurrent refreshes share one rebuild, and a build that was cancelled never becomes the served state.

keyExports.RepovineRuntime: The runtime: the current state, the single-flight refresh, the forced abort used at shutdown, and the semantic index sync.
keyExports.RepovineRuntimeOptions: Whether to start from a cold snapshot, the build progress hooks, and a signal for cancelling the startup build.

assumptions: The state is swapped as one object rather than mutated, so a handler reading it mid-rebuild sees the previous build whole rather than a half-updated one.
Refresh is single-flight: several callers arriving during a rebuild join the same promise and receive the same result.

Cancellation of that shared rebuild is reference-counted — it aborts only once every attached caller has cancelled, and a caller that supplied no signal makes it uncancellable. One client pressing escape must not end a rebuild another client is still waiting for.
The shutdown path aborts unconditionally, bypassing that count, because at that point no one is waiting for the result.

Cancellation is honoured at stage boundaries and once more immediately before the swap, since a build can finish before an abort reaches an internal checkpoint; that final gate is what preserves the previously ready graph on a late cancel.

The annotation store instance is kept across refreshes and re-read from disk rather than reconstructed, so its single pending-write timer survives the swap — a replaced store would leave an orphaned timer able to clobber or resurrect records.
The second stage is offloaded to a worker so a rebuild does not block the request path.
The embedding library is resolved from the analyzed workspace rather than the working directory, because the engine may be running from a package cache.
Verified 2026-07-23: RepovineRuntime class shape and import set (stage1/stage2, annotations/store, semantic/*, mcp/onboarding-state, mcp/boundary-index) unchanged; content-hash refresh only.

sideEffects.description: runs extraction and graph composition, the latter in a worker
persists the snapshot cache, the semantic index, the onboarding state and the boundary index when a build completes

risks.text: Refresh cancellation is shared and reference-counted, so a caller must supply its own signal to participate and must not assume its cancel ends the build; another caller's signal keeps it alive.

risks: An embedder failure degrades — the previously cached vectors keep serving and a warning is logged — but a cancellation during embedding is deliberately not treated that way.
A cancel arriving during the semantic index write can still leave that file written; it is a hash-validated cache, so the next build revalidates it rather than trusting it.

The resolved build configuration is captured at construction and changes only when a refresh explicitly asks for a config reload, which swaps in a freshly built runtime. Domain patterns and the recorded advisory declines are re-read from disk on every build, so an ordinary refresh already applies edits to those.
patterns: One runtime per process, one in-flight rebuild, one state object replaced atomically.
Per-build parameters — the active signal and whether to emit build hooks — are passed down rather than stored as mutable runtime mode.
Every persisted artifact is written only after the build that produced it has succeeded.
invariants: The served state is always the last build that completed without being cancelled.
Concurrent refresh callers share one rebuild and one result.
The annotation store instance outlives every state swap.
A cancelled build performs no state swap.

annotation.dataFlow: configuration → startup build under the controller → served state; a refresh joins or starts the shared rebuild → extraction, graph composition in a worker, annotations, token and semantic indexes → cancellation gate → whole-state replacement and the derived artifacts written.

keyExports.moduleLinkCount: Counts buildNodeView links for a module.
keyExports.resolveModulePackageId: Returns pkg: id from contains edge or 'unknown'.

Secondary pattern matches can inflate module lists if includeSecondaryMatches is on.

Replay order regression breaks parity with pre-T5 inline assembly.

annotation.summary: Builds the detailed view for one node: the graph view, its annotation with freshness and quality, the investigate tags on its references, paginated children, and optionally a slice of source or a regular-expression search within it. One path serves every node kind.

keyExports.buildInspectNodeDetail: Assembles the whole response for a node from the runtime and the request arguments.
keyExports.graphEdgeCount: A one-hop edge counter by kind and direction, which is the topology input the wiring and co-change tags need.

assumptions: Freshness is decided per node kind: a module against its own content, a service or resource against a resolved hash, a template against its own, and a domain against a hash rolled up from its members.
Reading source is opt-in: nothing is read from disk unless a body slice or a search was requested.

Search is bounded at every step — the pattern length is capped, obviously dangerous patterns are refused, the pattern is compiled before any file is read so a malformed one fails cheaply, and execution runs in a killable worker under a deadline.
The request's cancellation signal is threaded into that worker, so a client that cancels stops the scan rather than leaving it to reach its own timeout.
Secret-looking text is redacted in both the body slice and the search results, before either leaves this module.
Every truncation is reported: an over-long line, a capped match count, a body slice with more to come. None of them is silent.
Matches carry a few lines of surrounding context, deduplicated where matches are close together and returned in line order.

sideEffects.description: reads node source only when a body slice or a search is requested
runs pattern matching in a killable worker

risks: A domain's freshness follows a hash rolled up from its members, so a domain annotation reads as stale on member churn alone, even when nothing about the domain's own description is wrong. Which members count depends on how the domain was tagged: one carrying path or pattern tags rolls up only those members, while a domain assembled purely from a package rolls up all of them. This module reads the hash directly and does not apply the queue's exemption for package domains.
Requesting a body slice on a large node can approach the response ceiling; the slice is bounded by the requested limit and the truncation is reported.
Redaction is pattern-based, so it catches secret-shaped text rather than everything sensitive; a secret that does not look like one passes through.
patterns: Bound first, then execute: every limit is checked before the expensive step, so a bad request costs little.
Truncation is always visible in the response, which is what lets a caller tell an empty result from a trimmed one.
annotation.flowDescription: nodeId + pagination opts → buildNodeView → freshness branch per node type → annotation attach → optional readNodeBody/grepBody → paginated result.
invariants: No source is read unless the request asks for it.
Redaction happens before anything is returned.
A refused or failed search reports its reason instead of returning nothing.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by the inspection tool handler under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools; the view comes from mod:repovine/src/graph/node-view; source reading, pattern safety, redaction and the worker scan from mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/node-body; the tags from mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs; limits and child paging from mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination; annotation quality from mod:repovine/src/annotations/store, classification from mod:repovine/src/annotations/module-kind, and the service and resource hashes from mod:repovine/src/annotations/service-resource-hash.
annotation.dataFlow: node identifier and options → resolved node and its view → per-kind freshness and annotation quality → investigate tags on links and children → optional bounded search or body slice, redacted → paginated response.

annotation.summary: Decides which references in an inspection response carry an investigate flag, and how many. Detection belongs to the mechanics registry; what lives here is delivery — ordering tags by strength, capping how many reach one response, and guarding the direction of the pointers parsed out of annotation prose.

keyExports.HUB_PERCENTILE: Which percentile of the import distribution marks a hub.
keyExports.INVESTIGATE_DEP_GUARD_DEPTH: How far the dependency check walks when validating a pointer.
keyExports.INVESTIGATE_PRIORITY: The tag order, taken from the registry so there is one ranking.
keyExports.InvestigateOptions: The primitives the caller supplies: the node's own annotation, the dependency and membership tests, the import and edge counts, and the hub threshold.
keyExports.MAX_CO_CHANGE_REFS: Cap on the co-change tag per response.
keyExports.MAX_HUB_REFS: Cap on the heavily-imported tag per response.
keyExports.MAX_INVESTIGATE_REFS: How many flagged references one response may carry.
keyExports.MAX_INVESTIGATE_TAGS_PER_REF: How many tags a single reference may show.
keyExports.MAX_WIRING_REFS: Cap on the wiring tag per response.
keyExports.applyInvestigateTags: Tags the response's references in place and attaches the pointers derived from the node's own annotation.
keyExports.computeHubInDegreeThreshold: The adaptive threshold above which a target counts as heavily imported.
keyExports.priorityWeight: A tag's strength, used wherever ordering by salience is needed.

assumptions: Two channels feed one shared cap: the structural one covers direct imports and children with no guard, and the pointer one covers deeper dependencies the node's own annotation names, kept only when the node really depends on them.

The hub threshold adapts to the repository rather than being a constant, because a fixed floor floods a large repository where every shared module clears it; a floor still applies so a small repository needs a real count.
That threshold costs one pass over the graph and is computed per build rather than per request, which is what keeps the per-request check to a single hop.
A capped advisory tag is removed from the excess references while the references themselves stay, so a cap never hides a reference that carries a stronger reason.
A missing primitive disables its tag rather than defaulting it, so a caller that cannot supply import counts simply never sees that tag.
One mechanic is reserved and never fires; its place in the vocabulary is held deliberately.

sideEffects.description: writes the tags onto the response structure passed in

risks: The topology-edge tags are capped by collection order, so a reference can lose wiring or co-change for its position in the response rather than for the strength of its signal; the heavily-imported cap ranks by importer count instead and keeps the strongest.
A pointer naming a node the graph does not contain is dropped silently, so an annotation pointing at a renamed module loses its flag with no report.
The direction guard only applies when the caller supplies the dependency test, so a caller that omits it gets tags in both directions.
patterns: Detection and delivery are separated: adding a reason means adding a mechanic, while how much reaches the reader is decided in one place.
Both channels are ranked together and truncated once, so the response has a single noise budget rather than one per source.
invariants: Ties in rank resolve to the structural channel, which is collected first.
Dropping references for the cap is recorded on the response rather than left implicit.
The tag ranking comes from the registry, so priority is defined once.
annotation.integrationPoints: Detection predicates, the tag vocabulary and the hub floor come from mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry and mod:repovine/src/mechanics/types; the pointer prose parser from mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-links; the response shape from mod:repovine/src/graph/node-view; called by the inspection handler under mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib, and the same ranking is reused by the response pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: response references and the node's own annotation → per-target mechanic detection → per-reference tag cap by strength → pointers filtered by the dependency guard → one ranked truncation across both channels → advisory tags trimmed to their caps.

annotation.summary: Repo-contained source reader and secret redactor for inspect_node. Body reads are admitted by the shared containment guard, which resolves symlinks, so a link that names an in-repo path but resolves outside the root is refused. Agent grep regexes are screened for catastrophic backtracking, run in a worker_thread with a hard parent timeout, bounded by per-line and match caps, and admitted through a shared bounded pool so concurrent inspect_node calls cannot spawn unbounded workers.

keyExports.displayPath: Repo-relative label for messages, or [outside-repo]; lexical, so a refused symlink still names the in-repo file.
keyExports.isUnsafeRegexPattern: Rejects catastrophic-backtracking patterns before RegExp compile.
keyExports.readNodeBody: Async read: full module file or export-symbol slice from the parent module, admitted by the containment guard.
keyExports.redactSecretLikeText: Heuristic redaction of secret-like substrings in returned source text.
keyExports.scanLinesWithRegex: Runs a screened regex in a pooled worker_thread; honors an AbortSignal and returns a bounded RegexLineScanResult.

assumptions: Never serves bytes from outside the resolved repoRoot; unsupported node types return {error} without filesystem access.
Module filePath values arriving from the graph are absolute.
The grep worker pool (createLimiter, min(4, cpu-1)) is shared across all inspect_node calls in the process.

sideEffects.description: reads module source files only when the path is inside repoRoot
runs each screened regex in a worker isolate, admitted through a shared bounded limiter

risks: A request cancelled while QUEUED behind the limiter bails immediately (does not wait for admission), and an admitted-then-cancelled request skips spawning the worker — the cancel maps to the empty/timed-out result, keeping the contract 'resolves on cancel'.
Secret redaction is heuristic — novel credential formats may leak in grepBody output.
The containment guard resolves the path and readFile re-resolves it, so a target swapped between the two is read as found.
Full module reads without a lineRange can be large — bounded by the caller's bodyLimit.
patterns: Returns {error: string} instead of throwing for missing parent, out-of-repo paths, or missing files.
A refusal names the repo-relative path, so the out-of-repo target never appears in the message.
displayPath labels a path; isPathInsideRepo decides whether it may be read.
invariants: Never serves bytes from a path whose realpath resolves outside repoRoot.
Unsupported node types return {error} without filesystem access.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/inspect-node-core (includeBody + grepBody, threads the request signal); containment guard from mod:repovine/src/fs/containment; grep concurrency primitive from mod:repovine/src/semantic/serialize.
annotation.dataFlow: nodeId + nodeType + lineRange → resolve filePath → isPathInsideRepo (realpath) → readFile → slice lines → scanLinesWithRegex (pooled worker, signal) → optional redactSecretLikeText.

annotation.summary: Module src/mcp/lib/not-ready-response.ts in repovine
Pure mapper from stage-3 SemanticSyncReport to compact SemanticSearchRefresh (disabled/up_to_date/updated/failed) surfaced by refresh_context output.

keyExports.outsideRepoReport: Files refused because they resolve outside repo; distinguishes past-root paths from link-escape paths.
keyExports.semanticSearchRefreshFromSync: Maps SemanticSyncReport | null plus enabled/error/cachedTotal options to SemanticSearchRefresh for refresh_context.

assumptions: Propagation review: verified upstream semantic/store and mcp/types.
risks: SemanticSyncReport field drift breaks refresh_context clients expecting embedded/total/status shape.
patterns: Pure formatter — no graph mutation.
annotation.flowDescription: refreshContextCore → semanticSearchRefreshFromSync → SemanticSearchRefresh status block for refresh_context envelope.
invariants: Output fields must remain backward compatible with refresh_context concise envelope.
extensionPoints: Add optional timing fields when semantic embed reports latency.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called from mcp/lib/annotations refreshContextCore; output lands in refresh_context semanticSearch field.
annotation.stateShape: SemanticSearchRefresh: {status:'disabled'} | {status:'failed',total,error?} | {status:'updated',embedded,total} | {status:'up_to_date',total}.

annotation.summary: Computes trace_flow runtimeHandoff entries that route runtime resources to editable handler modules when annotations, secret bindings, or exact runtime scoping make the handoff high-signal.

keyExports.computeRuntimeHandoff: Builds capped runtime handoff items from current trace service ids, exact resource/module scope seeds, annotation risk, and secret-binding signals.
keyExports.resolveHandlerModuleId: Resolves resource -> handler mod: via stable-sorted infra edges, with a handler-label fallback.

assumptions: serviceIds is the current trace response candidate set; broad traces omit plain resources without annotation or secret signals.
Exact resource scope, or a module scope with one primary runtime seed, may emit a scoped-resource handoff without other priority signals.
Secret detection follows graph binds_to/uses_env edges to runtime-resource nodes whose kind is secret; it never reads secret values.
risks: Stale running MCP processes need restart before the new runtimeHandoff payload appears in live tool responses.
Multiple infra handlers collapse to the first stable-sorted module in v1.
invariants: RUNTIME_HANDOFF_LIMIT remains 3 and omittedCount reports candidates beyond that cap.
Priority order is secret-binding before annotation before scoped-resource, with lexicographic tie-breaks.
The helper stops at the handler module; deeper domain logic remains inspect/import closure.
annotation.integrationPoints: src/mcp/tools/trace-flow attaches runtimeHandoff to the envelope and navigation; src/annotations/format provides consumer/boundary scoped risk checks; graph uses infra, binds_to, and uses_env edges.
annotation.dataFlow: trace_flow service ids + resolved scope -> candidate runtime resources -> handler module resolution -> trigger classification -> priority sort/cap -> runtimeHandoff result.

annotation.summary: search_context post-processor: detects annotation-matched top hits and sets gaps/navigation to escalate agents to inspect_node instead of trusting truncated search payloads.

keyExports.SEARCH_ANNOTATION_ESCALATION_GAP: Gaps line when annotation match suppresses inline annotation fields.
keyExports.SEARCH_ANNOTATION_ESCALATION_NAV_REASON: Navigation reason for deeper inspect_node after annotation hit.
keyExports.searchAnnotationEscalation: Returns shouldEscalate and top1Annotated from search hit list.

assumptions: annotationMatched on search hits means token overlap with annotation text fields.
Escalation fires when top hit is annotation-matched but gaps still recommend inspect_node.
risks: False escalation when annotation text matches query but content is stale.
Missing annotationMatched flag on hits skips escalation silently.
patterns: Prevents agents from treating annotationMatched search hits as fully understood without inspect_node.
invariants: SEARCH_ANNOTATION_ESCALATION_GAP is stable agent-facing copy for gaps array.
topResultsHaveAnnotationMatch checks configurable topN (default 3).
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/search-context handleSearchContext; mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/envelope nav gaps.
annotation.dataFlow: search_context matches → searchAnnotationEscalation checks top hits → navigation.deeper inspect_node when shouldEscalate.

annotation.summary: search_context ranking engine: token index scoring with AND/OR relaxation, optional semantic RRF fusion, export-symbol dampening, and suggestedScopes for domains/runtime-resources.

keyExports.applyExportSymbolDampeningIfNeeded: Down-ranks export-symbol hits when semantic search active.
keyExports.searchGraph: Token + semantic fusion ranking for search_context.

assumptions: Read-only — never mutates graph or annotations.
Semantic rankings passed in by search_context async embed path.
risks: Weak-token suppression may hide valid short-query matches.
patterns: OR-relax from AND when strict match empty.
empty results delegate to searchEmptyDiagnostic.
invariants: Respects limit/offset pagination.
Export symbols dampened when flooding during semantic search.
annotation.integrationPoints: mcp/tools/search-context handler; SearchIndex from mcp/types RepovineState.
annotation.dataFlow: query → searchTokenize + optional semantic RRF → token scores → export-symbol dampening → paginated matches + suggestedScopes.

annotation.summary: Inverted token index for search_context: searchTokenize splits camelCase/plain identifiers, buildTokenIndex maps graph node labels and annotationSearchText bodies to nodeIds, indexableAnnotationTokens applies length/stopword/WEAK_SEARCH_TOKENS filters, and suggestVocabulary offers prefix/substring/Levenshtein hints for unknown query tokens.

keyExports.SearchIndex: tokens: Map<token, Set<nodeId>> plus annotationText: Map<nodeId, flattened text>.
keyExports.WEAK_SEARCH_TOKENS: Short/generic tokens filtered from index and suggestions.
keyExports.annotationSearchText: Flattens all annotation content strings for token indexing.
keyExports.buildTokenIndex: Tokenizes graph labels and fresh annotation bodies into inverted index.
keyExports.suggestVocabulary: Vocabulary hints when search_context query token misses index.

assumptions: Propagation review 2026-06-20: upstream types hash changed; SearchIndex/StoredAnnotation types unchanged.
risks: WEAK_SEARCH_TOKENS and stopword filters may drop valid short symbols (e.g. id, api).
Stale annotations excluded from index until rewritten — search may miss recently renamed modules until refresh.
patterns: Graph label tokens and annotation tokens share the same inverted index structure.
Annotation indexing boosts search_context recall when module notes are fresh.
annotation.flowDescription: Graph modules + annotations → buildSearchIndex tokenize → inverted index for search_context.
invariants: buildTokenIndex indexes annotatable graph nodes plus annotation text keyed by nodeId.
suggestVocabulary ranks prefix > substring > bounded Levenshtein distance.
annotation.integrationPoints: RepovineState.searchIndex; mcp search-context and search-graph handlers; refresh_context searchTokens count.
annotation.dataFlow: RepositoryGraph node labels + StoredAnnotation content → buildTokenIndex inverted map → search_context token scoring and suggestVocabulary for missing query tokens.

annotation.summary: Runtime topology projection for trace_flow MCP: projectRuntimeTopology walks runtime-resource nodes, assembles triggers/envRefs/publishes/consumes, surfaces routes_to/routedFrom for ingress routing hops, reports the grant-derived access mode per resource binding, and derives queue-mediated dataFlows from resourceMap.

keyExports.projectRuntimeTopology: Returns {scope, services, resources?, dataFlows?} for runtime-resource subgraph in scope.

assumptions: Scope hull from mod: seeds infra-linked runtime-resources; from resource: expands uses_env/publishes/consumes/routes_to neighbors.
routes_to edges surface k8s Ingress→Service hops as routesTo/routedFrom on each service entry.
includeApiRoutes and includeResources default true; set false to trim trigger/resource sections.
resourceMap builds producer→queue→consumer dataFlows when both sides present.
risks: Incomplete IaC scan or pruned runtime-resources yield sparse topology for k8s-only services.
patterns: Pairs with infra-runtime-links pass2Infra edges (infra, uses_env, publishes, consumes, routes_to).
Queue-mediated flows use resourceMap flowConsumers; routes_to is direct resource→resource routing.
annotation.flowDescription: trace_flow MCP → projectRuntimeTopology(scope) → services[] with handler/domains/triggers/publishes/routesTo plus optional resources map and dataFlows.
invariants: publishTypeForRuntimeResource maps aws-sqs/sns/lambda/eventbridge prefixes to publish type labels.
Domain scope matches tagged edges; pkg scope walks infra→contains from package node.

Env-ref targets resolve through the scoped resolver with the service's own declaredIn/namespace, the same scope the graph builder used — a global label scan here would re-introduce the cross-template match the builder refused.
access is 'unknown' with accessSource 'not-declared' whenever the IaC document declared no readable grant; the projection never substitutes a default mode.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/graph/resolve-infra-ref for scoped env-ref resolution; mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/trace-flow turns unresolvedRefs into response gaps.
annotation.dataFlow: scope filter → per runtime-resource assemble triggers, scoped envRefs with access, publishes, consumes, routes_to, unresolvedRefs → resourceMap → optional dataFlows array.

annotation.summary: Keeps a small local file describing how far onboarding has got: the graph's size and build time, annotation coverage and backlog totals, and which domain suggestions the user has declined. It is workspace-local and untracked, so it records a person's choices rather than anything the repository commits.

keyExports.OnboardingStateFile: Its shape: version, graph facts, and the onboarding counters.
keyExports.buildOnboardingState: Computes the file contents from the built state and a declined set.
keyExports.mergeDeclinedDomainsSuggestions: Combines new declines with the stored ones and returns the result without writing.
keyExports.readOnboardingState: Reads it back, or nothing when it is missing, unreadable or of another version.
keyExports.writeOnboardingState: Writes the current state after a build, preserving the declined set when the caller does not supply one.

assumptions: Every read tolerates failure: a missing file, unparseable content, or a version this build does not recognize all read as absent, so a corrupted advisory file degrades to no suggestions rather than an error.
The write is best-effort and logs rather than throwing, since failing to record advisory state must not fail the build that produced it.
Merging declines is pure and returns the combined set; persisting it is a separate call, so a caller can compute a result without committing to it.
Declined ids are deduplicated and sorted, which keeps the file stable across writes.
Coverage counts every annotatable node type together, and an empty repository reports full coverage rather than dividing by nothing.
Preserving the stored declines is the default on write, so a build that does not mention them cannot silently clear a user's choices.

sideEffects.description: reads the advisory state from the local cache
writes it back after a build

risks: A failed write leaves the previous file in place, so the counters can describe an older build while looking current; the only signal is the warning at the time it happened.
The declined set lives only here and the directory is untracked, so clearing the cache restores every suggestion the user had dismissed.
The counters are a snapshot taken at build time and are not recomputed on read, so a consumer reading the file without a rebuild sees the state as of the last one.
patterns: Advisory state is local and disposable: losing it costs suggestions reappearing, never correctness.
Reads fail soft, the write fails soft, and the only strictness is the version check.
annotation.flowDescription: Read/write .repovine/onboarding-state.json tracking declined domain suggestions and annotation onboarding progress.
invariants: An unrecognized version reads as absent rather than being partially trusted.
Declined ids are always deduplicated and sorted.
A write never throws.
annotation.integrationPoints: Written by the server runtime after a build under mod:repovine/src/mcp; the declined set is consumed by the domain advisor in mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-advisor and extended through the advisory-decline tool; graph counts come from mod:repovine/src/graph and annotation counts from the store on the state; the cache location from mod:repovine/src/paths.
annotation.stateShape: Version, graph status with build time and counts, annotation coverage and backlog totals, and the domain suggestion counts with the declined ids.
annotation.dataFlow: built state plus the stored declines → graph and annotation counters → advisory file in the local cache → read back by the domain advisor to hide what was declined.

annotation.summary: Single-flight runner for refresh_context({reloadConfig:true}): builds a fresh runtime from the re-read config, drains the outgoing annotation store, re-reads the incoming one, then swaps the ready runtime. Dependency-injected (no direct runtime/controller imports) so the swap lifecycle is unit-testable.

keyExports.ReloadConfigDeps: Injected steps: loadNextConfig, buildRuntime(cfg, signal), drainOutgoing, reloadIncoming, publish, onDrainWarning.
keyExports.ReloadConfigResult: { configReloaded: true, drainWarning? } — drainWarning surfaces a non-fatal outgoing-drain failure.
keyExports.ReloadConfigRunner: run(requestSignal?) coalesces concurrent calls onto one swap; abortActive() is the shutdown handle; isInFlight gates annotation writes during the handoff.

assumptions: Deps read the CURRENT runtime at run time (e.g. drainOutgoing hits whatever runtime is ready), not a value captured at construction.
buildRuntime honors the combined signal at its own internal checkpoints; the runner adds the outer checkpoints.

sideEffects.description: single-flight coalescing; combines request signal + owned controller via AbortSignal.any
in-flight promise + abort controller held on the runner instance

risks: publish() (replaceReadyContext) is the one non-reversible step; the post-build checkpoint and the FINAL checkpoint immediately before publish must reject a late cancel so the current runtime is preserved.
Coalesced joiners share the initiating request's signal — the initiator governs the shared build; a joiner's cancel is not independently refcounted.
annotation.integrationPoints: Constructed in mod:repovine/src/mcp/index with live deps (RepovineRuntime.create as buildRuntime, controller.replaceReadyContext as publish, current store.drain as drainOutgoing); abortActive() is invoked by mod:repovine/src/mcp/shutdown.

annotation.summary: MCP response shaping layer: concise mode compacts standard tool envelopes and deduplicates navigation scope strings via NavigationRefRegistry; debug returns raw payloads; toCallToolMcpResult serializes final tools/call JSON.

keyExports.CallToolMcpResult: MCP tools/call payload: content[{type:text}] plus optional isError.
keyExports.NavigationRefRegistry: refFor/resolvesArgs — deduplicates long scope strings into $hash refs per request.
keyExports.shapeToolResult: Concise envelope compaction with navigation/resolvedScope/refs map.
keyExports.toCallToolMcpResult: Final JSON text payload with oversized-result guard.

assumptions: Concise mode compacts only standard envelopes.
NavigationRefRegistry caps at 500 refs and trims LRU when exceeded.
Debug mode bypasses all compaction.
risks: New envelope fields omitted from compactNavigation are lost in concise mode.
Oversized JSON responses are truncated with warning.
patterns: Concise mode drops unlisted envelope fields — extend compactNavigation when adding new top-level keys.
invariants: isToolErrorResult sets MCP isError:true on handler error envelopes.
annotation.integrationPoints: All mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/* handlers; instantiated per request.
annotation.dataFlow: Tool handler result → shapeToolResult (compact envelope + refs) → JSON.stringify → CallToolMcpResult.content[0].text for MCP tools/call.

annotation.summary: Turns an empty tool result into an explanation. Each tool has a factory that works out why nothing came back, states it with a confidence, and offers concrete next calls with their arguments already filled in. An agent that hits an empty result learns whether the repository lacks the thing, the scope was wrong, or its own filter removed everything.

keyExports.EmptyDiagnostic: The shape: reason, message, confidence, next actions and optional detail.
keyExports.architectureEmptyDiagnostic: Why an analysis produced no findings.
keyExports.configSurfaceEmptyDiagnostic: Why no configuration or resource bindings matched.
keyExports.dependenciesEmptyDiagnostic: Why a dependency query returned nothing.
keyExports.dependencyModeScopeMismatchDiagnostic: Why a mode and a scope are incompatible.
keyExports.emptyAction: Builds one suggested next call: the condition, the tool and its arguments.
keyExports.graphEmptyDiagnostic: The answer when nothing is indexed at all.
keyExports.mapContextEmptyDiagnostic: Why a map came back empty, including paging past the end.
keyExports.searchEmptyDiagnostic: Why a search returned nothing, distinguishing suppression, no token hits, a type filter and an unsatisfiable combination.
keyExports.traceFlowEmptyDiagnostic: Why no runtime topology was proven.
keyExports.wireEmptyDiagnosticCollectors: Binds the tool-layer collectors at startup, which is how the circular import between this module and the handlers is avoided.

assumptions: The checks run in order from cheapest and most decisive: an unindexed graph first, then an unresolved scope, then a filter that removed everything, then the tool-specific reasons.

Filter attribution is verified where a collector can be re-run: the entrypoint and config-surface factories ask again with a limit of one and state exclusion at high confidence. The search and architecture factories infer it from weaker evidence — token hits in the index, or the mere presence of a filter argument — and state it at medium confidence.

Domain scopes are special-cased in the entrypoint and runtime-flow factories, where the explanation states the domain tag owns no handlers, pages or runtime resources; map-context tells a tagged-but-empty domain that no modules carry the tag. The config-surface, dependency and architecture factories return their generic explanation for a domain scope, the last two adapting only the suggested next call.
Confidence is stated per diagnosis: a resolved structural fact is high, an inference about why a repository lacks something is medium.
Collectors are injected at startup rather than imported, and calling one before it is wired raises a message naming the fix.

Verified 2026-07-23: 14 exports (architectureEmptyDiagnostic, configSurfaceEmptyDiagnostic, dependenciesEmptyDiagnostic, dependencyModeScopeMismatchDiagnostic, entrypointsEmptyDiagnostic, graphEmptyDiagnostic, mapContextEmptyDiagnostic, searchEmptyDiagnostic, traceFlowEmptyDiagnostic, wireEmptyDiagnosticCollectors, emptyAction, and the 3 type exports) unchanged; content-hash refresh only.
risks: The reasons are a closed set, so a genuinely new cause of emptiness is reported as the nearest existing reason rather than as an unknown one — a confident but wrong explanation.
A new tool that forgets to call its factory returns a bare empty result, and nothing detects the omission; the wiring is by convention rather than enforced.
The suggested calls carry pre-filled arguments, so a suggestion that drifts from a tool's actual schema sends an agent into a rejected call rather than a useful one.
patterns: An empty result is an answer with a reason, not a null; the reason and the next step travel together.
Distinguish absence from exclusion by asking again without the filter, so the two are never conflated.
invariants: An unindexed graph always suggests a refresh first.
Every diagnosis carries at least one next action.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called from the zero-result path of every tool under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools; scope resolution from mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve; paging defaults from mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination; the token index from mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-index; the result shape from mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/envelope.
annotation.dataFlow: a tool returns nothing → its factory checks graph, scope, filters and kind in order → a reason with confidence and pre-filled next calls → attached to the response envelope.

annotation.summary: Standard MCP tool response envelope builder: scope, resolvedScope, summary, confidence, result, gaps, navigation, attention — consumed by response-format and all graph/annotation tools.

keyExports.dedupeNavigation: Caps each navigation section to 4 items and dedupes by tool+args key.
keyExports.envelope: Main builder: merges result with confidence, gaps, navigation, attention.
keyExports.envelopeError: Low-confidence error envelope with scopeNavigation fallback.
keyExports.publicResolvedScope: Serializes ResolvedScope to client-safe {kind, id, raw, nodeId?, domainId?}.

assumptions: Confidence defaults to medium when omitted.
dedupeNavigation caps each navigation section to four items.
risks: Navigation section limit (4) may hide useful follow-up tools on dense inspect_node responses.
envelopeError scopeNavigation may suggest tools for unknown scopes.
patterns: Standard MCP tool response envelope — never return raw objects from handlers.
invariants: navigation always has all five sections after dedupeNavigation.
Every MCP handler should return via envelope() or envelopeError().
annotation.integrationPoints: All mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/* handlers; mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination for list slices; mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/navigation scopeNavigation.
annotation.dataFlow: handler result + ResolvedScope + optional navigation partial → envelope() → mod:repovine/src/mcp/response-format shaping → MCP client.

annotation.summary: Shared pagination utilities and default limits for MCP tool responses: limitFrom/offsetFrom parsers, paginateNodeViewChildren, pathFromRootPaginated, and DEFAULT_* limit constants for search, map, inspect, architecture, and validation tools.

keyExports.DEFAULT_BODY_LIMIT: 12000 — max source slice chars for inspect_node includeBody.
keyExports.limitFrom: Parses args.limit with fallback and max cap (default max 200).
keyExports.paginateNodeViewChildren: Slices drill_down with childPagination metadata and optional summaryOnly mode.
keyExports.pathFromRootPaginated: Paginated ancestor path + focus node for inspect_node includeBody flows.

assumptions: Propagation review 2026-06-20: upstream types and graph hash changed; pagination helpers unchanged.
risks: Changing DEFAULT_* constants affects all tools simultaneously — test envelope shapes after tuning.

risks.text: summaryOnly mode hides drill_down children but exposes topChildren preview — clients must handle both.

patterns: namedLimitFrom/namedOffsetFrom support non-standard arg names (exportLimit, exportOffset).
childPagination.hint tells agents exact offset for next page.
invariants: limit always clamped to [1, max]; offset always >= 0.
paginateNodeViewChildren never mutates input NodeView — returns new PaginatedNodeView.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used by inspect_node, map_context, search_context handlers; imports mod:repovine/src/graph pathFromRoot and mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs salience ordering.
annotation.dataFlow: handler args → limitFrom/offsetFrom → paginateNodeViewChildren → childPagination in inspect_node/map responses.

annotation.summary: Advisory semantic recovery for scope misses: appendSemanticScopeSuggestions embeds the failed scope/nodeId text, ranks graph node cards via SemanticIndex, and appends up to 3 same-tool retry actions to emptyDiagnostic.nextActions. Suggested ids are filtered against the current graph so a stale index cannot suggest removed nodes.

keyExports.appendSemanticScopeSuggestions: Async enrichment; no-op unless result.emptyDiagnostic.reason === 'scope_unresolved' and handlerArgs.scope is a non-empty string.

assumptions: Runs post-handler for every tool; reads state via ctx.getState at call time.
Embedder failure degrades to the unchanged token-only diagnostic (never throws).

sideEffects.description: mutates the passed response envelope: appends actions to emptyDiagnostic.nextActions
semanticIndex.embedQuery when enriching scope_unresolved diagnostics

risks: Suggested hit ids are filtered by graph.nodes.has against the pinned state, so a semantic index lagging the current generation cannot suggest a removed/renamed node as a retry scope.
Over-suggesting broad domains adds noise to agent navigation hints.
patterns: Post-processor on search_context/map_context envelopes.
annotation.flowDescription: MCP tool response → appendSemanticScopeSuggestions when semantic search under-resolves scope.
invariants: Never resolves a scope silently — suggestions are advisory nextActions only.
Max 3 suggestions; the original raw scope/nodeId is never suggested back; retry args never carry nodeId (it would take precedence over scope and miss again).
Resolved non-query scopes (package/module/domain) with empty results are never enriched.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/index executeTool (sole caller); mod:repovine/src/semantic/store SemanticIndex; consumed by agents reading emptyDiagnostic.nextActions.
annotation.dataFlow: executeTool → handler response → scopeMissDiagnosticOf gate → semanticIndex.embedQuery(scope||nodeId) → query + score floor → filter by graph.nodes.has → dedupe → push {when, tool, args} actions.

annotation.summary: Scope-aware MCP navigation hint generator. Given a ResolvedScope, returns suggested follow-up tool calls (deeper/sideways/up/cross_layer/validate sections) tailored to package, domain, module, or export-symbol scopes — used in envelope responses to guide agents toward relevant next MCP calls.

keyExports.scopeNavigation: Builds Navigation object with up to 4 items per section based on scope.kind.

assumptions: Propagation review: verified upstream envelope/pagination.
risks: Domain navigation suggests search_context with heuristic query — may miss runtime anchors on sparse domains.
Package scope always suggests get_entrypoints even when package has no runtime entrypoints.
patterns: Only scopeNavigation is exported; local nav() duplicates envelope.nav pattern.
validate section always suggests get_annotation_status coverage for package/domain scopes.
invariants: Returns empty deeper/sideways for kind:all except up map_context.
Never mutates scope — read-only hint generation.
annotation.integrationPoints: Imported by mcp/response/envelope envelopeError and handlers that attach navigation; uses ResolvedScope from scope/resolve.
annotation.dataFlow: ResolvedScope → scopeNavigation → partial Navigation → merged into envelope() by callers.

annotation.summary: MCP scope resolution: translates human/agent scope strings and forgiving aliases into ResolvedScope for all graph tools; nodeInScope filters handler results.

keyExports.ResolvedScope: Parsed scope with kind, nodeId, domainId, packageId, query.
keyExports.nodeInScope: Membership test for handler result filtering.
keyExports.resolveResourceInfraAlias: Forgiving resource:/infra: lookup by label or bare name.
keyExports.resolveScope: Main parser for mod:/export:/domain:/pkg:/resource:/infra: and path aliases.

assumptions: Ambiguous relaxed package matches return undefined — never pick arbitrarily.
Bootstrap import enables pluginUsesLooseNameSeparators for Python package names.

sideEffects.description: Bootstrap registers source plugins for loose name separators

risks: Ambiguous package name matches stay unresolved.
patterns: normalizeLookupPath for case-insensitive path matching.
firstResultId/topSearchResultIds bridge search_context to navigation.
annotation.flowDescription: Forgiving scope parser bridging human/agent shorthand (paths, package names, service labels) to canonical graph node ids.
invariants: scope 'all' never carries nodeId.
resource:/infra: alias requires exactly one matching node.
annotation.integrationPoints: Every mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/* handler; mod:repovine/src/mcp/boundary-index resolveNodeRelPath; mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/bootstrap. TypeScript tsconfig discovery (transitive): mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/list-tsconfig-files.

annotation.summary: Ordered graceful-shutdown sequence for the MCP server, dependency-injected so the phase ORDER is unit-testable outside the CLI entry. createShutdownSequence runs a fixed 6-phase teardown; abortMcpBuilds fans cancellation across the independent build owners.

keyExports.ShutdownBuildDeps: Injected per-owner abort handles for abortMcpBuilds.
keyExports.abortMcpBuilds: Live-owner adapter: starts startup + refresh + reloadConfig aborts concurrently before awaiting any, so a slow owner does not block the others; per-owner failures are logged and absorbed.
keyExports.createShutdownSequence: Returns a once-guarded handler running: close admission → abort all build kinds → drain in-flight tool calls → inline plugin teardown → drain annotations → after-flush hooks → transport close → exit. A reserved cleanupTailMs stops the build-abort wait and tool-call poll before the deadline so teardown/drain always run.

assumptions: exit(), log(), and the phase operations are injected — the module owns no process/global state itself.
deadlineMs defaults 8s, buildAbortGraceMs 4s, cleanupTailMs 2s of that deadline.

sideEffects.description: unref'd hard-exit backstop timer + build-abort grace timer
races build-abort against the grace budget; polls inFlightToolCalls until the cleanup boundary

risks: Phase order is load-bearing: aborting builds before the tool-call drain unblocks refresh long-polls so the drain can finish; reversing it deadlocks until the deadline.
The reserved cleanup tail is what lets a hung build plus a stuck tool call still reach annotation drain before the unref'd hard-exit backstop fires; shrinking it to zero re-opens that starvation.
annotation.integrationPoints: Wired by mod:repovine/src/mcp/index (createShutdownHandler passes live process state); abortMcpBuilds drives controller.cancel(), mod:repovine/src/mcp/context abortActiveRefresh(), and mod:repovine/src/mcp/reload-config abortActive().

annotation.summary: Module src/mcp/tool-defs.ts in repovine

keyExports.ToolDef: One entry: name, description and argument schema.
keyExports.getRequiredArgs: Derives the required argument names from the schema's own optionality.
keyExports.getToolDef: Looks a definition up by name.
keyExports.toolDefs: The ordered catalog, every entry extended with the shared response and session arguments.

assumptions: The shared arguments are added to every tool in one place rather than repeated per definition, so no tool can be published without them.
Required arguments are read off the schema rather than listed separately, so the two cannot disagree.

Descriptions are part of the contract, not documentation: they carry when to reach for a tool, what an empty result means, and which follow-up to make, and that prose is what steers an agent's choice.
Some of that prose comes from the same shared guidance constants the generated client assets use, so a rule is worded once and appears everywhere.
A definition and its handler are registered separately, and a definition without a handler fails at startup rather than at call time.
risks: A tool's description can promise a bound the server does not honour, and nothing checks prose against behaviour.

Adding a tool means changing the catalog, the handler and the always-on reference together. A definition and its handler are registered separately and reconciled only by a test, so a definition with no handler is advertised normally and fails on first call as an unknown tool.

risks.text: A schema that admits an argument the handler ignores validates successfully and does nothing, so the public surface should expose only parameters a handler honours.

patterns: One definition drives both registration and validation, which is what keeps the published schema and the enforced schema identical.
The behavioural contract lives beside the machine one, so a change in how a tool should be used is made where the tool is defined.
invariants: Every published tool accepts the shared response-format and session arguments.

Registration walks the catalog, so the two sets are never compared. A handler with no catalog entry is never registered and is unreachable — silently absent rather than diagnosed. A catalog entry with no handler advertises and validates normally and fails only when an agent calls it, unless the server answers that name itself before reaching the handler, which is how the build-status tool is served.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered and validated by the server entry under mod:repovine/src/mcp; shared guidance prose comes from mod:repovine/src/cli/onboarding-assets; the analysis categories enumerated in one schema come from mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/types; session and phase vocabularies from mod:repovine/src/agents/protocol.
annotation.dataFlow: definitions with schemas and descriptions → shared arguments appended → registration with the protocol library and per-call validation → the tool list and call behaviour an agent sees.

keyExports.handleAnalyzeArchitecture: Runs detector suite, returns categorized RefactoringFinding list with optional detail expansion.

assumptions: strictness and thresholds from mod:repovine/src/config analyze_architecture block.
detailFindingId triggers mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detail expansion.
risks: strict vs balanced strictness changes security-sensitive category volume.
annotationReasoning omitted when detectors do not opt in.
patterns: Read-only candidate report — findings are architectural hypotheses, not proven safe refactors.
annotation.flowDescription: Scope + categories → handleAnalyzeArchitecture → ranked architectural candidates with optional detail expansion.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detectors; mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/detail refactoringCategoryDetail; mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/envelope.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + mode → state slice from ctx.getState → runRefactoringReport|runRefactoringOpportunityDetail → envelope with findings navigation.

annotation.summary: MCP analyze_dependencies handler: resolves scope, selects mode (impact, package-boundaries, interfaces, callgraph), dispatches to lib/dependencies analyzers with empty diagnostics.

keyExports.defaultDependencyMode: Selects default analyze_dependencies mode from ResolvedScope kind.

assumptions: defaultDependencyMode picks impact for modules, package-boundaries for pkg: scopes.
Mode dispatch delegates to mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/* analyzers.
risks: Wrong mode for scope kind returns dependencyModeScopeMismatchDiagnostic.
exportName only affects impact mode downstream filtering.
patterns: Contract axis — run before editing shared exports or package boundaries.
annotation.flowDescription: scope + mode → handleAnalyzeDependencies → dispatches impact/import-map/package-boundaries/callgraph analyzers.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/impact; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/package-boundaries; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/interfaces; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/dependencies/callgraph.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + mode → resolveScope → analyzer → envelope with mode/analysis/emptyDiagnostic.

annotation.summary: The two annotation-merge tools. One reports whether the annotation file currently carries conflict markers and what merge review is outstanding. The other runs the semantic merge on disk, optionally as a dry run, forgets entries deleted on the other side, and reloads the engine state when a write actually happened, then points the caller at the nodes that still need manual resolution.

keyExports.handleGetAnnotationMergeStatus: Reports the annotation file's merge state without touching it.
keyExports.handleMergeAnnotations: Runs the on-disk merge, optionally dry, and refreshes engine state when the file was written.

assumptions: A dry run reports what would happen and never writes, so a caller can inspect the outcome before committing to it.
A write is followed by a state reload, because the in-memory store would otherwise diverge from the file just rewritten.

A deletion the merge honors is forgotten rather than resurrected, so the reload that follows does not write it back. Honoring turns on whether the other side left the entry untouched, not on which side deleted it: a deletion the other side contested with an edit loses, and the edited entry survives with a conflict recorded.
Verified 2026-07-23: handleGetAnnotationMergeStatus/handleMergeAnnotations and the delegation to mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance unchanged; content-hash refresh only.

sideEffects.description: the merge rewrites the annotation file unless the call is a dry run
reloads the engine state after a successful write

risks: A merge running concurrently with a git operation on the same file has no lock between them, so the two writers can interleave.
Nodes whose conflict the merge cannot resolve are listed for manual resolution; leaving them means the file still carries unresolved state even though the tool reported success.
patterns: Thin wrappers over the disk-merge helpers, with the state reload attached here because only the tool layer knows about the engine context.
invariants: A non-dry merge reloads the engine state only when it wrote the file. A merge that finds nothing to resolve reports success and leaves the loaded state untouched.
The status tool never writes.
annotation.integrationPoints: Both delegate to the merge helpers in mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance; the state reload goes through the MCP context.
annotation.dataFlow: merge request → on-disk merge or dry-run report → state reload when written → response listing what merged and what still needs manual resolution.

annotation.summary: refresh_context MCP tool wrapper — synchronization barrier after code or annotation edits. Calls lib/annotations refreshContextCore for graph rebuild with stats, optionally deletes orphaned annotations when cleanupOrphans:true.

keyExports.handleRefreshContext: Synchronization barrier after code changes — rebuilds graph and reports orphan count.

assumptions: Synchronization barrier — rebuilds graph after code/annotation edits.
cleanupOrphans:true deletes annotations for removed modules (irreversible).

sideEffects.description: Triggers full graph rebuild
Optional orphan deletion when cleanupOrphans set

risks: cleanupOrphans:true irreversibly deletes — requires git restore to undo.
patterns: Synchronization barrier.
annotation.flowDescription: Optional cleanupOrphans → refreshContextCore → optional cleanup → envelope with payloads.
annotation.integrationPoints: mcp/lib/annotations refreshContextCore; mcp/context IndexBuildController; mcp/response/pagination (envelope).
annotation.dataFlow: cleanupOrphans flag → refreshContextCore → optional cleanup → envelope with refresh+cleanup payloads.

annotation.summary: The annotation-status tool wrapper. Resolves the requested scope, then routes the requested view to the matching helper: coverage, the unified drain queue, the propagation-only filter, the propagation preview for one upstream, the orphan list, the risk-scope candidates advisory, the carrier-gap advisory, or everything at once. Paging and domain filtering are applied here rather than in each helper.

keyExports.domainLabelForQueue: Strips the domain prefix off a resolved scope so the queue and coverage filters can use a bare label.
keyExports.handleGetAnnotationStatus: The tool entry: resolves scope, dispatches the view, and attaches the refresh follow-up navigation.

assumptions: The queue is one unified backlog across node types; the view selects a projection of it rather than a separate list.
The view argument is a closed set checked before the handler runs, so an unrecognized name is rejected as an invalid argument; the coverage default applies only when the view is omitted.
Scope, paging and domain arguments are resolved once for every view; each helper applies them to its own list.
The advisory views (risk-scope candidates and carrier gaps) are paged and do not affect the work counters, so a clean queue can still list them.
risks: Queue offsets shift as annotations are written, so paging deeper while draining skips items; the queue is meant to be drained from the top.
patterns: A thin dispatcher: every view's computation lives in the annotation library, and this module owns only routing, scope filtering and paging.
annotation.flowDescription: The requested view and scope select one helper, whose result is wrapped with navigation pointing at the natural follow-up.
annotation.integrationPoints: All views are computed by mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/annotations; the scope is resolved through mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve and paging defaults come from mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: resolved scope plus view → the matching annotation helper → response envelope carrying that view's payload and its follow-up navigation.

annotation.summary: The annotation-validation tool wrapper. Runs the health check of the annotation store against the current graph and returns its counts, the merge state of the file, the advisory findings, and navigation pointing at the natural follow-ups. Read-only: it reports what is wrong without repairing anything.

keyExports.handleValidateAnnotations: The tool entry: runs the health check for the whole workspace or a named scope and wraps the result with follow-up navigation.

assumptions: The check compares the stored annotations against the graph as currently built, so its verdict is only as fresh as the last graph refresh.
A scope argument narrows the reported work without changing what is validated globally, which is what lets a sub-agent see just its own slice.
Verified 2026-07-23: handleValidateAnnotations and its delegation to mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance health check unchanged; content-hash refresh only.
