risks: The queue sample in the response is truncated, so it indicates the head of the backlog rather than enumerating it; the status tool is the paged view.
Because the verdict is computed against the current graph, running it before a refresh reports staleness that a refresh would resolve, and misses staleness a refresh would reveal.
patterns: A thin wrapper: the whole computation lives in the annotation maintenance module and this handler only shapes the response.
invariants: The check never mutates the annotation file.
annotation.integrationPoints: Delegates to the health check in mod:repovine/src/annotations/maintenance, resolves an optional scope through mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/resolve, and points follow-ups at the merge, refresh and queue paths.
annotation.dataFlow: engine state and workspace root → health check against the graph → counts, merge state and advisories → response envelope with follow-up navigation.

annotation.summary: write_annotation MCP tool wrapper. Delegates to lib/annotations annotateModule (schema validation, secret rejection, quality scoring, importBaseline, in-memory store set); the store persists via an 800ms debounced save, so the write is in memory now and on disk shortly. When args.durable===true it awaits annotations.flushAsync() and reports persistence.{durable,persisted,lastSaveError} so the response reflects a durable commit; a flush failure is reported (persistenceError) while the annotation stays safe in memory. Wraps the result in the standard envelope with a post-save inspect_node navigation hint.

keyExports.handleWriteAnnotation: MCP entry for annotation writes — never hand-edit repovine.annots.json.

assumptions: Delegates to annotateModule for schema validation and secret rejection.
Post-save navigation hints inspect_node on the written nodeId.

sideEffects.description: Persists via AnnotationStore in annotateModule

risks: Bypassing annotateModule (manual JSON edit) corrupts merge metadata and freshness.
patterns: Thin MCP wrapper — business logic lives in mcp/lib/annotations.
annotation.flowDescription: MCP args → handleWriteAnnotation → annotateModule → quality score + persistence → envelope with navigation hint.
invariants: write_annotation must merge partial updates without dropping unrelated fields.
Quality score is completeness only — consistency checked separately.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/annotations annotateModule; mod:repovine/src/annotations/store AnnotationStore. Envelope pagination (transitive): mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: nodeId + annotation JSON → annotateModule → envelope with quality score.

annotation.summary: MCP tool handler for get_context_session_quality: looks up a worker-runtime context session report from contextQualityStore with optional policy overrides (phase, mode, thresholds, assignmentScope) and consume/retain flags. Not the harness protocol compliance gate — use CLI validate/compliance for that.

keyExports.handleGetContextSessionQuality: Returns scored context session report or error when store unavailable or sessionId not found.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream mcp/types; context session quality handler unchanged.

sideEffects.description: Optional consume/retainSession mutates store when args.consume or args.retainSession are true

risks: Store unavailable in lightweight CLI subprocesses returns a clear error, not a silent empty report.
Invalid sessionId returns not-found error rather than partial report.
patterns: Meta tool — excluded from its own quality recording.
annotation.flowDescription: contextSessionId → aggregate per-tool byte counts → quality score vs threshold.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered in mcp/tools registry; contextQualityStore populated by recordContextQualityCall in mcp/index.ts.
annotation.dataFlow: args.sessionId + policy → contextQualityStore.getReport → JSON report or error envelope.

annotation.summary: One MCP surface for recording that an advisory was reviewed and rejected, dispatched by a required kind argument. The domains kind merges the declined suggestion ids into the workspace onboarding state and recomputes the remaining suggestions; the carrier-link kind validates the requested targets against the pairs actually flagged, stamps each with the target's current risk hash, and merges them into the carrier review file. An unknown or missing kind returns an error naming the valid kinds and writes nothing.

keyExports.DECLINE_ADVISORY_KINDS: The accepted advisory kinds, also used to build the error message for an unknown one.
keyExports.DeclineAdvisoryKind: The union derived from that list.
keyExports.handleDeclineAdvisory: The handler: dispatches on kind to the domains or carrier-link decline path.

assumptions: Both kinds of state are workspace-local and stored separately, so declining one advisory never touches the other's record.
A carrier-link decline is stamped with the target's current risk hash, so the suppression expires when the target's consumer risks change.
The per-kind result payload shape is part of the tool contract and is asserted by the handler tests.

Verified 2026-07-23: DECLINE_ADVISORY_KINDS and handleDeclineAdvisory dispatch (domains -> stage2/domains-advisor + mcp/onboarding-state; carrier-link -> annotations/carrier-review + annotations/carrier-links) unchanged; content-hash refresh only.

sideEffects.description: writes the onboarding state or the carrier review file on a successful decline; nothing is written for an empty request, an ignored id, or a bad kind

risks: A decline reason is persisted only for the carrier-link kind; the domains path accepts a reason and discards it, since that state stores bare ids.
Requested targets are validated against what is currently flagged, so declining a target that is not presently a gap is silently ignored rather than rejected.
invariants: An unknown or missing kind writes nothing and returns an error listing the valid kinds.
Carrier-link declines record the risk hash alongside the decision.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered in the MCP tool dispatch table; the domains path delegates to mod:repovine/src/mcp/onboarding-state and mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-advisor, and the carrier path to mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-review and mod:repovine/src/annotations/carrier-links.
annotation.dataFlow: tool call with a kind and target ids → validated against the current advisories → merged into the matching workspace-local state → result reporting what was recorded.

annotation.summary: get_config_surface wrapper that turns invalid/unsafe filter results into error envelopes, otherwise adds binding navigation and scoped empty diagnostics.

keyExports.handleGetConfigSurface: Scoped env/secret/resource listing with optional kind and namePattern filters.

assumptions: Reports env var names only — never secret values.
Empty scope uses configSurfaceEmptyDiagnostic helper.
risks: Dynamic env access may be under-detected vs declared envDependencies in annotations.
patterns: Env names only — never values — extracted for agent safety.
annotation.flowDescription: scope → scan config + env var names + resource bindings → concise config surface envelope.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/config-surface collectConfigSurface; mod:repovine/src/mcp/scope/navigation per-binding inspect_node hints. Envelope pagination (transitive): mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + filters → collectConfigSurface → envelope.

annotation.summary: `get_entrypoints` MCP tool thin wrapper. Delegates to `lib/entrypoints.collectEntrypoints` (frontend file routes, IaC triggers, Python FastAPI/Django/DRF backend API routes), adds drill-down navigation and `entrypointsEmptyDiagnostic` on zero results.

keyExports.handleGetEntrypoints: Scoped entrypoint listing with kind/layer filters via collectEntrypoints.

assumptions: Entrypoint slots come from stage2 interpreter registry.
Empty scope returns entrypointsEmptyDiagnostic.
risks: Missing layer contributions yield empty entrypoints for non-TS stacks.
patterns: Pairs with trace_flow for user-journey anchoring.
annotation.flowDescription: scope + filters → list runtime entrypoints (HTTP, queues, schedules) from graph entrypoint store.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/entrypoints; mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-store. Envelope pagination (transitive): mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + args → collectEntrypoints (incl. Python backend api) → envelope with navigation hints.

annotation.summary: The inspect_node tool handler. Resolves the requested scope, delegates the detail build to the core, attaches the runtime handoff for resource nodes, assembles the navigation hints, and hoists the obligation-carrying investigate references into a top-level attention block so a caller sees what it must look at before treating the node as understood. The advisory structural tags stay inline on the reference and never reach that block.

keyExports.handleInspectNode: The tool entry: scope resolution, detail build, runtime handoff, navigation, and the attention block.
keyExports.selfBoundaryAttention: Attention when the inspected node is itself a boundary surface, gated by the boundary mechanic.
keyExports.selfWiringAttention: Attention when the node sits in the deployed runtime topology, gated by the wiring mechanic and the graph's edge counts.

assumptions: The detail build, including annotation metadata and the investigate tags, belongs to the core module; this handler arranges and hoists rather than deciding what is flagged.
Self-attention is gated through the mechanics registry, so the same predicate decides a self flag here and a neighbour flag elsewhere.
A domain scope resolves through the scope's domain id rather than by string matching.

risks.text: The hub tag is deliberately excluded from the attention block to avoid flooding on a large repository, so a caller must still read the inline investigate tags on high-in-degree references.

risks: Must-inspect pointers are capped in the navigation, so a node with many obligations shows a subset and the rest are reachable only by paging.

A body search on a very large file can hit the time cap; the search then reports the deadline and carries no matches at all, so an incomplete search is distinguishable from an empty one only by that error. The line-length and match-count bounds behave differently — they return partial results and flag the truncation alongside the matches they did assemble.
patterns: Resource nodes get their handler hint pushed to the front of the navigation, so the code that owns the resource is the first thing offered.
A node inspected without a body gets a bounded body hint rather than the body itself.
annotation.flowDescription: nodeId + body/export pagination → buildInspectNodeDetail → annotation meta + navigation hints.
invariants: The hub tag never enters the attention block.
An unresolved scope returns an empty diagnostic with search and map next actions rather than an error.
annotation.integrationPoints: Builds detail through mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/inspect-node-core, resolves investigate references through mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/investigate-refs, attaches resource handoff through mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/runtime-handoff, and gates self-attention through mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry.
annotation.dataFlow: scope resolution → detail build → optional runtime handoff → navigation assembly → attention hoisted from the drill-down, links and investigate pointers → response envelope.

annotation.summary: map_context MCP tool handler. Maps resolved scopes to code-structure overviews: all (repo stats + packages), domain (summary or modules view via lib/domain-map), query (searchGraph fallback), or node path-from-root paginated ancestry. Attaches mapContextEmptyDiagnostic on empty domain/module views.

keyExports.handleMapContext: Scope router with view=summary|modules and pagination.

assumptions: summary and modules views delegate to domain-map helpers.
Query scopes rank on the token index only; semantic ranking reaches searchGraph from search_context alone.
risks: Domain scopes are path tags — may be runtime-empty for untagged packages.
patterns: summary view first for large domains — paginate with limit/offset.
annotation.flowDescription: scope + view → paginated domain/package summary or module list with connectivity sorting.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/domain-map; mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-graph; mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/pagination. Domain slice pagination (transitive): mod:repovine/src/mcp/domain-pagination.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + view → resolveScope → domain-map or pathFromRoot or searchGraph → envelope.

annotation.summary: The dispatch table for the public MCP tools: one plain map from tool name to handler, covering the navigation, runtime, dependency, architecture, config and annotation tools plus the advisory and session-quality ones. Importing this module also wires the empty-diagnostic collectors, which is how the diagnostics module gets its dependencies without importing the tools back and creating a cycle.

keyExports.toolHandlers: The complete name-to-handler map for the public tools.

assumptions: The map is a literal listing every public tool by name; the answerable-name set is fixed by the tool definitions and the map is consulted after that gate.
Every handler receives the same runtime context assembled by the MCP server.
The collector wiring happens as an import side effect, before any handler runs.

sideEffects.description: wiring the empty-diagnostic collectors mutates that module's state at import time

risks: The wiring runs on import, so the effect depends on this module being imported before the diagnostics are used; a second registry would silently overwrite the collectors.
A handler added to a tool's own module but not listed here is unreachable, and nothing reports the omission.
patterns: A single dispatch table, so the set of public tools is readable in one place rather than assembled across registrations.
Dependency injection through the wiring call, which is what lets the diagnostics module ask about entrypoints and config without depending on the tools.
annotation.flowDescription: Side-effect import wires empty-diagnostics collectors; mcp/index executeTool looks up toolHandlers[name] after IndexBuildController ready gate.
invariants: The map supplies the handler for every public tool except get_build_status, which the server answers itself ahead of the lookup so it stays callable while the graph is building.
The collector wiring precedes any handler invocation because it is an import-time side effect.
annotation.integrationPoints: Imports every handler under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools, wires the collectors declared in mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/empty-diagnostics with the entrypoint and config-surface libraries, and is looked up by the MCP server when it executes a tool.
annotation.dataFlow: tool call → name looked up in this map → the handler runs with the runtime context → response envelope.

annotation.summary: The search_context handler: tokenized graph search with an AND or OR strategy, an optional semantic ranking boost, escalation of annotation-matched hits into inspect navigation, and a diagnostic explaining an empty result. It pins one engine state snapshot at entry and threads it through every read, so ranking and graph lookups cannot straddle two graph generations across the embedding await.

keyExports.handleSearchContext: The tool entry: token search with type filters and optional semantic boost, over a single pinned state.
keyExports.isWeakRelaxedSearchMatch: Whether a relaxed match is weak enough that the caller should confirm it by inspecting rather than trusting the hit.

assumptions: The match mode controls how tokens combine. Weak tokens carry reduced weight and a smaller candidate budget; the auto-relaxed OR path suppresses them outright when no strong token hits the index, and reports that as weakTokenOnlySuppressed with an empty result.
Annotation-matched top hits are escalated into inspect navigation, since an annotation match means someone already wrote about the node.
Semantic ranking is available only when embeddings are enabled in the workspace configuration.
Verified 2026-07-23: handleSearchContext/isWeakRelaxedSearchMatch and imports (search-graph, config-surface, entrypoints, search-annotation-escalation) unchanged; content-hash refresh only.
risks: A relaxed match on a single token is a weak signal that needs confirmation by inspection; treating it as an answer is how a search leads somewhere plausible and wrong.
Semantic ranking silently does nothing when embeddings are disabled, so results differ between workspaces without any indication in the response.
patterns: State is captured once and threaded, rather than re-read per step, which is what makes a concurrent refresh unable to mix one generation's ranking onto another's graph.
The primary orienting tool: it is meant to run before any blind file reading on a fuzzy task.
annotation.flowDescription: Query tokens are searched against the index, optionally re-ranked semantically, merged with auxiliary config and entrypoint matches, and returned with navigation.
invariants: Every read inside one call observes the same engine state generation.
The empty diagnostic is omitted when auxiliary config or entrypoint matches exist, since the result is not truly empty.
annotation.integrationPoints: Searches through mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-graph with the pinned state, escalates annotation hits through mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-annotation-escalation, and folds in auxiliary matches from the config-surface and entrypoint libraries.
annotation.dataFlow: query → pinned state → optional semantic ranking → graph search fusion on that same state → auxiliary matches → response with navigation and, when empty, a diagnostic.

annotation.summary: Read-only tool returning the domain-config suggestions the build already computed, together with two ready-to-write previews: the merged config that excludes the suggested noise, and the keep config that instead marks those resources as deliberately kept so they stay visible and stop being suggested. It never writes; applying a preview is the user's decision.

keyExports.handleSuggestDomainsConfig: Returns the pending suggestions, the merge strategy, and the two config previews with follow-up navigation.

assumptions: The suggestions are computed during the build and merely read here, so this handler never recomputes them.
The two previews are symmetric alternatives for the same suggestion: exclude the resource, or commit a keep marker for it.
Ids the user wants neither to apply nor to keep seeing are recorded through the shared decline tool rather than here.
Verified 2026-07-23: handleSuggestDomainsConfig and its read of stage2 domains-advisor suggestions plus stage2/domains-schema merge strategy unchanged; content-hash refresh only.
risks: Applying a preview without reading it pollutes the committed domains config, which is why the tool returns a preview rather than writing one.
The keep preview appears only when at least one suggestion is of a keepable kind, so its absence means the suggestions offer no keep option rather than that keeping is unavailable in general.
patterns: A passthrough handler: the advisory computation lives in the build pipeline and this tool only presents it with the two actionable shapes.
annotation.flowDescription: The build computes the suggestions into engine state; this handler reads them and returns the additions alongside both config previews.
invariants: The domains config file is never written by this tool.
The keep preview is surfaced only when the suggestions include a keepable kind.
annotation.integrationPoints: Reads the suggestions produced by the domains advisor in the stage2 pipeline and the merge strategy declared in mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-schema; declines are recorded through the shared advisory decline tool in mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools/decline-advisory.
annotation.stateShape: The response carries the additions, the merged config, an optional keep config, the merge strategy and the axis metadata.

annotation.summary: MCP trace_flow handler: projects runtime services/resources/data flows, filters services to the resolved scope before pagination, optionally adds entrypoints, runtime handoff, diagnostics, and navigation.

keyExports.handleTraceFlow: Projects scoped runtime topology and reports service totals/truncation from the filtered service set.

assumptions: Runtime services, resources, flows, and entrypoints originate from stage2 interpreter graph facts.
The public tool does not advertise an unimplemented traversal depth or destination constraint.
risks: Missing interpreter facts yield an empty trace with a diagnostic rather than proving no runtime behavior.
Broad topology projections are bounded by pagination.
patterns: User/runtime flow axis — pair with get_entrypoints for entry discovery.
Filter service scope before slice/total/truncated calculation.
annotation.flowDescription: resolveScope → projectRuntimeTopology → scope-filter services → paginate services/resources/flows → optional entrypoints/runtime handoff → envelope and empty diagnostic.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-store; mod:repovine/src/mcp/response/empty-diagnostics traceFlowEmptyDiagnostic.
annotation.dataFlow: scope + include + offset/limit → topology projection → scoped service page and independent resource/flow pages → response totals, handoff, diagnostics, navigation.

annotation.summary: The contract every server tool handler is written against: the shape of the built repository state, the runtime a handler receives, the handler signature itself, and a small helper that normalizes a caller-supplied node identifier. Types and one function, with no runtime effects of its own.

keyExports.McpToolRuntime: What a handler is handed: accessors for the state and the configuration, a way to trigger a rebuild, the repository root, the optional per-request cancellation signal, and the context session.
keyExports.RefreshRepoStateOptions: Whether a rebuild should also re-read the configuration.
keyExports.RefreshRepoStateResult: Whether the runtime was actually replaced with one built from reloaded configuration.
keyExports.RepovineState: Everything built per graph build: the graph, the snapshot, the module index, the token and semantic indexes, the annotations, the domain configuration and its suggestions, the resolved analysis thresholds, and when it was built.
keyExports.SemanticSearchRefresh: The four possible outcomes of a semantic index sync.
keyExports.resolveNodeId: Returns the identifier the graph knows, trying an exact match and then a normalized form.

assumptions: The state is replaced whole on each build rather than mutated, which is why the runtime exposes an accessor instead of the object: a handler that reads it once and holds it across a rebuild is working from the previous graph.
The build timestamp travels with the state so a response can say how old the graph behind it is.

The cancellation signal belongs to one request and is raised when the client cancels; a handler that ignores it simply runs to completion, so honouring it is a property of each long-running operation rather than something enforced here.
The context session identifier is placed on the runtime by the executor because the raw arguments are stripped before a handler runs, so a handler cannot recover it from its own arguments.

Identifier normalization drops a source extension and a trailing index segment from an identifier that is already package-qualified, rescuing a stored id copied with the extension attached or with the index segment spelled out. Resolution is exact lookup on both forms, so a bare file path is not a graph key and resolves to nothing here.

risks.text: This is the contract the entire tool surface is written against: a change to the state or runtime shape reaches every handler and the compliance checks at once. Removing or retyping a field fails the build at every reader and at the site that assembles the state, so the cost is the breadth of the edit. What fails quietly instead are the optional runtime fields, which a handler can omit and still compile.

risks: Identifier normalization strips a fixed set of source extensions, so a path in another language normalizes only if its identifiers already omit the extension; anything else resolves to nothing rather than to a near match.
The cancellation signal is optional on the runtime, so a handler written without it compiles and runs unbounded; nothing marks which operations should be honouring it.
patterns: Accessors rather than values, so a handler always reads the current build instead of a captured one.
One types module for the whole tool surface, which is what keeps thirty-odd handlers agreeing on their context without importing each other.
invariants: The state carries the timestamp of the build that produced it.
A handler never receives the state object directly, only a way to fetch the current one.
Identifier resolution returns nothing rather than a guess when neither form is in the graph.
annotation.integrationPoints: The state is assembled by the server runtime under mod:repovine/src/mcp and consumed by every handler under mod:repovine/src/mcp/tools; its parts come from mod:repovine/src/annotations/store, mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/search-index, mod:repovine/src/semantic/store, mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains and its advisor, mod:repovine/src/analysis/architecture/config, and mod:repovine/src/context-quality/session-store.
annotation.dataFlow: a build produces the state → the runtime wraps it with accessors, the request signal and the resolved session → a handler reads the current state, may trigger a rebuild, and returns its result.

annotation.summary: The delivery-mechanics registry: the single place declaring which risk-delivery mechanics exist, in what priority, what primitive each reads, and how each is detected. Array order is the tag priority. Detection predicates are referenced from the rule modules that own them rather than reimplemented here, so the registry stays dispatch and the rules stay where they are defined.

keyExports.DELIVERY_MECHANICS: The ordered mechanic entries; array order is the tag priority.
keyExports.DELIVERY_MECHANIC_PRIORITY: The priority list derived from registry order.
keyExports.HUB_IMPORTER_FLOOR: The absolute importer floor for the hub mechanic, also the floor under the adaptive threshold.
keyExports.deliveryMechanic: Lookup by tag id; total, since every tag has a registered mechanic.

assumptions: The registry declares seven mechanics in this order: risk, boundary, effect, unannotated, wiring, co-change, hub.

Annotation-derived detection is referenced from the rule modules that own it; topology-derived detection is declared in the registry itself, including the hub importer floor that other modules re-export from here.
The consumer mechanic emits the tag named risk; that naming skew is inherited and visible in the API responses.
The co-change mechanic is semantically symmetric, but the direction enum has no symmetric value, so it is declared as propagating to keep it out of push admission.

sideEffects.description: a declarative registry with pure detection predicates

risks: Array order is the tag priority, so inserting or reordering an entry changes the priority for every delivery channel at once.
Detection is all the registry currently dispatches: the channel and direction metadata is descriptive, and the delivery machinery does not yet route through it.
The hub mechanic self-gates to false when no importer count is supplied; the threshold falls back to the floor when no adaptive threshold is supplied.
patterns: Adding a mechanic means declaring an entry at its priority slot; each detect self-gates to false when its primitive is absent, so no core edit is needed.
Each entry records which primitive it reads, which keeps the annotation-derived mechanics distinguishable from the topology-derived ones.
invariants: The priority list is the registry order and is pinned by a unit test, so a reorder fails loudly rather than silently changing tag precedence.
The unannotated mechanic is reserved: its detection always returns false and no channel produces it.
The wiring mechanic fires on a resource-to-handler in-edge or a handler-to-resource out-edge; the resource-side relations belong to flow tracing rather than to this mechanic.
The co-change mechanic fires on an implements edge in either direction.
annotation.integrationPoints: Composes predicates from mod:repovine/src/annotations/format and mod:repovine/src/annotations/side-effect-vocab, takes its tag type from mod:repovine/src/types and its context type from mod:repovine/src/mechanics/types, and is consumed by the investigate-reference resolution and the node inspection tool.
annotation.dataFlow: context (node id, annotation, importer count, edge counts, hub threshold) → each mechanic's detect in registry order → emitted tags → callers cap and order them downstream.

annotation.summary: The contract the mechanics registry implements. A mechanic is one detect-and-deliver unit: its trigger is the primitives it reads plus its detection predicate, and its delivery is the channels it reaches plus whether the signal describes the node itself or obligates its consumers. Detection is what the current version actually dispatches; the channel and direction fields document delivery that each surface still performs itself.

keyExports.Channel: The delivery surfaces a signal can reach: pull-self, pull-neighbor, pull-carrier, push and advisory.
keyExports.DeliveryMechanic: One mechanic: emitted tag id, the primitives it reads, its direction, its channels, and its detection predicate.
keyExports.DeliveryMechanicContext: The inputs available to detection; only the node id is guaranteed, with the annotation and the topology accessors optional.
keyExports.Primitive: The graph primitive a trigger reads: the three annotation scopes plus absence, and the in-degree, runtime-edge and implements-edge topology inputs.

assumptions: A mechanic is scoped to a language by reading a primitive only some plugins emit, never by a conditional on language; when that primitive is absent, detection simply returns false.
The registry composes the rule predicates from the annotation modules rather than owning them, and is not their only caller.
Repo-specific judgement lives in annotation content, not in the mechanic definitions.

sideEffects.description: type-only module

risks: The channel and direction fields are descriptive in the current version: a reader who assumes the registry routes delivery will not find that machinery here.
patterns: Universal mechanics read primitives every plugin emits, while language-scoped mechanics read one only some plugins emit, so applicability is declared in data rather than branched on in code.
Every optional context input corresponds to a mechanic that self-gates without it.
invariants: Detection is total: it returns false rather than throwing when the mechanic's primitive is absent from the context.
Only the node id is guaranteed on the context; every other input is optional by contract.
annotation.integrationPoints: Implemented by mod:repovine/src/mechanics/registry; the tag and annotation types come from mod:repovine/src/types and the edge vocabulary from mod:repovine/src/graph/model. The context is assembled by the investigate-reference resolution in the MCP layer.
annotation.dataFlow: graph and annotation state → a context assembled by the caller → each mechanic's detection → emitted tags rendered per surface.

annotation.summary: Filesystem layout resolution for the engine: finds the workspace root (REPOVINE_ROOT override, else the nearest ancestor holding .git), names the committed config files, and derives the .repovine artifacts and cache directories. Also owns the non-removable engine scan ignores and the containment check that keeps a configured annotations path inside the repo. Reviewed against current source: export set (findRepoRoot, findWorkspaceRootWithin, resolveWorkspaceRoot, mergeScanIgnorePatterns, domainsConfigFilePath, resolveAnnotationsFilePath, cacheDirFor, repoRoot, packageRoot, ARTIFACTS_DIR_NAME, DOMAINS_CONFIG_FILENAME, ANNOTATIONS_FILENAME, REPOVINE_ENGINE_SCAN_IGNORE_PATTERNS, artifactsDir, cacheDir) is unchanged from the prior note.

keyExports.ARTIFACTS_DIR_NAME: Name of the engine artifacts directory, .repovine.
keyExports.REPOVINE_ENGINE_SCAN_IGNORE_PATTERNS: Engine-owned scan ignores covering .repovine paths; always applied.
keyExports.artifactsDir: The .repovine directory for the process workspace root.
keyExports.cacheDir: Cache directory for the process workspace root.
keyExports.cacheDirFor: Cache directory for a given artifacts directory; the per-repoRoot form.
keyExports.domainsConfigFilePath: Absolute path to repovine.domains.json for a repo root.
keyExports.findRepoRoot: Walks parent directories until one contains .git.
keyExports.findWorkspaceRootWithin: Finds a workspace root at or below a starting directory, if any.
keyExports.mergeScanIgnorePatterns: Prepends the engine ignores to the user's configured patterns, de-duplicated.
keyExports.packageRoot: repovine package root resolved eagerly at module load.
keyExports.repoRoot: Workspace root resolved eagerly at module load.
keyExports.resolveAnnotationsFilePath: Validates a repo-relative annotations path and returns it absolute.
keyExports.resolveWorkspaceRoot: Resolves the workspace root from the REPOVINE_ROOT override, else from the cwd walk.

assumptions: The annotations path is a repo-relative value from workspace configuration; REPOVINE_ANNOTATIONS_FILE overrides it and is validated by the same containment check.
repoRoot and packageRoot are resolved once at module load, which suits CLI and MCP cold start but fixes them for the process lifetime.
A repo is identified by the presence of .git in an ancestor directory.

sideEffects.description: findRepoRoot and package-root resolution stat .git and package.json while walking parents
reads REPOVINE_ROOT during workspace root resolution

risks: Using the process-wide cacheDir for a repo root other than the process workspace writes the snapshot cache to the wrong place; cacheDirFor(artifactsDir) is the multi-root form.

risks.text: Callers handling more than one repo root must pass that root explicitly rather than relying on the eagerly resolved repoRoot and cacheDir constants, which are fixed at module load.

patterns: Eager root resolution at module load keeps CLI and MCP cold start free of repeated parent walks.
Engine ignores are merged in front of user patterns so they cannot be dropped by configuration.
invariants: The .repovine scan ignores are non-removable: mergeScanIgnorePatterns always includes them.
resolveAnnotationsFilePath rejects an absolute path and any .. escape that would leave the repo root.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/annotations/store for the annotations file, mod:repovine/src/mcp/context for artifact and cache locations, mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains-schema for the domains config path, and stage1 scan-root resolution.
annotation.dataFlow: cwd or REPOVINE_ROOT → resolveWorkspaceRoot → repoRoot → absolute paths for the config, domains and annotations files plus the .repovine artifacts and cache directories.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_ROOT: Overrides the cwd parent walk when resolving the workspace root

annotation.summary: Opt-in build profiler for the repovine graph pipeline. A process-global singleton records RSS and heap deltas per named phase, accumulates PerfCounters over the build (packages, modules, imports/exports, infra, templates, graph nodes/edges, search tokens, snapshot bytes), appends a crash trail to disk, and prints a summary table. Entirely inert unless REPOVINE_PROFILE is set.

keyExports.MemoryProfiler: The profiler singleton reached via ensure(): phase(), setCounter/addCounter, measureJsonBytes, summaryLines(), logSummary(), reset().
keyExports.MemorySnapshot: RSS and heap figures in MB: rssMb, heapUsedMb, heapTotalMb, externalMb, arrayBuffersMb.
keyExports.PerfCounters: Build metric totals accumulated across the pipeline.
keyExports.PhaseRecord: One phase measurement: label, elapsedMs, deltaRssMb, deltaHeapMb.
keyExports.isProfileEnabled: True when the REPOVINE_PROFILE env flag is on.
keyExports.isProfileGcEnabled: True when the REPOVINE_PROFILE_GC env flag is on; forced GC needs node --expose-gc.
keyExports.profilePhase: Sync phase marker wrapping fn with a phase() boundary.
keyExports.profilePhaseAsync: Async phase marker wrapping a promise-returning fn.

assumptions: Profiling is off unless REPOVINE_PROFILE is 1 or true; the flags are read through a helper rather than a static process.env member, so the graph's static env detection only picks up REPOVINE_PROFILE_FILE, not REPOVINE_PROFILE or REPOVINE_PROFILE_GC.
Optional forced GC requires node --expose-gc when REPOVINE_PROFILE_GC is set.
REPOVINE_PROFILE_FILE overrides the crash-trail path; otherwise it falls back to a cwd default.

sideEffects.description: reads REPOVINE_PROFILE, REPOVINE_PROFILE_GC and REPOVINE_PROFILE_FILE at call time
writes and appends the crash-trail file via fs.writeFileSync/appendFileSync
globalThis.__repovineProfiler singleton shared across stage1 and stage2
calls global.gc() between phases when REPOVINE_PROFILE_GC is enabled

risks: Peak heap must stay a reduce rather than Math.max(...phases): the spread throws RangeError on the ~130k-phase arrays a long-lived process accumulates.
reset() must clear counters as well as phases, or a build reports the previous build's searchIndexTokens through the process-global singleton.
Trail truncation is isMainThread-gated so a Stage 2 worker isolate does not wipe the main thread's Stage 1 trail.
Forced GC skews phase timing when enabled, so profiled durations are not comparable to an unprofiled run.
patterns: Zero-cost when disabled: phase markers short-circuit before taking a memory reading.
One globalThis singleton spans stage1 and stage2 so counters survive the pipeline boundary.
invariants: With REPOVINE_PROFILE unset the profiler is a no-op: no counters, no phases, no file writes.
PhaseRecord carries the MemorySnapshot fields plus label, elapsedMs, deltaRssMb and deltaHeapMb.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by mod:repovine/src/stage1, mod:repovine/src/stage2 and mod:repovine/src/mcp/context, which resets at pipeline start and calls logSummary after the last counter is set.
annotation.dataFlow: REPOVINE_PROFILE=1 → profilePhase/profilePhaseAsync mark build boundaries → phase() records RSS/heap deltas → setCounter/addCounter accumulate PerfCounters → crash trail appended → logSummary prints the table.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_PROFILE_FILE: Overrides the crash-trail file path (default under cwd)

annotation.summary: Host-path canonicalization for in-memory maps keyed by absolute host paths, reconciling producers that legitimately disagree on path form (tsconfig enumeration, ts-morph sf.fileName, ts.resolveModuleName emit forward slashes; filesystem walkers emit native paths) and win32 NTFS case-insensitivity.

keyExports.hostKeyedView: Returns a canonical-keyed view (Map) of an absolute-path→id map, memoized per source Map instance via WeakMap and invalidated when the source Map's size changes; one O(n) fold pass per stage-1 worker, not per import.
keyExports.hostPathKey: path.resolve(p), lower-cased only on win32 — canonical key for an absolute host path. Resolver/map identity only; explicitly must NOT be used for security-sensitive containment checks (e.g. harness attach path-overlap), which keep strict case-sensitive comparison.

sideEffects.description: WeakMap memo caches (hostKeyedViews, hostKeyedViewSizes) keyed by the source Map instance
console.warn on a case/separator fold collision between two different module ids

risks.text: hostKeyedView's WeakMap memo is invalidated only by Map.size change; mutating an existing key's value in place without changing size, or replacing an entry, will not invalidate the cached view — the source map is expected to be construction-frozen.

risks: A fold collision between two different committed paths differing only by case/separators keeps the first entry and only warns; the repo builds different graphs on case-sensitive vs case-insensitive filesystems in that scenario.

annotation.summary: CLI dev entry for memory-profiling a cold graph build: validates a writable workspace root, defaults REPOVINE_PROFILE to 1 before static imports, loads engine modules, bootstraps RepovineRuntime with coldSnapshot, and prints node count plus the MemoryProfiler's heap/RSS summary to stdout.
assumptions: Invoked via npm run profile or node --expose-gc dist/profile.js from repo root.
REPOVINE_PROFILE is set before the MemoryProfiler singleton is first constructed; the profiler reads the flag at construction rather than at module load.
Workspace root resolved via paths.repoRoot / REPOVINE_ROOT must be writable.

sideEffects.description: process.exit(1) on invalid or non-writable repo root
mkdir probe under .repovine/.cache
defaults process.env.REPOVINE_PROFILE, enabling MemoryProfiler when the caller has not already set the variable
profiling status and node-count/RSS memory summary

risks: Running from the wrong cwd produces a misleading memory baseline and node counts.
patterns: Cold snapshot build isolates RSS baseline for graph build profiling.
annotation.flowDescription: assertWritableRepoRoot (.repovine/.cache probe) → loadConfig → await RepovineRuntime.create with coldSnapshot → MemoryProfiler table to stdout.
invariants: Dev-only entry — not used by the production MCP server path.
process.exit(1) when the repo root is missing, is not a directory, or is not writable under its artifacts dir.
annotation.integrationPoints: npm run profile CLI entry; mod:repovine/src/perf/memory-profiler (MemoryProfiler.ensure) and mod:repovine/src/mcp/context (RepovineRuntime.create) do the real work.
annotation.dataFlow: assertWritableRepoRoot (.repovine/.cache probe) -> loadConfig -> RepovineRuntime.create with coldSnapshot:true -> node count and MemoryProfiler table to stdout.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_PROFILE: Defaults to '1' at startup before imports. A value inherited from the caller wins, so 0 or empty runs this entry with MemoryProfiler instrumentation off and produces no profile table.

annotation.summary: Compiles workspace scan include/exclude globs into matcher objects and answers per path whether source or infra walk should descend. Each pattern carries a scope, so a path can be excluded from infra while visible to source. Engine-owned paths always skipped.

keyExports.CompiledScanPattern: A compiled pattern: a GlobMatcher (not regex) and the scope it applies to.
keyExports.CompiledScanPatterns: The compiled include and exclude sets.
keyExports.compileScanPatterns: Compiles configured patterns into scoped sets.
keyExports.shouldScanSourcePath: Gate for source discovery; declaration files scanned only when explicitly included.

assumptions: Include evaluated before exclude.
Engine artifact paths always skipped.
Patterns are scoped per walk.
risks: Over-broad exclude hides modules entirely rather than signaling config error.
Excluding only for infra scope leaves source walk indexing it.
patterns: Compile once, answer per path.
annotation.flowDescription: Configured patterns compile once into scoped include and exclude sets, and each candidate path is then tested against them for the walk that is asking.
invariants: Include is checked before exclude.
The engine-owned path check always applies, whatever the configuration says.
annotation.integrationPoints: Patterns from workspace config via mod:repovine/src/paths; gates applied by stage1 file walk and source plugin discovery.
annotation.stateShape: Two arrays of compiled patterns, each entry pairing a regex with the scope it applies to.

annotation.summary: Deterministic natural-language cards for semantic embedding: projectNodeCards walks eligible graph nodes, gates identifier-only nodes via cardHasSemanticSignal, buildNodeCard folds exports plus annotation summary/keyExports/risks/dataFlow/integrationPoints for SemanticIndex.sync.

keyExports.SEMANTIC_CARD_NODE_TYPES: Set(module, runtime-resource, template, package, domain) — export-symbol/capability nodes excluded.
keyExports.buildNodeCard: Deterministic NL card: label, path tokens, description, exports slice, annotation prose lines.
keyExports.projectNodeCards: Walks graph nodes, filters by type and cardHasSemanticSignal, returns nodeId→card map.

assumptions: SEMANTIC_CARD_NODE_TYPES uses satisfies readonly NodeType[] — capabilities/export-symbol excluded.
Module graph node id === ModuleInfo.id (both mod: prefix).
Identifier-only nodes skipped by cardHasSemanticSignal — token index still covers label/path/package.
Card text rebuilt every sync; SemanticIndex re-embeds only when card hash changes.
risks: Stale annotation prose embeds until node re-annotated and semantic sync runs.
patterns: Graph-node RAG: semantic hit is a node id pluggable into inspect_node, not a text chunk.
stringValues helper embeds structured integrationPoints/dataFlow objects into card lines.
annotation.flowDescription: refresh_context semantic sync → projectNodeCards → buildNodeCard per eligible node → embedder writes semantic-index.json.
invariants: buildNodeCard capped at MAX_CARD_CHARS (2000) and MAX_EXPORTS_PER_CARD (30).
Annotating a previously identifier-only node promotes it into semantic index on next sync.
annotationCardLines folds summary, keyExports, risks, invariants, flowDescription, dataFlow, integrationPoints.
annotation.integrationPoints: RepovineRuntime.syncSemanticIndexAsync calls projectNodeCards before SemanticIndex.sync; uses mod:repovine/src/annotations/format risk helpers.
annotation.dataFlow: refresh_context semantic sync → projectNodeCards (signal gate) → buildNodeCard NL text per eligible node → SemanticIndex.sync embedding corpus.

annotation.summary: The local embedding backend behind semantic search. Inference runs in process against a small MiniLM model at full precision, with no cloud call and no external daemon. The library that provides it is an opt-in peer dependency the engine does not pull, because its runtime is orders of magnitude larger than the engine itself.

keyExports.Embedder: The contract: a stable identity and a batch embed that preserves input order.
keyExports.__setTransformersModuleForTest: Injects a stand-in library and clears the memo, so the embed paths can be exercised without the real runtime.
keyExports.createEmbedder: Returns an embedder for the configured model, or nothing when embeddings are switched off.
keyExports.importTransformersFromWorkspace: Loads it from that resolution, unwrapping the module interop.
keyExports.resolveTransformersFromWorkspace: Resolves the library from the analyzed workspace, or nothing when it is not installed there.

assumptions: Lookup is two-step: the plain specifier first, then a resolution rooted at the workspace. The second step is what makes a user install take effect, because when the engine is launched through the package runner it executes from a cache that never sees the workspace's dependencies.

The inference serializer and the loaded pipeline are shared across every embedder instance, not held per instance. A rebuild or configuration reload can leave two generations alive at once; per-instance state would run concurrent inference and hold two copies of the model in memory.
The memo is keyed by workspace as well as model, since the resolution itself depends on the workspace.
Switching embeddings off returns nothing and never attempts the import, so a workspace without the library pays nothing.
A missing library raises an actionable message at the first embed rather than at construction, so startup is unaffected.
The identity encodes the model, and an index built under a different one is discarded rather than reused.

sideEffects.description: dynamically imports the embedding library and runs inference in process
reads model weights, downloaded once and cached
routes all inference through one process-wide queue

risks: Workspace resolution loads and executes code from the analyzed repository's own dependencies, so the version that runs is whatever that repository installed; the declared range only states what the calling surface was written against.
The first embed downloads the model, so a cold start pays both the download and the load before any result appears.

An embedder failure during a sync leaves the previously cached vectors serving and logs a warning on every build; embeddings being off is a standing condition reported in the refresh response rather than a failure.
The shared serializer and memo are load-bearing rather than an optimization: making them per-instance reintroduces concurrent inference and duplicated model memory across generations.
patterns: Opt-in and degradable: without the library the token search still works and only fuzzy ranking is absent.
The heavy dependency is reached through a dynamic specifier so it is never a load-time cost.
Deterministic tools stay deterministic; embeddings rank fuzzy queries and nothing else.
invariants: Embeddings switched off means no import is attempted.
The identity must match the one recorded in the index or the index is discarded.
Two workspaces never share one resolution.
Inference never runs concurrently within a process.
annotation.integrationPoints: Constructed by the server runtime's semantic index sync under mod:repovine/src/mcp with the configured flag and the workspace root; the queue primitive comes from mod:repovine/src/semantic/serialize; the model name from mod:repovine/src/config; the vectors are stored by mod:repovine/src/semantic/store.
annotation.dataFlow: configuration flag and workspace root → library resolved beside the engine or in the workspace → pipeline loaded once per workspace and model → batches embedded through the shared queue → pooled, normalized vectors stored against card hashes.

envDependencies.LOCALAPPDATA: Base cache directory on Windows when the override is unset
envDependencies.XDG_CACHE_HOME: Base cache directory on Linux when the override is unset

annotation.summary: Bounded-concurrency admission-control primitive for resources with no other cap (ONNX inference, transient worker threads). createLimiter(n) runs at most n tasks at once and FIFO-queues the rest; a queued task whose AbortSignal fires leaves the line immediately instead of waiting for admission.

keyExports.Limiter: <T>(task, signal?) => Promise<T> — the callable admission gate.
keyExports.createLimiter: Returns a Limiter capping concurrency at max(1, floor(n)); a rejecting task frees its slot, a pre-aborted signal rejects before running, and an abort while queued removes the waiter without ever consuming a slot.
keyExports.createSerializer: createLimiter(1) — tasks run one at a time in submission order.

assumptions: Callers rely on FIFO admission order and on the abort-while-queued fast path.
A task's own rejection surfaces to its caller only and does not stall the queue.

sideEffects.description: counting semaphore with a FIFO waiter queue

risks: An aborted queued task relinquishes its place without having incremented the active count — the accounting must stay balanced or the limiter leaks or under-counts concurrency.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/semantic/embedder (one module-scoped serializer shared across embedder generations) and mod:repovine/src/mcp/lib/node-body (bounded grep-worker pool).

annotation.summary: The file-backed vector index over graph node cards. It loads persisted vectors, re-embeds only the cards whose text changed, drops entries for nodes that left the graph, and answers a query by scanning every vector. There is no vector database, because the corpus is thousands of nodes rather than millions of chunks and a full scan takes milliseconds.

keyExports.SEMANTIC_INDEX_FILENAME: The file the index persists to.
keyExports.SemanticHit: One result: the node and its similarity.
keyExports.SemanticIndex: The index itself: load, sync against the current cards, embed a query, and search.
keyExports.SemanticSyncOptions: An optional progress callback during embedding.
keyExports.SemanticSyncReport: What a sync did: embedded, reused, removed and the resulting total.
keyExports.cardHash: The content key: the embedder identity and the card text hashed together.
keyExports.semanticIndexFilePath: That file's path inside a cache directory.

assumptions: The embedder identity is part of the content key, so changing the model invalidates every vector rather than mixing incompatible ones.
A persisted file from another model or another format version is discarded whole rather than partially reused, and an unreadable file simply starts an empty index that the next sync rebuilds.
Vectors are normalized on the way in, which is what makes the similarity a plain dot product.
A sync raises when the embedder fails rather than swallowing it, leaving the caller to decide whether a stale index is still worth serving.
Entries are written in sorted order so the file diffs stably between builds.
Entries whose dimensions do not match are skipped during a search, which keeps a partially migrated index usable rather than broken.

sideEffects.description: reads the persisted index
writes the index atomically after embedding or pruning
embeds pending cards in batches

risks: Saving streams the entries rather than serializing at once, and it has to: the encoded vectors make this the second-largest artifact, so a single serialization would both stall the event loop and risk the engine's string-length ceiling. A change back to whole-file serialization reintroduces both.
Searching scans every entry, so cost grows linearly with the graph; that is fine at the intended scale and is the trade that removes the database.
A failed sync leaves the previous vectors in place, so results stay answerable but describe an older graph, and only the caller's warning says so.
patterns: Content-keyed incremental sync: only what changed is re-embedded, and what disappeared is pruned in the same pass.
No external service and no database, which keeps the whole feature a local file plus an optional library.
invariants: The identity of the embedder is baked into every entry's key.
An index built by a different model is never partially reused.
The persisted file is written atomically and in a stable order.
Stored vectors are normalized.
annotation.integrationPoints: Vectors come from mod:repovine/src/semantic/embedder; the streamed atomic write from mod:repovine/src/fs/atomic; the cards are built by the semantic card layer and the sync is driven by the server runtime under mod:repovine/src/mcp, which also reports its outcome on a refresh.
annotation.dataFlow: node cards → content hashes compared against the persisted index → changed cards embedded in batches, absent nodes pruned → index streamed to disk → a query is embedded and scored against every entry, top matches returned.

annotation.summary: Module src/source-plugins/python/index.ts in repovine

keyExports.default: The plugin descriptor: identity, prerequisite, availability probe, capabilities, the two pass handlers, and the termination hook.

assumptions: The prerequisite is stated twice on purpose: declaratively as a required runtime, and as an availability probe that actually tries to import the module extraction needs. The declaration documents the dependency; the probe is what decides.
Missing the interpreter is a supported state rather than an error, so the engine skips the language and continues.
This language produces no user-interface surfaces, so the frontend detectors stay empty by construction rather than by returning nothing.
Distribution names treat the separator characters as interchangeable, which the capabilities declare so name matching is loose for this language only.
The termination hook exists because the parsing subprocesses belong to the host process rather than the worker thread that spawned them, so terminating the thread alone would leave them running.

sideEffects.description: the declared handlers spawn and signal interpreter subprocesses; the effect is realized in the extraction module

risks: Skipping is quiet by design, so a repository whose Python is never indexed looks the same in the graph as one that has none — the single warning is the only signal.
Route extraction covers what can be proven from a file's own syntax, so a route assembled across files is absent rather than partially reported.
Extraction spawns per batch, which adds a fixed cost that becomes visible on a repository with many packages.
patterns: Declare the prerequisite and probe it: the engine can decide applicability without importing anything language-specific.
The descriptor mirrors the other language plugin's shape, differing only where the language does — no interface surfaces, loose name separators, and a termination hook.
annotation.flowDescription: Same SourcePlugin object pattern as typescript: SourcePlugin default export whose setup registers the python SourcePlugin with non-overlapping .py extensions.
invariants: Nothing on this path throws when the interpreter is absent.
The declared extension list is the same one used for matching and for the capabilities.
The termination hook is the single point the engine uses to reap in-flight subprocesses.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered among the built-ins by mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/bootstrap; discovery and the interpreter probe come from mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/python/discover, extraction and the child reaping from mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/python/extract; the descriptor factory and the handler resolver from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/factory and mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/handler-resolver.
annotation.dataFlow: registration → availability probe → discovery finds packages and files → extraction parses them in a subprocess → module records; on cancellation or shutdown the termination hook reaps any live subprocess.

annotation.summary: Python discovery: locate packages by marker files, walk source files, resolve interpreter for extraction. Nothing parsed here — syntax comes later from subprocess; this pass only lists files and detects Python availability.

keyExports.PYTHON_PACKAGE_MARKERS: Two marker files: pyproject.toml and setup.py
keyExports.PythonExtractContext: Resolved interpreter (or null) handed to extraction pass.
keyExports.detectPython: Resolves interpreter once per process; null when neither candidate works; now resolves ABSOLUTE path only, skipping empty/relative/cwd PATH entries.
keyExports.discoverPython: Runs the pass: packages, pending file records, context with interpreter.
keyExports.isTrustedInterpreterPathEntry: A PATH entry is trusted only when absolute and not cwd — rejects empty/relative entries.
keyExports.safeInterpreterCwd: A temp directory used as working directory for interpreter subprocesses — hardening so repo-local python.exe cannot execute.

assumptions: Detection probes for stdlib module the extractor needs.
Package init file collapses into its directory's id.
Package name read by regex, no format dependency.
Walk descends after finding marker, so nested packages discovered as their own.
Test dirs/files excluded during discovery.

sideEffects.description: probes for usable interpreter once per process; runs subprocesses from safe non-repo cwd
walks tree for markers and source files

risks: Package name is first assignment found, regardless of section.
Nested package file claimed by whichever package walked first.
Script outside package root invisible.
Interpreter cached for process life; environment changes not revisited.
patterns: Discovery and extraction are separate passes: this one touches no syntax and only produces records plus the context the next pass needs.
Directory entries are sorted during every walk and the package list is sorted by path, which keeps output stable across runs.
annotation.flowDescription: detectPython → discoverPythonPackages → discoverPyFiles per package → SourceDiscoveryResult with extractContext.pythonBin.
invariants: Every record produced is stamped with this plugin's id.
A file already claimed by an earlier package is never reassigned.
A file resolving outside its package root is skipped.
Missing interpreter yields an empty result rather than an error; the user-facing warning is raised once at the engine boundary.
annotation.integrationPoints: Calls from mod:repovine/src/stage1; context used by extraction module.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root → interpreter probe → marker walk producing packages → per-package source walk with scan and test filters → pending records keyed by absolute path → result carrying the interpreter forward.

annotation.summary: Maps a Python module's external imports onto side-effect kinds, using a deliberately short table of modules whose import unambiguously contradicts a purity claim: child processes and threads, HTTP clients, raw sockets, opaque cloud SDKs and database drivers. The result feeds the annotation consistency axis, which compares a declared-pure module against the effects its imports imply.

keyExports.effectImportsFromPythonImports: Maps external import specifiers to de-duplicated, deterministically sorted kind and source pairs.

assumptions: The table lists only unambiguous cases; near-universal modules such as the standard os, sys and json are deliberately absent.
Only external imports are considered, so an internal repository import never contributes an effect hint.

The kinds are written as plain strings that match the shared side-effect vocabulary; nothing binds them to it, and a kind outside the vocabulary is dropped during the consistency check rather than reported.
risks: The table drifts against the Python ecosystem over time, but a missing entry only means the purity check is skipped for that module, never that a wrong effect is claimed.
An over-broad prefix would false-flag a legitimately pure utility that merely re-exports from such a module, which is the failure this table is kept short to avoid.
A read kind is used as the minimal honest claim for HTTP and database clients, since import time cannot distinguish reading from writing.
patterns: Asymmetric error preference: under-detection is acceptable, over-detection is not, because a false effect would contradict a correct purity declaration.
invariants: Effects are never fabricated for internal imports.
An empty result is valid and simply means the module contributes no effect hints.
Output is de-duplicated and sorted, so the same imports always produce the same hints.
annotation.integrationPoints: Takes the import record type from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, is called by the Python extraction path when assembling a module record, and its output is read by the detection helper in mod:repovine/src/annotations/side-effect-vocab during the consistency check.
annotation.dataFlow: external imports -> prefix table lookup -> effect hints on the module record -> compared against a declared-pure annotation during the consistency check.

annotation.summary: Python extraction: parse shard of .py files with stdlib ast in one subprocess. Maps JSON result to ModuleInfo. Reused modules now re-resolve imports against current module set, so incremental refresh equals cold build.

keyExports.extractPython: Runs pass: classifies reusable, parses rest, returns per-module results.
keyExports.runPythonAst: Runs parsing subprocess; rejects on spawn fail, non-zero exit, or overflow.
keyExports.terminateLivePythonChildren: Kills every live subprocess and waits for reap.

assumptions: Subprocesses are host-process children for proper reaping.
Parsing async (runs inline for small/refresh).
Per-file error is normal; subprocess failure is transient.
Results emitted in input order; parse stable.
Only top level examined; no type inference.

sideEffects.description: spawns interpreter subprocess per shard
tracks live subprocesses in set
loads parsing script on first use

risks: Teardown signal uncatchable; child ignoring catchable signal outlives rejection.
Output cap fails whole shard; one pathological file costs shard.
Missing interpreter ends shard; modules come back with no semantics.
Transient failure never caches.
patterns: Every bound explicit: output cap, wall-clock backstop, error buffer cap, teardown wait.
annotation.flowDescription: Python AST walk → extractPython → ModuleInfo exports, imports, semantic-hints for graph.
invariants: Subprocess removed from live set on close.
Backstop timer never holds process open.
Output beyond cap ends run.
Transient failure never caches under real hash.
annotation.integrationPoints: Plugin contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk; interpreter and pending from mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/python/discover; import resolution from resolve-import; hints from framework-hints and effect-imports.
annotation.dataFlow: pending modules with engine-supplied fingerprints → reuse-or-parse classification → file paths written to the subprocess → structured parse results → import resolution and hint derivation → one result per module.

annotation.summary: Pure adapter turning the route rows produced by the Python AST pass into the semantic-hints slice the engine consumes. Normalizes every framework's URL paths by one rule -- a regex path passes through untouched, any other path gains a leading slash when it lacks one -- and tags each route with the framework and the detection source.

keyExports.PythonWebFramework: The frameworks this adapter recognizes: fastapi, django, drf and flask.
keyExports.RawFrameworkRoute: One row from the AST pass: path, optional method, handler component, optional line, optional rendered template names.
keyExports.frameworkHintsFromRaw: Maps the rows into the hints slice, normalizing paths, upper-casing methods and sorting deterministically; returns nothing when there are no routes.
keyExports.normalizeApiPath: Prefixes a leading slash for plain paths, leaves a regex path untouched, and turns a relative Django-family segment into a rooted one.

assumptions: The route rows come from the Python AST pass in the extraction module, not from this adapter, which only shapes them.
An empty route list yields no hints object at all rather than an empty one, so callers must handle the absent case.
The recognized framework changes how a route's detection source is tagged -- decorator for the decorator-based frameworks, AST for the Django family -- not how its path is normalized.
Every route emitted here is an API route; page and template routes are not produced.
This local framework union includes flask, while the SDK's known-framework list covers only fastapi, django and drf; flask passes through as a local label.
risks: Path normalization is syntactic: mount prefixes and trailing-slash behaviour are not modelled, so a normalized path can differ from the URL the framework actually serves.
A row without a method omits the method entirely rather than defaulting to one.
Rendered template names reflect same-file AST detection only, so templates resolved across modules are missing.
patterns: Backend-only hints: the output feeds the entrypoint layer rather than any UI surface.
annotation.flowDescription: Raw route rows are normalized and sorted into the hints slice that the extraction path attaches to the module record.
invariants: A regex path is left unchanged so the Django regex form survives normalization.
Rendered template names are carried through to the route record when same-file detection found them.
Route ordering is deterministic, so identical input yields an identical hints slice.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumes the route and hint types from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src; the shaped hints are attached to the module record by the Python extraction module and read downstream by the entrypoint interpreters.
annotation.dataFlow: AST route rows -> frameworkHintsFromRaw -> hints slice -> module record -> backend API entrypoint interpretation.

annotation.summary: Structural resolver mapping a Python import statement to an internal module id. Works purely from the global path-to-id map and the discovered package list: a relative import resolves from the importing file's directory, an absolute one is tried inside the importing package first and then across packages, and an absolute import that resolves nowhere is reported as external while a relative miss simply yields no id.

keyExports.PythonImportResolution: The result: the resolved module id when internal, plus the external flag.
keyExports.ResolvePythonImportInput: The resolution context: importing file and package, relative level, dotted module name, import kind, the path-to-id map, the package list and the repo root.
keyExports.resolvePythonImport: Resolves one import statement to a module id or marks it external.

assumptions: Resolution is structural and offline: the map and the package list are the only sources of truth, so nothing is stat-ed or read during the pass.
Standard-library and third-party modules are simply unresolved and marked external; no placeholder node is created for them.
This is the Python counterpart of the TypeScript specifier resolver and is expected to behave the same way at the graph level.

Module lookups go through hostKeyedView/hostPathKey from mod:repovine/src/platform/paths, a memoized canonical view of absPathToId, so native path.join candidates match map keys even when the keys are POSIX-shaped.
risks: Package-root discovery drives cross-package resolution, so an unusual nested source layout can leave internal imports resolving as external.

`from . import name` resolves to the package initializer, so the import edge lands on `__init__.py` and the individual names -- including submodules that exist as their own files -- get no edge of their own.
patterns: Try the narrowest interpretation first: relative, then same package, then across packages, with external as the terminal fallback.
annotation.flowDescription: An import statement plus the module map resolve to an internal module id or to an external marker.
invariants: A non-zero relative level always resolves from the importing file's directory.
An empty dotted name at level zero is reported as external.
Resolution never touches the filesystem.
annotation.integrationPoints: Takes its package type from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src, resolves host-vs-POSIX path key mismatches via mod:repovine/src/platform/paths, and is called by the Python extraction path when it wires import edges.
annotation.dataFlow: extracted import statements plus the global path-to-id map -> resolvePythonImport -> module id or external marker -> import records on the module -> graph import edges.

annotation.summary: Module src/source-plugins/typescript/index.ts in repovine

keyExports.TypeScriptExtractContext: What discovery hands extraction: the parsed compiler options for each package.
keyExports.default: The plugin descriptor: identity, ownership, capabilities, and the two pass handlers.

assumptions: One constant feeds both the file matcher and the declared capabilities, so the two lists cannot drift apart.
The parsing library is imported on first extraction rather than at load, so a run that discovers nothing to parse never pays for it.
This plugin declares that it produces user-interface surfaces and supplies the dotted-path handler resolver, which is how references to a handler resolve back to a module.
Extraction is grouped by package because the compiler options are per package; a package without options in the context has nothing to parse against.
The orchestrator knows only the descriptor, which is what keeps the compiler dependency inside this directory.

sideEffects.description: dynamically imports the extraction chunk on first use

risks: A package whose compiler options are absent from the context is skipped without a message, so it appears in the graph with no extracted semantics rather than as a failure.
Because the extraction chunk loads lazily, a problem with it surfaces during extraction rather than at discovery, well after the run has committed to this plugin.
When several packages share a name the first one wins, so in a workspace with a duplicate name the modules of one are extracted against the other's package record.
patterns: A declarative descriptor with two handlers: everything language-specific stays behind it, and the orchestrator stays language-agnostic.
The heavy dependency sits behind a lazy boundary, which is what lets discovery run cheaply on repositories with nothing to parse.
annotation.flowDescription: Manifest register(ctx) registers the SourcePlugin object; orchestrator routes .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs files and tsconfig.json package markers to this plugin's discover/extract pair.
invariants: The owned extension list is declared exactly once and reused.
The compiler and the parsing library are reachable only through this plugin.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registered among the built-in source plugins during the first build stage; discovery is implemented in mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/discover, extraction is reached through mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/lazy-extract, and the compiler configuration those depend on is read by mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/list-tsconfig-files; the descriptor factory and handler resolver come from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/factory and mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/handler-resolver.
annotation.dataFlow: orchestrator → discovery returns pending modules plus the per-package compiler options → extraction chunk loaded on demand → modules grouped by package and extracted → results with reuse counts.

annotation.summary: Lightweight call-site collector for Stage-1 export-symbol metadata in the TypeScript plugin: walks a SourceFile and records identifier/property-access call targets per exported declaration, filtering boilerplate builtins and capping at 50 names.

keyExports.ModuleCallAttribution: byDecl map (per exported decl) plus module-level call name list.
keyExports.collectModuleCalls: Walk SourceFile, attribute call expressions to exported decls, return filtered call names (max 50).

assumptions: exportedDecls is the set of top-level exported declaration nodes for the module.
Call names are derived from getText() without TypeChecker resolution.
risks: Method calls on non-identifier receivers collapse to property name only.
Dynamic/indirect calls (computed names, spread) are invisible.
IGNORED_CALLS filter may hide domain-relevant calls that share names with builtins.
patterns: AST call expression collector feeding typescript export call metadata.
annotation.flowDescription: CallExpression nodes → collectModuleCalls → per-decl and module-level call name lists for graph call edges.
invariants: Never invokes TypeChecker; uses getText() for call expression names.
Caps at 50 call names per declaration; IGNORED_CALLS filters boilerplate builtins.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called from mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/exports during Stage-1 export metadata collection.
annotation.dataFlow: exported declaration Node → walk CallExpression descendants → filtered string[] → ModuleCallAttribution.byDecl and .module → ExportInfo.calls on small exports (≤500 lines).

annotation.summary: Module src/source-plugins/typescript/discover.ts in repovine

keyExports.discoverTypeScript: Runs the pass and returns the packages, the candidate file records, and the per-package compiler options for the next pass.
keyExports.shouldSkipRepoRelativePath: The subtree filter, exported so every discovery path applies exactly the same exclusions.

assumptions: A package's file list comes from its compiler configuration rather than a walk, so the configuration is the discovery contract.
Compiler options are captured here and handed forward, so the extraction pass never parses the configuration again.
Component files register under a virtual path with a script extension, which is what lets the extraction pass treat them as ordinary modules.

Files are collected from three directions — the configured file list, the component scan and the explicit-include walk. When two directions claim the same path, the package sitting deepest above the file takes it, so a later claim can displace an earlier one; only the explicit-include walk leaves an already-claimed path alone. Packages are visited outermost first, so in a nested workspace displacement is the ordinary case and is what keeps a file under the innermost package containing it.
Exclusion is applied by path and by filename separately, so a test file outside a test directory is still excluded.

sideEffects.description: reads compiler configuration, component sources, and walks the tree for explicit includes

risks: Directory names are excluded wherever they appear in the tree, and the list includes ordinary words such as test, build and out, so a package that genuinely keeps sources under one of those names disappears from the graph with no diagnostic.
A package without a compiler configuration is invisible to this pass, which is how a plain JavaScript package ends up absent rather than partially covered.
A malformed configuration skips the whole package after one warning, so a single bad file removes everything under it rather than degrading.
A component whose script block cannot be extracted is skipped quietly, leaving the file absent rather than flagged.
The explicit-include path walks the whole repository, so a non-empty include list makes discovery cost scale with the tree rather than with the packages.
patterns: The exclusion predicate is exported rather than duplicated, so the configured file list, the component scan and the include walk cannot drift apart.
Discovery and extraction are separate passes, and everything the second pass needs is carried forward in the result rather than recomputed.
annotation.flowDescription: discoverPackages → per-package parsePackageTsConfig → shouldSkipFilePath → moduleRelPathFor → registerPendingModule → discoverSfcFiles → SourceDiscoveryResult.
invariants: Every record produced is stamped with this plugin's id.
Paths are normalized to forward slashes on every platform before any comparison.
Build output, dependency directories, test subtrees, test-named files and source maps never become modules.
annotation.integrationPoints: Package roots come from mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/packages, the compiler configuration from mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/list-tsconfig-files, component script extraction from mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/sfc-extractor, scan filtering from mod:repovine/src/scan-filters, module id construction from mod:repovine/src/stage1/utils, and warnings are reported through mod:repovine/src/cli/ui; the result shapes come from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/types.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root → package discovery → per-package compiler configuration → configured files, component files and explicit includes → subtree, filename and scan-pattern filters → candidate records keyed by path, plus the compiler options carried to extraction.
