annotation.summary: Collects a TypeScript file's exported declarations into export records: kind, signature, parameters, return type, type value, interface fields, non-public class members, internals of very large functions, and per-declaration calls. Per-declaration details are read from the written syntax; the exported-declaration list itself comes from the type checker, and extraction stays affordable across a repository because module resolution is bounded to workspace files.

keyExports.CollectedExports: The result: the export records and the calls not attributed to any export.
keyExports.collectExports: Walks the file's exported declarations and returns their records plus the module-level calls.

assumptions: Only declarations defined in this file are collected; a symbol re-exported from elsewhere belongs to its own file.

Enumerating the file's exports resolves the module symbol through the type checker, so extraction cost tracks import resolution as well as file size; installed dependencies are held out by a resolution guard.
The module-level call bucket exists so a non-exported helper's calls remain visible to the reverse lookup by name.

sideEffects.description: collecting a file's exported declarations reads the workspace files it imports, and the standard library declarations, from disk

risks: A barrel that only re-exports contributes no export records of its own, so its surface appears empty and has to be understood through its re-export edges.
Types are read as written, so an inferred type is absent while an explicit one is captured; a very long type value is truncated.
A function assigned to an exported constant is classified as a function, which is usually right but flattens the distinction from a plain value export.
patterns: Syntax-only extraction with per-declaration attribution, so cost scales with file size rather than with the size of the type graph.
Expensive details are gated by size: internals only for very large functions, calls only for files below a line threshold.
annotation.flowDescription: A parsed source file yields its exported declarations, each turned into a record with its kind, signature and line range, plus the leftover module-level calls.
invariants: Type text is never inferred: every type string is the syntax as written, so an unannotated declaration yields no type.
Function internals are collected only for functions past a size threshold, and calls only for declarations below one.
annotation.integrationPoints: Uses the call attribution in mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/call-graph, the declaration helpers in mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/ts-utils and the type rendering in mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/type-syntax; emits the export record type from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src.
annotation.dataFlow: parsed source file -> collectExports -> export records plus module calls -> the module record in the snapshot.

annotation.summary: TypeScript/JavaScript extraction: parse changed modules and emit language semantics. Modules whose fingerprint unchanged reuse prior result. Now re-resolves import/re-export specifiers against current module set on reuse, so incremental refresh graph equals cold build.

keyExports.ExtractPackageInput: Package, pending modules, previous results, compiler options, workspace path index, source text.
keyExports.createTypeScriptExtractionProject: Builds bounded parsing project; dependency resolution blocked, library files unloaded.
keyExports.extractPackage: Extracts one package: classifies reusable/changed, parses changed, returns per-module results.

assumptions: Dependency resolution deliberately blocked.
Project created only when parse needed.
Parsing runs against real filesystem.
Component pseudo-module fingerprinted against whole raw file.
Library files not loaded.

sideEffects.description: builds and traverses syntax tree per parsed module
module resolution, workspace sources, package manifests during parsing

risks: Failure to construct project warns; modules needing parse skipped while cached emit.
Unparseable module skipped without message.
Component with unextractable script parses empty.
Reuse keyed on fingerprint alone; dependencies outside bytes untracked.
patterns: Classify first, parse second.
annotation.flowDescription: moduleTextFor → fingerprint cache check → optional Project → loadIntoProject → extractModuleDelta. The mapped text arrives from the engine and the delta carries the semantic subset, not a whole ModuleInfo.
invariants: The plugin computes no hashes of its own; text and fingerprints arrive from the engine.
Dependency-directory resolutions are discarded for both module and type-reference lookups.
Reuse and parse counts always account for what the pass did.
annotation.integrationPoints: Import/export from mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/imports; specifier resolution from mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/resolve-specifier.
annotation.dataFlow: pending modules with engine-supplied text and fingerprints → reuse-or-parse classification → lazily created project → per-module import, export and semantic collection → one result per module plus reuse counts.

annotation.summary: Extracts the import and re-export edges from a TypeScript file's syntax tree. Walks the top-level import declarations into import records with their named and namespace bindings, and the top-level export-from declarations into re-export records marking star versus named. Both resolve their specifier through the shared resolver rather than resolving paths here.

keyExports.collectImports: Walks the top-level import declarations into import records.
keyExports.collectReExports: Walks the top-level export-from declarations into re-export records, distinguishing star from named.

assumptions: Only static top-level declarations are walked, so a dynamic import expression contributes no edge.
Specifier resolution is delegated entirely to the shared resolver, so this module contains no path logic of its own.
The compiler-options context is optional and simply narrows what the resolver can resolve when absent.
risks: A specifier the resolver cannot place leaves the record without a target, so the graph under-links rather than reporting a failure; a sparse import graph is the symptom.
Dynamic imports are invisible here, so a module loaded only at runtime shows no import edge from its loader.
patterns: Re-exports are collected separately from imports, which is what lets a barrel be recognized as a redirect rather than as an ordinary dependency.
annotation.flowDescription: The file's syntax tree yields its import and export-from declarations, each specifier is resolved, and the records are attached to the module.
invariants: Only static declarations at the top level are walked.
An external package is marked as such when the resolver reports it, and carries no internal target.
annotation.integrationPoints: Resolves through mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/resolve-specifier and reads specifier text through mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/module-specifier; the records are attached to the module by the TypeScript extraction path.
annotation.dataFlow: syntax tree → top-level import and export-from declarations → resolved specifiers → import and re-export records on the module → graph edges.

annotation.summary: Process-wide lazy dynamic import of the heavy TypeScript extract chunk (ts-morph + extractPackage). Keeps typescript/index.ts free of static ./extract imports so Python-only repo scans never load ts-morph at startup.

keyExports.isExtractModuleLoaded: True once extract import promise has been created
keyExports.loadExtractModule: Dynamic import('./extract.js') cached per process; returns extractPackage module
keyExports.resetExtractModuleCache: Clears module-level cache for isolated tests

assumptions: First TS shard triggers loadExtractModule; later shards reuse cached module/promise.
resetExtractModuleCache is test-only — not used in production pipeline.

sideEffects.description: Dynamic import('./extract.js') on first TS extraction; caches module in module-level variables.

risks: Concurrent first callers share one promise — safe, but failed import poisons cache until reset.
Module cache is global per process; worker threads each have isolated state.
patterns: Defers ts-morph startup cost until first TS package extract.
annotation.flowDescription: Dynamic import of heavy extract module on first use → cache until resetExtractModuleCache.
invariants: extractModule short-circuits after first successful load.
isExtractModuleLoaded true once promise is created, not necessarily after resolution.
annotation.dataFlow: typescript/index extract handler → loadExtractModule() → dynamic import extract.js → extractPackage passed to shard runner.

annotation.summary: Parses a package's tsconfig.json via the TypeScript compiler API, resolving project references and supplementing entry-only configs with a src/ tree walk; returns fileNames plus compilerOptions for the stage1 discover/extract phases.

keyExports.parsePackageTsConfig: Parse root tsconfig.json, resolve project references when the primary fileNames list is empty, then optionally supplement entry-only configs with a src/ walk; returns the parsed fileNames and compilerOptions.

assumptions: pkgAbsPath points to a package root containing tsconfig.json.
ts.sys.readFile and node:fs are available for config parsing.

sideEffects.description: reads tsconfig.json, referenced fragment configs, and walks src/ directories for entry-only config supplements

risks.text: This module throws on tsconfig.json parse or read failures; the caller must handle a missing or invalid config.

risks: Reference configs matching spec/test/e2e are skipped, and the entry-only src/ walk separately filters test/spec files.
patterns: Bridges tsconfig.json (including Angular-style references and entry-only roots) to stage1 file discovery.
annotation.flowDescription: parsePackageTsConfig → primary fileNames; if empty, resolveFromReferences merges sibling configs; supplementEntryOnlySources may walk src/.
invariants: listTsConfigSourceFiles is a thin shim over parsePackageTsConfig(...).fileNames.
shouldFollowReference skips out-of-package references, test/e2e-named configs, and references pointing at a directory with its own nested tsconfig.json.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/discover uses parsePackageTsConfig for package file enumeration.
annotation.dataFlow: package absolute path -> parsePackageTsConfig (parse primary config, merge referenced fragments if empty, supplement entry-only file lists with a src/ walk) -> fileNames + compilerOptions -> typescript discover/extract.

annotation.summary: Safe static import/export module-specifier text extraction for TypeScript AST and ts-morph ImportDeclaration nodes. Reads string literals and no-substitution template literals via compilerNode; returns undefined for dynamic/computed specifiers instead of throwing through ts-morph getters.
assumptions: Only static import specifiers are needed for graph linking and semantic-hint heuristics; computed specifiers are intentionally ignored.
risks: Call sites must use this helper instead of ImportDeclaration.getModuleSpecifierValue() to avoid shard-level extraction failures on edge-case syntax.

annotation.summary: Discovers the TypeScript packages in a workspace by walking for directories that hold a TypeScript config, reading each one's package manifest for a name and version, de-duplicating by normalized path and returning the result sorted. This is the first step of the TypeScript plugin's discovery phase.

keyExports.discoverPackages: Walks the workspace for config-bearing directories and returns the de-duplicated, sorted package records.

assumptions: A package is identified by the presence of a TypeScript config, so the config is the marker rather than the package manifest.
Skip patterns are matched against the path relative to the workspace root, not the absolute path, so a root that itself sits under a directory named like a skip segment is still discovered.
A directory without a readable manifest still yields a package, named from its path.

Every package path and derived slug is POSIX-separated by explicit split/join on path.sep, not path.normalize, since pkg.path is a persisted identity minted into module ids and must not carry win32 backslashes on Windows.

sideEffects.description: walks the workspace directories and reads the config and manifest files it finds

risks: A package with no TypeScript config is invisible to this discovery, so a plain JavaScript package is never scanned.
A malformed manifest silently falls back to a path-derived name rather than surfacing the parse failure.
patterns: Skip patterns are evaluated relative to the scanned root, which is what lets a fixture repository nested under a skipped-looking path still be discovered.
annotation.flowDescription: Monorepo scan -> discoverPackages -> PackageInfo[] with name, path, version.
invariants: Every returned package corresponds to a directory holding a TypeScript config.
Results are de-duplicated by normalized path and sorted, so discovery is deterministic.
Package path and slug are always forward-slash separated, on every host platform.
annotation.integrationPoints: Returns the package record type from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src and is the first step of the TypeScript source plugin's discovery phase.
annotation.dataFlow: workspace root -> config-bearing directory walk -> manifest read per directory -> sorted package records -> the plugin's discovery output.

annotation.summary: String-first resolver for TypeScript import specifiers, working from the path-to-id map built in the discovery pass. Handles relative imports, config path aliases, and workspace bare and sub-path specifiers, and reports everything else as external. Keeping the hot path off the compiler's own resolver is what makes import linking affordable on a large repository.

keyExports.PathsContext: The importing package's compiler options, used for path-alias resolution.
keyExports.SpecifierResolution: The result: the resolved id when internal, plus the external flag.
keyExports.isNodeModulesPath: Whether a path lies inside a dependency directory.
keyExports.resolveSpecifierFromMap: Resolves a specifier to a module or package id, or reports it external; returns nothing on a relative miss.

assumptions: The path-to-id map from the discovery pass is the primary source, so resolution is string work rather than a compiler query for the common cases.
The dependency-path guard exists to keep resolution from descending into installed packages, which is where a naive walk becomes both slow and memory-hungry on a large tree.
Package name indexing is cached per package list, so repeated resolution against the same workspace does not re-index.

sideEffects.description: caches the package-name index per package list
the path-alias fallback can consult the compiler's resolver, which reads the filesystem

risks: A workspace sub-path that does not resolve falls back to the package id, which over-links the import to the package node rather than to the file it actually names.
An external dependency resolves as external with no id, so a graph built here has no nodes for installed packages by design.
The alias fallback stubs file contents for paths already known to the map, so it must not be relied on for anything but resolution.
patterns: Try the cheap string forms first and fall back to the compiler's resolver only for path aliases, which is the one case the map cannot answer.
annotation.flowDescription: A specifier plus the importing file resolve through the map, the alias table, or the workspace package list to an internal id, or are reported external.
invariants: A relative specifier is never marked external.
A bare workspace specifier resolves to the package's entry module when the file map holds a root or src index barrel, and to the package id only when it holds neither.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by the import collection and extraction paths of the TypeScript plugin, which fall back to a compiler query when this returns nothing; package-name extraction comes from mod:repovine/src/stage1/utils.
annotation.dataFlow: import specifier plus the path-to-id map and package list -> resolveSpecifierFromMap -> resolution or nothing -> import records, with a compiler fallback for the misses.

annotation.summary: Collects the semantic hints for one TypeScript source file. Derives routes from several independent signals (JSX elements, router config objects, router ASTs, controller decorators, file-path conventions and server handler registrations), then adds conditional renders, referenced environment variable names, runtime actions, security signals, UI architecture hints and server-rendering markers. Returns nothing when the file yields no signal at all.

keyExports.collectSemanticHints: Builds the hints for a source file, using the relative path for file-convention route inference; returns undefined when nothing was found.

assumptions: Environment variables are recognized from source references only; no environment file is ever read, so the result is the set of names the code mentions rather than the values behind them. Names are resolved from the access site, so a computed key, an aliased container or a name arriving as an argument yields nothing.
Route collectors are tried in order and their results merged, so a file matching more than one framework convention contributes routes from each.
Returning undefined rather than an empty object is the signal that a file carries no hints, and callers rely on that distinction.

A signal is claimed from code, not from prose: a pattern match landing inside a string, a template literal or a comment is skipped, and framework identity is taken from imports and syntax rather than from a filename.

sideEffects.description: reads the file text and walks the syntax tree during collection

risks: Framework detection is heuristic, so an unusual layout or naming scheme can produce a false positive route.
A large file with many elements raises traversal cost roughly with its size; collection makes about ten separate descendant walks per file.
A lazily-loaded route is recorded with a placeholder component because the runtime target is not statically knowable.

The layer reports what it can name and stays silent otherwise: a construct written in a form a collector does not recognize yields no hint rather than a wrong one, so an absent hint is not evidence the behaviour is absent.
patterns: Independent collectors per signal kind, merged at the end, so adding a framework means adding a collector rather than editing a parser.
annotation.flowDescription: The file's text and syntax tree feed the route collectors first, then the environment, security, UI and rendering sub-collectors; the merged result is the hints object or nothing.
invariants: A file yielding no signals produces undefined rather than an empty hints object.
Route records carry the detection source, so a consumer can tell a decorator-derived route from a file-convention one.

A pattern match inside a literal or a comment never sets a flag or raises a count -- this holds for the qwik-macro and JSX-framework flags, the runtime-action and delegate-call counts, and the validation/mapping count, all guarded by syntax-tree position.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumes the hint and route types from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src and resolves specifiers through mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/module-specifier; the collected hints are attached to the module record by the TypeScript extraction path and validated against the SDK schema when written.
annotation.dataFlow: source file -> route collectors plus environment, UI, rendering, security and runtime-action collectors -> merged hints -> module record -> entrypoint and UI interpreters.

annotation.summary: Regex-based Single-File Component (SFC) script extractor for TypeScript source plugin: extracts <script> blocks from Vue (.vue) and Svelte (.svelte) files so ts-morph can parse SFCs as synthetic .ts modules.

keyExports.ExtractedScript: Interface { ts: script text, isTypeScript: boolean from lang attribute }.
keyExports.SFC_EXTENSIONS: Set of extensions (.vue, .svelte) recognized as SFCs.
keyExports.extractTypeScriptFromSfc: Extract TS content and lang detection from SFC file content; dispatches by extension; returns null for unknown extensions.
keyExports.isSfcFile: Predicate checking if a file path has an SFC extension.

assumptions: Caller reads file content upstream; this module transforms in-memory strings only.
Vue may have multiple script blocks (<script setup> appends after regular <script>).
Regex-based extraction; non-standard markup or formatting may be missed.
risks: Regex extraction heuristic: can miss non-standard <script> attributes or malformed markup.
Svelte template stripping via regex: broken markup may leak HTML into downstream hints.
patterns: SFC_EXTENSIONS checked before invoking extractTypeScriptFromSfc in typescript plugin discover path.
annotation.flowDescription: Vue/Svelte file → extractTypeScriptFromSfc → script block SourceFile for TS plugin.
invariants: Returns null for non-SFC extensions.
Empty ts with isTypeScript false when no script blocks found.
annotation.dataFlow: Vue/Svelte file path + raw content → extension switch (extractFromVue | extractFromSvelte, regex split) → ExtractedScript { ts, isTypeScript } → typescript plugin extract() builds virtual .ts for ts-morph.

annotation.summary: Shared ts-morph AST helpers for the TypeScript source plugin: unwrap FunctionDeclaration, arrow, or function-expression nodes from a Node, and normalize type text for export signatures (strip import() qualifiers, cap length).

keyExports.getFunctionNode: Unwrap FunctionDeclaration or variable initializer arrow/function-expression from a Node
keyExports.normalizeType: Strip import("pkg"). prefixes and truncate type text to maxLength (default 150)

assumptions: Callers pass valid ts-morph Node instances from an already-parsed SourceFile.
normalizeType maxLength defaults to 150 when omitted.
risks: getFunctionNode only unwraps variable declarations whose initializer is arrow/function expression; other patterns return undefined.
normalizeType truncates long type strings and may hide complex generic tails.
patterns: Small shared AST helpers for typescript plugin.
annotation.flowDescription: ts-morph nodes → getFunctionNode/normalizeType → FunctionLike wrappers for extract collectors.
invariants: Never invokes TypeScript TypeChecker — syntax text only.
normalizeType strips import("pkg"). prefixes before length check.
extensionPoints: Add helpers when new ts-morph node kinds need normalization.
annotation.integrationPoints: typescript plugin extract, exports, call-graph, semantic-hints collectors.
annotation.stateShape: No runtime state — FunctionLike is a exported type alias; helpers return FunctionLike | undefined or normalized type strings.

annotation.summary: Syntax-only type label helpers for Stage-1 export signatures in the TypeScript plugin: reads type/return annotations from ts-morph AST text (never TypeChecker) and formats param/function labels for graph export metadata.

keyExports.paramTypeLabel: Format name or name: type for export param lists
keyExports.syntaxReturnTypeText: Return normalized explicit return type annotation from a function-like node
keyExports.syntaxTypeText: Return normalized explicit type annotation text from a typed node

assumptions: Derived review: ts-utils normalizeType contract unchanged; dataFlow/keyExports still accurate.
risks: Missing explicit return/type annotations yield undefined labels — inferred types are intentionally omitted.
Relies on source text fidelity; macro-generated types may be opaque.
patterns: Shared type pretty-printer for typescript plugin modules.
annotation.flowDescription: ts-morph Type nodes → syntaxTypeText/syntaxReturnTypeText → stable string labels for exports.
invariants: Never calls ts-morph TypeChecker or program.getType().
functionTypeLabel omits return suffix when returnType is undefined.
annotation.dataFlow: ts-morph declaration nodes → syntaxTypeText/syntaxReturnTypeText → normalizeType → paramTypeLabel/functionTypeLabel → exports collector signatures.

annotation.summary: The first build stage: apply plugin configuration, discover packages and files through language plugins, extract them inline or across a worker pool, then add infrastructure and templates and assemble the facts snapshot. Fails loudly — any extraction failure ends the run before a partial snapshot is finalized or cached.

keyExports.STAGE1_ANALYSIS_VERSION: The snapshot shape version; mismatch invalidates cache. Currently 2, covering added ExportInfo.defaultLocalName and hint corrections.
keyExports.collectRepositoryFactsAsync: Main orchestrator: prepares plugin config, discovers packages/files, extracts in shards (inline or pooled), adds infra/templates, assembles snapshot.
keyExports.dedupByModuleIdPreservingOrder: Dedup pending modules by resolver priority, preserving order.
keyExports.mergeResults: Merges shard results and reuse/rescan counts.

assumptions: Extraction inline when worker count is ≤1, pooled otherwise.
Cancellation is cooperative and checked before each package and after each await.
Worker sizing accounts for container memory limit, not just host memory.
Reusing a prior snapshot requires shape version AND engine build identity match.

sideEffects.description: runs pooled extraction across worker threads
reads snapshot cache and sizing calibration
writes sizing calibration after run

risks: Engine build identity is development-only and absent from installed packages, so in production only shape version guards reuse.
A plugin not registered is skipped with warning, so its modules are absent rather than reported as failure.
Failure is all-or-nothing: one unparseable package ends the whole build.
patterns: Fail loud rather than degrade: a partial snapshot is never finalized or cached, because a quietly incomplete graph is worse than no graph.
The engine stamps ownership rather than trusting plugins to self-report, so a plugin that omits its own identifier still yields correctly owned modules.
Sizing is measured and remembered: a calibration from previous runs advises the worker count for the next.
annotation.flowDescription: plugin configuration → discovery → sharding → inline/pooled extraction → infra/templates → snapshot assembly.
invariants: Any shard error aborts before snapshot is finalized or cached.
Every module carries owning package's plugin identifier.
annotation.integrationPoints: plugin-loader, source/registry, source/extract-runner, worker-pool, calibration, stage1/infra, stage1/templates.
annotation.stateShape: The snapshot carries packages, modules, infrastructure modules, the analysis version, and optionally the linking configuration and the bundle handler map.
annotation.dataFlow: plugin configuration → per-plugin discovery → package jobs and shards → inline or pooled extraction with cancellation checkpoints → fail on any shard error, otherwise merge → infrastructure and templates → facts snapshot, plus an updated sizing calibration.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_MAX_PACKAGE_WORKERS: Caps the worker pool when the option is not supplied

annotation.summary: Portable repository-facts snapshot cache with sync/async load/save and two SHA-256 guards: snapshotContentFingerprint (analysis/build/extraction-config identity, order-preserving) drives the dirty-skip write guard, while extractOutputFingerprint (sorted id+contentHash, excluding version fields) preserves the CI golden contract. saveAsync streams the write so no full-snapshot JSON string is held in memory.

keyExports.SnapshotCache: load/loadAsync/save/saveAsync/exists over the full RepositoryFactsSnapshot JSON.
keyExports.createFileCache: Factory for cacheDir+repoRoot; rewrites module filePath to portable repo-relative form around save/load; saveAsync streams the write so no full-snapshot JSON string is ever held in memory.
keyExports.extractOutputFingerprint: CI golden-guard fingerprint: SHA-256 over sorted-by-id module/template/infra id+contentHash only, excluding analysisVersion/engineBuildId; changes exactly when extract output changes.
keyExports.snapshotContentFingerprint: P2 dirty-skip guard: SHA-256 over analysisVersion + engineBuildId + each module/template/infra id+contentHash in original (unsorted) order; a match means the on-disk snapshot is already current and the write can be skipped.

assumptions: Module filePath is the only absolute field in a snapshot; toPortable/toAbsolute round-trip it repo-root-relative so the on-disk cache transfers across worktrees/CI checkouts/containers with identical content.
The portable-path rewrite in writeSnapshot/saveAsync is synchronous (no await between rewrite and revert), so nothing else on the event loop observes a mid-rewrite snapshot.

sideEffects.description: load()/loadAsync() read repository-facts-snapshot.json under cacheDir
save() writes atomically via writeFileAtomicSync; saveAsync() streams via writeJsonObjectStreamed (no full-snapshot JSON string)

risks: Large monorepos produce a multi-hundred-MB JSON string; writeSnapshot's JSON.stringify can hit Node's >512MB string-length cliff — its finally block still restores absolute filePaths if stringify throws.

risks.text: extractOutputFingerprint's exact hash shape (sorted mod/tpl/infra id+contentHash, excluding analysisVersion/engineBuildId) is the CI golden-guard's byte contract over a fixed fixture corpus.

patterns: Two independent SHA-256 fingerprints: snapshotContentFingerprint (order-preserving, includes analysisVersion+engineBuildId) for the on-disk dirty-skip guard; extractOutputFingerprint (sorted by id, excludes both) for the CI golden guard.
invariants: Requires raw.modules to be an array on load or the cache is rejected (returns null).
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by a caller that loads a previousSnapshot and passes it into mod:repovine/src/stage1 collectRepositoryFactsAsync, then saves the returned snapshot back (cache functions are not called directly from stage1/index.ts itself); uses mod:repovine/src/fs/atomic (writeFileAtomicSync/writeJsonObjectStreamed) and mod:repovine/src/perf/memory-profiler phases.
annotation.dataFlow: Caller loads previousSnapshot via SnapshotCache.load()/loadAsync() → passed as SnapshotOptions.previousSnapshot into stage1 collectRepositoryFactsAsync → returned RepositoryFactsSnapshot saved back via save()/saveAsync().

annotation.summary: Zod-validated Stage-1 calibration persistence and advice: atomically stores finite positive build observations and clamps worker/shard recommendations to finite positive integers.

keyExports.adviseFromCalibration: RAM-budget 70% rule + cpuCount-1 cap; user maxPackageWorkers override wins.
keyExports.saveCalibration: Writes lastRun observed metrics after a build completes.

assumptions: saveCalibration called at end of successful graph build with MemoryProfiler peak.
Schema version 1; unknown versions are ignored.

sideEffects.description: loadCalibration reads build-calibration.json
saveCalibration mkdir + writeFileSync calibration JSON

risks: Stale calibration after hardware change skews ETA.
patterns: Persists timing samples under .repovine for ETA advice.
invariants: Calibration is best-effort — missing file uses defaults.
annotation.integrationPoints: .repovine calibration files; cli/build ETA estimates.
annotation.dataFlow: prior build timings persisted → adjust stage1 ETA in build-controller messages.

annotation.summary: Dev-only engine-build identity for stage1 snapshot-reuse gate. Fingerprints the engine's dist/ when running in dev (REPOVINE_DEV=1 or git checkout), else undefined for installed packages, preventing silent reuse of stale snapshot caches. Reviewed against current source: 5-export surface unchanged from the prior note.

keyExports.__resetEngineBuildIdMemo: Test-only: clears the per-process memoized id.
keyExports.computeEngineBuildId: Pure decision core: returns fingerprint when dev-mode detected, else undefined; deps injected for testability.
keyExports.currentEngineBuildId: Memoized per-process id: finds engine package root, detects git checkout, fingerprints dist/**/*.js files (path + size + mtime) via SHA-256[:16].
keyExports.engineBuildMatches: Reuse-gate predicate: true when current is undefined (release mode); else requires stored === current (dev mode).

assumptions: Consumed by mod:repovine/src/stage1 collectRepositoryFactsAsync to gate snapshot reuse alongside STAGE1_ANALYSIS_VERSION.
currentEngineBuildId() memoized for process lifetime; dist/ rebuild mid-process not detected without __resetEngineBuildIdMemo().

sideEffects.description: Walks up from module to find engine package.json, checks for .git, hashes every .js file in dist/ (size + mtime)

risks: In release mode (no REPOVINE_DEV, not a git checkout), currentEngineBuildId() returns undefined and engineBuildMatches is a no-op; reuse guard relies solely on STAGE1_ANALYSIS_VERSION.
invariants: engineBuildMatches always returns true when current is undefined (release mode).
fingerprintDist uses SHA-256[:16] over sorted-by-name .js file metadata (path, size, mtimeMs).
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/stage1 collectRepositoryFactsAsync imports currentEngineBuildId/engineBuildMatches for previousSnapshot reuse gating.
annotation.dataFlow: currentEngineBuildId() supplies real fs/git/fingerprint deps to computeEngineBuildId(deps), memoized in `memo` → stage1/index compares it against a loaded previousSnapshot.engineBuildId via engineBuildMatches.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_DEV: When set to '1', forces dev-mode fingerprinting even outside a git checkout.

annotation.summary: Computes one digest standing for every input that can change what extraction produces without any source byte changing: the scan patterns, the identity of the active plugins, and the per-plugin context carrying things like compiler options. The snapshot reuse gate stores this digest, so a configuration change forces a full extraction rather than reusing facts derived under different settings.

keyExports.ExtractionConfigFingerprintInput: The inputs that go into it: repository root, scan patterns, active source plugins, infrastructure plugin ids, and the per-plugin context map.
keyExports.computeExtractionConfigFingerprint: Returns the digest, truncated to twenty-four hex characters.

assumptions: The repository root is stripped from every string before hashing, in both path spellings, so the same checkout moved or cloned elsewhere yields the same digest and its cache stays usable.
Serialization is structural and order-independent where order carries no meaning: object keys sort, map entries sort by serialized key, sets sort.
Plugin order is preserved rather than sorted, because the first plugin to claim a file owns it and a reordering genuinely changes the outcome.
A plugin contributes its declared identity — id, version, markers, file matching, capabilities and requirements — rather than anything derived from its implementation.
Recursion is guarded, so a context holding a cycle serializes to a marker instead of looping.
risks: Only the declared plugin identity is hashed, so a plugin whose extraction logic changes while its descriptor stays the same produces an unchanged digest and the gate reuses facts built by the older logic.
Functions serialize to their name alone, so a context carrying a callback yields the same digest whatever the callback now does.

The digest covers only what callers pass in, so a plugin-specific input left out of the context map makes reuse more permissive than it looks, and the failure appears later as facts that quietly do not match the configuration.
patterns: Paths are made portable before hashing rather than after, which is what separates 'the configuration changed' from 'the checkout moved'.
One digest stands for many heterogeneous inputs, so the reuse gate compares a single value instead of re-deriving each condition.
invariants: The same configuration under a different repository root produces the same digest.
A change to a scan pattern, a compiler option or the active plugin set changes the digest.
Serialization is deterministic for equivalent structures regardless of insertion order.
annotation.integrationPoints: The digest is stored on the facts snapshot and compared by the first-stage reuse gate; scan pattern shapes come from mod:repovine/src/scan-filters and the plugin shape from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/types.
annotation.dataFlow: scan patterns, plugin identities and per-plugin contexts → root-relative normalization → stable structural serialization → digest stored on the snapshot and compared on the next build.

annotation.summary: Stage-1 IaC engine barrel: parser registry (registerParser, getParsers, kind/trigger metadata), shared utils (hashResourcePayload, attr helpers, path domains), and CLOUDFORMATION_SAFE_SCHEMA. Built-in vendor parsers register via separate bootstrap import, not this file alone.

keyExports.getParsers: Returns registered IaC parsers for file matching.
keyExports.hashResourcePayload: Re-exported from iac/utils for resource identity.

assumptions: Callers that need parsers loaded must import stage1/iac/bootstrap.js side-effect first.
setParsersForTest used only in unit tests.

sideEffects.description: Barrel re-exports; registry mutation happens in bootstrap/loader callers

risks: Plugin version mismatch can skip entire provider families.
patterns: Orchestrates plugin scan after TS module extraction.
invariants: Disabled plugins are skipped entirely at bootstrap.
annotation.integrationPoints: collectInfraModules from stage1/index; iac-plugin loader.
annotation.dataFlow: Configured IaC plugins scan repo → normalized infra/service descriptors on RepositoryFactsSnapshot.

annotation.summary: The ordered list of built-in infrastructure plugins and the code that registers them. Each plugin lives in its own directory and default-exports a declarative descriptor; this file names them in the order parsers should be tried and hands each to the registry. Importing the module registers them, so any module that only wants the side effect can import it bare.

keyExports.getBuiltinIaCPluginIds: The built-in plugin ids in registration order, which is the default preset.
keyExports.resetToBuiltinIaCPlugins: Clears the registry and re-registers exactly the built-ins, giving the external loader a fixed baseline.

assumptions: Adding a built-in means creating the plugin directory and adding one entry to the list; the registry and the shared helpers stay untouched.
Plugins never reach into the registry themselves — registration is the engine's job, here and later in the external loader.
The order of the list is the order parsers are tried against a document, so the list is a precedence declaration rather than an inventory.
Each plugin fixes the order of its own parsers inside its descriptor.

The reset helper is the recovery primitive rather than merely another way to clear: it ignores the registered-once flag and unconditionally rebuilds the registry, which is what lets the external loader empty the built-ins and restore them on the next build.

sideEffects.description: registers the built-in plugins into the shared registry on first import

risks: Reordering the list changes which parser claims a document whose shape more than one plugin recognizes, and the result is a misclassified resource rather than an error.
Registration happens as an import side effect, so import order decides when the registry becomes usable and a consumer that reads it too early sees it empty.

The registered-once flag is never cleared, so a future caller that expected the bootstrap to repopulate an emptied registry would get a silent no-op. Nothing depends on that today: the bootstrap has no caller other than its own module-load invocation, and the reset helper restores the registry without consulting the flag.
patterns: A declarative descriptor per plugin plus one explicit list, so precedence lives in a single readable place.
The bootstrap is idempotent and the reset is unconditional, which is what lets the external loader rebuild from a known baseline on every build.
annotation.flowDescription: import bootstrap → call each register*IacPlugin() → registry ready for infra scan.
invariants: The built-ins register in list order, and the reset reproduces that same order.
Repeated calls to the bootstrap register nothing further.
An emptied registry is always one reset call away from the built-in preset.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registration goes through mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/registry; the descriptor type and its authoring helper come from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src and mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/factory; the descriptors themselves are the default exports of the plugin directories under src/iac-plugins.
annotation.dataFlow: module import → each descriptor registered in list order → registry consulted by the infrastructure scan → first parser that claims a document wins.

annotation.summary: The process-global registry for IaC parsers and the infra metadata that stage2 reads. A plugin registers as a unit: its parsers plus its kind-to-domain mapping, resource-kind hints and trigger-type hints. Also answers the routing questions during the scan: does any parser claim this file, and in what document format should it be loaded.

keyExports.InfraKindDomain: The domain descriptor a kind maps to.
keyExports.TriggerEntryKind: The entrypoint kinds a trigger can map onto.
keyExports.getAllRegisteredKindDomains: The explicit kind-to-domain pairs, for seeding graph domains.
keyExports.getInfraKindDomain: Resolves a kind to its registered domain, or to the conventional one.
keyExports.getRegisteredIaCPluginIds: The registered plugin ids in first-registration order.
keyExports.getResourceKindMeta: Reads those hints during handler resolution.
keyExports.getTriggerTypeMeta: Reads those hints when building trigger edges.
keyExports.isInfraCandidate: Whether any parser claims the file, which is the scan-time gate.
keyExports.parserMatchesFile: Whether a parser's file match claims a basename and extension.
keyExports.pickDocFormatForFile: The document format of the first parser claiming the file.
keyExports.registerIaCPlugin: Registers a plugin descriptor's parsers and metadata as one unit.
keyExports.registerInfraKindDomain: Maps an infra kind onto its graph domain.
keyExports.registerParser: Low-level parser append, used by the bootstrap and loader.
keyExports.registerResourceKindMeta: Attaches resource interpretation hints such as owning a code handler.
keyExports.registerTriggerTypeMeta: Attaches trigger interpretation hints such as the entrypoint kind.
keyExports.resetIaCParsers: Clears the parsers for a loader rebuild baseline.
keyExports.setParsersForTest: Replaces the parser list and returns a restore callback.
keyExports.unregisterIaCPlugin: Removes the parsers a plugin owns.

assumptions: Registration order decides which parser claims a file that more than one could match, so a broad parser registered early shadows a specific one registered later.
Metadata registration is idempotent by key, so two plugins declaring the same kind simply overwrite rather than conflict.
An unregistered kind still resolves to a conventional domain, so an unknown infra kind is placed rather than dropped.

sideEffects.description: mutates the process-global parser list and the three metadata maps

risks: Resetting clears the parsers but deliberately leaves the metadata maps populated, so a reload keeps kind, resource and trigger hints from plugins that are no longer registered.
Because metadata is keyed by kind rather than by plugin, an external plugin redefining a built-in kind silently replaces its interpretation hints.
patterns: The plugin id is the stable key for enabling or disabling a plugin through configuration.
One descriptor registers parsers and metadata together, so a plugin cannot half-register.
invariants: An unknown infra kind resolves to the conventional domain for that kind.
Resetting clears the parser list and the per-plugin ownership map, not the metadata maps.
annotation.integrationPoints: Accepts the plugin descriptor and parser contracts from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src; populated by the stage1 IaC bootstrap and the external plugin loader, and read during infra collection and by stage2 when interpreting resources and triggers.
annotation.dataFlow: plugin descriptor -> parser list plus kind, resource and trigger metadata -> scan routing picks a parser per file -> stage2 interprets the resulting resources and triggers through the same metadata.

annotation.summary: Small helpers for Stage-1 IaC graph extraction: stable resource identity hashing, Terraform/CDK attribute normalization into string maps, and path-based domain labels derived from infra file relative paths.

keyExports.addAttr: Add normalized attr when attrValue is non-empty.
keyExports.attrValue: Coerce nested IaC attribute values into flat strings.
keyExports.hashResourcePayload: SHA-256 first 16 hex chars of JSON.stringify(payload) for resource nodes.
keyExports.isRecord: Type guard for plain object IaC attribute maps.
keyExports.pathBasedDomainsFromRelPath: Derives domain slug from path segments, skipping infra noise.

assumptions: Payload JSON serialization order is stable enough for dedup keys within a single build.
Relative paths use forward or back slashes as emitted by the scanner.
risks: YAML merge keys can confuse line attribution.
patterns: Shared YAML walk helpers for all IaC parsers.
invariants: No template evaluation — static structure only.
annotation.integrationPoints: IaC parsers for YAML/JSON traversal shared helpers.
annotation.dataFlow: parsed AST nodes → normalized resource ids and env var name hints for semantic-hints.

annotation.summary: js-yaml schema extension that preserves CloudFormation/SAM intrinsic tags (!Ref, !Sub, !If, etc.) as opaque nodes instead of failing parse — shared by all IaC YAML loaders in Stage-1.

keyExports.CLOUDFORMATION_SAFE_SCHEMA: DEFAULT_SCHEMA.extend with ! scalar/sequence/mapping types that pass through construct data.

assumptions: Used with yaml.load options referencing this schema for CFN templates.
Does not evaluate intrinsics — graph stores raw tag shapes.
risks: Custom tags not in schema drop nested resources.
patterns: Safe parse only — no custom tag constructors.
invariants: Unknown YAML tags yield partial trees, not throws.
annotation.integrationPoints: kubernetes/helm/sam parsers for safe YAML loading.
annotation.dataFlow: YAML text → schema-aware object tree → resource fields extracted without executing templates.

annotation.summary: Finds infrastructure definitions during the first build stage and turns them into records. It walks the repository for files any registered parser claims, reads each one in the format its kind implies, then offers every document to the parsers in registration order until one takes it. The parsers supply the infrastructure meaning; the identity, the file reference and the fingerprint are stamped here.

keyExports.InfraScanOptions: The repository root and the compiled scan patterns.
keyExports.collectInfraModules: Runs the scan and returns one record per infrastructure module found.

assumptions: The parsers are registered by importing the bootstrap for its side effect, so the registry is populated before the first scan.
Structured formats are parsed and the rest is handed over as raw text, which is how a container definition and a template can share one dispatch path.
The template format is read with a schema tolerant of the intrinsic tags cloud templates use, so those files parse instead of failing on unknown tags.
One fingerprint is computed per file and shared by every document that file yields, since the documents come from the same bytes.
An unreadable file yields an empty fingerprint rather than a wrong one, so a later run treats it as changed and reads it again.
Records sharing an identity come from the same file, so merging them only concatenates their resources.
The packages option is accepted and ignored: discovery here is driven from the filesystem, not from the package list.

sideEffects.description: walks the tree and reads candidate infrastructure files

risks: The first parser that both matches the filename and claims a document takes it, and the search stops there whether or not the parser produced anything — a parser that claims a document and returns nothing silently prevents any later parser from seeing it, and the resource simply does not appear.
Because claiming is ordered, registration order decides the outcome for a document more than one parser recognizes; a reordering changes classification with nothing failing.
A file that cannot be read or parsed is skipped, and the warning appears only when verbose output is enabled, so a malformed template is invisible in a normal run.
Directory exclusions are by name anywhere in the tree and include ordinary words such as test and build, so definitions kept under such a directory are never discovered.
patterns: Parsers own the semantics, the engine owns the identity and the fingerprint, which keeps a parser from having to know how modules are addressed.
Discovery, format dispatch and claiming are three separate steps, so adding a format does not touch the walk.
invariants: A parse failure never aborts the build.
Every record's fingerprint is the hash of the whole file it came from.
Records with the same identity fold their resources rather than replacing each other.
annotation.integrationPoints: Parsers are registered through mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/bootstrap and resolved from mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/registry; the tolerant template schema comes from mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/yaml-schema; path filtering from mod:repovine/src/scan-filters; the record shape from mod:repovine/src/types, and the result is placed on the build snapshot by the first stage.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root → candidate walk → scan-pattern filter → format-specific read → first claiming parser per document → engine-stamped record, merged by identity.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Logs per-file read and parse failures

annotation.summary: Enriches Kubernetes IaC resource attributes from parsed YAML: enrichK8sResourceAttributes extracts container env, envFrom secret/configMap refs, secret volumes, HTTP probe paths/ports, and Ingress backends for runtime linking.

keyExports.enrichK8sResourceAttributes: Dispatches workload kinds and Ingress to pod/env/probe enrichers; returns deduplicated InfraEnvRef[].

assumptions: Propagation review 2026-06-20: upstream types hash changed; enrichK8sResourceAttributes unchanged.

sideEffects.description: Mutates attrs Record in place only

risks: Helm-templated names pass through verbatim without resolution.
Non-workload kinds other than Ingress return empty envRefs from workload path.
patterns: Shared workload enrichment used by kubernetes iac-plugin parsers/workloads.
invariants: Deduplicates envRefs by varName:refType:targetLogicalId key.
Ingress backends collected separately from workload pod specs.
annotation.integrationPoints: kubernetes iac-plugin parsers/workloads; graph runtime-resource linking.
annotation.dataFlow: K8s manifest doc → enrichK8sResourceAttributes mutates attrs + returns InfraEnvRef[] → kubernetes parser attaches to InfraResource.

annotation.summary: Normalizes repovine.config build.linking into deduped NormalizedLinkingConfig (handler search roots, bundle scripts/autoDetect, container dockerfile roots) persisted on RepositoryFactsSnapshot.linkingConfig for stage-2 infra→code linking.

keyExports.hasLinkingConfig: True when normalized handlers, bundles, or containers sections are non-empty.
keyExports.normalizeLinkingConfig: Dedupes array fields and applies defaults for missing linking subsections.

assumptions: Propagation review 2026-06-20: upstream types hash changed; linkingConfig snapshot shape unchanged.
risks: Typo in handlers.searchRoots leaves Lambda handlers unlinked in stage-2 graph.
patterns: Shared normalization for CLI build and MCP RepovineRuntime snapshot paths.
annotation.flowDescription: repovine.config build.linking → normalizeLinkingConfig → snapshot.linkingConfig for stage2 runtime-links and lambda-bundle-loader.
invariants: hasLinkingConfig true when any normalized section has non-empty values.
bundles.autoDetect defaults false when omitted.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage1/index snapshot assembly; stage2/runtime-links; lambda-bundle-loader.
annotation.stateShape: NormalizedLinkingConfig three sections: handlers.searchRoots[], bundles.scripts[] + autoDetect boolean, containers.dockerfileRoots[].
annotation.dataFlow: repovine.config build.linking → normalizeLinkingConfig → snapshot.linkingConfig → stage2 runtime-links and lambda-bundle-loader.

annotation.summary: Applies the plugin configuration for one build: resets the registries to the built-in preset, drops anything disabled, then loads the external plugins the configuration names. External code is resolved from the analyzed repository's own dependencies, gated on a declared interface version, and treated as untrusted — what it produces is schema-validated before it reaches the graph.

keyExports.LoadedPlugin: One loaded plugin: its package name, its id and which registry it joined.
keyExports.PluginLoadReport: The outcome: loaded plugins, refusals with reasons, disabled ids, whether defaults were off, and which source ids came from outside.
keyExports.PluginsConfigInput: The configuration slice: whether the built-ins apply, what to add, what to disable.
keyExports.RepovinePluginManifest: The manifest shape read from the package's own metadata.
keyExports.applyPluginConfig: Applies the configuration and reports what loaded, what was refused and why, and what was disabled.
keyExports.getActivePluginIds: The currently registered plugin ids, for diagnostics.

assumptions: Nothing is ever installed automatically; naming a package in the configuration is the trust decision, and this module only loads what is already present.
Resolution runs against the analyzed repository's dependencies rather than the engine's, so a plugin is a dependency of the project being analyzed.
A declared interface version must match the one this engine implements; a mismatch is a refusal with a reason rather than an attempt to run it.
Whatever an external plugin produces is validated against the fact schemas before use, and malformed output is dropped with a warning rather than trusted into the graph.
The registries are reset to the built-in baseline on every build, which is what makes repeated builds in a long-lived process independent of each other.
A source plugin from outside forces extraction to run inline, because the worker isolates carry only the bundled preset and could not load it.

sideEffects.description: dynamically imports external plugin entry modules
resets and repopulates the source and infrastructure registries
resolves and reads package metadata from the analyzed repository

risks: Loading an external plugin executes third-party code in the engine's process, and the only gate is that the user named it in configuration.
A refused plugin is reported and the build continues, so a configuration naming a plugin with a stale interface version yields a quietly smaller graph.
Turning the defaults off removes every built-in, so a configuration that does that without supplying replacements yields an empty graph.

The registries are process-global, and the loader re-derives them from the built-in baseline whenever it runs — which is only when the configuration names plugin work. A default bundled-only configuration never reaches the loader: the active set is whatever the one-time bootstrap registered on first import, and it persists for the life of the process.

A plugin's fact output — module semantics from extraction, an infrastructure parser's result — is schema-validated and a malformed one is dropped with a warning. Its discovery output is taken as given: the packages it names, the files it claims and the opaque payload it threads into extraction enter the build unchecked, and the paths it returns are read from disk as-is.
patterns: Reset then apply: every build starts from the same baseline rather than from whatever the previous one left behind.
External output is validated at the boundary rather than trusted by declaration, so a plugin's mistake degrades its own contribution instead of corrupting the graph.
invariants: A plugin whose declared interface version does not match is refused rather than loaded.
Nothing is installed; only already-present packages are resolved.
External fact output is schema-checked before it reaches the graph.
Every refusal carries a reason in the report.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registration and removal go through mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/registry and mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/registry; the baselines come from mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/bootstrap and mod:repovine/src/stage1/iac/bootstrap; the interface version, the fact schemas and the untrusted wrappers come from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/runtime and mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/fact-schemas; warnings are reported through mod:repovine/src/cli/ui.
annotation.dataFlow: configuration → registries reset to the built-in baseline → disabled ids removed → named packages resolved from the analyzed repository and their manifests validated → interface version checked → plugin registered behind untrusted validation → report of loaded, refused and disabled.

annotation.summary: The list of built-in language plugins and the code that registers them. Each language lives in its own directory and default-exports a plugin; this file names them and hands each to the registry. Importing the module registers them, mirroring the arrangement on the infrastructure side.

keyExports.bootstrapInternalSourcePlugins: Registers the built-in language plugins, once.
keyExports.getBuiltinSourcePluginIds: The built-in plugin ids, which is the default preset.
keyExports.resetToBuiltinSourcePlugins: Replaces the registry contents with exactly the built-ins, giving the external loader a clean baseline.

assumptions: Adding a language means creating its directory and adding one entry to the list; the orchestrator and the registry stay untouched.
Order decides ownership only when two plugins claim the same extension, and the built-in pair does not overlap, so it carries no weight today.
The registry is process-global, which is why the loader resets to this baseline on every build rather than assuming a clean start.
The built-in set is an explicit array rather than directory discovery, so what ships is visible in review.

The reset is the recovery primitive: it ignores the registered-once flag and replaces the registry contents outright, which is what lets the external loader empty the built-ins and restore them on the next build.

sideEffects.description: registers the built-in language plugins into the shared registry on first import

risks: Registration happens as an import side effect, so a consumer that reads the registry before this module is imported sees it empty.

The reset replaces the registry wholesale through a helper named for test use, so a production path depends on a function whose name suggests it is not one; renaming or restricting it would break the loader baseline.

The registered-once flag is never cleared, so a future caller that expected the bootstrap to repopulate an emptied registry would get a silent no-op. Nothing relies on that today, since the reset helper rebuilds the registry without consulting the flag.
patterns: A default-exported plugin per language plus one explicit list, matching the infrastructure bootstrap so both axes read the same way.
The bootstrap is guarded and the reset is unconditional, which is what gives the loader a repeatable starting point each build.
annotation.flowDescription: Explicit manifest list + trusted context mirrors stage1/iac/bootstrap.ts for the IaC plugin axis — symmetric dual-bootstrap design.
invariants: Repeated calls to the bootstrap register nothing further.
The reset leaves exactly the built-in set, dropping anything externally loaded.
An emptied registry is always one reset call away from the built-in preset.
annotation.integrationPoints: Registration goes through mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/registry; the plugins themselves are the default exports of mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript and mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/python; the plugin shape comes from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/types. The compiler-configuration reader the TypeScript plugin depends on is mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/typescript/list-tsconfig-files.
annotation.dataFlow: module import → each built-in plugin registered in list order → registry consulted by the orchestrator to route files to a discovery and extraction pair.

annotation.summary: Thin adapter between the stage-1 pipeline and a source plugin's extract contract. Reads each pending module's source, hands the batch to the plugin, maps every returned delta onto a module record, and reports how many modules were reused from the previous snapshot against how many were rescanned.

keyExports.RunSourceExtractionArgs: The inputs: the plugin, workspace root, packages, pending modules, previous modules by path, the path-to-id map, the plugin's own extract context and the analysis version.
keyExports.RunSourceExtractionResult: The outputs: the module records plus reused and rescanned counts.
keyExports.runSourceExtraction: Runs a plugin's extraction over a batch of pending modules and returns the module records with reuse counters.

assumptions: Reuse is decided by content fingerprint against the previous snapshot, so an unchanged file is not re-parsed.
The pending modules and the source map come from the same discovery pass, so their keys line up.
The plugin's extract context is passed through untouched; this runner does not interpret it.

sideEffects.description: reads the source of each pending module
invokes the plugin's extraction implementation

risks: A plugin failure during extraction surfaces here as a failed or partial batch, so one misbehaving plugin can block the shard it owns.
Reuse accounting depends on the pending set and the previous snapshot lining up; a mismatch degrades the counters rather than the correctness of the result.
patterns: An adapter that owns the file reading and the reuse decision, leaving the plugin responsible only for turning source into a delta.
annotation.flowDescription: The pipeline assembles the arguments, this runner reads sources and calls the plugin, and it returns normalized module records with the reuse counters.
invariants: The returned records correspond to the modules of the current pass.
The counters reflect what the extraction actually reused rather than an estimate.
extensionPoints: Extra extraction telemetry can be added to the result without touching the plugin invocation.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called from both extraction paths: the inline path in mod:repovine/src/stage1 and the pooled path from mod:repovine/src/stage1/worker, which is why the type crossing the worker bridge is a module record array. Speaks the plugin contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/types.
annotation.dataFlow: pending modules plus previous snapshot -> source read -> plugin extraction -> module records and reuse counters -> snapshot assembly.

annotation.summary: The process-global registry of source plugins. Built-ins register themselves at bootstrap and the external loader adds or removes further ones; file ownership is resolved by scanning the registration order and taking the first plugin that claims the file. Also aggregates the capabilities the orchestrator needs: the union of known extensions, whether a plugin reports UI surfaces, and whether it uses loose name separators.

keyExports.getKnownExtensions: The union of extensions across registered plugins.
keyExports.getRegisteredSourcePluginIds: The registered ids in registration order.
keyExports.getSourcePlugins: A read-only view of the registered plugins in order.
keyExports.pickSourcePluginIdForFile: The first registered plugin claiming a file.
keyExports.pluginHasUiSurfaces: Whether a plugin reports UI surfaces; an unknown id defaults to true.
keyExports.pluginUsesLooseNameSeparators: Whether a plugin treats name separators loosely; an unknown id defaults to false.
keyExports.registerSourcePlugin: Appends a plugin to the registry.
keyExports.setSourcePluginsForTest: Replaces the whole registry and returns a restore callback.
keyExports.sourcePluginMatchesFile: Whether a plugin's file match claims a given basename and extension.
keyExports.unregisterSourcePlugin: Removes a plugin by id, used when configuration disables one; a no-op when the id is absent.

assumptions: Ownership is first-registered-wins, which matters only when two plugins claim the same file; the built-ins use non-overlapping matches.
The registry is populated by importing the bootstrap module for its side effect, before the orchestrator queries it.

An absent plugin id defaults UI surfaces to true and loose separators to false; the split preserves two older predicates, one keyed on the id being missing and one on the id being python. An id that is present but not registered resolves through neither branch, so both capabilities read false.

sideEffects.description: mutates the process-global plugin array on register, unregister and test replacement

risks: The registry is a process-global singleton that accumulates: a loader applying configuration must bring it back to the baseline first.
A plugin without a file match claims nothing, so registering it affects only the capability aggregates and never file routing.

A plugin that omits capabilities contributes nothing to the known-extension union. It still discovers and owns its files, since ownership is decided by fileMatch alone; what it loses is extension stripping when IaC handler references are resolved to module ids, so those ids stay un-normalized.
patterns: An ordered array rather than a map, because ownership resolution depends on registration order while lookup by id is rare enough to scan.
annotation.flowDescription: bootstrap/loader -> registerSourcePlugin -> plugins[] -> pickSourcePluginIdForFile and capability aggregators.
invariants: A plugin without a file match never claims a file.
The test replacement returns a restore callback, so a test cannot leave the registry mutated.
Ids are returned in registration order, which is the same order ownership is resolved in.
annotation.integrationPoints: Holds descriptors satisfying the plugin contract from mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/source-plugin/types; populated by the stage1 bootstrap and by the external plugin loader, and queried by the extraction orchestrator when routing files.
annotation.stateShape: A module-level ordered array of plugin descriptors; lookup by id scans it, and file routing takes the first match.
annotation.dataFlow: bootstrap and loader register plugins -> ordered registry -> file routing picks an owner -> capability aggregates inform the orchestrator.

annotation.summary: Finds server-side template files during the first build stage and records what each one declares about its neighbours. It walks the repository, keeps files that sit under a templates directory and carry a recognized extension, hashes the content, and pulls the parent, include and block names out of the body by regular expression. The second stage turns these into template nodes and the edges between them.

keyExports.collectTemplates: Walks the repository and returns one record per template file, sorted by path, carrying the content hash and the body hints.
keyExports.parseTemplateBodyHints: Pulls the parent template, the included templates and the declared block names out of a template body.

assumptions: A file counts as a template only when it sits under a templates directory, which is what keeps stray markup in static, docs or coverage output from being picked up.
Recognized extensions are the markup pair and the three Jinja-family ones.
The engine is recorded only when the extension names it; plain markup is ambiguous across engines, so the field is left off rather than guessed.
Literal sections and comments are removed before the hints are read, so a tag shown as documentation inside a template is not mistaken for a real one.
Hints come from regular expressions rather than a parse, which is enough for the static forms and nothing more.
Directory entries are sorted during the walk and the result is sorted by path, so the same tree always produces the same records.

sideEffects.description: walks the repository tree and reads template files

risks: A template that cannot be read becomes an empty one rather than an error: the walk continues, the record is still emitted, and the hash is the hash of nothing, so the file looks present and empty instead of unreadable.
An include or extends whose target is a variable or an expression yields no hint, so the edge is simply absent from the graph rather than reported as unresolved.
The skip list and the extension set are literal, so a repository using another template extension or nesting templates below a skipped directory produces no template nodes and no diagnostic.
patterns: The templates directory acts as the anchor, which is what makes discovery precise without any per-repository configuration.
Discovery mirrors the infrastructure-module path: stage one collects file records, stage two projects them into nodes.
invariants: The first record wins for a given path, so a repeated visit never overwrites an earlier one.
Output is ordered by path, which keeps the content hash comparison stable between builds.
annotation.integrationPoints: Emits the record type defined in mod:repovine/src/types; path filtering comes from mod:repovine/src/scan-filters; the records are projected into template nodes against mod:repovine/src/graph/model in the second stage.
annotation.dataFlow: repository root → sorted directory walk → extension, directory and scan-pattern filters → read and hash → body hints → one template record per file, sorted by path.

annotation.summary: Language-agnostic stage1 identity and path helpers: module ids (via makeModuleId re-export of SDK mintModuleId), package job keys, path ownership dedup, resolver priority (extension + index precedence), and package name extraction. Free of AST dependencies (no ts-morph/typescript) so the orchestrator can import without pulling in a language toolchain.

keyExports.extractPackageName: Extract @scope/pkg or first segment from non-relative specifier.
keyExports.modulePathResolverPriority: Lower score wins when multiple files map to same moduleId (.ts > .tsx > .d.ts > .js > .jsx > .mjs > .cjs).
keyExports.pathPrefixLength: Longer owning package path wins pending-module dedup in discover.

assumptions: Propagation review 2026-06-20: upstream types unchanged; identity helpers and path logic intact.
makeModuleId is re-exported from SDK mintModuleId but consumed locally; the re-export not detected as a module export in this analysis.
risks: Platform path normalization edge cases can affect cache keys and dedup winners.
patterns: Shared hashing and path helpers for stage1 subtree.
invariants: No ts-morph/typescript imports — safe for lightweight orchestrator bundle.
annotation.integrationPoints: Used by source-plugins/typescript/discover, resolve-specifier, and stage1/index dedupByModuleIdPreservingOrder.
annotation.dataFlow: Discovery paths → makeModuleId/modulePathResolverPriority → pending module map; extractPackageName → post-extract import pkg: resolution in orchestrator.

annotation.summary: Stage-1 worker_threads entry that runs registered source extraction for package shards and posts assembled modules or a serialized error message+stack back to PackageWorkerPool. Its shutdown handler kills and reaps any in-flight plugin subprocesses (python AST children) before closing parentPort.
assumptions: Worker receives a package slice via workerData and returns a ModuleInfo batch per JobMessage.
Extract errors are captured per shard as a serialized message+stack without aborting the worker.

sideEffects.description: worker_threads child runs source extraction; shutdown handler SIGKILL-reaps plugin subprocesses
bootstrap registers source plugins in this worker isolate

risks: A shutdown message must reap the plugin's OS child subprocesses (via the plugin terminateInFlight) before parentPort.close(), or Worker.terminate() orphans them.
A missing sourcePluginId registration fails the shard.
patterns: WorkerInit carries frozen absPathToId and extractContext maps.
annotation.flowDescription: JobMessage → getSourcePlugin → plugin.extract → postMessage result|error.
invariants: No public exports — worker_threads entry only.
Throws if parentPort missing.
annotation.integrationPoints: mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/extract-runner; mod:repovine/src/stage1/source/registry; dispatched by mod:repovine/src/stage1/worker-pool; plugin teardown via SourcePlugin.terminateInFlight (e.g. mod:repovine/src/source-plugins/python/extract).
annotation.stateShape: WorkerInit carries packages, absPathToIdEntries, repoRoot, extractContextEntries, analysisVersion; parentPort JobMessage in, ModuleInfo[] | Error out.
annotation.dataFlow: JobMessage → getSourcePlugin → runSourceExtraction → postMessage ModuleInfo[] | error; shutdown → terminateInFlight → parentPort.close.

annotation.summary: Persistent worker-thread pool for stage-1 package shards. Each slot tracks one job, so a crash rejects that job and marks the slot dead. No respawn: capacity degrades until destroyed and recreated. Shutdown is graceful first (let workers reap subprocesses) before terminating.

keyExports.PackageJob: One shard: package, owning plugin, pending modules, previous entries, shard position, optional solo flag.
keyExports.PackageJobResult: Shard modules, reuse/rescan counts, or error string.
keyExports.PackageWorkerPool: The pool: submit shard, receive result, or destroy.
keyExports.chooseWorkerCount: Parallelism heuristic: minimum of CPU-derived bound, memory-derived bound, and optional cap.
keyExports.effectiveTotalMemBytes: The smaller of host memory and container constraint.

assumptions: A worker replies exactly once per dispatched job.
Job payloads must survive structured cloning across the thread boundary.
Graceful shutdown window is bounded; workers are terminated after timeout.

sideEffects.description: spawns and terminates worker threads; dispatches jobs by message

risks: Sizing against host memory inside a container over-provisions workers and invites container kill.
Dead slot never respawned; build that loses workers slows then fails.
Dispatch failure surfaces as rejected job rather than retry.
patterns: One in-flight job per slot, tracked by id.
Graceful shutdown before termination.
invariants: Dispatch targets only non-busy, non-dead slots.
Solo jobs mutually exclusive; non-solo not blocked by solo.
annotation.integrationPoints: Driven by pooled extraction path in stage1; each worker runs plugin extraction; results merged back.
annotation.stateShape: Per-slot worker handle with busy, solo, dead flags and the current job id, plus a map of pending jobs by id.
annotation.dataFlow: shard job -> dispatched to a free live slot -> plugin extraction in the worker -> reply -> resolved result -> merged into the snapshot.

annotation.summary: The second build stage: turn facts snapshot into the served graph. Interpreter layers contribute structural and infrastructure edges first, inert resources are optionally pruned, then domain passes tag and classify. An asynchronous form runs composition in a worker.

keyExports.composeRepositoryGraphAsync: Composition in a worker, falling back to inline when unavailable.

assumptions: Interpreters run before domain tagging because domain passes depend on edges they contribute.
One mutable graph runs through every pass; no patch handed between them.
Entrypoints carried explicitly across worker boundary rather than via side table.
Worker path resolved lazily and remembered; absent when compiled worker unavailable; offload failure falls back to inline.

sideEffects.description: builds and mutates one in-memory graph through every pass
asynchronous form runs composition in worker isolate

risks: Silent inline fallback on worker error; REPOVINE_STAGE2_WORKER_STRICT turns it into failure.
Graph validation warns outside development; a pass that drops record or leaves dangling edge degrades graph quietly in release.
patterns: Contribute, then prune, then classify: each stage sees a graph the previous finished with.
annotation.flowDescription: Stage-2 orchestrator: interpreters enrich the graph first (modules, runtime resources, infra links, entrypoint fragments), then multi-pass domain tagging and classification mutate the same in-memory RepositoryGraph.
invariants: Interpreter composition always precedes domain tagging.
Pruning runs between interpreter layers and domain passes.
Every snapshot record projects into graph and no edge dangles.
annotation.integrationPoints: stage2/interpreter/bootstrap, composer, entrypoint-store; stage2/prune-inert-resources, graph-validate; stage2/domains; worker beside this module.
annotation.dataFlow: facts snapshot → interpreter contributions and entrypoint fragments → inert resources pruned → domain, content, propagation, classification and subdomain passes → validation → the served graph.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_DEV: Turns graph-validation problems into a failure instead of a warning
envDependencies.REPOVINE_STAGE2_INLINE: Forces inline composition, skipping the worker
envDependencies.REPOVINE_STAGE2_WORKER_STRICT: Turns an offload failure into a failure instead of an inline fallback
envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Reports per-domain counts and offload availability

annotation.summary: Stage 1 snapshot helper living under src/stage2/: regex-parses bundle build script source (esbuild/webpack/rollup entry-to-output literal maps) and auto-detects conventional scripts/bundle.{js,ts} plus per-package script conventions expanded from root package.json workspace globs. buildSnapshot stamps the resulting bundle-output-to-source map onto RepositoryFactsSnapshot.bundleOutputHandlerMap; the infra-runtime-links interpreter reads it during Stage 2 composition. The mechanism is bundler-shaped, not provider-shaped: it recognises three bundler config forms and names no cloud vendor.

keyExports.loadBundleOutputHandlerMap: Merges explicit build.linking.bundles.scripts configs with autoDetect candidates, reads each script that exists inside the workspace root, and returns the merged output-to-source map.
keyExports.parseBundleOutputScript: Regex-parses a build script's source without eval; recognizes esbuild (entryPoint/outputFile), webpack (entry/output) and rollup (input/file) key patterns in either declaration order.

assumptions: Bundle scripts use string-literal entry/output pairs recognizable via regex; scripts requiring evaluation to resolve their paths are not covered.

autoDetect reads root package.json and expands workspace entries ending in '/*' one directory level deep; both the array and { packages: [] } workspaces shapes are accepted. Literal paths and deeper globs contribute no candidates.
