Configured script paths are repo-root-relative and are read only when they resolve inside the workspace root.

sideEffects.description: reads configured bundle scripts on every build; autoDetect additionally pulls workspace globs from root package.json to widen the candidate set

risks: Bundle formats outside the three recognized literal-pair shapes produce no output-to-source alias; handler resolution falls back to path-shape lookup and loses linkage only where the bundle renames the entry relative to its output.
A configured script path that resolves outside the workspace root is skipped silently, so a typo pointing past the root yields no mappings rather than an error.
patterns: Optional pass: when no scripts configured and autoDetect finds nothing, proceeds without bundle mappings.
Containment is applied before the stat, because path.join normalizes a parent segment away instead of rejecting it.
invariants: Only establishes a mapping entry when entryBase and outBase both resolve to a non-empty, differing path after extension stripping.
A candidate script is read only when it resolves inside the workspace root and is an existing file.
Vendor-neutral by construction: the parser keys off bundler config vocabulary, never a cloud provider's.
annotation.integrationPoints: Stage 1 buildSnapshot reads config path build.linking.bundles.scripts and the autoDetect flag; containment guard from mod:repovine/src/fs/containment; the resulting map rides the snapshot into the stage2 graph build, where the infra-runtime-links interpreter consumes it as handlerPathMap.
annotation.dataFlow: bundle script source -> parseBundleOutputScript (regex sweep over esbuild/webpack/rollup key pairs) -> per-script output-to-source map -> loadBundleOutputHandlerMap merges across configured + auto-detected scripts that pass containment -> RepositoryFactsSnapshot.bundleOutputHandlerMap.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: gates a console warning when reading a bundle script that exists on disk throws

annotation.summary: Stage-2 domain tagging engine: path-segment tags, basename heuristics (suffixes like .controller, .service), import-graph cluster propagation via label propagation, repovine.domains.json pattern/alias matching, package labels, infra resource exclude/keep matching, and heavy vs lightweight classification into module domain tags and tagged edges.

keyExports.collectAllDomainTags: Primary entry: returns {tagsByModule Map, classification Map} — heavy/lightweight domain tiers.
keyExports.evaluateBasenameCandidate: Promotes stem from suffix files (.controller, .service) when graph connectivity threshold met.
keyExports.getClusterDomains: Label propagation on import graph for emergent package-adjacent domains.
keyExports.getPathBasedDomains: Directory-segment domain tags excluding structural dirs.
keyExports.resolveDomainToCanonical: Maps config aliases to canonical domain id strings.

assumptions: Propagation review 2026-06-20: upstream types unchanged; domain logic unchanged.

sideEffects.description: loadDomainsConfig reads repovine.domains.json during collectAllDomainTags

risks: Overlapping repovine.domains.json patterns can double-tag modules.
Cluster propagation may over-merge unrelated modules in dense import hubs.
patterns: Tagged edge tagSource distinguishes path, package, cluster, and pattern origins.
Basename suffixes and PascalCase stems evaluated with graph connectivity gates.
invariants: Domain tags are additive — a module may carry multiple domain labels.
Lightweight domains (1-2 modules) hidden from anomalies unless explicitly included.
annotation.integrationPoints: repovine.domains.json via domains-schema; stage2 graph build; map_context domain scopes; domains advisor.
annotation.dataFlow: repovine.domains.json patterns + path/cluster heuristics → module domain tags → tagged edges → domain: scopes in map_context and annotation roll-ups.

annotation.summary: First-run domains advisor: scans snapshot infra resource suffix histograms (INFRA_NOISE_SUFFIXES), witness-aware mixed-suffix patterns (infra.excludePatterns), PascalCase module basename ratio, and infra folder path clusters to propose repovine.domains.json additions. Returns mergedConfig (accept/exclude preview) and keepConfig (committed infra.keep preview); applyDomainsSuggestion/applyDomainsKeep merge without writing disk.

keyExports.applyDomainsKeep: Symmetric to applyDomainsSuggestion: maps infra suffix/pattern suggestions to infra.keep.suffixes/patterns so resources stay visible and stop being proposed.
keyExports.applyDomainsSuggestion: Merges accepted additions into DomainsConfigFile (excludeSuffixes, excludePatterns, basename.pascalCase, domains.paths).
keyExports.computeDomainsSuggestion: Runs infra suffix/pattern, PascalCase basename, and infra folder path heuristics; filters declined ids; builds mergedConfig and keepConfig previews.
keyExports.readDomainsConfigFile: Reads repovine.domains.json via DomainsConfigSchema; returns {} on missing/invalid.

assumptions: Never writes repovine.domains.json without explicit user approval.
Mixed suffix buckets emit infra.excludePatterns with spared witnessed labels instead of blanket excludeSuffixes.

sideEffects.description: readDomainsConfigFile reads repovine.domains.json

risks: Auto-applying infra excludeSuffixes/patterns without review can hide legitimate domain tags on noisy resource labels.
keepConfig commits survive .repovine/ wipe unlike declined cache — user must understand keep vs decline.
patterns: INFRA_NOISE_SUFFIXES list drives infra.excludeSuffixes suggestions from runtime-resource label histogram.
computeInfraDomainPathSuggestions proposes domains axis entries for ^infrastructure/<folder> patterns.
annotation.flowDescription: Suffix histogram + graph module paths → computeDomainsSuggestion → formatDomainsConfigFile preview for MCP/CLI onboarding.
invariants: basename.pascalCase suggestion requires ≥12 PascalCase modules and ratio ≥0.25.
Non-infra axes are no-ops in applyDomainsKeep.
annotation.integrationPoints: MCP suggest_domains_config and decline_domains_config_suggestions; cli domains-advisor; RepovineRuntime domainsSuggestions after build.
annotation.stateShape: DomainsSuggestionAddition discriminated by axis infra.excludeSuffixes | infra.excludePatterns | basename.pascalCase | domains; DomainsSuggestion wraps additions[], axes[], declinedHidden, mergedConfig, keepConfig previews.
annotation.dataFlow: RepositoryFactsSnapshot infraModules + module basenames → computeDomainsSuggestion → DomainsSuggestion with mergedConfig preview → suggest_domains_config MCP / CLI onboarding.

annotation.summary: Schema and loader for repovine.domains.json. Validates with a strict Zod schema (domains paths/aliases, infra exclude/keep/pruneInert, basename rules, package grouping, structural dirs), compiles globs to GlobMatcher (avoiding regex catastrophic backtracking) and aliases to a lookup map, hands stage2 the compiled DomainsConfig for domain tagging and inert-resource pruning.

keyExports.DomainsConfig: DomainsConfigFile plus compiled caches: _aliasToCanonical Record, _fileAsDomainInclude/Exclude GlobMatcher[], _structuralDirs Set.
keyExports.DomainsConfigSchema: Strict Zod schema for domains{paths,aliases}, infra{excludeSuffixes,excludePatterns,keep,pruneInert}, basename, packages, structuralDirs.
keyExports.GlobMatcher: { test(path: string): boolean } — the compiled glob pattern interface.
keyExports.compileGlob: (glob: string): GlobMatcher — linear DP glob matcher avoiding regex backtracking.
keyExports.loadDomainsConfig: (repoRoot: string): DomainsConfig | null — reads and validates repovine.domains.json.

assumptions: Missing repovine.domains.json is normal: loadDomainsConfig returns null.
infra.pruneInert defaults off; infra.keep is the per-resource opt-out.
Alias lookup is case-insensitive; canonical names and aliases are lowercased in the map.

sideEffects.description: loadDomainsConfig reads repovine.domains.json from repo root
reports schema validation and parse failures

risks: pruneInert=true drops unwitnessed runtime-resource nodes; a misconfigured keep marker silently hides resources.

risks.text: Callers must treat null as 'no config' not an error; must not assume compiled cache fields are present on a hand-built config.
repovine.domains.json is a committed config contract: one unknown top-level key fails validation and the file is discarded. A key must exist in DomainsConfigSchema before consumers can write it.

patterns: compileGlob is shared between loader and domains advisor preview, so suggestions match loader behavior.
Compiled caches are computed once at load and carried on the config object.
annotation.flowDescription: Zod-parse repovine.domains.json, compile globs to RegExp plus an alias map and a structural-dirs set, then expose the DomainsConfig used for stage2 domain tagging.
invariants: The schema is strict: unknown top-level keys are rejected rather than ignored.
DOMAINS_CONFIG_MERGE_STRATEGY marks infra.pruneInert as set-once during a setup merge.
annotation.integrationPoints: Consumed by stage2 domain tagging/inert pruning, MCP suggest_domains_config advisor, CLI domains flow; resolves config path through mod:repovine/src/paths.
annotation.stateShape: DomainsConfigFile (DomainsConfigSchema): optional domains record {paths?,aliases?}, infra {excludeSuffixes?,excludePatterns?}, basename {pascalCase?,files{include?,exclude?}}, packages {enabled?,exclude?,rename?,merge?}, structuralDirs?; DomainsConfig extends with compiled caches _aliasToCanonical, _fileAsDomainInclude/_Exclude RegExp[], _structuralDirs Set.
annotation.dataFlow: repoRoot → repovine.domains.json → Zod safeParse → compiled aliases/globs/structural dirs → DomainsConfig → stage2 tagging and pruning.

annotation.summary: Read-only post-composition integrity gate: validateComposedGraph checks that every stage1 snapshot module/template projects to a stage2 graph node and no edge references a missing node; summarizeGraphValidationProblems formats results. Wired into composeRepositoryGraph — warns by default, throws under REPOVINE_DEV.

keyExports.summarizeGraphValidationProblems: One-line summary of the first N problems for log/throw.

risks: If composeRepositoryGraph changes its pruning/mutation passes, re-verify invariants still hold.
Node dropped together with all its edges yields no dangling edge; missing-module still catches it, but co-dropped pairs are a by-design blind spot.
invariants: Never mutates the graph; intentional inert-resource pruning leaves a consistent graph.
annotation.integrationPoints: Called by stage2/index composeRepositoryGraph after domain passes; consumed by FindingF3 audit gate.

annotation.summary: Built-in interpreter bootstrap. Imports INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS from interpreters/index and registerInterpreter each into stage2/interpreter/registry; auto-invoked on import before stage2 compose.

keyExports.bootstrapInternalInterpreters: Registers all built-in interpreters from INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream interpreters and registry; bootstrap side-effect still accurate.

sideEffects.description: Populates interpreter registry on first import

risks: Missing interpreter in INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS silently omits graph or entrypoint contributions.
patterns: No manifest ceremony — built-ins register directly like source plugins.
annotation.integrationPoints: interpreters/index INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS; stage2/index imports bootstrap side-effect before compose.
annotation.dataFlow: import bootstrap → registerInterpreter for each INTERNAL_INTERPRETERS entry.

annotation.summary: Runs the interpreter layers over the built graph. It decides which interpreters apply to this repository, orders them by their declared dependencies, then lets each contribute graph changes and entrypoint fragments. Interpreters that do not apply are recorded rather than run, so an enrichment that produced nothing is distinguishable from one that never ran.

keyExports.ComposeInterpretersOptions: The graph and snapshot to work on, the module index, the domain configuration, an optional interpreter override and an optional logger.
keyExports.InterpreterCompositionResult: The applied and skipped identifiers plus the collected entrypoint fragments.
keyExports.composeInterpreters: Filters, orders and runs the interpreters, returning which ran, which were skipped, and the entrypoints collected.

assumptions: Two independent conditions gate an interpreter: the languages present in this repository must include one it declares, and the hints it requires must be present.
The hint check walks a dotted path and gates on the key being present, so an interpreter whose required hint no module emits never runs. A slot present but empty still enables it.
Ordering follows declared dependencies, so an interpreter that builds on another's contribution sees the graph after it.

Graph contributions are applied on the trusted path: the schema check exists but is switched off here, so a node with a bogus type or a foreign data shape reaches the graph unchecked and the interpreter is still reported as applied. The application step enforces only referential rules — a node id already present is skipped, an edge whose endpoints are absent is dropped without a warning. The shape contract rests on the type system and a whole-pipeline law test.
Both hooks are optional; an interpreter may contribute graph changes, entrypoints, or neither.
The interpreter list can be supplied directly, which is what lets tests compose a known set instead of the registry.

sideEffects.description: applies validated deltas to the graph passed in

risks: The skipped list records the identifier but not the reason, so an interpreter missing because the repository lacks its language looks identical to one missing because a hint was never produced — the two need very different fixes.
A skip is silent in the sense that the pipeline succeeds: the enrichment is simply absent from the graph, and nothing downstream can tell it was expected.
The applied list names every interpreter that was ordered, including one that implements neither hook, so it reports what was enabled rather than what actually contributed.
patterns: Filter, order, then run: applicability is decided before anything touches the graph.
One shared context serves both hooks, so an interpreter sees the same view whichever it implements.
invariants: An interpreter that fails either gate is recorded and never invoked.
An empty interpreter set returns an empty result rather than failing.
annotation.integrationPoints: The registered interpreters come from mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/registry; the hook contracts from mod:repovine/src/interpreter/types; validation and application from mod:repovine/src/graph and mod:repovine/src/graph/delta; the domain configuration from mod:repovine/src/stage2/domains; entrypoint fragments carry the slot marker defined in mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-slots.
annotation.dataFlow: registered interpreters → language and hint gates → dependency order → per interpreter, a validated graph delta and any entrypoint fragments → applied and skipped identifiers with the collected fragments.

envDependencies.REPOVINE_VERBOSE: Enables informational logging from the default logger

annotation.summary: The shared vocabulary that lets independent interpreter layers label the entrypoints they produce. Each produced entry carries a hidden slot marker naming the kind of entrypoint it is. The server shell later replays entries slot by slot to reproduce a fixed public ordering, then removes the marker so what callers see matches the older inline shape exactly.

keyExports.EntrypointSlot: The eight slot names an entry can carry: python-api, file-api, jsx-route, tanstack-route, angular-route, conditional, file-page, service-trigger.
keyExports.LAYER_ENTRYPOINT_SLOT_KEY: The hidden field name the marker is stored under.
keyExports.SlottedEntrypointFragment: An entrypoint fragment that carries the marker.
keyExports.stripEntrypointFragmentInternals: Returns a shallow copy of an entry with the marker removed, for public output.

assumptions: This lives outside every layer on purpose, so the frontend, backend and infrastructure producers can all use the same slot names without importing one another.
Ordering authority belongs to the server shell, not to the layers: producers only label their entries and the shell decides the sequence.
The marker is an internal detail with a reserved-looking name, which is why it is stripped rather than documented.

risks.text: Slot names are matched as strings by the replay index rather than resolved through types, so callers depending on entrypoint ordering must verify their slot set against the replay list rather than assume a rename propagates.

risks: The strip is shallow, so nested objects stay shared with the original entry and a later mutation of the returned copy reaches the source.
patterns: A neutral vocabulary module breaks what would otherwise be cross-imports between sibling layers.
Producers label, one consumer orders: the layers stay unaware of the public sequence.
invariants: The marker never appears in public output; it is removed on the way out.
Every slotted fragment carries exactly one slot name.
annotation.integrationPoints: The slot names are attached by the interpreter layers that produce entrypoints and consumed by the server-side entrypoint index, which replays by slot and then calls the strip before returning; the fragment type comes from mod:repovine/src/interpreter/types.
annotation.dataFlow: layer produces a fragment → marker attached → shell indexes fragments by slot → replays them in the fixed order → marker stripped → public entrypoint list.

annotation.summary: In-memory entrypoint store keyed by RepositoryGraph. rememberInterpreterEntrypoints saves interpreter collectEntrypoints output; getInterpreterEntrypoints supplies mcp/lib/entrypoints replay during get_entrypoints and trace_flow.

keyExports.getInterpreterEntrypoints: Returns fragments stored for this graph instance.
keyExports.rememberInterpreterEntrypoints: Attaches collected EntrypointFragment[] to graph WeakMap.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream interpreter/types and types; WeakMap entrypoint store unchanged.

sideEffects.description: WeakMap entry per RepositoryGraph for collected entrypoints

risks: Replacing graph object without re-compose yields empty get_entrypoints until refresh_context.
patterns: Graph-scoped side store — not persisted in .repovine cache JSON.

annotation.summary: Shared display helper for graph module and infra-module node labels. Neutral utility extracted from the old stage2 inline passes for use by code-structure and infra-runtime-links interpreters.

assumptions: Used for graph node labels in MCP map_context and inspect_node — not full paths.
Strips .ts/.tsx/.jsx extensions before splitting path segments.
Paths with ≤2 segments returned whole; longer paths show ellipsis prefix plus last two segments.
risks: Two-segment collision possible for unrelated files sharing same parent/name suffix — acceptable for display-only labels.
Does not strip .cpp/.py extensions — only TS/JS-style suffixes.
patterns: Extracted from former inline copy in stage2/index.ts so code-structure and infra-runtime-links layers share one implementation.
invariants: Pure function — no I/O or global state.
Always returns forward-slash joined segments even on Windows inputs.

annotation.summary: Builder-level witness rule (D6): after the graph composer finishes, drops runtime-resource nodes that carry only structural contains/tagged edges (no load-bearing witness). Gated by infra.pruneInert (off by default); infra.keep suffixes/patterns opt out per resource label via matchesInfraResourceExclude.

keyExports.pruneInertRuntimeResources: Mutates RepositoryGraph in place — deletes unwitnessed runtime-resource nodes and incident edges; returns pruned count (0 when pruneInert disabled or nothing to prune).

assumptions: Must run after every load-bearing edge is added (post interpreter composer) and before graph consumers.
Inert resources only carry contains/tagged, so pruning never orphans load-bearing edges.

sideEffects.description: Mutates graph.nodes, graph.byType, graph.edges, graph.outEdges, graph.inEdges in place

risks: Enabling pruneInert without reviewing keep markers can remove resources agents expect in topology queries.
Misconfigured keep patterns may fail to protect intended resources.
invariants: No-op (returns 0) unless config.infra.pruneInert is true.
Resources matching infra.keep suffixes/patterns are never pruned.

annotation.summary: Phase 3.1 projection layer: maps enriched semanticHints.routes with source:'file' into legacy FileBasedRoute records for MCP get_entrypoints replay. keyExports.inferFileBasedRoutes: Iterates snapshot.modules; keeps routes where source==='file' and both framework and fileType are set.

assumptions: Propagation review 2026-06-20: upstream types hash changed; file-based route inference unchanged.
risks: Routes missing framework or fileType are silently skipped — under-reporting when plugins omit fields.
Novel framework fileType conventions may mis-classify via fileBasedEntryKind heuristics.
patterns: Thin compatibility shim between stage-1 RouteInfo hints and MCP entrypoint consumers.

fileBasedEntryKind returns only page | route | api.
annotation.integrationPoints: source-plugins/typescript collectFileRoutes (upstream inference); ui-entrypoints collectUiRouteEntrypoints; mcp/lib/entrypoints fileApiLayerKey/filePageLayerKey replay.

annotation.dataFlow: collectFileRoutes (stage-1) → RouteInfo with source:file → inferFileBasedRoutes → fileBasedEntryKind → interpreter slots → MCP replay.

annotation.summary: Maps IaC service trigger records to MCP entrypoint kind strings using registered trigger-type metadata from the IaC plugin registry. Enables infra-runtime-links and get_entrypoints to classify Lambda/API Gateway/SQS/etc. triggers consistently, with a webhook sub-kind when an api trigger path suggests webhooks. Kept in stage2/runtime (not MCP) so interpreters own entrypoint construction without importing MCP internals.

assumptions: Derived review: verified upstream (iac/bootstrap, iac/registry); integrationPoints and dataFlow still accurate.

annotation.summary: worker_threads isolate entry for the Stage 2 compose offload (D3): runs composeRepositoryGraph inside a worker so the synchronous compose never blocks the MCP control plane. Executes on import in the worker; returns the graph plus interpreter entrypoints to the parent by postMessage.
assumptions: Spawned only via worker_threads with { snapshot } in workerData and a live parentPort; throws otherwise.
modulesById is rebuilt from snapshot.modules inside the worker — only the serializable snapshot crosses the boundary.

sideEffects.description: runs Stage 2 compose in a worker isolate; unref's parentPort so it exits after replying
reroutes console.log → stderr and silences the pipeline log sink to protect the parent's JSON-RPC stdout channel

risks: The reply shape { type:'ok', graph, entrypoints } is the contract with mod:repovine/src/stage2/index runStage2InWorker; interpreter entrypoints are posted EXPLICITLY because their WeakMap sidecar does not survive structured clone — dropping the field silently yields zero entrypoints in the parent.
console.log lands on stdout by default, which would corrupt the parent's JSON-RPC stream — the reroute is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
annotation.integrationPoints: Spawned by mod:repovine/src/stage2/index (runStage2InWorker); the parent re-keys the posted entrypoints onto the cloned graph via rememberInterpreterEntrypoints in mod:repovine/src/stage2/interpreter/entrypoint-store.

annotation.summary: Central repovine type hub for plugin facts, graph taxonomy, MCP views, and annotations. Snapshot config identity (analysisVersion, engineBuildId), original Kubernetes kind, capped-link pagination, and bounded-grep metadata are explicit typed contracts; stage1/plugin-sdk types are re-exported, graph-stage types are defined here.

keyExports.AnnotationContent: Writable annotation field bag; sideEffects typed as SideEffect[].
keyExports.GraphDelta: Interpreter patch {nodes, edges} validated by mod:repovine/src/graph/delta.
keyExports.GraphNode: Discriminated union keyed by NodeType with NodeDataByType payloads.
keyExports.NodeViewDetail: MCP inspect payload: NodeView plus optional body/grepMatches/pagination.
keyExports.RepositoryFactsSnapshot: Stage-1 snapshot: modules[], infraModules[], templates?, linkingConfig?, bundleOutputHandlerMap? (bundle output path to source entry path), outsideRepoPaths? (candidates refused for resolving outside the workspace root), analysisVersion? (manual cache-invalidation version), engineBuildId? (dev-only reuse-gate fingerprint, mod:repovine/src/stage1/engine-build-id).
keyExports.RepositoryGraph: In-memory graph container {nodes, edges} consumed by MCP tools.
keyExports.StoredAnnotation: Persisted note with contentHash, importBaseline, schemaVersion, provenance.
keyExports.TagEdgeSource: Provenance for tagged edges: path | package | cluster | pattern.

assumptions: Stage-1/plugin-sdk types are re-exported from @repovine/plugin-sdk; graph-stage types are defined in this file.
AnnotationContent.sideEffects uses SideEffect[] from mod:repovine/src/annotations/side-effect-vocab.
risks: Wide fan-in (~63 downstream) on GraphNode, NodeType, or RepositoryFactsSnapshot changes.
keyExports must reference symbols exported from this module graph node, including re-exports tracked by the builder.
patterns: Shared contract hub — breaking changes ripple stage1, stage2, MCP, annotations, and plugins.
Producer/engine split: Semantic*Delta types carry language/infra semantics; engine stamps ids/paths/hashes.
annotation.flowDescription: Stage-1 modules populate ModuleInfo → stage2 graph nodes/edges → annotations attach to graph node ids.
invariants: SemanticModuleDelta.transient=true forces empty contentHash so poisoned extractions are not cached.
Re-exported plugin-sdk types must stay compatible with mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/types.
extensionPoints: NodeDataByType and DomainNodeData tier/weight fields extend graph metadata without new NodeType values.
Open-string InfraKind/WebFramework slots allow additive plugin vocabulary.
annotation.integrationPoints: Hub for stage1 finalize, stage2 runtime-links/domains, MCP inspect_node/search, annotations read/write; re-exports mod:@repovine/plugin-sdk/src/types.
annotation.dataFlow: Plugin-sdk types re-exported → stage1 fills RepositoryFactsSnapshot → stage2 builds RepositoryGraph/GraphNode → MCP emits NodeView/NodeViewDetail → StoredAnnotation keyed by graph node id.

annotation.summary: Compose service `cli` (profile cli): one-shot `node scripts/langgraph-cli.mjs` run for CI/local debug. Shares the egress-gw network namespace, NODE_OPTIONS heap guardrail, and the hardened x-harness-app settings (read-only rootfs, cap_drop ALL). Command args pass through to langgraph-cli.mjs; exits non-zero when compliance fails or credentials block the worker. Verified against current compose.yaml: unchanged.
assumptions: Profile cli: docker compose --profile cli run --rm cli --task "...".
Command args pass through to langgraph-cli.mjs after image entrypoint.
Depends on egress-gw healthy; gateway verifies allowed npm/provider egress before cli can run.
Exits non-zero when compliance fails or credentials block the worker.

sideEffects.description: Runs full LangGraph Agent Protocol cycle via provider worker
Writes artifacts under .harness in the bind-mounted sandbox

risks: Missing provider credentials yield blocked runs with exit 1.
Long multi-agent runs can hit HARNESS_MEM_LIMIT despite NODE_OPTIONS if subprocess memory grows.
Stale local .env ALLOW_DOMAINS can block runtime_check GitHub fetches.
patterns: Compose profile isolates CLI runs from http/tg-bot long-running services.
invariants: One-shot container — not a long-running service.
Shares the egress-gw network namespace for controlled outbound access.

This service is the sandbox half of the pair: resource:generic:cli-attach runs the same entrypoint against a mounted host worktree, and only this one waits on workspace-init and mounts the managed .workspace.
annotation.integrationPoints: repovine/examples/agent-harness-demo/compose.yaml profile cli; scripts/langgraph-cli.mjs; x-harness-app Dockerfile build.
annotation.dataFlow: compose run cli → shared harness-app image → langgraph-cli.mjs → invokeGraph → .harness artifacts on bind-mounted sandbox.

annotation.summary: Compose service `cli-attach` (profile attach-cli): the attach-mode counterpart of `cli`. Mounts a pre-created host Git worktree at /workspace instead of the managed sandbox, and runs one-shot `node scripts/langgraph-cli.mjs` as the worktree owner so writes land with the operator's uid and gid. Verified against current compose.attach.yaml: unchanged (extends harness-base, required-no-default ${VAR:?} bind sources, git-guard ro pointer).
assumptions: scripts/attach-launcher.mjs is the supported entrypoint: it runs the fail-closed preflight and creates the state layout before any docker call.

The YAML merge is wholesale per key: declaring local volumes, depends_on or environment replaces the anchor's value entirely, which is how attach avoids mounting .workspace and avoids waiting on workspace-init.
HARNESS_TARGET_MODE=attach and HARNESS_REPO_ROOT=/workspace mark the run for the target-repo policy; HOME points at the container state dir.

sideEffects.description: writes into the operator's mounted worktree as the operator's uid/gid
runs the full protocol cycle through a provider worker

risks: A direct `docker compose --profile attach-cli up` with hand-set environment bypasses the launcher preflight. That is a deliberate operator override, unsupported and not prevented here.

Attach vars deliberately avoid the `${VAR:?}` required form, because Compose interpolates the whole file before profile filtering and a required-var error would break every sandbox invocation. An unset var falls back to a path under a device file so container create fails instead of Docker auto-creating a root-owned host directory.
annotation.integrationPoints: Launched through scripts/attach-launcher.mjs; shares the harness-app image and the egress-gw network namespace with mod:repovine-agent-harness-demo/lib/target-repo deciding attach policy.

annotation.summary: Compose service egress-gw: Alpine sidecar with dnsmasq, ipset, iptables, GitHub CIDR bootstrap, and startup/healthcheck egress probes. Harness containers attach via network_mode:service:egress-gw for fail-closed provider, Telegram, npm, and GitHub release-asset egress. Declared twice: full definition in compose.yaml plus a profiles-only stub in compose.attach.yaml.
assumptions: ALLOW_DOMAINS, UPSTREAM_DNS, GITHUB_CIDR_BOOTSTRAP, and EGRESS_SELF_TEST* come from compose/.env; defaults cover OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, Telegram, npm, github.com/api.github.com, and common githubusercontent release asset hosts.
LLM_PROVIDER selects the default provider self-test URL; EGRESS_SELF_TEST_ALLOW_URLS can override the provider probe list.
Publishes HARNESS_HTTP_PORT on loopback via this service because http/bot/harness use network_mode: service:egress-gw.
Only this sidecar holds NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW; harness apps keep cap_drop ALL.

sideEffects.description: Configures iptables/ipset default-deny egress filtering for the shared harness netns
Fetches api.github.com/meta at startup when GitHub CIDR bootstrap is enabled
Runs dnsmasq and curl-based startup/healthcheck probes for allowed npm/provider egress and blocked example.com

risks: Misconfigured ALLOW_DOMAINS blocks provider APIs, Telegram long-poll, npm installs, or GitHub-hosted binary/release downloads.
Over-broad domain allowlist weakens fail-closed egress posture.
GitHub meta/bootstrap outage falls back to DNS allow-list only, which is less robust for runtime_check binary fetches.
Provider, npm, or upstream DNS outages make the gateway fail startup self-test or become unhealthy.
invariants: Only this sidecar holds NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW; every harness app keeps cap_drop ALL and reaches the network through this namespace.

Both halves of the topology attach here: the sandbox services and their attach-mode counterparts share this namespace, so the egress posture is identical whether the run targets a managed sandbox or a mounted host worktree.
annotation.integrationPoints: docker/egress-gw Dockerfile (curl, jq, dnsmasq, ipset, iptables); all harness-app services depend_on egress-gw healthy; .env.example documents allowlist/self-test knobs.

annotation.summary: Runtime resource for the main harness Dockerfile: two-stage image building repovine CLI from monorepo source, baking demo workspace defaults, smoke-testing agents protocol, and supplying REPOVINE_CLI to profile-gated cli/http/tg-bot services.
assumptions: Runtime resource mirrors infra:dockerfile:examples/agent-harness-demo/Dockerfile — graph tracks both IaC module and resource node.
Build context is monorepo root; compose references this dockerfile path.

sideEffects.description: docker build runs npm install/ci, npm run build, apt-get, and layer export

risks: Stale cached image hides engine changes until docker compose build --no-cache.
Missing typescript copy from builder breaks stage1 imports at runtime.
patterns: Self-contained compile-from-source eliminates host dist/ drift.
Two-stage split keeps devDependencies out of runtime layer.
invariants: Image smoke-tests node dist/mcp/index.js agents protocol at build time.
Runs as uid node with cap_drop ALL in compose — no docker socket access.
extensionPoints: Demo lib/agents bind-mount overrides baked COPY at runtime without rebuild.
annotation.integrationPoints: compose.yaml x-harness-app build; infra:dockerfile node; domain:infra-dockerfile.
annotation.dataFlow: docker compose --profile cli|http|tg-bot build → builder compiles repovine dist → runtime copies demo tree → REPOVINE_CLI env → harness entry scripts.

annotation.summary: Runtime resource for egress-gw Dockerfile: Alpine sidecar building dnsmasq+ipset+iptables allow-list gateway whose network namespace is shared by hardened harness worker containers.
assumptions: Harness-app containers use network_mode: service:egress-gw — all outbound traffic filtered here.
ALLOW_DOMAINS, EGRESS_ALLOW_CIDRS, and EGRESS_ALLOW_HOST_DOCKER_INTERNAL tune allow-list.

sideEffects.description: Mutates iptables/ipset and runs dnsmasq at container start

risks: Misconfigured ALLOW_DOMAINS blocks LLM/npm/GitHub silently.
Local model host IP must be allow-listed via EGRESS_ALLOW_CIDRS when not using host.docker.internal on worker netns.

invariants: Only egress-gw holds NET_ADMIN — harness worker keeps cap_drop ALL.
Healthcheck invokes /entrypoint.sh healthcheck before dependent services start.
extensionPoints: EGRESS_SELF_TEST_ALLOW_URLS adds ad-hoc probe URLs during gateway startup.
annotation.integrationPoints: compose.yaml egress-gw service; infra:dockerfile:.../egress-gw/Dockerfile; published HARNESS_HTTP_PORT on this netns.
annotation.dataFlow: compose build egress-gw → entrypoint configures dnsmasq+ipset+iptables → harness shared netns → healthcheck self-test → cli/http/tg-bot egress.

annotation.summary: Base compose service in examples/agent-harness-demo/compose.yaml (profile 'harness-base', never requested — inert by design). Exists so cli-attach/http-attach/tg-bot-attach in compose.attach.yaml can `extends: {file: compose.yaml, service: harness-base}` to inherit build context, resource ceilings, read_only, cap_drop, tmpfs, and network_mode from the shared x-harness-app anchor without inheriting the sandbox workspace mount or workspace-init depends_on gate (this service's own volumes/depends_on are empty).

PORT and HARNESS_HTTP_TOKEN injected via harness-env override.
Port published on egress-gw (127.0.0.1:8080 by default), not on http service itself.
Depends on egress-gw healthy before start.

Provider-backed graph and ask runs via shared harness-app env
